title: Family Meal at Blue Hill
history: Blue Hill New York opened in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village neighborhood in April of 2000.The restaurant has evolved over the last two decades, sourcing ingredients from Blue Hill Farm, the Barber family’s dairy in Great Barrington, MA; from the Stone Barns Center for Agriculture in Pocantico Hills, NY; as well as from farms within 250 miles of New York City. Family Meal began in the summer of 2021 and welcomes guests to a menuless dinner experience of shared plates.

reviews.review: Still exceptional, all these years later. From their service to their beautiful presentation, I loved every single bite. The ambiance is still fantastic and they go out of their way to make you feel welcome. I wish I could point out what specific thing or things I enjoyed the most, but alas, I just loved everything lol. If anything, this made me want to book a table at Stone Barns, just so I relieve that magical experience all over again.

Lovely michelin starred farm to table dining experience with seasonal ingredients and cozy vibe

I love a good farm to table place and this is one of them. They take their ingredients, especially vegetables, very seriously so what's not to love? Tucked in a quieter street by wsp, the restaurant has a cozy welcoming vibe that doesn't feel overly pretentious. Most guests were dressed smart casual. 

We were seated in the middle of the restaurant and found the service friendly and attentive. There isn't a menu per se since everything is seasonal and adjusted based on ingredient availability but just know you're in for a great four course family style meal. I loved every dish! The trout and squash were my favorite. We all walked out quite full so no worries on portion sizes.

Definitely recommended if you're looking to celebrate a special occasion in a relaxed setting or just want to treat yourself! Only small inconvenience was that the bathroom towards the back was very cold (but hey it's winter after all and didn't really impact my dining experience)

Came here to celebrate my friend making partner last night. I thought this spot was amazing. Every course was unique and delicious, my favorites were the fish centric ones. I thought the main course (beef) was good but less impressive than everything else. I had the merlot which was great. The cocktail was amazing as well. Everything was amazing

This place was nothing special. I honestly could've made all of it myself at home. We didn't even want some of the dishes. Bowl of clam chowder, two eggs with hash, chicken and mushrooms with barley, pita with black garlic and horseradish...only the pink radicchio with citrus dressing was interesting. The dessert was almost insulting...a scoop of sorbet with a scoop of granola in a paper cup. I have no idea why they have a Michelin star? We gladly gave our leftovers to a homeless man in the park and agreed that that's what made the meal worth it. He ate and we didn't have to revisit our disappointment. Sorry, gotta be honest. I wouldn't want anybody else to waste their money.

Cozy and inviting restaurant nestled in a basement a few steps away from Washington square park. My partner and I love stone barns, so we were very excited to try Family Meal! 

Our waitress was very attentive and did an excellent job explaining the dishes and ingredients. Some highlights for me were the salad and the squash, but my favorite was the bread - so pillowy, soft, and fragrant. The other dishes were less memorable. The timing of the meal was a bit off - we waited quite a bit for our drinks, the first few courses came out very quickly, and then we again waited quite a bit for the salad and then the main course. 

All in all, the service was excellent, vibes were great, and food was good, but I had hoped for more exciting food experience.

Blue Hill, as it was formally known, was a special go to place when we visited NYC. Its farm to table menu and upbeat atmosphere were particularly enticing. Last week we had the opportunity to visit the new Family Meal version of Blue Hill.  Sadly, that evening the menu was not up to par. The menu is now fixed price only. That night dinner was $145 per person. The portions are small and many of the courses included raw fish, something one of our guests does not eat. Our guest was encouraged to wait for the steak course. When it arrived it was cooked medium rare. Normally this temperature would be perfect for a filet, however this was a skirt steak and it was chewy and barely edible. For dessert large bowls of yogurt with warm maple granola were served family style. For the money spent I would think a pastry chef might have delivered a better option- one that  did not appear to be a breakfast bowl. The tables were full the room was noisy.  It was difficult to carry on a conversation. The service was initially attentive but gradually became lack luster as our frustration with the menu became apparent.  Until this farm to table restaurant ups its game we won't be returning. Disappointed!
Update: To Blue Hill's credit the manager contacted our group and apologized. She also credited us for a portion of our bill and invited us back to make amends. Kudos to Blue Hill for stepping up.

Hey Dan. I'm pretty sure you're reading this, given what you've said about yourself on television and the impression I got when we met. So I'll skip to the straight dope.

The room, as always, is a pleasure - warm, inviting, welcoming, especially on a chilly evening. The service is also very good, with particular kudos to the sommelier, who was really knowledgeable and didn't try to upsell us (hopefully that's okay with you). It did take a while for our table's lone cocktail to make it to the table. I'm a pretty firm believer that food shouldn't be served until the drink order is filled.

Anyway, the food. Great product as always, but a few niggles. We had two dishes that sort of sat in a green broth. Looked similar, tasted different. One was underseasoned, one overseasoned. Apart from that, everything savory was pretty tasty. Very nice seafood preparations.

Dessert was a bit of a disappointment. A crumble with yogurt? We could make that at home. In fact, the crumble was sort of a warm granola, which left us feeling like we'd had breakfast for dessert. Maybe something a bit more soigné would make a better end to the meal.

So overall a good night, though maybe not quite Michelin-worthy. Our guests from out of town said they hadn't eaten so well in a while. Just a few things that the more experienced and perspicacious NYC diners might want to see improve...

P.S. We dithered about coming in, given the revelations a couple of years back about the working environment and practices at Stone Barns. Obviously Family Meal doesn't make the same claims about the food, and I haven't seen anything negative about the staff. We hope things have improved upstate.

Honestly the setting was stunning, the mood and energy so relaxing, basking in the sun having some good food outdoors and doing a mini hike afterwards. So nice

Service was cafeteria style, but even then the servers walk you through the entire meal.

Only issue is the price. Personally I found it a bit steep for what it is. But definitely worth the experience.

TLDR: The food was delicious, but DEFINITELY not worth the price. Food was also extremely fresh though

FOOD
As we charted our way through the menu there were a few things that I will remember as being delicious. I enjoyed about 80% of the menu and some dishes were outstanding (I'm looking at you bread + potatoes).

But there were some misses. 1) The portions were small - I wish for ~$250 a person (after taxes and tip) I had more than a small medallion of tenderloin 2) Some dishes were misses i.e., the salad, the halibut which lacked flavor, and the tuna crudo whose texture felt like it was put through a meat grinder

SERVICE
Service was exceptional. Like 1/2-mich level service which I really appreciated. I liked that our server intimately knew the menu and talked about the farm. There is also coat and bag check which is great

ATMOSPHERE
Really great atmosphere - love the vibe of the restaurant. Sheek and clean. Bathroom was fantastic and love that they have their own brand of soap

Vegetarian options: If you let them know of your dietary restrictions ahead of time, they can accomodate vegetarian restrictions
Food was amazing! Didn't look as fancy as some other flamboyant Michelin restaurants, but the quality and taste was def above other picture fancy restaurants

We had heard rave reviews of the family meal at Blue Hill, so we made a reservation for lunch for this past Sunday. I'm sorry to say that we were sorely disappointed:
1. The choice of dishes was shockingly bad - it felt like they pulled together some random dishes with whatever was left over in the kitchen from the day before. What's even worse, the quantity was woefully inadequate. There were 3 of us. We each were served 1 small shrimp, 2-3 small pieces of chicken (most of which was skin), a few spoons of rice, some deep fried parsnips that were so hard they were inedible (they might as well have served us a dog biscuit each), a little bit of lettuce, and a piece of flatbread. Dessert was one small cake that had to be split 3 ways. We're small eaters to begin with, and even we were left hungry! For $85 per person, this was a complete rip-off.
2. Service was terrible. No one from the wait staff or manager team bothered to stop by even once while we were eating to ask how everything was.

We did not expect a Michelin-rated restaurant to scrimp on the food and not care about the dining experience. It was very disappointing. We will NEVER go back.

No wonder Michelin awarded a star. Family Meal at Blue Hill has it all.

This stylish little neighborhood gem offers warm, personal service from friendly servers and staff, and the entire dining experience felt like a visit to the chef's kitchen table. I sat at the bar, and the bartender's polished yet genial presentation made for a relaxed and truly enjoyable dinner service.

The parade of dishes per course reminded me of my meal at Sketch in London (3 Michelin stars) for its delightful storytelling and well-conceived menu. I loved the journey and appreciated the twists and turns along the way. My favorite dish of the evening was a stunning chowder made with fresh corn and lobster. I cherished every bite with my eyes closed so that I could focus my senses on those flavors, ironically simple yet deliciously complex.

Dessert was a comforting delight. I wished I had the appetite to finish it.

I will be sure to enjoy a "Family Meal'  here every time I visit NY :)

Y'all....I ain't never dined like this before WOW
My friend is vegan and brought us here, I was concerned we weren't going to feel full when leaving but wow was I wrong. The number of courses we had, although each portion was on the smaller side, with SO many courses, we walked out of there well fed and HAPPY! 
I was thoroughly surprised, even more so by the service. Holy. 
The attention we got at our table, which I think everyone got, was incredible. There was never a single crumb on our table. Drinks were constantly refilled. They came by every 5 minutes it was almost excessive but wow really made the experience. They explained each course thoroughly, I ordered non alcoholic wine for the first time and they gave me the whole experience (maybe that's normal but idk I felt v special hahah) like that I wasn't missing out on the experience of smelling, tasting, and okaying the wine! It was really something. 
Everything was great, ambiance, the restrooms even were beautiful. We were so taken care of, would love to be back. Felt very homey, we felt so welcomed. Like all in all just a stellar experience.

We came here for dinner last week. Parking was easy (which was nice in NYC) and the restaurant is in a quaint basement of a brownstone near Washington square park. I like the idea that's its family style and that you don't know the menu ahead of time. They had a great wine menu, with a variety of price points, plus some different cocktail options. Our server was very friendly, and great at talking about the wines.  First we started with a Smokey tomato water, with some berries in it. A little odd, but perhaps it's considered a palate cleanser. The next course had two different type of fish (one bite of each, literally 1 inch long)  and there was one other item which I am now forgetting. The fish was good, but it was just a taste, and I don't remember it being super flavorful. The second course had a scallop and corn dish, which was by far the best of the meal. Then there was a white fish with something called corn smith and a corn pancake with some sort of tomato chutney on it. The smut is weird tasting so it ruined the fish for me and the corn cake was just basic. The third course was a tomato and mozzarella salad with some fruit( I thought it was peaches, but my sister said apple), pork with roasted peppers, hen of the woods with pate and some bread. Nothing wow'd here, except maybe the bread and butter. Usually dessert was my favorite, but this was a frozen yogurt made with boiled down rye bread and then all this bread topping on it.  It was just way overdone and ruined what probably was a good base of yogurt. I have been to a couple of Michelin restaurants so my expectations were higher than the rest of my party.  I'm sure they would've given it a 5, and I really would've given it a 3 so I met in the middle at a 4

The service and the ambience were impeccable, and the food was truly memorable. I am a very picky eater. There were some things on the tasting menu that were not to my liking, but there was still plenty of food for me to eat. I will say that the cornbread (I hope I got that right) was unbelievably delicious.

This place has been around for more than a decade... I think. I revisited it a couple of times in the past few weeks, and I have to say I know why this place hasn't faded away like so many other places in the hyper competitive NY restaurant scene.

Everything they do is just good. Ambiance is classy without being stuffy. The food is just well executed and interesting. The service is fluid. The wine list is well priced and extensive enough to find something to drink.

Hugely disappointing!

This was our second time dinning at Family Meal at Blue Hill, but the experience was very different. I had the fluke for the entree, and it was dry. The mackerel was extremely fishy, and the overall flavors were not well balanced. Lastly, the dessert seemed to just be frozen berries and very tart, not edible.

Service was ok and ambiance is nice. Overall, not worth it. At this price point consistency is key but this is lacking.

Everything was absolutely delicious! From the tomato dishes to corn dishes to drinks, truly a unique blend of vegetables and sauces. I had the vegetarian courses and could not recommend more. Staff is very kind and knowledgeable of the menu. Respectful of allergies. Takes about 2 hours for two people. Only con is the dessert at the end, personally I was not impressed and did not love it. 
Bathrooms are clean.

What a spectacular meal! 

+ Service - Amazing. Everyone was so attentive to the details, especially to our main hostess. 

+ Food - Wow, the crudite basket full of persian cucumbers, lemon cucumbers, and sweet mini peppers was fantastic. Paired with the spring onion and trout dip, the vegetables really shined. 

Outside of the starter, we also loved the chicken and batter-fried okra, corn, and ricotta-corn fraiche-ish stuffed squash blossoms. I usually feel terrible after eating anything fried, but wow, I would love to enjoy the squash blossoms, again. AND THE CHICKEN! So tender and juicy--the best chicken I have ever had at a restaurant.

The crudos were all interesting, but our family found the dehydrated tomato-infused (garlic?) oil and fluke combination to be quite intriguing and refreshing.

We left, feeling immensely satisfied and stuffed--true to the name, "family meal" was indeed a true family meal.

A fresh, earnest meal with an equally earnest team who made our experience truly special.

I've walked by the restaurant several times in the past and only recently did I look into making a reservation. I'm glad I did, and I had a lovely Sunday lunch here with my girlfriend. The food is incredible fresh, coming directly from their farm as well as other farms in the area, and the chefs work hard to blend these ingredients in such a way that they taste great eaten in any combination or individually, where you can really assess the full flavor and depth of the care put into each ingredient. I highly recommend Family Meal at Blue Hill.

This is the restaurant that I was most wanting to try in all of NYC... and it lived up to my high expectations. It is honestly easy to walk past. It is the bottom level of a brownstone building. There is bar seating, indoor seating, and a greenhouse sort of seating on the back patio. There is a set menu for everyone, so the only order you make is for beverages. The service is impeccable. The food is delectable. I recommend just trying everything because the ingredients are so high quality and the food is so well prepared; someone who "doesn't like fish" might end up really enjoying the river trout and someone who normally doesn't get pleasure from eating vegetables might end up loving a seasonal salad. You really cannot go wrong here! The only recommendation I have to the restaurant is to assign food runners to certain sections of the restaurant, so that only the waiter and 1 food runner are going to a table. I think it was a little bit syncopated to have 3 different employees introduce courses to us and I think the experience would be more intimate/familiar if each table just had 1 waiter and 1 food runner. Just a thought!

If you have an opportunity to eat at Family Meal, do it!  It is an incredible dining experience and wonderful for a special occasion. 

First, the ambience. It is dark and intimate but the tables still ranged from large groups to couples. Knowing their whole concept is "family meal" I was initially concerned if it would be appropriate for a couple. They adjusted the food amount accordingly and we felt comfortable the whole time. 

There is no menu. It is a prefixed 4 course meal based on seasonal ingredients, while accommodating allergies and dietary restrictions. The staff were very knowledgeable about each dish, explaining all the ingredients and where they were sourced. This is farm to table served at an upscale level without being pretentious. 

The palette opener was a quartet of cucumber and aioli, which was pleasant enough. The first course was a crudo trio with striped bass, fluke and brook trout -- each prepared and flavored differently. The curdo felt very luxurious and was fun to try. The second course was monk fish with peas, romano beans, and an entire flatbread. Calling it a "flatbread" does not do it justice -- it was like a flatbread and naan had a pillowy baby that was absolutely delicious! Wish I could eat that bread everyday. The greens were also fresh and vibrant. Admittedly, I do wish the monk fish portion was a pinch bigger (it was our fish time having monk fish and would have loved more of it!). The third course was chicken from the Blue Hill Farm, freekeh and a caesar salad of dino lettuce. Again, another course of outstanding ingredients packed with flavor. I can't recall the ingredients of the chicken jus, but boy was it good! For dessert, we had vanilla ice cream with short bread and granola crumble and strawberries. 

Service was attentive and the food was well-paced. We didn't wait too long between courses, nor ever felt rushed. The whole meal took a little over two hours. 

We absolutely loved the family style and small dishes as it enabled us to try many different flavors and foods. It gave us a strong understanding of their cooking style, and we cannot recommend it enough. When you go to a fancy Michelin star restaurant, you worry if you'll leave hungry and need to find the closest McDonalds. But fear not, we were utterly stuffed! Our bellies were full and our spirits happy!

P.S. We opted not to do the wine pairing and ordered drinks a la carte. But I'm sure their drink recommendations would be great. 
P.S.S. Photos don't do the food justice (dark and romantic lighting) - go and let your tastebuds experience it!

Blue Hill Family Meal offered an extraordinary dining experience for my daughters birthday dinner. With its commitment to sustainable, high-quality ingredients. Each dish surpassed expectations, AMAZING flavors and top quality food. From farm-fresh produce to wonderful flavors...every bite is a testament to their dedication to excellence. It's not just a meal; it's a culinary journey that celebrates the pure simplicity of good food and flavors. Exceptional to say the very least!

Really tasty meal with top notch ingredients.  We ate at the bar and had the tasting menu.  Service was spectacular, with the bartender/waitress explaining each course and paired wine with exceptional detail.  I'm a big carnivore, but the focus here was on the produce.  It was kind of a new experience - most non-vegetarian meals treat the protein as the star, but here it was simply a compliment to the preparation of the vegetables.  Big highlight was the radicchio with raspberry vinegarette and pistachios.  Worth both the Michelin star and the price tag.

A really lovely meal overall, with some real standouts! My favorite was the tuna sashimi which had just enough flavor from other elements to complement but not overwhelm. The asparagus was so tender -- just in season, apparently! There was also a lovely vegetable in the main steak dish that I missed the name of.

I did feel like some of the dishes were either too salty or sour for perfect balance, and there was a potato dish that was simply undercooked. The dessert was also far too sweet for my taste, and the accompanying blueberries very mid.

I wish they had a proper menu with descriptions of the food, as it was difficult to remember all the elements of the food when they were served as multiple dishes at once.

If you're fragrance sensitive, note that both bathrooms have quite strong candles going.

The idea of this restaurant--serving a full meal made of seasonal food--was an interesting one, and the service was warm and welcoming. The problems is the food and behind it the chef. My first two courses were seriously over salted and almost inedible. When I mildly pointed this out, I was told that the salt on the food had not dissolved properly. The next course had no salt but was over-peppered. The first three courses were wasted on me; I could not taste the food for the salt and then the pepper. The next course, the main dish consisted of a piece of fish; I took one bite and pushed it away. It had no salt, no pepper and no seasoning of any kind; it was utterly tasteless. Seems to me that committing to a full meal carries the risk that the food will have no savor. That's the case, I think, with this restaurant. I left hungry and won't be back.

This place is amazing and I was totally blown away. Was here for a special family event and we couldn't have found a better way to close things out for that weekend. The service was incredible and we were amazed by our entire meal. 

I went in slightly worried given how much hype, yet I was able to get a reservation. Seemed weird as it's typically hard to with a restaurant like this. My worries were unwarranted and I very very highly recommend this place.

i really enjoyed my experience at Family Meal at Blue Hill.  i don't love family meals, but the ambiance was very nice and most of the dishes were totally delicious.  we especially enjoyed the raw fish starters.  the main beef dish and squash cheesecake dessert were not standouts.  cocktails were pretty good.  all in all, it was a solid meal and i'd definitely return!

I usually anticipate being a little hungry after fine dining but that was not the case with Family Meal. Our group thoroughly enjoyed dinner here. The portions were generous for fine dining and being able to share dishes family style was a great experience since you don't usually get to do that at fine dining establishments. The service was impeccable. 

The meal was a great value and experience. I look forward for coming back to try the new menu!

Perfect meal from top to bottom, and the service was top-notch. We went for my partner's birthday and they made a gluten-free birthday cake. Very attentive and accomodating to food restrictions. The ambiance was as sweet as ever. Just a New York gem.

What a great experience shared among friends! I'm a huge proponent of family style dining and it's made even easier when the menu is set for you! The menu changes based on the fresh ingredients that are available for around 145/person not including tip and tax.

We brought 2 bottles of alcohol. There's a 50 dollars per bottle corkage fee and their only rule is the bottle cannot be available at the restaurant. They were very kind to us when one of us broke this rule.

We started off with a beautiful plate of cauliflower tempura, peas and peppers with a delicious concoction of sweetness in the peppers. This was followed by yellowfish and fluke crudo. The fluke came with a delicious mole like sauce. Then we were surprised by a fish stew, warm bread with cheese and rye butter as well as some squash. We finished it off with potatoes, beef and lettuce. The dessert was a squash cheesecake that was just ok. 

Overall, I felt like this was a great experience for a nice communal meal set in a very laid back comfortable dining environment. Was the food the most amazing I've ever had? No. But the quality, the thoughtfulness, the ease of everything made it a 5/5 experience.

Food is always incredible and brings me back 10 years after moving away from  NYC.  However, without the service it would just be another great restaurant in a city with loads.  The service makes it the place that my wife and I will always return to.  It's been 15 years since we started coming to Blue Hill.  Let's shoot for another 15.

You remember those movies where they show the quintessential cozy restaurant, tucked away in the middle of the village in Manhattan; it's fall and slightly chilly, everyone's bundled outside but people are  having a lovely dinner in a warmly lit restaurant? That's Family Meal - the perfect farm to table restaurant here in the city, nothing pompous, but elevated yet and relaxed. 

The food and concept are all based on the famous Blue Hill at Stone Barns in Westchester. Family Meal provides a lovely seasonal tasting menu that changes regularly. Very accommodating to dietary restrictions like vegetarians. The food speaks for itself and is simply delicious. Service, inviting and friendly yet very knowledgeable. Ambiance and setting, well, I think I painted a nice picture in the beginning. It's a must try!

I could not really tell you a single thing that I ate, or I could try and not do it justice, but you'll have to believe me that this place is incredible! I love the concept of eating a meal with food served in the center (except sometimes it's a fight to get all the bites) and not knowing what I'm going to get but knowing that it is really fresh ingredients. I ate things I would've never ordered or thought I would've liked and that's what made it an incredible experience.

Some of the highlights from my particular dinner in October 2023 was the fluke with honey nut squash, the tuna with pickled onions, and the kale bean dish, and the bread with homemade rye butter and homemade cheese. The bread was so fluffy, I think it was one of the best breads I've ever had in my life. It came out piping hot and it came out with homemade cheese and homemade butter. Like... what!!!

We also had some other peppers, tempura vegetables, which were really good, and the main dish was grass fed beef, but I didn't like the pepper sauce. 

Inside the ambience is really nice. I love the dim lighting, and the flowers. Our server could have been a little more attentive to details of our allergies, and sometimes I felt like he disappeared in the small room but luckily it didn't take away from this incredible experience.

I highly recommend coming here! I will happily back!

My 600th review!

Chef Mark really knows how to turn it up.

I love that whenever you come to Blue Hill, the menu is always a surprise, but every bite is remarkable. 

Blue Hill is probably the most thoughtful restaurant in New York when it comes to exceptional produce. Every vegetable that you eat is thoughtfully planted, harvested, prepared... and knowing that makes it so much more meaningful to eat. Even down the the boiled potatoes harvested by Dan Barber himself.

We were lucky enough to be served an outrageous deboned chicken, one of the most perfect chickens I've ever eaten. It was a whole chicken, completely deboned, cooked to perfection, and smothered in a delicious pepper sauce. Very memorable.

It's always a pleasure to dine here and a special experience to share with great company. A must eat restaurant in the city, especially if you can't make it all the way up to Stone Barns.

GORGEOUS!!! I came here on a Thursday night and the food was INCREDIBLE. I told them we are vegetarian and they were so great on accomodating us. I would skip the wine pairing to be honest; I don't think it was worth it
One of my top favorite restaurants, the service is excellent, the ambience was lovely and everything was delicious. It's good food prepared well.

Beautiful ambiance, a lovely non-menu of produce-forward food. I loved dining solo at the bar here - service is polite, knowledgeable, and perfectly attentive - you'll never want for a single thing but you won't often be interrupted either. 

Four courses doesn't sound so daunting until you realize what that means. All small plates, event he first course of "snacks" consists of a colorful plate of sunkissed tomato, peppers, and cucumber, a couple of corn hush puppies in crème fraiche with perky pepper jelly, a fantastic fluke ceviche, and a beautiful slab of yellowfin tuna topped with a rich spread of tomato and fried garlic. The smokiness is unforgettable.
The highlight of the second course is a Flatbread with Barber wheat, to be smothered in a rye cultured butter that leaves you with the fragrance of lingering grain. 
The Succotash is the one I can't stop eating - the fried eggplant melts away with a single, candied crunch, like pork belly without the fat.
There's also a salty, creamy Ricotta with tomato and an assortment of herb-smoked beans. Lightly cooked grapes are sour and sweet, the perfect palate cleanser.
Third course is the "main", a nice steak with potato pancake, but the real standouts are the dill cream underneath, the earthy eggplant purée, and the meaty shiitake and chanterelle. The Salad has sweet balls of vine-ripe melon and more tomato, topped with arugula and pine nuts and a Barber wheat cracker that's lighter than air. Too good to be just a salad.
A standalone of Wow Corn with blueberry butter glaze is so simple yet so good. 
Final course: dessert. I'm visibly struggling through the Ricotta Cheesecake, but the bartender notices and takes pity on me. He introduces me to an Amaro, a licorice-finish spirit that gives me a bit of a reset. 
Still, I get the assorted fruit bowl to go, and the peaches, blueberries, and husk cherries are great for breakfast.

Blue Hill is a blend of all the polish and precision I love about fine dining with none of the stuffy snobbery. I come from California where the entire cuisine is farm-fresh, but I don't think I'll ever get tired of places that highlight produce, and Blue Hill managed to impress and enchant. And 5 stars for the succotash!

One of the best restaurant experiences I ever had - family meal with the wine pairing was steep, but worth it. Everything tasted so good, like phenomenally good, and the services was top tier. Highly recommend !!

Absolutely stunning 14 course meal. Amazing drinks, amazing ambience, amazing service.

Our meal's focus on Corn was exceptional, from the hush puppies to the corn-based old fashioned.

Very down to earth Michelin star experience. Would go again!

Sorry I was so absorbed by the meal I only took 2 photos!

Family Meal at Blue Hill, this was the highlight of our trip this time around to NYC.  I hadn't watched the documentary on Netflix prior to dining so I had no idea what I was getting. All I was expecting was really good vegetables according to my hubby, and with all the traveling I've been doing lately my body really needed veggies and this would be a perfect place to nourish my body with some outstanding veggies. 

While reserving a spot for the four of us, courtesy of my ever-discerning hubby, who's an expert at sourcing the finest dining establishments globally, we stumbled into what could only be described as a gastronomic overture to the forthcoming adventure at the farm itself.

If you're interested, check out Chef's Table Episode 2 of Season 1 on Netflix to learn who Chef Barber is and how he pours his passion into growing and cooking food and how he desires to impact the world with sustainable food.

As per its moniker, it is a family meal that everyone shares. You don't order anything here. They highlight the ingredient they're working with that night and just bring you the courses as if you're dining at a friend's house. A fancy chef friend that has an incredible farm in the backyard that is.  

What we ate:

* Kirby, Quirk, and Lemon Cucumbers paired with lunch box pepper, enlivened by a cucumber leaf sauce. Crunchy and sweet, these cucumbers shattered preconceived notions, prompting raves from my son the cucumber hater.  
* Donko Shiitake Doughnuts, mystical in execution, melted in my mouth and chewy in tandem, defying logic!
* Montauk Fluke sashimi, bedecked with cherry and yeasted brown butter, delivered a symphony of freshness.
* Bristol Bay Sockeye Salmon, perched atop avocado squash, was accompanied by Marigold-dusted Yukon potato chips - an amalgamation of textures and flavors.
* Barber wheat flatbread, matched with an extraordinary yeasty and creamy butter, was a warm, fluffy indulgence.
* Grass-fed milk ricotta crowned with sungold tomato jam was an ideal dipping for the flatbread.
* Dayboat scallops served with succotash, corn, tetra squash, and Jimmy Nardello pepper - scallops were cooked to perfection and veggies were vivacious!
* Summer bean bundle with young ginger. These bean bundles came out with wood chips still smoking underneath the wire basket. Cool touch for a place that doesn't really pay much attention to plating. Green beans, white beans, and snap peas were so sweet and crunchy! If all veggies are this good, I become a vegetarian. Seriously!
* Grass-fed beef, escorted by eggplant, morel mushrooms, and brisket, offered a succulent meaty segue.
* Potato roast, a marvel of contrast, juxtaposed crispy outer layers with creamy interiors, rendering it unforgettable! Raves all around for this dish!
* Heirloom tomatoes and melons, adorned with lemon verbena, pine nuts, and lemon basil, encapsulated summer's bounty.
* Shiso wrapped strawberry sorbet, bronze fennel and pistachio. I never had a shiso wrapped sorbet until now. Not the best dish or execution, because you need to eat it fast as it comes on the table. We were busy talking and the sorbet melted too much. But still very good.
* The finale, a Farmer's Cheese Cheesecake adorned with Sorghum graham cracker and peach. Basically a deconstructed peach cheesecake, but there's nothing basic about it. This farmer sure knows how to make good cheese. My son's gf who dislikes cheese and cheesecake, LOVED this dessert! So creamy and flavorful!

Hubby did the wine pairing and the rest of us opted for cocktails (1 per person. We're not much of drinkers). Total bill came to about $200 per person + tip which is about what you'd expect to pay at a 1 Michelin starred restaurant. As mentioned before, exquisite plating wasn't the focus; rather, the brilliance lay in the ingredients' quality. Our server was an eloquent and friendly young lady of Korean decent. I wish I remembered what she explained about all the wines that were being served, but I don't remember the details. They all have a very interesting story behind the winery and the theme of the night was that most of the wineries were started by college professors! Overall a very good experience and I look forward to experiencing their restaurant at Stone Barns.

Huge fan of Family Meal at Blue Hill. I was afraid to be disappointed because I was blown away by the Tarrytown location, but the Blue Hill in the city was amazing as well. I love the family meal, menu-less concept, and I was pleasantly surprised. Several shared plates per each of the 4 courses were presented using the freshest of ingredients. There wasn't a single dish I didn't like. I particularly enjoyed the day's bread course and chicken main plate. Service is was on point as well.

Went here a month ago and i'm still thinking about the food!

We did the fixed menu with the wine progression. Every course that came out was amazing. So many different flavors working together. 

We chose to sit at the bar, which ended up being a great decision because of Antanas, the phenomenal bartender. He was very attentive and made sure we had a great time. 

Cant wait to go back!

The family style farm to table and one of the most exclusive New York City's new restaurants is located walking distance from the famed NYU and Washington Square Park. It's an expensive place but worth the premium price since you only have one life to enjoy the slice of heaven that this premier dining experience offers. First of all the chef's versatility is immeasurable. The creativity for Vegan, Pescatarian, and us omnivores were amazingly displayed with precision and perfect execution. The five wine pairing was perfect. The main waiter was beyond knowledgeable. Each dish which was presented was perfection. I loved simplicity and elegant taste. The Chef made everything in order to preserve the true natural taste. Arancini was perfectly seasoned and deep fried, turnips and string beans with original organic green sauce were perfect. The flattened sirloin with shiitake mushrooms was heaven for meat lovers. Ricotta cheese with tasty brown gravy sauce was just well balanced. The thinly sliced fatty tuna just melted with fresh flavor. There were so many variations of traditional and avant-garde dishes that came one after another, my tastebuds were delirious until the end that I didn't want to end. When you are in NYC, certainly you should try this daringly best of the best place.

Came here in November 2021 and was probably only 3.5/5 (the meal was too earthy/vegetable heavy for our tastes), but decided to give it another shot tonight and WOW, absolutely incredible! Every dish was delicious, and the cocktails were perfect too. My wife has never ordered a whiskey drink before in her life but liked mine so much she ended up getting one also. Our waitress Danielle was also very knowledgeable about every dish and gave us extra info about the farms and sources of all of our dishes. My wife and I have eaten at a lot of amazing restaurants all over the world and this is now probably one of our top 5 meals of all time. Can't wait to come back!

I'm usually not the guy that writes reviews but I would be remiss if i didn't at least give a brief shout out to Blue Hill for providing me with an experience that everyone deserves to be a part of once in their life. From the warm genuine greetings from the staff, to the unique delicious food, the Blue Hill experience should not be missed. A special shout to Sebastian and Jason for making the experience something I wont ever forget. Another special shout out to the chef that made that "pizza dough" with the cheese and sungold tomato compote. One of the best bites I've had in a while.

I went with my husband to celebrate my birthday and it was perfect. The food was DELICIOUS, we could feel the freshness of the ingredients, and they give you more than enough food... we were full after we left. Service is on point and the place is small which makes it very unique and exclusive.

We had a 6pm reservation and stayed until 9pm which was surprising to us that we were there for 3 hours!

For a fixed menu, we paid $145 per person before tax and tip. It's divided into 4 courses. 

The first course was lots of veggies and raw fish dishes that were probably my favorite out of the meal. There was this one black bass wrapped in something that was outstanding.

The second course had heartier food such as bread and eggs. I was already full after this course.

The third course was the entree where we had potatoes and meat. This was good but maybe my least favorite out of the courses.

The fourth course was dessert, and they had this fantastic farmer's cheesecake that made me think of what I imagine a cheese plate for dessert should taste like. Like people say about this place, the ingredients really shine through.

For our engagement, they did a mini brownie on top of the dessert course, which was a nice touch.

The dress code is dress as if you are having dinner at a friend's; I came in shorts and no one gave me any problems with that.

The food was great and they don't skimp on portion which makes the price worth it, but this was too much food for a meal for me. I was bloated by the end, so I would lean more towards a Michelin restaurant that was slightly cheaper for slightly less food.

Finally visited Blue Hill after wanting to come here for years!!

Celebrated my boyfriend's birthday here and had a great meal. We started with the cherry sour and Buzzword cocktails, which were both fantastic, then did the tasting menu. Highlights included the little gem lettuce, fluke, carrots, and semifreddo.

You get a ton of food, and we were both super full after. Service was also excellent; our server Amelia was wonderful. 

Hoping to make my next stop Blue Hill at Stone Barns!!

Came here for a business dinner and it was really great! Our table was a bit complicated with a dairy allergy, vegetarian, and seafood allergy, but the kitchen didn't miss a beat. 

Each course came out tailored with clear directions on who could eat what and each was more creative that the next. Two of us did the wine progression, which I would highly recommend. 

Service was great!

When reviewing a venerable institution like Blue Hill you think twice before posting anything but the positive.  That very well may be the issue - everyone is so lost in reputation that they forgot to eat the food or review service.  I talked this place up to my crew - as it was a regular in the rotation years ago.  Even made my youngest watch a show about the farm.  

The wine pairings were interesting and worthy of a try.  They were different than standard and all had a compelling story that warranted their inclusion - the wine program stood out tonight.  

We went with family - it's named family  meal after all.  The main - beef - was inedible.  It was boot leather tough.  I didn't bother to provide them this feedback (I would've gotten a speech about it being grass fed, and then given the service - they would have inferred me too much a heathen to understand the quality) - felt like they knew, as they didn't ask.  If anyone tried that beef, they would have decided on a slow cook preparation that kids under 16 would actually eat.  Ours didn't.  

The produce was generally delicious and fresh and indicative of what you would expect from a local farm.  No doubt the highlight.  Transitioning to a vegan offering wouldn't warrant the same price, but might rationalize their existence.  

The service was very slow - annoyingly so.  They didn't clear plates for far too long.  And they weren't busy.  My daughter actually stacked a couple to say hello - my guess is that sent the evening into the abyss.  

And the prices don't warrant the product.  You'll be mad at yourself if you do.  But, whatever - many New Yorkers like a good slap in the face.  If that's your thing, get after it.

We had a lovely and intimate meal here while sitting at the bar. My husband is vegan and I don't have any restrictions so they were able to accommodate this through their family-style dining experience. We also got the wine pairing, which paired well with each course. Service was great and everyone there were so friendly and inviting. Would definitely come back if we're in the city again!

Highly recommend!! Everything was of top quality ingredients and tasted full of flavors. We chose the vegan and seafood sets to share. Could really tell the chef's attention to detail and creativity in the presentation and depth of flavors. They took our dietary restriction very seriously and nothing had refined sugar, including desserts. They created special yummy desserts made without refined sugar. Servers were all knowledgeable and friendly.

Phenomenal. Food, service, ambiance, all of it. Dined with my wife (party of two which they recently started to accommodate) who is a vegetarian. We both left very full. They were very kind to compress our tasting a bit since we told them we had to be in and out in two hours. Did not feel overly rushed despite this. Can't wait to go to Stone Barns.

Every dish was out of this world. Truly. Highly recommend coming for a special occasion or ANY occasion you need a special night. Danielle was our server and made
our experience incredibly easy and special. You will not regret coming here - especially w a hot date. I promise you that. Major shout out to Danielle - she was so informative about the wine and food. It was an education.


PS. Spilled a sauce on my khakis. Told Lucy one of the servers - I got club soda, 2 clean napkins, a shout wipe,

Love this place. Will be back asap.

FINALLY! I have been waiting years to try this restaurant after seeing Dan Barber's Chefs Table special on Netflix years ago. The space is minimalistic in the most elegant way. The staff is kind, intelligent and passionate. The food is truly divine and everything I had hoped it would be.

We started with a vegetable tar tar that had a beautiful smokiness to it, a radish dish and a delicious fish. The bread course was heavy but tasty. The fighting spinach was new to me! We enjoyed trying that! The salads executed the perfect balance of bitter, sweet, acid, crunch and softness. Dessert was a home run for me. 

I would love to meet Dan next time he comes into the restaurant. Try out Family Meal and be sure to ask questions about what you're eating! A lot of effort and heart goes into every plate.

Went to Blue Hill for a Holiday splurge! They brought out so many little dishes I couldn't keep up with taking pictures and taking mental notes. So I'll try my best to describe what I remember. 

Potato chips with golden beet tartare - meh, it was fine

Sashimi with I think a mushroom sauce? - Delicious

Adorable little red peppers - so sweet! the sauce it came with was amazing - no idea what it was! 

Sweet potato nuggets - crispy, delicious, not overly sweet

Cornbread - AMAZING, ONE OF THE BEST ITEMS

I think a parfait, but instead of yogurt I think it was whipped cream

Consider this a preview of what you might get at Blue Hill. There was definitely a lot more items that were served to us that night. Over all there were a few stand outs, a few things we really didn't like and everything else fell in the middle. For the price tag, I would've wanted to be wowed every time.

Such a great experience! From the moment I made the reservation, the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcomed and accommodated. 

Being pregnant, I was asked if I had any dietary restrictions or preferences. While I normally wouldn't speak up, because I was asked, I felt comfortable asking for no raw meats/fish. There were also multiple options for mocktails and wines (juices). 

The food was amazing at every course. We felt educated and informed throughout the entire meal. It was very refreshing to not have to order from a menu. I felt we could settle in and trust the staff.

This place will leave you speechless! I am impressed beyond being impressed with the thoughtfulness of the dishes. There is something here for everyone even picky vegan eaters. I promised my self I would have a good experience. It is difficult to find restaurants that truly care about the quality of food people are consuming. This place is superb and exceptional. Defj I Troy going back again. The ginger tea with fresh pressed ginger was perfectly done. I enjoyed every moment. The staff is courteous and took time to actually have conversations with the patrons. Looking forward to going back again! Thanks so much for the amazing food and good vibes !!

fantastic food to be sure as well as wonderful service and ambiance, but not worth the price tag in my personal opinion.

first off, the ambiance is dimly lit and feels very sophisticated. our server was very sweet and knowledgeable as well, and worked previously at the original blue hill farm upstate. for food, i really enjoyed the beet tartare with homemade potato chips as well as the pork shoulder. the spinach was also delicious, probably the best spinach i've ever had (not that the bar is high!) the flavors in every dish are truly very refined and complex, and dining is definitely an experience. 

while i enjoyed the courses i had at blue hill and i can see the michelin star quality, i personally do not believe it's worth $145 pp + $20 per drink...i've had equally satisfying (and more filling) meals for a much smaller price tag, but i guess that's new york for you!

overall, a great experience, but just too high of a price tag for the quantity. probably will not be back myself, but i would recommend coming if you don't mind spending almost $200 pp :)
My  favorite restaurant in New York. Incredibly clean, healthy, delicious and unique. Words cannot describe-  you just have to experience it .

We were stoked to eat here during our visit to NYC. the food, especially one dish, was outstanding. Service was ok-- we weren't greeted by our server nor told what to expect from this unique experience until after being seated for almost 30 minutes. For the price point, we were happy to pay for the farm-to-table fresh food but the service could use some attention. I'm sure they get stuck in the day-to-day but we were left wondering what to expect. Not likely to return with all the other outstanding dining options in the area.

A friend and I enjoyed our dinner at "Family Meal."

The service was very friendly and attentive. While there's no menu we were asked about our allergies, dietary choices, and preferences to craft our meal. Some of the vegetables were exceptionally good, and the restaurant did a good job highlighting their flavors. I especially enjoyed their pork (the only meat course, my pescatarian friend received a fish dish at the same time), some green beans with ginger, and the "cheesecake" dessert. 

Unfortunately not everything was great and some of the dishes just didn't do much for me.

With one drink per person, tax, and tip, the meal was about $200 per person.

Disappointing. I walked out of there hungry, because the portions were so small. It just felt pretentious. They really ape nutritional quality and local ingredients, which I appreciate, but they also use the dynamic of American overabundance to justify their contrast of tiny portions, which seems just as problematic. It also seemed greedy. If someone wants to do this and charge $30 for people to try new foods and flavors and gain a greater education about the state of food, that's seems ok, but this just isn't worth $100+ a plate. People want to come here and pat themselves on the back because someone else told them it's good. Cuisine should be about sustenance and enjoyment.  Not ego and hubris.

Service was phenomenal. Knowledgeable, extremely friendly, timely. 

We sat in the garden room- a beautiful 'outdoor' space enclosed with a skylight. 

Food had highs and lows. Stuffed zucchini blossoms with yogurt dipping sauce was fantastic, cantaloupe soup dessert didn't hit the right notes (far too bitter). 

Overall I'd recommend giving it a shot at least once, prices are more than fair for NYC Michelin joints.

Family Meal at Blue Hill is Blue Hill Restaurant's pop-in located in Manhattan.  And yes it is menu-less. It's casual family style meal and it is ok, rounded up to a 4 star because of the great service.

I have to say maybe I am consistently spoiled by Thomas Keller at Ad Hoc (similar family concept by Michelin starred chef) I felt everything served at family meal is only ok but really not much to rave about.

The plus:  The Watermelon claw cocktail is refreshing and well balanced.  Great way to start the meal!  Half bottle Champagne $59 is quite a steal.  Extensive list of burgundies - Found a red burgundy from Beaune for $100.  Loved the big eye tuna crudo appetizer.   Great service with casual atmosphere.

The negatives:  The meal is not memorable.  The flat iron steak was meh.

When you step down into the restaurant you are instantly greeted by the hostess and brought right to your seats. The ambiance reflects a cozy modern intimate feel complete with candles and dim lighting. Most of the courses were vegetarian- I am not but my date is. I was enamored by the chefs ability to capture flavorful food and presentation. You will NOT leave hungry. The staff is world class. They were able to explain the cooking process for each of the foods and had detailed knowledge of each wine we had. I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant so I will end with this: If you are even considering this restaurant, do not hesitate and make the reservation.
It's incredible. Service is impeccable, the vibe is intimate and the food is so innovative... this place made our anniversary dinner great!

Dirty west village basement that serves you the same vegetables you'd get at Trader Joe's for 3$ but are sold to you here at $130 per person. 

You are literally being served raw vegetables. I can cook them better myself at home than whatever 'chef' they have in the kitchen. 

This isn't haute cuisine.  It's a place that scams gullible New Yorkers for their money into thinking farm fresh vegetables are something special or unique. 

Literally drive up to any farm and eat the raw vegetables there for free than at this restaurant. 

Also my partner had an allergen that was not respected by staff and she has been sick and throwing up the whole night.
Only been a handful of times but every time is the new best meal I've ever had. Will completely change your perspective on what you think good raw vegetables taste like! Wonderful wait staff.

I have tried numerous Michelin star restaurants and set course haute cuisine in NYC, yet Blue Hill family meal was by far the best and exceeded my expectations. The appetizers were creative, making me curious with the pretty plating, while surprising me with completely different tastes at the same time in good ways. In the main dishes, the eggplant was superb - nothing close to anything I tasted before. The pork dish was just perfect, well-balanced with tender texture and very tasteful. We were served several dessert dishes as part of the family meal, which was nice, but I was initially not thrilled as I'm not a dessert person. Nevertheless, I emptied all the dessert dishes. They were so delicious, yet they were not that sweet. All the dishes are great, but I must say the wine pairing was on another level. I felt like I was journeying through exquisite wine countries like Champagne, Burgundy, and Napa. The head sommelier was super passionate and introduced me to his perfect wine selections. The ambiance was also great. All the restaurant employees were super friendly. They all made us feel very comfortable and helped us enjoy the food, wine, and ambiance. I will definitely come back again when I visit NYC next time. Thank you!

Very interesting place. Would recommend if you are not a fussy eater and like creative dishes. It was definitely worth the $115/pp because you get so much food for that. Good place for a group or a date night!

Dan Barber is a supernova of the food world. He is simply operating on an entirely different level than other top chefs. He has taken farm to table to an entirely new level. Having grown up on Blue Hill Farm in Massachusetts, Barber has a special way with produce, vegetables never tasted so good. The current format at Blue is Family Meal. Not a tasting meal, a shared meal. An amazing shared meal. Mostly vegetables and grains with a small amount of protein. Simply the best food you have ever eaten. Their special cocktails are incredible and the service is amazing. Everyone is really made to feel at home. With a casual ambiance it is a night to remember.

Food poisoning. Both me and my sib had food poisoning from this dinner and spent 24 hrs with stomach pain and diarrhea on our vacation. Unfortunate bc we're both fans of Barber and veggie-forward cooking, but food poisoning from a fine dining est w a $300+ check is ridiculous

This is a really good option if you don't manage to score a reservation in their upstate location. This review is for the family meal at NYC

Very intimate with great vibes. Thanks to the other reviews I knew to search for hidden stuff to eat lol. It's a pretty good exercise I must say. 

They have a great selection of cocktails and wine. We took a bottle for four of us along with a cocktail each. The dishes start pretty strong (those dynamite donuts and fresh salad) with impeccable complimenting flavors and lovely dishes. But then they get quite standard. Dessert was nice but nothing extraordinary IMHO

I took inspo from their butternut squash pasta dish and use that for a pasta sauce now so thanks to the team for that. That mushroom skillet dish is also melt in your mouth amazing, beautiful flavors coming together 

I will certainly try and go ti the stone barns location if they ever give me a reservation. I have been told they're better. 

Definitely recommend the NYC location for a nice meal. They do know how to take care of you  :)

Blue Hill is running a new concept in their Greenwich Village location called "Family Meal". Inside, you are treated to a lively atmosphere, and a tasting menu that is meant to be shared with the group. Unlike other tasting menus, you never receive a menu at the beginning or the end of the meal (just like if you were to go to a friend's house for dinner), so be sure to listen closely to the servers as they bring out the food. 

Our favorite courses were the - radish tacos, asparagus basket, and pork dish. I don't think they had a sommelier the day we went but the staff were all very knowledgeable about the wines. 

Something to keep in mind is that Blue Hill's mission is sustainability and prioritizes serving seasonal vegetables that are grown on their properties. Therefore, the majority of the courses are plant based - we had only one pork course. This may be a turnoff to some if you are a heavy carnivore or pescatarian. However, as long as you keep this in mind, we really appreciated the creativity (yet simplicity) of each meal. For example, there was a basket of asparagus - very simply cooked and presented, yet I would say some of the most masterfully done asparagus I've had. 

Overall, highly recommend this meal - delicious, fun concept, and at an affordable price point of $115 / person!

Highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a fun, light, celebratory dinner. The dishes are vegetable heavy but we were pretty full by the end. I wasn't super full, but I also didn't leave hungry. The family-style service made it interactive and unique. The presentation was beautiful. We were a group of four and we had indicated that two of us were vegetarian while two of us were vegan. They didn't seem to have the right notes from our booking, but thankfully they double checked with us and were able to accommodate all our restrictions. My husband also indicated that he doesn't like mushrooms and they made special arrangements for him. 

The first course was a bit too eggy for me but the crackers were great. The fresh vegetables with dip were beautifully displayed and the dips were all good. The corn Patties were served with a delicious honey dip. The bread was amazingly soft and crunchy. The salad was fresh and light. The potatoes with green purée were my favorite thing of the night. All the servers were so friendly, funny, knowledgeable and helpful. The desserts were a bit underwhelming but I did really like the yogurt and honey bowl. It was also nice of them to bring an extra cake with a candle since we were celebrating. 

The drinks were great and creative. I tried the drink with whey from ricotta, mint, and rum. We also tried a few wines and my favorite was the Bordeaux white which was a change from the usually seen Bordeaux reds. 

The restaurant is not too big which makes it seem more personal. And the farm to table concept is really central to the experience. It's a little pricy for the amount of food and number of courses, especially considering it's family style instead of individual plating.

Blue Hill NYC's Family Meal is an exquisite showcasing of local ingredients. The ever-changing menu, highlighting produce and grains, has been delightful to sample over my past three visits. Blue Hill's latest dinner concept is a must visit for NYC foodies and restaurant aficionados.

Eating at Family Meal is an exercise in humility and appreciation for the food that is grown around us. As the meal progresses in loose, family-style courses one is exposed to the science of preservation and fermentation, an understanding of the required labor of farming, the seasonality of ingredients, and the creativity and experimental endeavors of the chef. For one to enjoy the meal, the diner has to be open to the ideals of farm-to-table (Blue Hill Farm, nonetheless) rather than the displays of indulgence found at some other high class restaurants. For some, it comes naturally but for others, it may require a suspension of preconceptions.

On our past visit to Family Meal, we were wowed by fresh turnips with poppy seed butter, hearty whole wheat bread with sunflower cream and rich whipped butter, mushroom buckwheat donuts, hearty Fighter Spinach, mushrooms, tilefish with sweet, crunchy carrots and ginger, and make-your-own sundaes with maple ice cream and toasted meringue. We were enthralled by the fresh vegetables and grains that were placed before us that incorporated unique flavors, textures, and aromas.

To be fair, not every dish over my visits has been my favorite but I appreciate the variety and experimental nature of the menus. 

The general manager, Jason, and the maitre d, Grace, run an incredible restaurant; they spare no detail in creating a welcoming atmosphere and exciting experience. Jason and Grace have welcomed us on each visit and have made us feel like family. We so appreciate their hard work, attention to detail, and friendship.

Finally, Family Meal goes above and beyond to accommodate a number of allergies and dietary restrictions including vegetarian, vegan, pescatarian, gluten free, and nut-free. My wife had celiac and cannot eat gluten; Family Meal accommodates her in a way that no other restaurant in the city does. It is unfortunately rare for New York restaurants to so seriously attend to its patron's dietary needs. 

My wife and I will continue to return to Family Meal, season after season until the pop-up is done. We are so supportive of Blue Hill's vision and mission and are impressed with how spectacular this iteration of the restaurant is. Highly recommended.

**This may just be an issue of personal taste so read on, because you might disagree with me!**

It makes me super sad to write this, but I just didn't like the food. It's not that anything was "wrong", I just didn't like it. The menu is extremely vegetable-based, and I thought that would be ok. I like asparagus, broccoli, onions of all sorts, potatoes, yams, cabbage, etc. If you asked me for my two least favorite foods in the world, I would have told you beets and mushrooms. Well, guess what vegetables were in nearly every single dish of the evening? Total bummer.

I had similar  luck with the cocktail menu, which features 5 drinks. I don't think of myself as an overly picky drinker, but through sheer back luck each option had an ingredient that ruled it out for me. Then we got to dessert. I gave up sweets for lent, so they were kind enough to bring apple slices,  pepper jelly, and the only cheese on earth I don't eat... blue cheese.

By now I am sure you've decided the blame is on me and not on the restaurant. That is fair. I really do think this may have been terrible luck. I've been fortunate to do several tasting menus in my life and have often not known what would be served. Something like this has never happened to me.

First course is slivers - AND I DO MEAN SLIVERS - of raw, pickled vegetables. And although each bite was tiny, I quickly became tired of eating individual bites of pickles. There was also whole wheat bread with whipped lard that would have been 100 times better if it had been salted. The meat course was well cooked but the cut was extraordinarily tough (as in, coudl barely cut with the steak knife) and chewy.

This is one of the most expensive meals we've had in our lives, including Michellin star restaurants in Paris, so needless to say I was really disappointed that it didn't turn out how we'd hoped.

The big thing to know is that right now they are doing Family Style (which is just what it sounds like, you share things by passing them around family style) and not a tasting menu. So this means the base is about $115 for the food and decently reasonable fancy wine/cocktail bar prices for alcoholic drinks.

BUT with that... YOU GET ALL THE AMAZING GLORY OF BLUE HILL. 

- Food: The most amazing vegetables and meats with such rich flavor that you have ever tasted. The dessert was simply the best of Americana. We pretty much cried out of delight.
- The Service: Super exciting servers that played in on our jokes and really made us feel special
- The Ambiance: Given the space limitations, it had a truly homey and lovely feel 

Great For:
- Dinners after getting a new job
- Close friends and family having a bonding experiencing
- Making your sister drive from Jersey for this
- A managable splurge
- Date #21 

Bad For:
- Break ups
- Frenemy get together
- People who struggle to share 
- People with a small stomach

Super delicious veggie centric family style restaurant.  Really liked the food and atmosphere.  Will definitely make reservations for the Blue Hill Farm in Tarrytown this summer when New York vegetables are at their peak.

I didn't think I would enjoy eating so many vegetables, but yet - here we are, me eating and enjoying. 

Blue Hill is currently serving up Family Meal. Prefix menu, everyone share the plates in the middle. I started off with a glass of their Syrah, which was indeed good. The waiter said he gave a "chunky" pour, which is a funny way to describe a pour so I had a good laugh, but indeed it was not chunky whatsoever...

Enough with the wine talk, let's talk about the courses. Pickled veggies magically appeared. It was a cleanser and tasty. Followed by bread with amazing dips. I held off as to not be too full. The stars came shortly after which were the mushroom donut and potatoes. Both, imho, best in class and creative. The one protein dish , which was pork, perfectly cooked, tender and juicy, accompanied by beans that were to die for. We concluded with some deserts which was rather lackluster but it did fill that portion of the stomach reserved for deserts. 

Service throughout the meal was top notch. Venue is relatively small, but that's mostly true for many restaurants in nyc. They do have another location next to their actual farm which I would love to visit. 

Overall, a solid experience and I would recommend.

While the "experience" of dining at blue hill was unique and the concept interesting, the actual food and presentation did not justify the hefty price tag.  Unsanitary in these times to say the least (food hidden under a part of the table that the diners handle and place on the table/no serving utensils until we asked for them), and underwhelming presentation would make this the last NYC restaurant I would return to.   Be prepared for bold attempts to push the culinary boundaries (hello bone marrow served in a Fred Flinstone carved out BONE ?!) without delivering the goods.... And dare I mention the heat in the restaurant had to be broken because it was 85 degrees during the entire meal...

God, how I miss Del Posto for an extra special celebratory dining experience.

'family meal' price fixe $300 for 2 people, with one drink. Awful value for money. Both left hungry a displeased with amount of food offered. Quality was average a far from remarkable/ original. Very bland mediocre offering with what must be an insane mark up on basic inexpensive ingredients.

DO NOT MISS FAMILY MEAL! 

We got engaged a few weeks ago but haven't been really able to celebrate because of Covid. All the servers immediately wished us congratulations when we entered and on our table was this adorable little welcome note they had drawn with two piggies in love saying "congrats on your next chapter"! It was so touching. They sat us in a quiet section with such a friendly an attentive server. He was so invested in making sure we had a great experience- which was also moving given how hard it is to be in the service industry during these times. The food was creative, super filling, and delicious for both veg and nonveg audiences alike. You have not tasted cream, eggs, or cheese before like this - and may never be able to go back to what you had before! Everything is so fresh - like egg laid that morning fresh - and you can tell that these are happy animals. Also - it was so reasonably priced - $115 for the entire 6 courses and you are left feeling very satisfied. 
We are already thinking about when we will come back again, and would be excited to know what seasonal and curated menu they have next!

Have been waiting forever to dine here and it was worth the wait. Family Meal is an experience dinner that doesn't give you a choice for what you're getting! It's all locally sourced from their upstate farm and brought into the city day of. The fresh vegetables were what shocked me. Everything was so fresh and delicious. When we sat down there was a Brussel sprout tree on the table that ended up being one of our sides. 

My favorite part of the meal was the potatoes severed with the pork. The flavors were out of this world. 

It is a ton of food and it's $115 a person so it's a special occasion restaurant and hard to get reservations so make sure you're checking a month beforehand on OpenTable when reservations open up and snag your seat. 

We worked with Joy on our reservation and had Ally as our server. Everything was beautiful and I hope to dine again one day. 


#bluehill #bluehillfamilymeal #familymeal #greenwichvillage #washingtonplace #foodblogging #dinner #pork #vegetables #farm #nyccarbs #comfortmeal

First of all I do not work for Blue hill restaurants. I am someone who has serviced the restaurants since day one . I have never seen in my 40 plus years a Chef that cares more about the operations of his restaurants. He puts more time and effort into them then any chef I ever come across . His restaurants are spotless. His food preparation is out of this world . That is why he is more then just the an award winning chef .    i will remain anonymous

fucking fantastic.

I love places like Blue Hill, where you can get a top-notch dinner for ~100/pp - enough that the produce and labor is exceptional, but not too much that it feels stuffy or like you are nervous to eat. The place was super cozy, not too dark, and the staff were very inviting and sweet.

We came for Blue Hill's "Family Meal," a designation I didn't understand beforehand and still do not fully understand. I guess this means that they serve you more food and don't split up every dish (like they would with a tasting menu) but to us there was no difference. They provide no menu, online or when you arrive, and simply ask you to state your restrictions (of which they are extremely accommodating) when you book. My girlfriend booked as gluten free and they replaced all of the gluten in the meal with something different. She loved the seedy bread that she received and didn't feel like they were just cutting the wheat out but replacing it with something better.

The quantity of food was astronomical, though we didn't realize it at the beginning. The meal started with a small dish of beet tartare and crackers with fresh radishes. We continued to receive small dishes (soup, salad, donut, and more I cannot even remember). The level of complexity and layering to each course was astonishing; a single donut came with one powder and two sauces.

At some point, we thought the meal was done and we were mostly full - then they brought out the main course: a composition of several dishes including a mushroom stuffing, whole wheat biscuit, cranberry sauce, etc. (this was on Black Friday after thanksgiving). Then we received a second main course. Then we received a suite of desserts. We were stuffed.

The food was incredible. I love the connection they have with the upstate farm and all of the science they do with selective breeding to create new varieties of vegetables; this in and of itself is a luxury worth experiencing. The squash soup was delicious and incredibly deep in flavor. Everything was perfectly executed. The style was more traditional - soup, salad, etc. - with the focus on the ingredients and the execution. Do not expect to receive any foams or out-of-left-field flavor pairings, at least as part of the "Family Meal" concept.

The service was also incredible. We had a great experience and I thank my beautiful girlfriend for surprising me to dinner here.

Wow! A great foodie experience that I've been missing for almost two years. We enjoyed several delectable courses over the course of about two hours. I'm relying on my memory here because the family meal is not on a menu, but the standouts for me were: the peppers, hen of the woods mushrooms, corn bread, prosciutto, cheese, and chocolate covered nuts. Every single thing we were served was packed with flavor. Loved it all! Extremely warm service from our servers and our gracious bartender (since we were sitting at the bar). Parties of two will be at the bar, more than two, at a table. Cocktails were strong and the wine was great. Highly recommend Blue Hill for their unique flavors and excellent preparation of the dishes. I didn't take pictures as the lighting was very dark, but trust me the food was delicious. The place is tiny so make sure you have a reservation. Reservations are sometimes booked weeks/months in advance, so try the week days very early dinner.

The Family Meal at Blue Hill was so delicious and the service was amazing (my glass of water was never empty - the wait staff was always so attentive to every table)!  Our server explained the concept of family meal; since they were closed for 18 months they reopened to allow customers to sit and share a meal together and enjoy each other's company.  Since it's chef's selection for family meal they're able to change up the menu daily so that they can source all of their ingredients locally.

They first serve you the snacks which were already hiding on the tabletop.  It was fun to be able to find the bowls and pull them out from underneath the counter.  The wheat bread with the whipped lard and chives was really good.  The bread was soft and the spread was so creamy but at the same time felt light and airy where you didn't feel guilty for spreading more of it on the bread.  

All of the dishes were really flavorful and fresh - the veggies tasted as if they were just picked from the garden and put on a plate.  My favorite dish was the squash.  It had a nice char on the top and the inside was soft and sweet (you could even eat the skin) - it reminded me of a sweet potato.  

Hopefully we'll be able to visit at the Stone Barns to try their tasting experience!

author.name: Stephanie T.
author.location: Town of Hempstead, Long Island, NY

reviews.review:
Blue Hill Family Meal is simple, farm-fresh food executed flawlessly. No, there aren't any fancy or obscure ingredients like caviar or shiso or tuna belly because everything comes from their farm in upstate NY.

The food is served in loose courses, family-style. And just like a family meal at home might be, they never skimp on the bread. The dinner opens with crackers, bread, and a beet tartare that made me think there was tuna in there. I didn't care so much for the fried mushroom bites, but the main courses were excellent: the simple yet decadent egg and mushroom omelet, the roast chicken with a flavorful bean gravy were standouts. I enjoyed the peanut butter butternut squash as well. Lettuce salad didn't feel quite seasonally appropriate, and the dressing was just ok. The creamed spinach was tasty, but also nothing to shout about. The bread, although served generously, was rather stodgy and moist.

Despite all of these flaws, Blue Hill is a place I would return to again and have no hesitations recommending. There's no pretension - or at least, very little - to their food, and because of the vegetable-heavy nature of the meal, it felt like the kind of food I would make at home, and I could eat this daily and not get sick of it. Even dessert mirrored the nutritiousness I value: sliced apples with crisp delicacy, sliced peaches (albeit unremarkable) and a panna cotta.

They change out one of their dishes every day, so there should be an entirely new menu in a couple of weeks' time.

We went to Blue Hill for a family meal for my birthday, it was amazing! The service was incredible, staff were so friendly. The food exceeded our expectations, beyond delicious. They even had accommodations for my sister's boyfriend who follows a gluten free diet. Thanks so much for a wonderful experience, we very much enjoyed the food and accompanying wine progression. I will definitely be back!

Great dining experience. We had a large party and were able to secure the back room which is private and quasi outdoors.

Service was stellar - all aspects could not have had a more charming and enjoyable experience.

The food was good - the standouts? The market salad was out of this world delicious, the eggplant purée, the mashed potatoes, eggs with tomatoes and mushrooms.

Everything tasted fresh and deliberate (a lot of thought was put into the seasonal menu)

Blue Hill was an amazing dinner experience, and even with some significant downsides I am still giving it 5 stars. 
The service was impeccable. Our server Allie was attentive, charming, and explained everything about the dishes. One of the other servers incorrectly told us that one of the desserts was chocolate covered hazelnuts and she overheard and quickly came over to  make a correction. The commitment to enthusiasm for the ingredients, such as explaining the value of abundance potatoes, was genuine.
The food..where to start? As far as I can tell, everything changes on a regular basis so what we ordered is not what you will get.
