Carrots, Bread with pesto, pea stew, and lard with chives made up our appetizers and one of the servers made sure to keep bringing us bread with dips whenever we ran out. Seriously, this bread was quite good.
For our entrees we started off with fresh ricotta, lamb sausage with fennel, eggs with chanterelles, a beautiful summer salad with melons, eggplants and potatoes with corn. These potatoes were actually life changing; easily the best potatoes I have ever consumed and I can understand their value now. The lamb sausage was juicy and not gamey at all. The summer salad, after I constructed a bite with a little bit of everything, was perfectly balanced and the melons were fantastic. Eggs and mushrooms are a fantastic combination and the egg dish was enjoyably yolky, leaving just enough delicious runniness to mop up with our second (or was it third?) order of bread. The ricotta was smooth and juicy, unwrapped fresh for us at the table. I wasn't a huge fan of the eggplant dish, but I still ate half of it, so that being the low point should tell you something.
But this is Blue hill, and that wasn't close to all of the food. We received another bowl of potatoes, this time with pork loin, and this was my absolute favorite dish of the night. The pork loin was deliciously salty and complemented the potatoes amazingly. 
We ordered mocktails, and after an initial kerfuffle where our drinks were mixed up, the mixed up drink was comped and we tried some delicious drinks. 
For dessert we had blueberries with cream, granola, chocolate covered macadamia nuts, and stonefruit. Dessert was definitely the low point of the meal. Up until now everything was farm to table and it showed. However, nothing from the dessert seemed to be from their farm -blueberries from California, chocolate covered macadamia nuts you could get at Costco, and generic granola. The stone fruit was delicious, but nothing special.
I think that our experience would have been truly perfect if we had received one more entree (we were still a bit hungry after eating everything, enough to eat a pizza) and the desserts received more focus. But I don't expect Blue Hill to get a pastry chef or dedicated dessert chef.
The ambiance was stunning, probably the best I have experienced in NYC. We will be coming back.

It is hard to imagine a more perfect summer dining experience than what's being offered at Blue Hill through August.  The food matches Chef Dan Barber's reputation for creativity, deliciousness and sensitivity to sustainability.  The staff is knowledgeable, friendly and delightful to be of service.  The casual atmosphere is welcoming and delightful.  I will go back again while this amazing offering is available through August.

Blue Hill is our special dining place for major milestones or celebrations. They seamlessly work with my multiple food allergies and make the dining experience a pleasure. 

I struggle to find the words for Blue Hill because it is a total experience which brings what the essence of dining should be back to the front and center. There is no temptation other than being in the present moment experiencing your meal's flavors and presentation and your dining company. There are no rushed thoughts or things you must rush to. The food is robust in freshness and flavor. The sourcing of the food is above and beyond any other restaurants of this caliber because not only are they sourced from local places but Blue Hill has their own farm. I do not like radishes but I LOVE the ones Blue Hill Serves. 

The love, attention and care put into the restaurant shows with every bite and minute in their dining room. 

My favorite place to sit is now in the back garden room which is also used for private events. It reminds me of a little secret dining garden the temperature even in the chill of fall was perfect and it was an intimate dining experience and lovely meal with my partner. 

Odd item to love but their hand soap in the restroom in phenomenal and I LOVE it!

In total this is an absolute must experience and not to miss restaurant. It is one of a kind in the world and genuinely deserves all of the accolades it has.

Blue Hill is the best restaurant in NYC, obviously my opinion, though I think anyone can make a case on this. They are so thoughtful about everything that they do. I've been here twice now and the service is truly unbeatable combined with absolutely out of this world food. If you are someone like me who appreciates great vegetables but is not a vegetarian by any means then you need to try Blue Hill. The vegetables are all the best version of that vegetable, it is hard to explain. The meats are also unbelievable, in the most recent trip they did a bone broth using bones from every animal on their farm and poured over ham hock, sausage, beets, and a number of vegetables. This was the most standout delicious meal to me. This is a must try in NYC and I look forward to visiting stone barns in the future.

We got the picnic as a special treat for our anniversary and had a lovely time eating in park seating with social distancing near Christopher St. pier. The food was really good! I only recommend bringing utensils. You can use the bread to dip a lot and get by if you don't though. For us it was enough to eat well for the next couple days or so. They do note how long everything lasts which was helpful.

Good service. 

Didn't think I'd be impressed but it exceeded expectations.

Wow! This is one unforgettable fine dining experience for me.

Blue Hill uses local food,  inspired by the week's harvest.
 a wine list with producers who respect artisanal techniques. Ingredients are from  nearby farms, including Blue Hill Farm in Great Barrington, Massachusetts, and Stone Barns Center for Food and Agriculture, a forty-five minute drive from New York City. 

Every dish is an art !
I highly recommend Blue hill in NY
Had a unique dinner experience at Blue Hill. Had the six course meal with the wine pairing.

What an incredible experience. My husband and I attended dinner for his birthday. We arrived early at sat at the bar. The cocktails and mocktails were top quality. Fresh juices and mixes made right into their drinks. Incredible flavor and beautiful presentation. 

We ordered two Daily Menus which consists of four courses with small additional bites given to you throughout the meal. Very unique food combinations that tasted amazing! The restaurant was extremely accommodating of dietary restrictions and very mindful in the substitutes they offered to me. 

Everything we ate was to the highest quality. The service was very attentive. The total meal took about 2.5/3 hours but well worth the time. It was an experience not to miss!
Everything  was great. The waiters were very attentive and helpful. The food was great. The atmosphere romantic. Not expensive for what it offers.

Solid 4.8 stars. Plan to spend at least 2-3 hours here and maybe more on a busy weekend night. Came on a Sunday night at we ended up here for about 3 hours. Had the 6 course option but came with some more appetizers and in-between dishes. Service is excellent and they explain what ingredients are on your dish. Extensive wine menu as well. 

Here's my night, won't go into details on each dish as all were unique in their own way and delicious. My favorite was the make your own taco. My only critique is to use less pear as 2 or 3 of my dishes had pear in it.

1. Raddish, turnip with honey lard, black pepper and lime
2. Liver with chocolate
3. Artichoke crusted with sunflower seeds
4. Tartar, carrot, egg
5. Sea bream, fennel
6. Make your own taco - scallops, pig ear, squash, herbs, yogurt, pear
7. Winter carrot, mushroom, beef, potato, spinach dip, tendon
8. Pear, vanilla ice cream
9. Chocolate, raspberry, ice cream
10. Blueberry white chocolate dessert
11. Fruit cake

Overall, definitely a special-occasion type of place and good to come at least once! ... unless you have time and money to blow everyday.
Seriously some of the best vegetables I've ever had. But I felt like both the fish and the lamb weren't anything special.
Amazing all around. Great food, incredible service. Well worth a nice date night. Will definitely be back

The most amazing dining experience I have EVER had. They put so much thought and effort into dish, but yet each dish is somehow simplistic. Nothing is obnoxious. Everything is just...perfect. 

Reservations must be made a 3-4 weeks in advance, at least, for prime time slots. Their dining room is pretty small and a few seats are available at the bar. They have two options for tasting menus. A four course and and six course, but you can also add two additional courses and/or a wine pairing. 

The night we dined, our server brought out two starter small bites to be enjoyed with our hands. They were simple and flavorful and prepared us for the remainder of our dining experience. My husband ordered the six course and I ordered the four course. They brought extra cutlery and plates for the two courses where I didn't have a dish. During the night, you would see servers walk from the kitchen with giant vegetables. Root and stalk. They would explain how it was grown and how it is used in the dish you are about to eat. My favorites of the night were the Brussels sprout salad with horseradish dressing and the gnocchi. The bread and butter was delicious, as well.  You must allow 3-3.5 hours to dine at Blue Hill. They don't rush you along at all. We had a show to make and we made it out of there in 2 hours and 45 minutes. There is a reason Blue Hill was among the top restaurants when I lived in NYC over a decade ago and is still to this day.

Thoroughly mediocre meal. Neither my dining partner nor I thought a single dish was a standout; the overall flow of the meal was unremarkable as well. I cannot imagine recommending this or returning: it really was that bad. Fine, but utterly bland and boring. There are so many excellent dining options in this city and so many better ways to spend an evening (and a few hundred bucks).

The vaunted bread and butter was - honestly - not better than the average; par at best. The various courses of vegetables were fine as well, but then again, so are the vegetables I get at any grocery store (don't lecture me on how I'm missing the point, please). A number of other courses were basically a hodge-podge of ingredients with little interest in presentation or assembly (do it yourself!). I was simply not impressed; if the taste had been memorably good, that would be one thing, but everything was just ok.

Service had a number of snafus - to provide just an abbreviated list: I thought a poor job was done explaining the options available in terms of courses; no explanation was given of beverage pairing options; as drinks were consumed, additional drinks were not offered though many courses remained; the kitchen was inexplicably inexcusably slow including relative to nearby tables; the seating itself was tight in a way that made it impossible to interface properly with servers (at best they could lean over my shoulder, standing behind me) which made it difficult to communicate with them; and though not a service issue, the tight seating also contributed to rudeness from nearby patrons - other comparable restaurants in this price band generally permit you a touch more privacy and slightly less of the feeling of being packed like sardines into a can. The intake flow could use work (from host to coat-check to seating) and the whole experience felt decidedly unexceptional (and even though I had offered details on my reservation by phone, these details were apparently not communicated to staff). 

Don't go here, seriously.

Highs:
Amazing atmosphere, delightful bartender (Ben), food cooked to perfection 

Low:
Hostess was not friendly at all and did not even offer to take my coat. She was not the new employee who
stood near the door. The hostess was lingering at the far end of the bar, closer to the tables. She needs additional training from real professionals at Stone Barns.

If you're the type of party-goer that continually grazes the vegetable platters or you pine for the warm summer months solely for the farm fresh/personal garden produce then, Blue Hill is definitely for you! All of their dishes shine with immense attention to quality and detail - without the flashy pizazz. Stone barns remains the gold standard of the farm to table experience, but to be honest, it was a lot less of a hassle getting reservations here.

We arrived early and indulged in an expertly crafted Gin and Tonic and the Gin cocktail* at the bar. Mid way through we were promptly escorted to the most charming and romantic spot in the restaurant  -- the garden room. It was quiet, decorated with lush plants and flooded with warm flickering candlelight throughout. You couldn't help but forget you were in the Village. 

Plentiful and delightful amuse-bouche graced our table before the main event items. The cherry tomatoes with the sea salt tarragon dipping sauce were the most notable and my personal favorite. 

We chose to indulge both the farmers feast and the weekly tasting menu to have the ability to try everything (why pick just one?) 

I have to agree with Maya N. -- The dish I was most excited for on my menu, the smoked eggplant BBQ with grilled watermelon was a little underwhelming. While the bone marrow and cantaloupe soup were surprisingly mouthwatering. Full on scraping and slurping of both commenced. I think I might even try crafting the soup at home when it's back in season. 

Like a camelon, the menu evolves and changes so I won't go into too detail about the rest of the courses. I will say, however the peaches and raspberry finish was clean and elegant. I did not walk out of here hungry. 

Overall, service was fantastic even if our primary waiter was a tad brief. 

Can we talk about how they even have their own branded toiletries in the loo? The hand cream was such an enjoyable treat!

-------
* The name escapes me, its probably off the drink menu by now.

It was simply one of my finest dining experiences from reservations to desserts. It's incredible that this establishment has been around for 19 years and they have been able to not only maintain but also raise the bar for what a dining experience should be. It's located in a very quiet and quaint block on Washington Place across from the beautiful park. The space is not particularly large allowing for a very intimate experience.  The reservation team led by Sasha and Daniella are professional, unpretentious and incredibly friendly and helpful.  When Sasha learned that our reservation was for special occasion, she went above and beyond to help make it memorable.

Upon our arrival, we were greeted by Grace who couldn't have been friendlier. A personalized card was placed on our table highlighting our celebration - a nice touch. The entire wait staff including the sommelier this Saturday evening was affable.  While the wine was something to write home about, our dishes were incredible.  Every dish was creative, flavorful and memorable. It is no wonder that Blue Hill is still one of the hardest venues to secure a reservation for even after 19 years. We will definitely return. Thank you Blue Hill team!

Blue Hill serves an ever-changing menu that's always vegetable-forward and incredibly fresh!

We did the Farmer's Feast, which consists of 6 courses, amuse-bouches, and the best bread you've probably ever had. I'm not one to order vegetables at restaurants, but the crunchy vegetables we started with were delicious; my dining partner is allergic to cucumbers and the servers easily replaced the first dish for him. Our only meat dish was duck and it was superb. My favorite dishes were the desserts, which were fruity and multi-textured. They also sent a small slice of cake with a candle since we were celebrating a birthday, as well as a sweet handwritten card. The only dish I did not enjoy was the tilefish tacos; the tilefish was tough and difficult to chew and the flavors were a bit dull compared to the freshness of the rest of the dishes. 

Personally, I had hoped for a bit more meat and fish overall but understandably with farm-to-table, it's dependent on what they have that time of year. Summer seems to be more vegetable-focused certainly. Headed to Blue Hill at Stone Barns in January and I can't wait to see what's in store!

This is a restaurant that's poorly managed, poorly staffed, and the food is waaaaay overrated. What was supposed to be a celebratory evening turned sour when my friend from out of town took me to this place and hated every plate, while taking over two hrs to have dinner. We had reservations for 9 and left after 11. 

I agreed that the sauces were heavy handed and the food took very long to come out but as a good friend, I tried to appease her by being good company. But when I got home, I immediately found out that the wait staff somehow spilled vodka sauce on the BACK of my silk shirt. This place is so cramped and so dark that I didn't notice until I got home and the stain was set in my silk shirt. Management offered to pay my $7 dry cleaning bill but when I spoke to the Director of Operations on the phone he made me feel like I was lying about the whole thing. My favorite silk shirt is now permanently damaged--they SHOULD be replacing my shirt not making me feel like a liar. 

If you want to wear your best outfit and get it ruined by an amateur careless wait staff, come here.

If you want to eat at a dark cafeteria elbow to elbow with people who pretend to like the food, come here. 

Their staff will do as little as possible to make it better. If you want above and beyond service, go elsewhere. 

No way am I ever coming back NOR would I recommend anyone to go here. PRETENTIOUS 100%
Blue Hill was such an exquisite treat, I visited 2 weeks ago. The food and service was just wonderful.

Blue Hill is a wonderful restaurant in every possible way. 
It is my restaurant of choice for special occasions, and has the ability to make all occasions special.
The food is seriously terrific, but without pretension and beautifully presented.  
The room is warm and welcoming as is the staff.  On birthdays, everyone working there, from hostess to servers, extend birthday wishes - not intrusively, but cordially.  
My favorite NYC restaurant.

I left feeling a little disappointed.  Maybe Blue Hill doesn't seem as fresh anymore; or maybe they had an off night; or maybe we ordered wrong.  But after looking forward to this dinner for a month, we left a little underwhelmed.  The service was great and very attentive, so no issues there, but the food just didn't really wow us.

We had the regular menu, and added a plate of the gnocchi.  I think that was our first mistake.  I think you really always have to go for the Farmer's Feast here.  It's much more creative, and I regretted our decision when we saw our neighbors' plates.

Everything just tasted plain to us from the starters of peppers & pears and brussels sprouts to the chicken and pork mains.  The best thing about the whole meal were the bread and the dessert, which is kind of sad when you're commenting on a multi-course meal.  

Also, another review mentioned that the kitchen is a little heavy-handed with the salt, and I agree.  We almost sent some things back.

My other criticism here is that the wine list doesn't really have many cabernet wines under $100.  I think the wine director here could be a little more open to some more budget-friendly wines.  We also got cocktails and they weren't really that good.  The bartender used too much vermouth in the martini.

The ambiance was a little disappointing too.  Last time we came to Blue Hill, it felt like a calm oasis. This time, it was a little hectic, with louder music, tables seemingly closer together and overall kind of cramped.  Maybe the last time we went was an abnormally quiet night, but for whatever reason, this time around dining here did not feel comfortable.

So I'm giving three stars here.  If we could give 1/2 stars, I'd probably give 3.5 because the service was really good and the staff is experts at remembering special occasions.  I still think Blue Hill is above average, but I think other places in the City are better.

Spectacular.  From the moment we walked in until we left everything on point.  We dined at the bar and service was impeccable.  Only thing better was the incredible food and parings.  Everything was perfectly prepared, surprisingly delightful, and made us make the nummy sound. Thank you for a great night.

Blue Hill was one of the freshest, unique dining experiences I've had in NYC. I went with my best friend to celebrate her birthday, and service was top notch. The restaurant is situated in a brownstone, so it is a bit on the small side and tables are very close to one another but it makes for a cozy romantic vibe. When we arrived for 5:30pm seating, it was quite empty but there wasn't a single table open by the time we left around 8:30. 

We did the farmer's feast, and the menu was fantastic. All ingredients are so fresh, and each course is uniquely prepared and presented. 

She even got a little card to wish her a happy birthday and they took such great care of us. A meal to remember :)

Wonderful experience from the food to the ambiance and service.  

To start, there were the veggie snacks: fennel, butter radish, and deep fried squash rings.  The fennel really was special with complex flavor and lasting essence.  I wanted a basket of the squash rings.  Radishes, I think I just prefer french rather than round.

First dish was the brussel sprout and goat cheese salad.  I'm lactose intolerant, and they were able to modify my options perfectly.  Goat cheese is low lactose, so they put it on the side for me.  They sourced the goat cheese from Nettle Meadow, and it was like brie...so freaking good.

The warm bread that comes with the meal is very nice.  If you're accustomed to specialty/heirloom grains, you'll not be disappointed by the bread or fresh creamed butter.  I ended up keeping my left-over goat cheese and eating it on the bread....yum!

Second dish, Montauk Monkfish, perfectly seared and still so very tender.  

Third, the waste-fed pig, wow.  Three different cuts of pork, cooked perfectly, with wonderful pork flavor in a sweet and tangy sauce.  

To finish, because I couldn't have the panna cotta, I was given a pear sorbet that tasted of bright, juicy ripe pear.  Fantastic way to end a meal.

I highly recommend Blue Hill for a special event, since they do try to accommodate all your needs.  To me, I think any meal at Blue Hill is going to be special.

I went with my boyfriend and we both ordered the Farmer's Feast. It was underwhelming. Raw turnip and radish with butter as a snack? The vegetables weren't that special! Nothing I haven't tasted from the Park Slope Food Coop.

Bad flavors overall, one of the worst pieces of steak I've had, and too damn expensive. Should've gone to Olive Garden.

I'm split on the rating. I would give the front room staff 5 stars easily. Whether by the host, the waitress or the runners, we were very well treated. The wine suggestions were perfect, and the cocktails were delicious. 

I would say all of the issues came from the kitchen, from the shellfish first course that should have been without shellfish (someone had an allergy and we had not only warned ahead but discussed it at length with the waitress), to waiting quite a bit between courses, to having to send back food twice. They brought us a Brussel sprout salad that was drenched in the horseradish dressing and we found it inedible and asked for it to be less dressed. There was a tile fish dish that was so salty (every element on the plate was salty) that we sent it back as well - but unfortunately when it came back, the flavors just weren't good. They also served a kind of squid corn succotash which was drenched in a brown sauce - it was supposed to be huitlacoche I think, but that has a subtle flavor - this brown sauce was cloyingly sweet and salty - I didn't taste the corn or the squid. My dish had lobster in it, but I didn't understand in what capacity as I couldn't taste it either.

Most of the dishes ran SUPER salty. I'm usually the kind of person who asks for the salt shaker and finds the absence of salt on a table presumptuous, but I had a really hard time even finishing these. The wait staff was so so kind - and they told the kitchen over and over again to mind the salt - our last couple of dishes were much better seasoned. The pork three ways with Lima beans was probably one of the best savory dishes of the night, and the plate with the roasted beets and watermelon was also fresh and tasty. The wait staff said that sometimes the kitchen is heavy handed on the salt, but honestly the flaws that I found in the dishes had to do with flavor profiles and balance - the person responsible is the chef who designs and oversees, not the sous-chefs that execute the vision. The tile fish for instance when they brought out a less salty version was hard to eat because of the incredibly bitter greens on it - so clearly the salt was there to balance it, but not in a pleasant way. It's just very hard to imagine these dishes are Michelin-star worthy. And I found this lack of balance in practically all of the dishes. Even the little foie gras amuse that supposedly had chocolate on it - that just tasted like caramel, and the paté was good for one bite and then incredibly salty. 

I think the desserts were my favorite. They were very understated, not very sweet, but subtle and much more nuanced than the rest of the savory dishes. As everyone has noted, the bread and butter is very good too. 
 
I did not think the portions were overly small, given the amount of dishes we got. I would really have liked to like this place more.

My husband and I went here for our 1 year anniversary. It was amazing!! They really went out of their way to make us feel special on our anniversary. Service as fantastic, everything we tried was delicious, cocktails were unique and tasty, and the ambiance of the restaurant was great. Very cool concept with them trying to eliminate food waste. We will definitely be back next time we are in NYC.

Celebrated a birthday here with dinner. We opted for the extended tasting menu and I am glad we did as the two best bites were the surprise dishes. The tasting menu is 6 courses, the extended includes two surprise dishes from the chef (not on any menu). They started by bringing out a bunch of fresh vegetables. Cucumber spears with a dipping sauce, radish with tarragon sauce, a non-spicy habanero pepper, grilled shishito pepper, and a cooked delicata squash. Then the courses came out. 

First was raw tuna with nectarine and sake lees. It was very nice and light but still had flavor. Next was sweet corn with squid which was enjoyable. The first surprise dish was a ginger noodle (light ginger flavor in the pasta) with uni butter. It was divine, not like any other dish I've tasted. This was easily the best thing we ate. 

Next was sour dough bread with homemade butter topped with grains which provided a nice crunch. Really tasty, exactly what you want from bread and butter. The second surprise dish as a thin pastrami steak with wheat germ and lobster mushrooms. The pastrami was good, but the star was the wheat germ. So flavorful and very satisfying, the wheat germ is like a lentil but bigger and more spongy. Next was the beef which came as two slices and pieces of short rib. The slice lacked flavor, but the short rib was perfect. It was served with pepper, plum and a pepita sauce. My issue was that none of these things really went with the other. The next course was eggplant with jujube bean BBQ sauce. It came with grilled watermelon, potato salad, beans with salsa verde and vegetable chow chow. Again, everything tasted good, the jujube sauce with the eggplant was delicious, but again, none of the items really went together. 

The last two courses were grapes with ginger and a light yogurt mousse and a peach raspberry puree with lemon verbena yogurt. The grapes were warm which was a nice contrast against the cold mousse, but there was a bit too much ginger for my liking. The peach and raspberry puree was tasty and had almonds in it, the lemon verbena yogurt provided a sour note. The dish was nice and not too sweet and good end to the 8 courses.

We ordered fresh mint tea and then they brought out a dessert to celebrate the birthday, a thin vanilla cake with a strawberry mousse on top. Very pleasant and followed by fruits they brought out before the check, peaches, white nectarines, figs, and a cherry that looked like a gooseberry.

The service was phenomenal, very friendly and knowledgeable. The ambiance is nice, though the tables are quite close together. Overall it was a very nice experience. I will say though I think we would have been a bit let down though if we hadn't had the two surprise dishes. All of the courses were enjoyable, but only 2-3 really stood out.

NYC's favorite speakeasy, tucked 3 levels below street level is as FRESH as fresh harvests can get. 

We had a "Farmer's Feast" which is literally inspired by that weeks harvest from local farm and also the classic tasting menu.

Experiencing UPSTATE NY potatoes with my Upstate NY friends was a rare moment of foodie pride for their kind. This with creamy, Non-goatey goat cheese was truly well executed.

Montauk Tilefish on a bed of cantaloupe gazpacho was sashimi grade based on my Montauk experiences at Showfish and Blue Hill came very close to the freshness of being at the Marina and Yacht club itself by the water - even if the portions were not very comparable

Some dishes were beyond inspired and creative which always wins over the foodie in me : the Sunflower Marrow - thoroughly vegetarian - served and plated to perfection with the illusion of being in a Half sliced celery fronting as an actual Bone 

Heirloom Tomatoes are in season and that was heavily reflected in the choices with Dill , plum and dishes but these were literally served with Fresh ricotta, with a consistency that was straight from the farm 

the heirloom cucumbers with Breaded yogurt was an early course appetizer but had the flavor of a hearty anglaise. 

There were a good amount of amuse Bouches which were sometimes even a bigger hit than the entrees themselves : tomato sugar water shots, 
The fluffiest warm whole wheat with the lightest cloud of puffed quinoa and roasted farro might even have stolen the show. 


Main courses: 

The potato potato was surprisingly great - smoked goat cheese helped

Smoked prosperosa eggplant BBQ: with the grilled watermelon - a little underwhelming , but otherwise very fresh 

Mocktails: 

PLUMS: plums, Thai basil, club soda
 
CRANBERRY: hibiscus, toasted cardamom, whey ( meh - too Bloody Mary like somehow) 

PEACHES : peaches , mint and ginger ( my fav)

Finally the desserts: Heirloom grapes with a cheese sorbet and the peaches and cream with a hint of raspberry, topped with maple foam was once again, inspired and creative while staying light and fresh. 

NV: they have a Garden Room supposedly which I look forward to coming back and exploring

Meh. Nice folks serving uninspired food. The dishes had one tone to them, which did not make my taste buds jump for joy. Service is amicable and drinks are good, not enough for me to come back and spend many of my $$ here.

This was outstanding. We went to Stone Barns for dinner a long time ago so it's hard to say exactly how it compares, but this holds up extremely well in its own right. 

We did the extended farmer's feast, which is their normal tasting menu plus two extra courses -- a pig dish and the pasta and tomatoes dish from their regular menu. (There were also lots of small bites in between, but it's possible that those all come with the regular farmer's feast.) This ended up being a pretty perfect amount of food -- we were full, but not sick at the end.

We had a tough time deciding which courses were our favorites. The eggplant barbecue is pretty tough to beat, but the beef course (which came with amazing peppers, even more amazing nectarines, and a fantastic green sauce) was also amazing, as were the heirloom tomatoes (which came with a small pouch of homemade ricotta), the tomato/water shooters, the old and new corn, and their "beet jerky." Of course, there was also the bread and seeded butter, which I think I could eat for every meal the rest of my life and still be happy.

Overall, just an outstanding meal. We really loved it.

My wife's review...

My husband took me to eat at Blue Hill this past July for my birthday. I had been looking forward to eating there for many years, and the experience did not disappoint the build up at all! I unfortunately have several digestive issues that prevent me from enjoying any tasting menu 'as is' and we had let the restaurant know this in advance. When we arrived, we walked into a cozy environment that is tastefully styled and lovely without being tight or giving the feeling that you are sitting with the party next to you. Our host got us settled without delay, at a table with a hand drawn and written card, wishing me a happy birthday. She also confirmed that I was the party requiring special attention to the way my food would be prepared, as did our server as well. When ordering cocktails and wine, we were presented with opinions and options, and a taste to see if our choice would actually be to our liking. The food was beyond delicious, and they took very good care to make sure that my restrictions were no impediment to my enjoyment of the experience. The best part of the evening was when they created a dessert especially for me, so that I could enjoy every course. It was of course the best dessert I've ever eaten! The flavors and decadence of the course was something that I had not experienced at any restaurant previously! As if that wasn't enough, about a week later, my husband and I received another hand written post card from Blue Hill in the mail, thanking us for dining with them and looking forward to serving us again. Such amazing service, attention to detail, and incredible food and drink, for not more than any other 'nice' restaurant would cost you - you can be certain that we will return for more!

I am obviously no expert and have admittedly only been to a handful of Michelin-starred restaurants, but personally, I think Blue Hill is more on the level of a two-star experience. I thought it was on par with Aquavit and better than The Modern.

The dishes presented here benefit from not only incredible flavors and the freshest-imaginable high-quality ingredients, but thoughtful conceptions of texture, temperature, and presentation. These often overlooked details allowed us to experience dining - and even foods' taste - in different ways and from different perspectives. 

Amuse-bouches: Don't remember too much about these, but they were understated and excellent. One was a cherry tomato that reminded me of a cross-breed between a wild grape and a tomato. I was a fan.

Experimental 7082 Cucumber (peaches, buttermilk and green tomato ice): This was a great example of a dish that plays with the temperature element. The tomato ice had a vinaigrette sort of flavor that added a lot to the way I experienced the dish. 

Lettuce tacos (bluefish salmon, fava bean guacamole, bacon, and watermelon hot sauce): This was a fun make-your-own-taco experience that utilizes lettuce in the place of taco shells. The lightly-cooked salmon was incredible and was the star of the dish. The watermelon hot sauce is buried in a tiny little bottle within the lettuce shells, I guess just because it's fun. The whole thing is fun. 

Pastured duck (peas, lovage and pistachios): No dish was a miss, not even close, but this would've been our last favorite if we had to pick one. The flavors were all still excellent, but the dish wasn't quite as exciting. 

Barbecued Badger Flame Beet Steak (corn on the cob, beet greens and gooseberry ketchup): So, beet steak. Tastes like a beet, but the flavor is sharper and more intense, as with dried foods, and the texture is - indeed - meatier. The beet greens reminded me a bit like spinach. The corn was wrapped in a mixture of some salty, crunchy grains, or something akin to it.

Blueberries (goat cheese, yogurt and buckwheat): So amazing! The chilled goat cheese/yogurt combo tasted of a creamy goat cheese ice cream, and I can't imagine eating something tastier. I've noticed buckwheat popping up in desserts and multiple restaurants like Blue Hill. It adds texture (crunch) and unique, pleasing, earthy flavor. 

Strawberries (mint, almonds and white chocolate): Not much else to say, just another delicious dessert. 

The extensive wine list is organized by its characteristics (smooth and earthy, ripe and luscious, etc.), which was helpful, and our server was knowledgeable about each bottle and helped us further narrow down our options. We ended up going with the 2008 Calabretta from Italy, which was just as described: medium-bodied, terroir-driven, smokey, and somewhat tannic. It was excellent.

We also tried one cocktail each. He got the Thinking Cap (gin, ramps, dry vermouth, & mushroom bitters): A vegetal-umami take on a gin martini that was obviously on target with Blue Hill's concept and that worked because of the high-quality gin and vermouth and also the mushroom bitters (didn't know those existed). I have to say that I enjoyed this drink more than mine, which had gin, gooseberry, and egg white, and which I thought lacked some depth.

The staff is perfect, their interactions with the diners and with each other seamless. We truly enjoyed chatting with our server. The ambience is fairly relaxed but formal enough to make it feel special. Oh, and I loved the bathrooms.

Lovely meal at Blue Hill. The experience is drawn out over several hours, which may seem very slow at first, but I think that is because we are all so used to being rushed in and out of restaurants that it can be a bit of an adjustment to eat a meal slowly and meaningfully. We ordered the farmers feast menu, which comes with several amuse bouches that are not listed in addition to the courses. The meal was excellent and I especially enjoyed how carefully the waiters explain each dish as you are served. Care is also taken to check for allergies. The space is small and the tables are close together. This is on par with the West Village, but I could see that it may come as a surprise if you are not used to this type of seating. I think the price is quite reasonable for a NYC Michelin star restaurant. I can't wait to return during a different season and see how the menu changes!

My first real tasting menu experience in New York. Heard about it from Chef's Table and was excited to have a great experience. We chose to do the feast (8 courses) which in hindsight was way too much food. Given that they give you extra little courses the six course menu would have been plenty. Honestly the best bites of food were in the amuses at the beginning, especially the vegetables with the lard, which was our favorite, and the liver. The butter served with the bread was also spectacular. Since it was a special occasion they also gave us an extra dessert which was generous. For the main courses the beets disguised as meat were quite clever but we were not as impressed with their play on a pastrami sandwich. Overall, a great experience and a good value for a new york tasting menu from an all star chef.

I can't say that it's the worst place I've ever eaten at but it puts up a strong competition! (it's definitely the worst in this price range!)

First off the ambience is terrible... we were in what we thought was the main dining room; which was all shades of grey and dark.  The service was coldly polite initially and then totally indifferent to our poor dining experience.

My husband and I came here for our wedding anniversary and it was a terrible disappointment in every way.

The first course was vegetables with a sort of dipping sauce which was not inedible but not particularly tasty.

I think his was followed by a lettuce wrap with crispy pig ear .... which was ok not terribly tasty however there were just two lettuce leaves in the big bread basket it came in.

The mains were particularly terrible.... my husband usually a non complaining man, had to spit out the beef since it was so chewy.... we had to send the dish back.
The replacement that came was equally raw ( despite asking for medium rare) however the cut of meat was a tad better.

I had chosen the pork from the tasting menu... it was so gamey and unflavourful I had to send it back after just one bite. They replaced it with the lasagna which was not very edible either.

The dessert seemed to be berries and cream, it wasn't inedible but I can make better in 1 min in my kitchen!

What was interesting is that the servers were aware that we weren't enjoying the food but didn't seem to particularly care!( maybe they are used to it!)

All of this for a lovely price tag of 300$.  We would have had a better experience and food if we would have eaten microwaved food at home!!

Save ur self the trouble , DONT go there!

One star for the bread and butter which was great and for seating us though we were late.

The waiting period for the food is overall not worth it. The waiting period is such a long time and the portions that come after are very small and barely filling. However, the quality of all the food is very good.

Inventive menu and delicious flavors in this quaint restaurant would be hidden forever if not for its well deserved michelin star status that had us seeking it out. It's tucked into the bottom of a pretty staircase that can be easily missed. The dishes focus on natural flavors of vegetables and are bright and sweet. My favorites were the kohlrabi rings and goose egg pasta with lobster. Service was friendly and well paced. Reservations are a must. I prefer this Blue Hill over the restauant at the Farm, though if you've never been to the farm it is a beautiful setting and be sure to go early to spend more time visiting the expansive gardens there.

Went back to Blue Hill and it was just as amazing as I remembered and just as affordable for the quality you're getting. Unlike a lot of other Michelin restaurants, Blue Hill really highlights the ingredients without trying so hard to razzle and dazzle you with gimmicks. It's just the best quality ingredients, cooked perfectly.

Drinks will run anywhere between $10 for a beer to $15-$20 for wine and cocktails. They have two menus: the Farmer's Feast ($108) and the standard tasting menu ($95). You can choose a different menu from your dining partners, which was very appreciated.

Relaxed vibe. Knowledgeable servers. Excellent veg dishes, breads, desserts. Good drinks. Passable beef. Fish meh. A few excellent wines. Overuse of foam perhaps :) Everything beautifully plated. Generally pleasant with some wow moments. We had both the left and right side menus. Both worth trying.

Not the place to go if you're looking for a reasonably-priced dinner.  But if you're looking for a place that changes its menu almost daily using the freshest available ingredients, and plates and flavor combinations that will impress even the most picky foodie, then this place is for you.  We had the extended tasting menu, which included 3 different amuse bouche, and each course was better than the next.  One of the duck dishes had some sinew, so was a little tough, but the rest was a home run!

One of the most memorable dining experiences I've ever had. Food, wine and service (thank you, Leslie) were impeccable. If you're visiting the city, this is certainly a stop you should put on your list. Came here for a celebration and will most definitely be back. Once again thank you: Leslie, Cole & Jason for the incredible hospitality!

Great food, ambience, and service. Will the food blow your mind? No, probably not. However, you will undoubtedly find a great experience here that is well worth the reasonable tasting menu prices. Again, think of this meal as more of a staple that you will dependably feel content about.

Blue Hill:
Tasting Menu:
1. Free bites(among them, foie gras is great)
2. Asparagus
3. Soft Shell Crab
4. Free Bread
5. Pastured Duck
6. Pea Crepes(duck thigh)
7. Rhubarb(goat cheese, yogurt)
8. Strawberries(white chocolate)
9. Free bites strawberry
A feast of strawberry and basil! The bread and butter is great, as well as the duck!

When my husband wanted to try Blue Hill for his birthday, I couldn't have been more excited. A month ahead of time, I made a reservation. When the day came, we were stuck in several hours of insane traffic (our 3 hour drive from RI turned into a 7 hour drive into the city-- and we've made this drive many times!!) I continued to call that day to update the restaurant on our delay, and they very courteously held our table. Finally when we were stuck in bumper to bumper traffic on our way, I called the restaurant again to let them know that we were going to be even later (an hour at this point). The hostess was incredibly honest and told me that we would be rushed out at that point to make room for a later reservation.
What held Blue Hill apart from the other high end restaurants we have been to, was the way that they reacted. Rather than telling me that we were SOL, the hostess told me that she could hold 2 seats at the bar for us an hour out from when we talked-- and she assured us that the bar was small and intimate. Hesitantly, I accepted this offer. We were dropped off shortly after our phone call, and grabbed a quick drink and appetizer at Babbo on the other side of the block (a fabulous way to kill time if you need to!!). When we got to Blue Hill, our experience was nothing short of superb. The service, even at the bar, was impeccable, and every course was timed perfectly to arrive after the last. I was so thrilled that we were able to attend this spot after the headache is took us to get there, and every dish that we had made the wait even more worth it. I recommend this spot to the everyone I know, and we can't wait to get back!

Food was great, as expected, as well as the service and ambiance! The mark of a good restaurant is one that makes you like an ingredient you usually don't like.... that happened for me for their delicious duck in two different dishes :)

I had dinner with a friend at Blue Hill. I like what Chef Dan Barber is trying to do with food and definitely support his philosophy. Full disclosure: I have not been to the Stone Barnes location. The restaurant in New York though was less than memorable. The service wasn't anywhere near a fine dining experience you would expect from such a restaurant. First the staff botched up our dinner service by not bringing in the the Maine Halibut and went straight to palate cleansing savories. Upon inquiring on the Halibut, they acted as though it was a simple mistake. "Oh we are sorry your courses are out of order. Your halibut should be on your way shortly!". This was right before dessert. They finally adjusted our check to take care of our drinks but by then my evening was ruined. Imagine sitting in a restaurant for couple of hours and trying to piece together every dish and the ebb and flow of a Chef's thought process while the service completely drops the ball. I'm not going to be back here again. 


P.S: The halibut was on the saltier side and so was the grassfed beef.

Blue Hill is the most memorable and amicable dining experience I have ever had. 
My wife arrived on time for our 5PM reservation. The maitre D'hotel was cordial, inviting, adorable. She gave us her name and offered the utmost sincerity with our travels. We were sat in several minutes and greeted by our server. 
There were no other tables in the dining room when we arrived. We followed our server's every suggestion and what followed was a full array of some of the most interesting, fully immersive dishes. Amazing. Service was excellent. Drinks were perfectly paired. Management was likewise engaging and genuine in approaching our table to see how our dinner was.
This place is so real that they actually sent us a postcard thanking us for joining them for dinner. 
1000 stars. Go to this place.

First, I've wanted to eat here since I first saw Dan on Chefs Table. It's been in my list for years. But I live in Seattle, so getting here has taken patience and determination. 

I'm so glad I was able to get in. I got a seat at the bar, and Mary, who was tending bar, introduced me to the menu. "I want everything on the menu" I said. She laughed and told me about the 8 course tasting meal with wine pairings. 

"YES!" I said. 

The first few bites arrived and were as yummy as you might imagine perfectly seasonable farm fresh veggies raised for flavor might taste. The radish was more radishy and the turnip more turnipy! And the pig lard with honey and black sesame made it 1000x better. 

Mary had told the manager about my interest in cookery and he kindly invited me into the kitchen to see the amazing chefs at work. A real treat for a foodie like me. And bonus, while there they gave me a bite of liver and chocolate! Wow! (Perhaps a contender for the bite of the night!)

The courses kept coming. A stinging nettle tart, a sugar snap pea with spec, seasonal asparagus with a cured hen yolk grated over it and a broccoli pea stew to dip them in. 

The next dish literally took my breath away. Halibut with celtuce, pine nuts and asparagus. The fish was cooked perfectly. But the sauce was singularly the best sauce I have ever tasted. I seriously wanted to lick the plate. 

One of the advantages of enjoying the wine pairing is that the Chef selected wines complement the dishes to perfection. What makes Blue Hills different is that the wines they select are also thoughtfully selected for their farming practices beyond their flavor. Mary knew the wines intimately and shared the winery stories of each bottle to make each sip more meaningful. I found the wines paired favorably with each dish although I prefer a flat wine to a sparkling wine for dessert, but that me. 

In the 8 course meal, the kitchen includes two off menu dishes. The first of these was mesmeric. Monk fish liver and fava beans with braised strawberries. Truly magical. Foie Gras of the sea! 

The wheat bread was more wheaty, the butter enhanced with kinwa sesame and faro. That was followed by duck with morels and fiddle heads - superb, grass fed cow with crushed potato and escarole - superb, abd the second off menu dish - Parsnip schnitzel with sourkraut spritzer creamed ramps and juju beans. This was at first, my least favorite dish, I say "at first" because my last bite included all the elements in perfect proportion so that true umami was created. Yum. 

Dessert was a Rhubarb, yogurt sorbet buckwheat and goat cheese treat followed by strawberries, white chocolate and cocoa nibs to finish.

I was thrilled to have had a chance to experience the thoughtful cookery, the elegant plating, the personable service and entire experience from start to finish in an atmosphere of happiness. I met a couple of fellow diners at the bar where I was seated, and all were also true fans of Blue Hill. 

Thank you Dan for creating a truly memorable experience for your diners! Great food, tastefully presented by an amazing knowledgeable generous and friendly staff. Highly recommend.

Maitre d' Jason ruined what would otherwise have been a very nice evening.  He is a dishonest scoundrel!  We made our reservation a month ago for eight, knowing that there were not tables that could accommodate eight. We requested then, and again a week before we arrived, to have two tables next to each other.  After all, we were eight people from five different cities trying to enjoy a graduation dinner together.  We knew there were no guarantees, but honestly, how hard could it be -- especially work a reservation earlier in the evening?

We arrived to find that our tables were not even close to each other, with two other tables in-between.  Not happy, and we let that be known!  When first one of the tables, and then the other, opened up a little while later, Jason came over and said they had been reserved by regulars who specifically requested those tables so we could not be reseated.  When my sister-in-law said she didn't believe him, I almost laughed.  What reason would he have to lie?  We watched for almost two hours while one of the two tables sat empty. What didn't occur to Jason was that restaurant guests could talk to each other. It quickly became apparent that he had lied to our faces -- the people at the other tables were neither regulars, not had they specifically requested those tables.  Rather than accommodating our request -- after all, we were spending more than $1000 in the restaurant -- he chose to spite us by keeping the table vacant for so long, and then lying to our faces.  What an ass!

Oh yeah, the food was good.

It is worth flying to New York to have this unique dining experience. The degree which the chef goes to shows up in all the plates. Most of the sourcing is from his own farm. We could have lived on the sensational bread and butter and been perfectly content.
Go for special occasions. You will create a lifetime memory.

Everything tasted so good, I ate stuff that I would never eat else where like raw radish and liver. I didn't give it to my husband this time around. All of their food tasted fresh, especially their vegetables. I think it's worth every penny, my husband think they taste better than Eleven Madison Park (we went there last year for our anniversary). They also gave us a post card that says happy anniversary and a piece of cake with candles, so sweet of them.

Hands down the best restaurant I've been to. I was blown away by the service and the level of detail. I have a nut allergy and not only was the whole staff aware, but they made any accommodation I needed and the chef had no cross contamination. The food is amazing and fresh. Such a delight.

We had a late seating Saturday night and stuffed our faces with the extended farmers feast tasting for 3 hours. We paired all dishes with a 2017 Pinot Noir by Nathan K from the finger lakes. It was a light bodied Pinot so I felt it went well for the majority of the meal. For this review, I'm going to focus on the stand out items, both good and bad.

The good: their crudo, with the white strawberries, nettle, and rhubarb was fantastic. We also really enjoyed the grass fed lamb and grass fed beef dishes. They were both really delish. The starter vegetables were also delicious with a lard based side to dip them in.

The bad: we did not care for the parsnip. I don't think it had a lot of flavor and it came later in the meal so I didn't have a lot of incentive to force myself to eat it. Also, the first of the asparagus was too salty for our tastes. The first bite made me feel like I was smoking a cigarette. That's the first time good has made me think of smoking...

Overall, I rate it 5-stars. The meal and wine were excellent. I didn't get egg in a pan so I'll have to come back a third time and try again...
This is by far one the the best kitchen experiences we had. Farm to table concept many healthy options great wine selection - must go!

OK so I Loooove to eat out and it has been a while since I have done a review... But I have to talk about Blue Hill.Let me start by saying PHENOMENAL... I took my son their for his 35 the BD. He is still talking about this place. He and I found out about this restaurant on Netflix " chef's Table"Do not be fooled by the small portion by the time the entire meal is finished you are stuffed. Every taste gives your month an experience. At the start you are served some single bites so don't be shocked... put that bite in your month and prepare to be sent to flavor heaven

My boyfriend and I went to Blue Hill for his birthday and I specifically picked this place due it its glowing reviews. The Obamas have been here and it is also a celebrity hotspot. Unfortunately it didn't live up to those expectations at all! 

First of all, the tables were too close to each other and we couldn't have a conversation- it seemed like the people sitting next to us were dining 'with' us. Definitely not the place for a romantic dinner, unless you don't mind knowing your neighbor's life story...

We started with a couple of cocktails- "In the Weeds" for me and "The Kitchen Sink" for him, both a bit underwhelming. For our meal, we decided to go all in and get the Farmer's Extended Feast, which is the Farmer's Feast plus 2 extra courses, 8 in total. The plates were extremely small and we were not full by the end of the meal. For such an expensive dinner, we were hoping to be stuffed and content. I'm not sure if any of those plates were complex enough to be memorable. I get that this is a "farm-to-table" restaurant and they want to highlight the qualities of fresh ingredients but there is no excuse to serve plain old grilled asparagus or a completely untreated radish (which came with an unappealing whipped lard, which to be honest tasted a bit like vaseline!). The radish was good but c'mon! 

My 3 biggest issues with them-

1. Some of the dishes were served on broken wedges of plates which had sharp edges. Super easy to get a cut in that dimly lit space when you're a few glasses of wine down. 

2. I got a call from them 24 hrs prior to confirm my reservation and they asked me if we have any dietary restrictions. I specifically told them my boyfriend does not eat onions or scallions- raw or cooked. They confirmed and that's that. Now during our meal, we didn't think to reiterate this fact (fancy restaurant, they have our preferences already etc) and one of the plates- their gnocchi came on a BED of scallions!! We waited a bit for this course and were super hungry so instead of sending the plate back he carefully picked out the gnocchi on to his side plate and ate them. This is completely unacceptable, especially on his birthday! 

3. We got some bread mid-way through the service, and it was great! Their whipped seeded butter was probably one of my favorite things from the night. They gave us 2 pieces of bread which we inhaled! We asked them for some more bread right away around course #4. Few mins later, nothing. We asked them again...and yet again. We finally got bread right before dessert, almost 40 mins later. We gladly ate it because we were still quite hungry. Again, unacceptable, especially for a place that had 4 servers serving a table.

All in all, quite a disappointing experience. Especially compared to his birthday dinner at Aquavit last year which was fabulous! 

Won't return.

This was the worst meal.  The food was so bad and poorly presented. Also the choice of food was ridiculously limited. 

The service was also so inconsistent. We got the first two course within minutes. Too fast. And then we waited 40 minutes for the main course.

We were put in the "garden room" which was like a paneled basement.

We were there when it opened almost 20 years ago and it has NOT held up.

I am saddened to report that my wife got food poisoning here.  I got it too, but to a way lesser extent. It's a shame, as we had been looking forward to dining at Blue Hill for a long time. We were in town on vacation and celebrating our friend's birthday. We think the poisoning was caused by the greens from the carrot, which was the first course. 

I will say that our server, Mary, was awesome. She was friendly, fun, informative, etc. The experience as a whole was good, although we've definitely had better food for more reasonable cost. But when my wife started violently throwing up about 6 hours later, our view understandably changed.

It got so bad that I had to take her to urgent care the next morning to get treated by a doctor.

It was then that I called Blue Hill to tell them what had happened. To their credit the manager I spoke with, Cole, seemed to take our situation seriously, telling me he would inform the chef, etc. and expressing sympathy for my wife's situation.

At this point, if you were in our position what would you expect a high-end, Michelin-star rated restaurant to do? Give your money back, right? I mean, it's not like it's Chili's and you spent $50. We spent almost $500... to get food poisoning!

At first I didn't say anything about the money, thinking that of course they would offer to refund at least part of our bill. Cole, who was also very nice, said they had a 48 hour procedure to follow and they'd need to see if anyone else got sick that night, etc and that he would call me back in two days. I said I totally understand and I look forward to speaking with him again.

He never called.

Again, a restaurant of this caliber... I felt like it was adding insult to injury. 
I called him five days later. But I don't want to paint this as dealing with nasty people or having a big screaming fight. It wasn't. Cole was very polite and apologized for not calling. We had a very civil, respectful conversation.

However, he said my wife was the only person to get sick and therefore they felt that maybe she got sick from somewhere else. Now, is this possible? Sure. From our perspective though, there was nothing else she or I ate that day that would be a suspect for causing food poisoning. It does seem highly more likely that carrot greens from a farm could have not been washed thoroughly. And that just because no one else got sick doesn't mean that the greens on HER plate didn't cause HER to get sick.

Cole then told me there was nothing else the restaurant was willing to do for us because they felt sure the food poisoning wasn't from them. Although, he did say he hoped we'd come back and give them another chance. Ha!

The thing is, it's not about the money. We chose to go there, as we have many other expensive restaurants over the years. We knew what it would cost and we decided to go. Not that we can afford this kind of dinner more than maybe once a year, but still. It's about customer care. A person comes to your restaurant and believes they got sick from your food. If I were the restaurant, especially a high-end one like this, even if I thought you may have gotten sick elsewhere, I'd say, "let me at least refund your wife's meal. I'm sorry your experience here was tainted." I mean, what does that really cost them? All it does is make them look good, make me feel cared for as a customer, and de-escalate the situation.

Again, I do understand where they are coming from and their point of view. I just think in terms of customer relations, PR, whatever you want to call it, there's a right way to handle these kinds of situations where with minimal output you can make everyone walk away feeling better. Instead, they chose to make my experience even worse.

UPDATE: After contacting upper management and posting this review, the owner of the restaurant emailed me personally to apologize and provide compensation. He was very gracious and he handled the situation as it should have been handled from the start. So for that, I am grateful.

My husband and I went for a celebratory dinner to Blue Hill last night. If I could rate it more than 5 stars I would- this place is truly exceptional. We had the extended Framer's feast menu and every single item was excellent. I've never had a tasting menu before that was this diverse, true to its own roots, elegant yet so unpretentious and every bite, a flavor explosion - or as I called it, a 'gift that keeps on giving'. From the mini radishes with lard to the celeriac Ruben with home made pastrami and humble bread to the two light and flavorsome dessert courses, everything was so well conceived and presented. Thank you for an amazing experience and can't wait to visit Stone Barns next!

I have nothing but good things to say about my experience dining here. Upon entering, the staff was quick to wish me a happy birthday and when we were seated, on our table was already a note card for me (a cute little memorabilia to remember the occasion by). The service was top-notch and the farm-to-table courses were delicious.

My boyfriend and I both went for the Farmer's Feast menu which was an ample amount of amazing plates one after the other.

I was surprised at how much I enjoyed even the simplest bread and butter which was served midway through the meal. The butter contained nuts/seeds and tasted so fresh and creamy. Very impressed. Special thanks to our wine curator, Jason, for making the experience even more memorable.

I definitely recommend Blue Hill to anyone looking for a place to dine. You won't be disappointed!

We were looking forward to this restaurant with eager anticipation and with very high expectations, since we had heard that the Obamas have dined here and we are big fans of theirs. Unfortunately, Blue Hill restaurant was a complete disappointment.

For such an expensive place, this restaurant has absolutely no ambience whatsoever. It's a clearly a converted basement of a townhouse, with very low ceilings, and it feels claustrophobic.

Our waitress was completely perfunctory, with no personality or smile whatsoever. These problems pale in comparison to the food. Although I have to admit it was tasty, my entrée was the tiniest I've ever been served in any restaurant anywhere in the world (and I've eaten in many). When it arrived, I was looking around to see if maybe there was a hidden camera or something - was this a joke of some kind? Fortunately, my date let may have some of her chicken, which was bland and seemed to have been cooked with no seasoning whatsoever.

The biggest laugh, however, was saved for dessert -- barely three bites' worth! Where do these people get the gall to sell such tiny portions for such high prices? They must be laughing all the way to the bank!

Stay away from this restaurant, unless you're anorexic.

I have ridiculous food allergies so I wrote back and forth with the staff several times to create a menu for me. My meal was presented beautifully and with such care. Delicious. Cannot recommend more highly!!

From the moment you sit down you are in for a treat!  The cocktails are so much fun.  I had the Yellow Jacket combination of honey, egg whites and turmeric which gives the drink the perfect color and balance.     Since the menu is ever changing I hope you can drive the diver scallop which is behind delicious and the Juice pulp cheeseburger which if even better as beefless.    Th beer ice cream is unusual as is almost everything here.  Presentation and fresh and amazing incredients and combinations that only a genius chef like Dan Barber could dream up.   The ambiance is also fantastic and the staff world class!

What is left to say about this place?

They serve up some of the freshest food in the city and have it coursed out in such a free flowing way. 

My friend and I opted for the wine pairing, which added a nice component to the meal as we took in all the info about each dish and each wine pour.

The hostess in the FOH was absolutely fantastic and super charming and informative--also didn't hurt that she was from my hometown.

Our waiter was also great and very attentive and friendly.

Though the food didn't totally blow me away like I was hoping--the ambiance and professionalism here is unmatched.

Definitely not a cheap dinner, but is an awesome experience worth checking out if you get the opportunity.

5/5 ambiance, 5/5 service, 5/5 food

Personally one of my favorite restaurants in NYC and deserving of another Michelin star.

I took my girlfriend here for her birthday and was blown away by the treatment. From the moment we stepped into the restaurant all the way until the end, they made her special day ever more special. One of the staff even drew her a personalized birthday card, it was super crafty and a unexpected gesture.

For dinner we had the farmers feast which is the restaurants take on the traditional prix fixe. It includes 6 or so dishes, ranging from pheasant to diver scallops, raw veggies, cooked veggies, etc. Most importantly every dish really captured and exposed the essence of the fresh ingredient, and really embellished the philosophy of farm to table. 

Must tries: 
diver scallops - very fresh scallop, fat and juicy, simple as it gets.
dessert oats - love the texture, once again very simple and text book
bread and butter - laughable but one of my favorite dishes, the butter tasted like it was churned on the spot
Was okays: beet steak - not very amusing 

Shout out the wine curator jason taking our experience to the next level!

How do you review an experience like Blue Hill NYC? It took me months to finally make a reservation when I would be in town, and the meal totally lived up to my expectations ... I think?

I ordered the Farmer's Feast ($108) while my companion ordered the Daily Menu ($95), and in the end the daily menu looked like much more food and arguably a better choice.

Every dish was bold and meticulous. Standouts to me were the carrot steak, or basically the Most Perfect Carrot You'll Ever Eat, and the koginut squash with Maine crab. Some were a bit too loud for me, such as the diver scallop with a very pungent sauerkraut/Borscht-style sauce, while felt like a slight antithesis to the "ingredients-first" approach when I could barely taste the scallop under the vinegar.

It's hard to argue though, that the overall experience was top notch, and frankly very reasonably priced for the city. If tasked to spend ~$100 somewhere in the city for dinner, I would probably pick Blue Hill time and time again. Unfortunately it seems like everyone else has the same idea, so for now I'll just daydream about the next time. And the next ... and the next.
It was everything people say it is. It took a long time to finally make it there. Every course was a delightful surprise. I hope we can return.

Looking for consistency in food and service is not easy. Blue Hill is not the place for" you get what you expect especially on your second visit. " I never had the experience of waiting over 15 mins for second course in a Michelin restaurant but Blue Hill. 

It is quite a disappointing experience at Blue Hill second time. Won't come back again.

Simplistic yet adventurous, upscale yet casual. My experience at blue hill was perfect, I'd definitely come back for their ever changing menu again and again. 

They start off the extended farmers feast (which includes 2 surprise courses) with a tiny carrot and radish with a light dressing. Also a hot pepper made to be sweet was delicious. All from their farm of course. Possibly some of the best vegetables I've ever had. 

Cheese foam was present in a couple dishes. Super light cheesy taste which accompanied the dishes great, without overpowering any ingredient in the course. 

Bread and butter, as everyone else says is absolutely delicious. Crust is perfectly toasted, bread is soft. Drooling just thinking about it. Butter is out of this world. 

Our courses (I may have even forgotten some, they gave us more than what was listed on our menu):
Very thinly sliced potato chips with a fish dill dip: I could eat this dip alone it's amazing. 
Gnocchi: melt in your mouth. 
Diver scallop with red borscht and sauerkraut: huge piece of fresh seafood, interesting dish. If you like scallops, you'll love this.  
Carrot steak: don't know how they managed to do this, but they successfully made a carrot taste like meat.
Various meat cuts: all amazing, tender, high quality, delicious. 
Liver sandwiched between chocolate: prob the most adventurous thing I tasted that night. Delicious though! Thick texture and the chocolate is very thin, crunchy.
Popovers with carrot ketchup (?!): best ketchup I've ever had. In my life. 
Mini Reuben sandwich: so delicious. They substitute the bread with something that kind of tastes like radish...? Either way it's cute and mini and fun to eat. 
Dessert: so interesting and so delicious! It's almost like rolled oats, with nuts and almost melted ice cream. I don't know how else to explain but it was the best darn oatmeal dessert I've ever had. 
Rum cake: also delicious 

The service doesn't make you feel rushed, our meal took about 2.5 hours. They time the courses perfectly, it's amazing to see how passionate these people are when talking about a dish, it makes you even more excited to try it. 

There's a bar area, the liquors are all organic. Extensive wine list as well.

I love!! If you come here you probably have a rough idea of what their whole shtick is with the whole farm to table thing. I did the extended menu and for the first time in my life I was too full from a tasting menu and actually wanted the meal to end sooner. The extended menu gave me one super delicious course (I think it was some liver and chocolate thing) but some questionable experimental ones (some reuben type thing).

Wine was good. Ambiance and atmosphere were good. All the courses were great really and the OATS AT THE END WOW

Spot on.Absolutely phenomenal dishes.Simply delicious.Pricey but worth it.Nice view,Warm and welcoming staff.The ceaser salad was different than we are used to and was amazing.The pastas had different flavors .Although it expensive but it was good value.

I had gone to Blue Hill in Tarrytown, which is possibly the best dining experience I've had in New York. I was really excited about trying the Blue Hill on WSP, which has a price point of around $100/pp for the Farmer's Feast, a third of its price in Tarrytown.

I guess my expectations were a bit too high, as I expected the same level of experimentation and presentation as Tarrytown that simply was not there. The standout dishes were definitely the ones that overlapped--the veggie appetizers in the beginning as well as the liver chocolate (probably one of my favorite things I've eaten ever). However, most of the other dishes were not that memorable and the beat steak in particular I think is a hit or miss. I came with two friends and one loved it while the other didn't, and I understand as it's a very unconventional dish. The desserts were a bit bland although I did enjoy the texture and warmth of the browned meringue.

Although I have mixed feelings about the pre-fixe, the service is exceptional. We had to catch an opera later that night which meant we had to finish a 3-hour dining experience in 2. We finished just in time! I'll definitely be back to try the vegan course. If you can make the trip to Stone Barns I would highly recommend it but for its price point the pre-fixe at this location is worth it--you won't be completely blown away by every dish but you'll still be eating the freshest food.

The most sophisticated restaurant in New York, with food and atmosphere as good as it gets.  The food is just right - delicious, intriguing, and fresh.  The decor is just right - beautifully simple, with low lights.  Atmosphere is sublime but straightforward, serene but with New York energy.  The perfect place to meet for business, a date, and even friends, if you are looking for extraordinary food in a place to take a vacation of the mind, feel taken care of, peaceful, and enjoy the best.

Fresh farm to table + amazing service
Food: 3.75/5
Service: 4.5/5

I came here for a dinner on a Thursday night. The atmosphere is refined but not too formal, good for a date or celebration. I had known the "farm to table" premise of the restaurant and that it was the one-Michelin starred urban counterpart to the renown Blue Hill @ Stone Barns, but not much else. The service was pretty impeccable, and that alone warranted the restaurant's Michelin star.

I had the tasting menu option with three dishes alongside a glass of Rose wine. Before they served the meal they brought out a tiny - no larger than a centimeter - radish that they said was grown in their garden. While the radish was not particularly flavorful, it added a whimsical touch to the meal, which I really appreciated.

For the appetizer, I chose to have the mushroom tartare, which was incredible and, as expected, extremely fresh tasting. For the entrée, I got the beef, which was incredibly chewy. I spent a good portion off my meal attempting to saw my knife through the beef. Eating it was also a struggle due to its chewiness ... perhaps my entrée was just not cooked properly. The flavors, however, were on point. For desert, I had the popcorn ice cream with chocolate chunks. It was the ideal balance of salty and sweet--perfect for those who are not fans of overly sweet desserts. All in all, was a great experience, save the chewiness of the beef.

Good but not great, for the food at least. The service here is what makes this place special, however I don't think the location in West Village does it justice for what we perceive on Chef's Table. 

It's a low lit, intimate and special type of ambiance where they mark on the menu asking politely not to use your phone. 

Also I went here in Feb 2019 - the menu rotates. 

I mentioned that we were celebrating a birthday and a card was waiting on the table after being greeted and handing our jackets to coat check.

When we started our course, we did the pre fix where we'd have chefs complimentary, two starters, an entree and dessert. 

1. Two baby carrots (although the carrots tasted different than regular carrots, I'm not going to lie, being served a carrot that was smaller than supermarket regular carrots made me question my decision to come here). 

2. Chicken Liver between chocolate - surprisingly very flavorful and delicious. Best of the night

3. Hake - the hake was alright, nothing special

4. Squid ink & celery risotto - honestly too salty, the squid ink although interesting was too overpowering to enjoy it fully

5. Lamb - two different cuts. Really strong in lamb taste, not in a good way. I think this might have just not been for me. I normally eat a good amount of Lamb

6. Rolled oats and some vanilla mixture, relatively delicious

For the price that I paid, I don't think I would return $230 for two people, which includes tip.

Also as a side note, they brought in food from the farm which was covered in black garbage bags but clearly animal carcasses, through the main dining room, which I thought was a little odd.

Amazing! I'm vegan and I let them know a couple days ahead a time and they were happy to accommodate. They were honest about not being able to do more than 3 courses, which I appreciated rather than them claiming to do more and serve something mediocre.
This is probably my favorite restaurant in NYC. I've been here a couple of times, and I have been delighted every time. The food and service are great. I feel I got much more than my money worth.

Five years taking the NYC dining scene and 450 venues later, I am reporting on January 22nd 2019, that I officially have a new Favorite Restaurant. Things may change, but as of this date, we have groundbreaking news. Somehow, my soaring high expectations were met and surpassed. I have been a huge Dan Barber fan since his feature on the first season of Chef's Table a few years ago. Farm-to-table is my preferred style of dining and it's not a stretch to say that Chef Barber is the king said genre. In addition to his wildly prestigious West Village spot, he has two farms--one in the Hudson Valley and one in the Berkshires--that he manages meticulously. This is a guy who cares deeply about agriculture and sustainability, and it shines through in his cooking. He prizes quality ingredients over any sort of whimsical cooking technique, and my god does he do a knockout job of it.
