Maureen is the benchmark of how you should interact with customers. Make sure you savor that rye bread. It is REAL rye bread. It will change your life.

An understated, yet sophisticated, "elegant casual" restaurant in the West Village, where even the Obamas have ventured out for date night; the epitome of farm-to-table and local produce cooked with artisanal technique.

Best margarita in the city. Seriously 
Seat at the bar corner and talk to everyone around you. They are all your peeps. And Ben will
Make you happy. Very.

My man and i dined here last friday evening after much anticipation. We both ordered the four course prix-fixe so that we could choose what we wanted. I dont eat red meat, so they allowed me to choose two courses from the second course instead of from the third course section. 

I had the risotto, egg, hake, and coffee dessert-- all were incredibly delicious, and i loved how every food item had a little story. With that being said, my bf and i have very small appetites and usually leave a prix-fixe meal stuffed; however, we left blue hill still hungry and had to stop at the bodega on the way home to buy snacks.

The service was great and i loved the atmosphere of the restaurant. But yes, pricey and very small portions. Enjoyable evening, but i would not return. Maybe one day will make it up to stone barns though!

What happened to Blue Hill??? Years ago I would have rated BH as one of my favorite restaurants in the city. We were pleased to get a table at a reasonable time to celebrate our 10 year anniversary. What a disappointment! First off, this is not the place to go if you don't eat red meat. That was not the case the last time I was here, though to be fair, that was years ago. When they confirmed our reservation, I was asked if anyone had any food allergies/restrictions and I mentioned that I don't eat red meat (but I do eat fish/chicken). This was apparently not an alarm bell for the hostess. 

I started off with a very flavorless mushroom/cauliflower burrito. I wish I had known it was served cold. And that it didn't have flavor. Despite not loving the appetizer (nor did I like my husband's salad), I was still optimistic for the rest of the meal. After all, we had been so happy in the past. 

For the second course we both ordered the egg over asparagus. That was pretty good - very fresh, well cooked and tasty. 

On the main course of the tasting menu they had only meat or a "parsnip steak" (most restaurants will have at least seafood or chicken or maybe even a meatless risotto). When I reminded the waitress that I don't eat red meat, she sold me on the parsnip. I don't love parsnips - I mean, what's to love? - but I figured the chef knew what he was doing. I actually could not eat this course. There was nothing enjoyable about it and for an $85 price/fixe, it's fairly disappointing to have one of the 3 food courses be inedible. 

That said, the service was fantastic (and the cocktails were good). Our waitress did bend over backwards to try to find something to fill me up/replace the unwanted course. Unfortunately she was offering more of the burritos or another egg/asparagus course. She really did try (and the chef clearly did too), and I appreciated that.  We were sent an extra dessert (or maybe two, it was hard to tell), and the dessert was decent enough. I had the cheese plate which was quite good and we tasted the bread pudding (didn't love and have never not loved bread pudding) and the apple tart which my husband liked. 

In my opinion, Blue Hill is teetering on the absurd. I love the farm to table concept, but when we were presented tiny baby carrots as an amuse bouche and encouraged to eat the (foot-long) greens at the end or the 2 inch carrot, it was almost like a caricature of a farm to table NYC restaurant. 

I miss the old Blue Hill. I will not be going back to the new one.

Go here if you dig: The best wait staff ever, food with a mission, a chef with a vision

Order: It's seasonable, but if you're around for the Venison, ooooooh wow, wow wow. 

Special Notes: I had the amazing luck to go to the WastED pop-up too. and I have never had a food experience like that. Best dinner of my whole life. I love Blue Hill in general, but WastED was so passionately charged, really, it was a game changer.
SO GOOD.  The bread is amazing.  Berkshire pig was excellent.  I also got the duck which was cooked perfectly.

Simply amazing. Did the farmers feast with my gf last week. 

The bread and butter was mind blowing. Whipped butter with puff quinoi, white and black sesame seeds. 

Everything was cooked and seasoned perfectly. The flavors were super concentrated like in the veg crackers.  The fresh farmers cheese was delicious. 

Was able to swap out the lamb for pork for my gf. So we were able to taste two meat courses. Both were equally delicious

My least fav dish was the the vegetarian burger with day old egg. The egg didnt taste pasture raised.  Maybe because it was the beginning of spring. The burger was also meh. 

Ordered the first two cocktails on the menu.  A beet juice vodka and a walnut infused bourbon. Both were highly disappointing. The bourbon cocktail just tasted like diluted bourbon. 

Including the birthday cake slice we received 4 courses of desserts.  They were all great. 

Overall, i Highly enjoyed this meal. I especially liked how the servers go into great detail about the ingredients. Dinner took us 3 hours and I enjoyed every minute.

The great service plus the unique and delicious food made my first visit to Blue Hill 5 star worthy. 

Our waiter was extra attentive, friendly, and knowledgable when it came to what to order.  Each course was better than the last and the drinks were unique and paired well with the menu. 

It's clear that the attention to detail and fresh ingredients were a focus at Blue Hill and I'm excited to come back to see what the seasonal menu will look like in the spring!

I can't believe it has taken me this long to write this update, but I only recently looked back into yelp.
Blue Hill contacted my boyfriend within a week of my writing that review and took complete responsibility for our experience.  They invited us in for a complimentary 13-course meal, with 5 wine pairings, in this best table in the house.  The manager apologized in person and met us at the door with champagne in hand.  All was forgiven!  There is nothing better than someone owning up to their mistakes and making amends.

Great food and attentive staff meets Wolf of Wall Street clientele, as cast by middle aged New Yorkers.

I'll start with the few pros: 
1) Really attentive staff; always on point, empathetic, and empowered to help
2) The venison and Berkshire pork entrees my girlfriend and I had were completely delicious and truly impressive dishes. I've never had venison as tender as that and rarely have I had pork that was so rich and tender.

But the cons really diluted the above strengths, and sadly weren't directly the restaurant's fault:

1) The crowd was really, really douchy. Table on the left were clearly over-served alcohol and made loud, obnoxious, and embarrassing comments throughout the evening. Bummer. Then the table on the right was a bitter married couple complaining to each other about their exes. Awkward. Our server comped drinks which was appreciated and kindly re-seated us.
2) The menu that night was obsessed with apples - obviously great if you like apples but a touch overwhelming for those who aren't the biggest of fans.

At the end of the day, I feel that there are many other options that have a similar or better menu but with a much more convivial atmosphere/clientele.

On the other hand, if you're 50+ and really identified with DiCaprio's character from Wolf of Wall Street, Blue Hill might just be the ideal venue for your next boozy, debaucherous dinner!

Beyond. Clever yet simple. The knowledge of food + the creative combinations is pretty stunning. Fresh organic everything right from the farm. And if you REALLY want a life-altering food experience, go to Blue Hill Farm. Like an edible Museum of Food.

3.5 Blue Hill was not as good I had hoped or was told it'd be. Perhaps it was an off day. I left wondering how the Michelin star was earned. On the other hand, the service was fairly good and the restaurant itself had a nice ambiance.

The plating and concept of the dishes were fun and/or fresh, but we didn't eat anything that really blew my mind. Actually, that's a bit of a euphemism... The food left a lot to be desired. 

In my party of two, we had three starters, two entrees and two desserts. We had a bottle of wine to go along with our dinner and my date also had two beers at the onset of the meal. The appetizers were the highlight of our experience. The chick pea fries (arranged like Jenga) were delicious and I thought the micro-vegetables presented on a wooden plank of nails were neat to look at. My meat-loving companion was advised to order the "vegetable steak" because in our helpful waitress' opinion, it was delicious. After a few bites, my date was very, very, sad that he had been recommended this dish. My entree, a pork dish, was fine, but nothing spectacular. 

I'd be open to giving this restaurant another try but not on my own account. 

Tips:
Not very many vegetarian options.
Make reservations. This place is popular so if you can't get a reservation on the desired date or time, try a premium credit card concierge service (offered by many companies).
Great atmosphere for an intimate date.

Went to Blue Hill in Greenwich Village to celebrate my wedding anniversary. For my surprise they have few and mediocre vegetarian options in their tasting menu. Waitress spent the whole evening talking to us at the table. She told us all about her, where she went to school, what are her interests in food, etc. At the end, she asked for my husband's business card to send him some information about cooking classes at their upstate restaurant. He gave  her my contact information. It has been already a month and she never wrote to me. I wonder why.... Totally annoying experience. Would never go back.

This is most definitely one of the best meals I've ever had in New York. 

We were two people and each had the smaller of the two tasting menus. For me, that was enough food for sure. The food was very unique, prepared very well, and beautiful. I also appreciated how our server was able to tell us so much about the origin of the food. I'm not usually one to ask about where my vegetables come from, but if offered intriguing information by my server, I'd absolutely take them up on it. Blue Hill does a great job showing you how your food gets to you. 

Service was spectacular, I loved my drinks...ambiance was beautiful and perfect for going out with your significant other or a few friends. I also loved that the space wasn't loud. I feel like an old man sometimes, but I often just want a relaxing place to have dinner where I don't have to shout over loud music or screaming patrons. This place was great for some relaxation.

5 stars. I'll be back. It was great.

Never have I paid so much for so little. Was it high quality? Yes. Was it served in an elegant manner? Yes. (Well, maybe not the "egg of the day" course which came in a miniature nest. Srsly.) Was the ambience warm and inviting? Yes. But what about the children? Where are they in all this? No one knows. This is the place to go after hitting the Powerball or if you need to impress some high class broad.

Ooops!  My friend mistakenly thought this place was participating in Restaurant Week when he made a reservation for us last Friday night.  Not a chance--they don't need the business. The place was packed at 9:30 PM when we arrived.  It was an amazing dining experience despite the sticker shock, and the manager comped us a glass of wine after seeing our discomfort at the mistake.  The food was very unusual as well as being delicious.  The service was absolutely top notch, even if our waiter wasn't particularly friendly (but knowledgeable and efficient).  It will certainly be a future special occasion restaurant for us.

I'll start by saying I've dined at Blue Hill before on two occasions and both times were  4 1/2 - 5 star dining experiences. That being said, last evening I attended Blue Hill for a special occasion and was very disappointed in the quality of service/attentiveness of the waitstaff (this does not discount the meal itself, which was excellent, as expected).
Our reservation was for 830pm and we were promptly seated. It took almost ten minutes for our server to come to the table to take a drink order and then we didn't get our drinks until 9pm, after our food had been served. I understand that there are times when the bar/kitchen is backed up, but it is the server's job to communicate this to the customers. I truly hope this was a one-time thing as I was planning on visiting the farm when the weather gets better.

An experience at Blue Hill is like an Octopus' Garden in the shade- a mysterious, warm and magical experience that makes you wonder why you never liked vegetables growing up. As if the decor and the ambiance aren't enough...the entire staff from the chef, to the General Manager, to the servers are outstanding. We had a tasting that went on for hours and I never wanted it to end. Their farm to table cuisine is unlike most that you would have in New York- even after a glorious feast of various vegetable concoctions, farm meats and cheeses AND succulent deserts, you still don't feel like you want to crawl into bed from being so full. It's nourishing, complex and mind-blowingly delicious. Can't wait to go back!
Incredible chefs tasting menu. I will never forget it. Probably the best farm to table menu in Manhattan.

This meal was exquisite in every regard, and unlike any I've ever had.

My wife likes to send us to these locavore restaurants. The sincerity is never in doubt, though these meals tend to be more memorable for the self-importance than the food.

The cynic in me was eager to surmise the same about Blue Hill, when our waiter, bearded in the au courant style, started our meal with a pair of spindly-looking raw carrots. But that turned out to be the best, most interesting carrot I ever ate. 

Likewise, each of the six courses in our tasting menu was not just delicious, but also surprising in terms of the flavors and textures. We were left saying to each other "I didn't know X could taste like that." The veal, from the restaurant's own farm, was the best I've ever had.

Truly wonderful all around.

Outstanding food in a nice, quiet ambiance.

I stopped by with two friends for one of their birthdays on a weekend evening, and we enjoyed a fantastic meal. We ordered the farmer's feast tasting menu, which was highlighted by several great dishes---we enjoyed a dish with the 898 squash, a unique smaller, sweeter squash which was delicious and went great with the bolognese and ricotta, the morning's farm egg, and the lamb and beef. The lamb in particular was the best lamb dish I've ever had, so well-prepared and tender. My cocktail was also great (the Sweater Weather), which came recommended by our waitstaff.

The service was also very nice throughout, and it's a nice place for a meal with quiet conversation. I would definitely recommend it as a great meal for smaller groups for special occasions.

I loved everything about this dining experience except for the hair in my granola. The staff replaced the item very promptly with apologies, but I paid the full price. I'm sorry, but this is upscale dining and they should have done better.

"Wonderful experience - delightful ambiance"
IMPORTANT: make your reservation 2 months in advance, especially if you have 4 or more in your party. 

The restaurant was a true delight - with just a few reservations. The food was incomparably fresh - the dishes wonderful. The chilled corn soup (first course) is probably the top offering - and should not be missed. It does not taste like anything - and certainly not like any corn chowder or soup - you've ever enjoyed before. It is marvelous. The braised Cod's Head is really wonderful - but you must "understand" what you are enjoying - if you don't know that the cheek is the prize - and aren't able to maneuver your utensils - the joy will be missed. Re entrees - The Lamb is well known - and with reason. It was delightful and the amount served was "just right" - not overwhelming. My husband ordered the "Freedom Ranger Chicken" - and was somewhat disappointed in that it was clearly undercooked and quite pink in the center. As we were with friends - he said nothing, ate around the edges of each slice (avoiding the center) and declared it quite good and perfectly seasoned. The Milk Fed Pig is also quite good - though if you are expecting an astounding dining experience - this isn't it. Just a very good very well prepared dish with the freshest of ingredients. Our group shared a "platter" of bite sized deserts - cakes and chocolates - and while delightful to share and end our meal on a sweet note - again - this was nothing particularly memorable. 

In addition - the staff - while offering outstanding and attentive, friendly, service - was indeed clearly watching the clock and the need for our table. We were responsible and did not dawdle at all - understanding their need. Still, it was noticeable that they were interested in getting us in, served and out... 

An extremely good value for the meal. I would definitely recommend Blue Hill - - particularly if taking friends - you can be assured of a great evening in an atmosphere that is not noisy where you can talk, and laugh, and enjoy your experience.

Yeah, I did it...I can't say I lived a five minute walk away for the last four years and never made an attempt to eat here can I?!  I think everyone would agree no.

I'm not going to give a run down of every dish, but I will say the extended farmer's feast is worth the price tag.  Actually, if there are two of you and you're looking for variety, the extended farmer's feast and the regular prix fixe is a solid combination.

The dinner is long, extended farmer feast will take you around 3 hours, but it never feels like you're waiting too long for a course.  The thing that impressed me most, the complexity of the flavors in a lot of these dishes, some of the combinations just work really well.  Go ahead and splurge, it's worth it!

I have wanted to try this place since I saw it 2 years ago on the food channel. It's prefixe and perhaps because of the season the options weren't the most interesting. Each dish tasted similar to the next sadly what I loved most was dessert and a very interesting pislner beer (dark malts I suspect. Wish I remembered the name) don't get me wrong the food was good, ingredients were fresh, I'm glad I went but would I go back. . .maybe, I would have to check the menu first.  Oh and we were a bit late for our reservation and almost lost a $400 deposit but it was a Monday. Thank god!

Saturday night review...

Started off with two cocktails...the gin and the rum cocktails. Both were very good and recommend trying. I think they were 15 each.

There were a few appetizers courtesy of the chef. One was a Jerusalem artichoke with peanut...best bite I had all year. It was warm, soft, and full of flavor. Was a very unexpected bite.

My wife and I got the farmers feast. She had the vegetarian version. I'm not a big fan of scallops, so I asked if I could substitute for something else, and it was no problem. The beef and hazelnut was a yummy combination. The only courses that we felt could have been eliminated all together with no overall effect to the meal was the farmers egg dish and the oatmeal. I didn't understand the oatmeal dish...just tasted like breakfast after eating dinner. The cranberry dessert was fantastic though. My wife liked the carrot steak and we had golden beets and cauliflower appetizers...both great.

The restaurant was very nice and staff all great. Well definetely be back again. Thanks :)

Food and service is over rated 
I went for dinner with my friend 
She reserved it through open table
She had special instruction of her diet.
Server didn't get the information and served her things that she doesn't eat.(vegetarian) 
The salad was good 
Service was fair      
Nothing special.

One of my favorite New York City meals. Can't wait to visit their upstate farm. Seasonal, local, cocktail pairings are spot on, proteins raised right...veggies on a fence.. This is a special meal so go on a special occasion. Memorable food 5 stars

My husband and I went to Blue Hill for a night out, and we were not disappointed.  We first heard about the restaurant through Dan Barber's book, The Third Plate, and we wanted to check out the restaurant for ourselves and have the farm-to-table experience.  Everything from the food to the drinks to the service to the ambiance was five stars!
Most delightful waitress in NY. Seriously, she was spot on with suggestions. Never before have I had a black carrot cutlet, by oh wow! It was amazing. Charming farm-to-table splendor.

Any other black, hispanic, or asian people experience discrimination here? The food was good here, but on the night that I came, it seemed very strange to me to be seated in the back corner of this restaurant when there were many open tables near the front and center of the room (note that my party of 2 had a reservation and was even there early). While eating, I couldn't help notice that the other tables next to me were people of color (black, hispanic, and asian). I felt like I was in some bizarre world where segregation was still in place, and it really is hard to believe it was coincidence that the 5 tables out of 20+ in the room with minorities were all in the back corner. I've heard of some restaurants doing similar "seating discrimination" practices, but did anyone else experience this?

My prior dinner at Blue Hill at Stone Barns was one of the worst dining experiences I've had to date [1], so the last thing I expected was to visit the Blue Hill location in Manhattan. To be fair, the decision to arrive at Dan Barber's one Michelin starred, New American restaurant hadn't been in my hands, but I was hesitant, to say the least, about what would come out of the kitchen.

Located just off of Washington Square Park, Blue Hill may not be the most well-windowed restaurant in the area, but there's a certain elegance that the space commands, evident in the dark plush seats and the immaculately set, perfectly spaced tables. We were promptly greeted and given an overview of the menu; unlike Stone Barns, Blue Hill has a four-course prix fixe, a six-course Farmer's Feast... and the bottom of the menu has a small note, inviting guests to try the Extended Version of the Farmer's Feast. Upon learning that it involved an additional two courses of the chef's choosing, the final decision to go with a total of eight courses was made.

After a few amuses, we were served a chilled plate of Blue Hill Farm Tomatoes. The tomatoes had been sliced and dusted with basil seeds, and were set on a light, perfectly acidic gazpacho. Each tomato was ripe and incredibly packed with flavor, but we were both enthralled with the "smoked cloud", a gelatinous creation that had the lightness and texture of silken tofu, but was somehow infused with a tomato taste. The dish that followed was another delight, a plate that featured Montauk Lobster over a "corn chowder". The chowder was almost overflowing with sweet, plump corn kernels, and the interspersed pieces of shrimp and clam added a unique brininess to each spoonful. With the finish of a juicy, seared portion of lobster, it was yet another piece of evidence that including seafood into my diet in the last year or two was the correct decision.

And then, a Zucchini Carbonara, which took strands of the vegetable as the pasta and melded in three generous cuts of bacon, Parmesan cheese, and a barely cooked egg yolk. The resulting bites were savory, crisp, and rich, without being unnecessarily heavy. The course that followed was the first of the extended menu: a Ricotta Gnocchi complemented by a few tart halves of cherry tomato and a drizzle of balsamic. The gnocchi was soft and pillowy, the ricotta cheese present in just the right amount to give it a little tang. With the balancing acidity in the tomatoes and balsamic, it was an innovative take on the traditional pasta. And the second dish of the extended menu featured a lightly seared cut of poussin paired with crisp haricot verts and a light horseradish-based sauce. The protein remained tender despite the crisp skin, and the additional texture from the haricots verts and an element of creaminess from the sauce made for a complete dish.

A final savory plate featuring various cuts of pork (loin, stomach, shoulder, leg) with grilled cantaloupe, plum, and roasted pepper slices demonstrated how a successful pairing of sweet and savory should be executed. Unlike my prior meal at Stone Barns, this dish was perfectly seasoned and the pork was cooked to the right consistency and tenderness. The meal ended on two sweet notes; the first, a  simple concoction of macerated blueberries in honey, topped with a yogurt sorbet, followed by scoop of cocoa nibs ice cream plated on top of chocolate cake and chopped strawberry.

I'm grateful I got a second stab at Blue Hill, as I can at least personally vouch for the Greenwich Village location. It's more suitable for a more formal occasion, as I believe we were some of the youngest diners seated that evening, but our server was one of the most considerate I have yet to encounter [2]. And when all the necessary elements of a memorable dining experience align... what additional reasons do you need?
--
[1] http://www.yelp.com/biz/blue-hill-at-stone-barns-pocantico-hills?hrid=T1C1e5rLZKT5lY7ofCnpDw
[2] She complemented my companion on his bouquet selection, and offered to keep it in water during the course of our meal.

What an incredible find. The food is fresh and thoughtfully prepared. I enjoyed it being a set menu where you could select from several options. I tried foods I would not have normally selected. The risotto was my favorite. I cannot wait to return on my next trip.

Visiting from the West Coast, we were sent here for a 40th birthday gift. Wow. Wow. Extended Farmers Feast was amazing. Every single bite was packed with flavor! Every bite was intense, and normally tastings leave me hungry, but we almost couldn't finish the last 2 courses except that they were so amazingly good how could we not. Our server was so incredibly knowledgeable about everything! The staff was on top of it...almost read our minds a few times! Highly highly recommend it. Best dining experience hands down.

Prepare to be wowed!!! My husband and I recently came here for my birthday, and it was simply amazing! I don't think there is any place where you can get a comparable experience in NYC - the farm fresh ingredients are a cut above, and everything is prepared with creativity, care and perfection. I mean, they somehow even managed to make eating a fennel frond an amazing experience! I also love the realistic and creative categories on their wine menu: "Ripe & Luscious", anyone?

My husband and I both got the extended Farmer's Feast and everything was incredible. Looking back, I probably could have done with just the Farmer's Feast but we managed to eat absolutely every morsel of food over the course of three hours.  A big highlight was the farm fresh egg in a skillet, and I must say that my whole understanding and appreciation of beans has skyrocketed.  I also must compliment the wait staff for being so effortlessly warm and professional, and genuinely excited about the the food they are serving. I was also surprised and impressed by the diversity of the staff. At one point we had about four people waiting on us at once, and it was like United Colors of Benetton - but with squash!

Tip: If you are interested in a more intimate experience, ask for a "quiet table" and they will seat you in the back room past the kitchen.

Blue Hill is truly incredible. The service is top notch, the atmosphere romantic, the food incredible... Can't say much more than just go and enjoy. Everything about this place is unique. Oh, and budget 3 hours, or so, for your dinner.
Had a great meal with great service. I am vegetarian and was very pleased by the menu options. Great drink pairings. Priced on point. We had a very romantic leisurely meal!

Blue Hill is reverential about vegetables.....the restaurant is really low-key in lighting, color palette and attitude.   Servers have zero pretension and are really knowledgeable about the food preparation.  We got two of the 5-course Farmer's Feast and they were more than happy to substitute another meat course for my husband so we could try two different ones.  Each dish was wonderful and the wine pairings by the glass we got were superb choices by the staff.  The meal starts with simple, unadorned vegetables with some light dip or garnish and the purity of the ingredients just gets better and better.  Instead of chocolates or petits four, the meal is finished with two beautiful miniature bunches of grapes. Definitely an lovely experience albeit an expensive one.

Perfectly executed vegetarian dishes and heavenly dessert.  Who knew an apple or a quince for desset could be so amazingly satisfying?? The space is lovely and the staff are attentive and wonderful.  Wasn't a huge fan of the meat dishes.  Must orders are the cauliflower, the risotto, the beets and the carrot cutlets.

From start to finish, this was a fantastic meal. The hostess was kind and attentive, our waiter was knowledgeable, and great in conversation about the background on the restaurant, his experience and passion for what Dan Barber & co are doing with Blue Hill and the farm.  We each ordered the four course Daily Menu. Highlights were definitely the wreckfish with manhattan chowder, Daily Egg, stone barns chicken and most importantly the burrata ice cream with tomatoes for dessert--it was truly delicious and something I have never had before.  There were small bites throughout the meal, ranging from fresh vegetables perfectly seasoned with salt, to a bell pepper sorbet that was delicious, and very interesting.  The cocktails were well curated, and wine list extensive (our waiter was extremely helpful here). Perfect experience for our anniversary.

had dinner at blue hill friday evening.service was impeccable.food,while different, was good,not great . my biggest complaint concerns the table placement. remove a few.having spent over $300 for two,i really don't enjoy. sharing my meal with complete strangers. the closeness will preclude me from returning

Extraordinarily disappointing, on nearly every front. My girlfriend and I are easy going so usually we find the best in every situation...this was a tough one.

I'm usually not the best at this (planning special dinners in the city) so often I rely on sites like Yelp to guide me. It was my girlfriend's birthday and the reviews for Blue Hill were exceptional. It seemed like an easy choice. 

We arrived on time and were promptly seated at a great table, where we sat for over 10 minutes before being approached by our less than interested waiter. I ordered the farm tasting and my girlfriend the daily menu. We received a few pallet cleansing dishes, especially loved the tomato burger. From then on it was all down hill. Partially the kitchens fault but it mostly fell on service.

The Zucchini was lifeless, although I faired a bit better. But most disappointing, both of our entrees (veal and pig) came to us stone cold. I'm going to guess this restaurant doesn't use heat lamps so this likely falls on the expediter and our waiter. We sat for what seemed an eternity before our waiter approached our table (he was usually no where to be found). When we told him, he offered to replace the dishes. Normally we would agree but at this point we were nearly 2.5 hours into our seating and were getting tired so given the pace we just asked for our desserts. 

Side Note: an hour and a half into our dinner we noted other tables getting bags of what looked like, amazing bread...we never got one. Also, the waiter was told by me it was my girlfriend's B-day. Based on the nearly 5 candled desserts placed at other tables while we were seated I knew they could accommodate something. It never happened.

We received our bill and expected an adjustment or at least a comped after dinner drink. There was none. We paid and left our 3 hour adventure.

Given the reviews I'm sure, and hopeful that our experience was isolated. We are very easy to please and rarely make a fuss. Unfortunately I feel compelled to write this review. Sadly, we won't be returning or recommending.

PS...we loved the wine!

One of my favorite restaurants in New York. Did the farmer's feast (which is definitely worth every penny). Every course had an amazing blend of flavors and textures all the while tasting fresh and delicious. Ambiance and service were great as well. Will definitely be coming back.

Each course was better than the last, ending heavenly with dessert. Service was amazingly on point yet never stiff or aloof, on the contrary, our server was very friendly and even offered more bread (a giant plus in my book). When I was picking a drink she asked what I flavors I was looking for and she had the bartender make me a custom concoction which was wonderful. 

What I love most is that executive Chef Dan Barber is dedicated to making TRUE farm-to-table accessible to us inner city folks. It's a noble yet difficult high road in the land of fine dining. He wants to educate people as to what it means for the seasons to dictate what ingredients are available to the restaurant. The whole idea of supply and demand and farm to table is eye opening. He can get me excited about crop rotations! Now all that talk about sustainability is great but what I care about most is how the food tastes. I came to taste his theory and I had the farm salad and gain soup which is exactly what he said, sustainable and delicious. 

Next time I come in I'll have the Farmer's Feast. I'd love to come here four times a year, more than that if I was richer, because the menu is ever changing like the city it is situated in, it is never boring.

I've been wanting to come here for awhile, and I finally got decent reservations.  I think this is a fantastic restaurant.  Service was friendly and professional and the food was fantastic.  It is expensive but I think it's worth it.  All the food, both what we ordered and those 'extra tastes' were delicious and perfectly prepared.  The menu changes a lot an I hope to try it during different seasons.

A delightful and natural-feeling dinner with a beautiful, intimate decor. There are some great dishes here with am earthy vibe that I was surprised to enjoy so much.

Although I'd think every dish has great quality, the curried zucchini and almonds stands well above the other first course options.

Blue Hill is a great one Michelin star spot close to Washington Square Park. I enjoyed it a good deal.

I ordered the Farmer's Feast tasting menu which included the following:

1) Blue Hill farm tomatoes - Not much to say about this. It's good but you are just eating a few cherry and heirloom tomatoes with a nice vinegar.

2) Lobster chowder - This was pretty good but was easy to eat up in a few bites.

3) Zucchini Carbonara - I loved this. Anything carbonara is a star for me.

4) Stone Barns pig - I thought this was OK, I wasn't the biggest fan of the texture but the flavor was good.

5) Some sorbet - Loved this. Came with yogurt and honey which ruled.

6) Chocolate cake and strawberries - Nothing particularly impressive about this one.

In total, this tasting menu took us almost 3 hours. 

I think if you are up for a great, intimate and creative type restaurant, I recommend coming here. Service is excellent. I think this doesn't yet deserve 5 stars because the food just isn't totally memorable compared to many other Michelin stars out there. There needs to be some sort of kick, special dish, or something that makes this place stand out and I just didn't see it this time around. I need to come back again and see if I could be wrong. Otherwise, I definitely recommend trying this out and maybe proving me wrong.

I cannot say enough good things about this place.
It was such an amazing experience!!

My boyfriend and I celebrated my birthday last night here and it was just beyond words as to how wonderful everything was.

We went for the extended tasting menu where the chef picks (2) additional dishes for us. The food was soo good and everyone stopped by the table to ask how everything was. They also offer a series of mocktails for people who do not drink which was awesome since I am not a heavy drinker. Just be sure to ask your server for the selections they are offering.

Each course was brought out in a very timely fashion with someone at the end always watching to clean up the table and reset again for the next course.  I could see all around me, people were celebrating birthdays and anniversaries, and this was definitely the perfect restaurant to do so. 

At the end of the meal when dessert was being brought out, they gave me a small birthday cake with a candle to help me celebrate. It was such a nice gesture. 

I loved the entire experience that I had there and would highly recommend this place to anyone.

Very good experience. This a place to go when not in a rush. Service is fine but because it is several courses they tend not to rush you, which is good. You are paying a good amount so take your time and enjoy the meal. Highlights are the vegetables. Each one so fresh you feel like its just been plucked from the earth. All the meat is very good too but some was not perfect duck was slightly too fatty and the pork loin was a bit too cold and tough. Those are the only real complaints. Wine list is fantastic. Beats with plum were amazing! Same for the zucchini! Great for a special occasion or just a really solid meal.

One of my girls tricked me into coming here by forgetting to tell me it was a tasting menu kinda deal. She was leaving to Singapore, so I sucked it up and took it like a champ.

The DUCK!!!! Duck, duck, goose!!! My mouth exploded with flavor and it was worth every dollar.

Ya I'd come back. Probably better with family. It's definitely a nice family dinner kinda place.

Price: $$$$
Food: DELICIOUS.
Ambiance: nice/upscale feel.

Food is really good. There's no ifs or buts about it. As most reviewers commented, the portion does seem small when it comes out. But since you're having a full 3 course meal, it fills you up nicely. I'm a fan of this place, but wouldn't go too often because it's just too pricey. 

As for the dessert, I would go with "peaches" or "cheesecake" next time. Didn't enjoy the "hazelnut" much.

After having eaten at Stone Barns I thought this place would never live up to that.  WRONG!  It was sooooo good and much more affordable.  I love them both but being as this is much more convenient to where I live, I have to give it the props is so richly deserves.  Thank you blue hill!

Amazing. Went back for my birthday with the suitor.  Requested Madeline, she was attentive and friendly and shared great information about each course.  Sat in the garden room - tiny and cozy - if it's just two of you, sit there.  The food was incredible, the experience was top flight, and we did not want to leave.  We will be back!

Dinner here during vacation in city.
Sat out back on patio which was quiet.  We wondered if we had been ushered out of sight but one couple got engaged, another were celebrating anniversary and yet another a birthday, so we felt special.
Service was great.  Friendly and knowledgable.
We both had tasting menu.  
Food included curried zucchini and almonds
Inman Ranch beef and head of pig.
Great amuse Bouches delivered including the fantastic tiny tomato sliders.
Overall, 3 hours that were thoroughly enjoyable.
Also visited the upstate farm connected to the restaurant.  Worth the trip.

I ate here about 3 weeks ago and was literally blown away by both the service AND food!  I arrived around 6pm, without reservations, with a small food allergy, and only a hour to dine.  Yes, I was one of "those" people I hate that fine evening!.  The staff was super helpful (well beyond my expectations), they organized the tasting menu to come out in exactly 1 hour time, they took care of my allergy towards Night Shades (yes, it does suck), and set me down right at the bar as I requested (I don't need a table for 1 :) ).  I love farm to table, I suppose you could even call this seed to table, and this place did not disappoint.  The food was simply amazing, everything was very fresh and flavorful.  Price was very appropriate, dare I say a good deal for NYC.  I will be coming back with my wife sometime soon.  She's already looking forward to it!

My new favorite restaurant. There are so many reasons to love this place. First, they are directly attached to a farm very close to NYC. We actually went to visit the farm the day before eating here. It is a beautiful and picturesque place, and only a 35 min trip via express train!
I have a ton of dietary restrictions, including no dairy, gluten or soy to name a few. They completely accommodated me, and never once did I feel as though I was missing out. Their chefs are creative and knowledgeable, and their staff is incredibly hospitable. The menu changes often depending on what is available via the farm, local, organic, etc. They even had a really delightful white wine from Long Island, NY.

Can not wait to return to NY to experience this amazing restaurant again.

I don't have a bad thing to say about my experience here. Brought my boyfriend for his birthday dinner last night, had asked for a quiet, romantic table - done. The overall ambiance is relaxing and low key. Our server was an absolute joy.
I'm vegan so they made sure to alter the dishes for me and each course was excellent. My carnivorous boyfriend enjoyed the duck and the beef. They brought out a little birthday treat for him at the end, subtle, like I had asked. 
We had a wonderful time and I would definitely go back. Very much worth the money for such a fabulous dining experience.

Went for a late dinner after a show. Live nearby but had never been. Decor is low key , located in basement of townhouse. Would expect it to be noisy but was easy to have a conversation despite the fact that all tables were full.
Menu has two separate prix fixe options. We had the four course option which was perfect. Portions are just right. The farm pig was really unique with different cuts of pork. Farm fresh egg was also tasty. 
Service was friendly and knowledgeable. Can't wait to return.

A great choice for special events.  Staff are always charming and welcoming.  I still remember "Tri-Sarah-Tops" engaging my 5-year old daughter and leaving a permanent impression.  In contrast to Blue Hill Stone Barns, the city location offers less of a commitment but a comparable menu.  Presentation of the amuse bouche is outstanding and reaffirms their commitment to farm-to-table.  Dishes are impeccable, simple, and honest.  Sense of welcome absolute - twice my daughter has left the table to venture to the kitchen to prepare her dessert!

Mixture of both pre-fixe (daily and farmer's feast)
Curried zucchini and almonds with sunflower seeds and vegetable broth
Artichokes with fava beans, chanterelle mushrooms and corn
Smoked eggplant and sesame 
Summer bean bundles with fennel and licorice cream, toasted almonds
Red wine and moscato sorbet
Mini tomato burger 
Trio sorbet - strawberry, mint, and pistachio 
Baby okra 

All the food was great as any fine dining that serves vegan food is. The one thing that stood out to me the most was their pistachio sorbet. I thought it was chocolate ice cream initially! The texture was so fluffy and the color was dark beige. The pistachio taste kicks in at the end of your spoon. 

Ambiance/seating - it wasn't as big as I expected; it's mainly paired seating and you have to move the table around to sit. There were a lot of couples here so I would recommend this to be a date spot. 

The staff is very social and nice. 

Water service - they were on top of it!
Bread service - they kept asking if I wanted more...I couldn't say no! It came with garlic and olive oil. Yum Yum!

Bathroom - super clean! They provide lotion too! They also have the super soft napkins to dry your hands after a nice wash with their hand soap. I think they make it themselves.

Very good and quite accommodating to different dietary needs (called me a day before to ask about them). When I ate here, I was gluten free and am always vegetarian, and they were good about being attentive to this. However, options were definitely limited as a result of this. Vegetarian options felt like a lot less than many other tasting places, and at this price, you don't want to feel like it's almost an after thought.

Drinks were terrific and strong, all food presented beautifully, and the multiple dessert courses phenomenal. Cauliflower "steak" was good, but not a huge portion - I get that it's a tasting menu, but as stated above, I've had other tasting menus that just felt like more thought went into them. Did love, however, that the food was locally sourced.

The prix fixe and tasting menus change quite often, so writing about the specifics of the dinner I had here a month ago wouldn't be so useful, but I will say that everything about it was perfect. Really! Perfect. 

The staff was attentive, engaging, and really just charming. Even their vests, ties, and aprons were so lovely. The dining room was sophisticated, without being stuffy or pretentious. 

The "daily menu" prix fixe allows you to choose three different courses (a light vegetable-heavy appetizer, a heartier item, and an entrée) and a dessert on top of that. My first salad was like a dream! It was plated in such an artful way, and the dressing only enhanced the fresh flavors of the raw vegetables. I like salads, but this one was a staircase full of steps above the rest. While Blue Hill may specialize in using quality fresh vegetables, its non-vegetarian dishes were just as fantastic. From J's pork ("I think this is the best pork I've ever eaten") to my chicken, everything was prepared with so much care and precision. Nothing, and I mean nothing, was dry or too fatty or under-seasoned. 

One thing that really left an impression on me was the wine list. I couldn't really tell if there were a lot of varieties, but I do know that the way that the wine list was organized was so informative and really quite creative! Wine lists are often divided by country and region, but this wine list divided everything into wine descriptors - there was a page of "fruit forward and tropical whites", of "petrol and stonefruit whites", "light and fruity reds", "ripe and luscious reds", and so on and so forth. I find that people usually have the flavor they want in mind, so this list is sure to be helpful. It also makes wines less daunting for those who aren't all too familiar with them.


Likelihood of another visit:
So likely!!

I've heard mixed things about the Blue Hill at Stone Barns, but I'm sure the ambiance is nice enough that it would be worth it. I just have to find a car...and some money...

It is a rare occasion when everything comes so perfectly together as it did tonight at Blue Hill. Staff, food, wine, music & friends were   absolutely  the greatest. Will be back more often. Btw. Plenty of food on every plate and oh solo good

Food: delicious
Wine: outrageously marked up by 400% versus retail
Service: very good, not snobby
Other diners: terrible
It's too bad there's no way for restaurants to screen for customers who will make their fellow diners miserable. I took my boyfriend here for his birthday. Waitress was lovely and down to earth and helpful (some of her colleagues a bit less so--they placed the dessert with birthday candle in front of me despite my telling them clearly ahead of time that it was his birthday), food was excellent, but the people next to us (evidently way too close to us--really wish the tables were further apart) were awful. We had to listen to this blowhard talk about his low carb diet for 80% of the mealtime. It was insufferable and try as we might to ignore them, they negatively impacted our experience.

Really a wonderful meal and overall experience.  I went with my vegan parents and omnivore boyfriend and they were really kind to us, informing us of our options and substitutions from the menu. The dishes were incredibly flavorful, creative, and beautiful plated. Every ingredient tasted incredibly fresh and impeccably prepared. The service was definitely "fine dining" without being stuffy. It is a long meal, ours was 3 hours, so be prepared for that. My dad and boyfriend did comment on the small portions, but guess what... We all left full, so that really wasn't an issue.
I've never had the same thing to eat when I come here, and no matter what I get it's always amazing. Keep it up blue hill

Wow....who knew pork fat could be rendered into a delightful spread!  Perfect balance of flavors, mild enough to taste the food but not bland as to blend into one another.  Gotta leave it at that, too much talk will ruin the experience.

I been looking forward to this place for over an year and finally got a chance to go few weeks ago. Sadly I have already forgotten what I ate. Food and quality is for sure superb but I would say it lacks a bit of creativity. For similar prix fix menus I'd rather goto Jungsik, Aquavit or Marea.

Had a wonderful dining experience with my mother.  We chose the four course menu because we liked that we could each pick different dishes so we could try a bunch of things.  We were blown away by the pea/white chocolate puree that they served with crackers to start.  We started with the rotation salad and the asparagus with beet yogurt followed by the purple potato gnocchi and the hake and for entrees we chose the pork and the cornish hen.  Lets not forget to mention the chcoloate and rhubarb desserts that we had.  All the dishes were so fresh and tasted to perfection.  The service was immpecable.  I was throughly impressed that I receieved a Thank You note in the mail from the restaurant  for dining with them.  I highly recommend this restaurant.  I look forward to getting up to Westchester to try their signature location this summer.

The warm and welcoming staff made the delicious food and lovely ambiance all the more enjoyable. They made a very special day for us all the more memorable, and I can not wait to come here again. Hands down the best dining experience in NYC.
Kinda stuffy, and uber expensive for what you get. But, the food is totally legit. I suggest going here on someone else's dime.

This was my first visit to Blue Hill and I immediately noticed that the staff is very friendly, talkative and welcoming. I started the visit with the Bumble and Bee drink, which was a nice gin and lemon marmalade cocktail. 

For food, I did the 4 course. As a vegetarian, my main concern was getting solid options. Our waiter and staff were very conscious of my dietary restrictions and had items on the menu that I could eat or modify to be meat free. The waiter was extremely knowledgeable of all the ingredients in their food. 

They started us off with some bread and vegetable crackers with peas puree. 
My first item was the rotation salad, a refreshing salad with nuts and cucumber slices. This was followed by the Purple Potato Gnocchi. The gnocchi was soft and delicious. Next, I had the Parsnip Steak (not beef), which was savory with a slight sweet taste. Finally, for desert, I had the Chocolate Hazel Nut bar, which was a crunch bar topped with chocolate and ice cream. 

Overall, it was obvious that all the food was carefully crafted. I was especially impressed with their ability to cater to my vegetarian diet.

An amazing meal.

I celebrated my 2 year anniversary with my fiancé at Blue Hill.  I had heard about it from friends and knew it was highly reviewed/rated on Yelp and other sites.  I also heard that the restaurant caters to vegetarians.

We had a 5:30pm reservation (quite early) and promptly arrived then.  We were seated in the corner booth area.  I ordered a mescal drink with grapefruit which was as smoky and delicious as it should be including a white wine from North Fork.  

We ordered from the $78 menu.  My boyfriend had the halibut, beet frankfurter, and the pig II.  I had the goose egg noodles (so tasty and fresh), this morning's farm egg, and the parsnip steak (vegetarian of course).  For dessert, they gave us madelines with rhubarb jam, our orders of the rhubarb cheesecake and hazelnut cake, including a small chocolate mousse on the side for our anniversary.

The service was impeccable, the space welcoming and overall a delicious meal.  I love the "speakeasy" type of feel to the restaurant including the bathroom!

Will be back, for sure.
Tooo slowwww. We paid too much money to wait for hours. The food was excellent though. The maitre d was kind about the problem though

Probably the best meal we had during our most recent visit to NYC.  The farm-to-table approach is flawlessly done.  The restaurant itself is a haven from the NYC rat race.  Very quiet and cozy...perfect for a relaxing meal.

I was not prepared for the limited menu options, but it turned out to be great.  Every dish was outstanding.  Not large portions, which is a good thing since the meal is anywhere from three to six courses.  Just plain fresh ingredients prepared to a wonderful way.

All of the staff were super friendly...not pretentious at all.  Service was excellent and attentive all evening long.

Definitely on the expensive side, but worth the trip for sure.
Service is spotless. Food is just of the right portion if you don't like eating too much, esp for tasting menu :)

I was very excited to take my sister here for her birthday, and left pretty disappointed.  But, maybe it was my fault for having expectations around what a 6 course tasting menu should/shouldn't be.

As a fairly petite lady, to prepare to eat my way through a 6 course tasting, I had only a small breakfast and a yogurt for lunch.  After all, if I'm going to drop over $450 (food + wine + tip) on dinner for two, I want to be sure I can get through it.  Little did I know that my preparations were for naught -- the servings at Blue Hill are comically small, literally.  By the end of the meal we were cracking up when the next microscopically portioned plate was brought out, and even resorted to begging the busboy to bring us extra bread.  

I enjoy fine dining and I'm happy to dole out cash for a great meal.  But part of a great meal is having enough of it that you can leave satisfied.  Rather, at the end of the meal, my sister and I were drunk (we ordered two bottle of wine as we went through the first rather quickly to fill the hole in our stomach not occupied by food), and ended up down the block at Chipotle to have something solid in our system before we went off to see a show.

A few other things: 
(1) Service was really attentive, but really, really slow! If you're going to serve 2-3 bite plates, then they should be paced accordingly.  We would have anywhere from 10-15 minute waits between the clearing of one plate and the arrival of the next.  For reference, we had a 5:00 reservation and did not get out of there till almost 8:00. 

(2) The ambience is beautiful.  Blue Hill is a very beautiful restaurant that serves very small portions.  

(3) The staff could not have been any nicer.  I want to emphasize this because while the food was a let down, the service was not.  

(4) The food actually was really tasty.  The little we had all tasted great.  The fish was served on the cool side, but that was probably owing to how little there was on such a large plate -- it'd be hard to keep the temperature as it moves from kitchen to table.  

Overall, if each serving was 50-100% larger, it would actually have been a lovely meal.  Unfortunately, we were so damn hungry (especially given the super slow pacing between plates) that it was hard to really savor the flavors as we hurriedly gobbled down the little that was put before us.

This is a good restaurant. It's refreshing to find real food in the US these days, prepared with vegetables that taste like something and meat from animals that actually ate real food themselves. But honestly, much of the rest of the world does not pee themselves over farm fresh eggs. Really - you can just buy them in the grocery store! Imagine that! What has happened to the food industry in the US when a restaurant can dehydrate a piece of kale and call it an amuse bouche - simply because it actually tastes of dehydrated kale and not some overly-seasoned flavoring?

I am not stingy when it comes to paying for proper food, but I felt the value equation really didn't work for me here. And it just left me depressed about food in general.

I don't write many reviews, but I just had to write a review of Blue Hill. We went for the 6 course tasting menu (farmer's feast), and every single item we had was delicious. Specifically the Goose Egg Noodles were excellent, along with the creamy wheat dessert. The ambience was great, the service was excellent and very attentive and accommodating. While you'll spend $200-$300 for a dinner for two, the experience is well worth it.

My absolute favorite date night splurge. My fiance and I celebrate every anniversary here. They serve hyper seasonal ingredients in an extremely beautiful way.
The service is always great and the food is ALWAYS consistently good.

I'm not going to go into too much detail of each dish, because this meal was an experience, and everything about it was spectacular. 

We had the pleasure of letting the kitchen dictate our meal.  After 5 amazing amuse courses, we went on to the baby leeks and broccoli rabe with caviar (amazing), then the parsnip steak (ridiculously good), then the farm egg (was goose egg.  beautiful and absolutely delicious), then last was the Halloran Farm Venison (absolutely the best venison I've ever eaten). 

The attention to quality product and simple but thoughtful cooking techniques truly showed at Blue Hill.  Every bite was amazing.  There was so much love in this food.  It showed throughout the entire experience. I can't wait to go back.

Thank you Blue Hill.  It was an honor.

My wife and I go to Blue Hill to mark all of our special occasions, because the food is amazing no matter what you order, the service is attentive, and the dining room is beautiful and comfortable. Every course is always delicious and we always leave extremely full. The sommelier makes terrific recommendations. Yes - the bill is huge - but for what you get it's practically a steal. (I said practically.)

We usually go about once a season, but more recently we were there twice within a few weeks. Even then the options were different and, as always, immensely satisfying.

We had a very good eating experience at Blue Hill.  Everyone in our party ordered the tasting menu and we all loved it. The staff was extremely knowledgeable and very nice. We will be coming here again.

Outstanding restaurant.  Inventive menu with very high quality ingredients.  The service was absolutely great.  If you like a more traditional steak/seafood/Italian meal, this is not your place.  The menu here requires a bit of an adventurous spirit.

Since my birthday no longer begins with 2, ok fine, has not begun with 2 for quite a few years, my fiancée decided it was time for us to celebrate my mature birthday at a restaurant that will cost him a leg.  

Food: fresh and you will get the "farm to restaurant" concept.  We had the tasting menu which gave us highlights of the dishes.  Pork and venison were both well executed.  Portion is something I typically struggle with fine dining places, but I walked out feeling satisfied.

Service: the best that I have had so far in NYC.  The staff knows their stuff, so please ask for their recommendation on wine since we loved both reds they suggested.  They made us feel welcomed and special.

Decor: very simple but pay attention to the eye level mirror panels they installed on the wall that will give you a panoramic view of the patrons in the restaurant.  I called it: peep in style...

Price: a leg... Or $250 for two

I want to start by saying what amazing service they have! All the wait staff were completely acute and helpful and made you feel comfortable if you had a question regarding the menu. We didn't need to ask them for anything they were very attentive and undisruptive. 

Now let me move on to the meal. Everything we ate starting with the amuse bouche tasted like it was made from the freshest, finest ingredients. Not once did the food displease us and it's amazing how Blue Hill can do something so simple as chicken beyond expectations. 

The only thing was that we were seated pretty close to the door and every time it opened we were hit with a draft and were surprised why we wouldn't have gotten a seat further from the door being one of the first few tables seated upon arrival.

BEST SERVICE I HAVE EVER HAD.   hands down.   such an enjoyable meal.   loved the "salad on a fence."    came here with my husband to celebrate a late valentines day, it was definitely a special experience.   again, service was impeccable.       will definitely be returning.

Had a splendid birthday dinner here with my husband. I had the five-course chef's tasting menu -- it was exquisite -- and he had three courses a la carte. This could have been awkward, but it was perfectly choreographed so that we were both always enjoying something. 
The food was wonderful, the service was amazing, the whole experience was everything it should be.
As a bonus, the selection of wines by the glass was excellent. 
If you like this style of cooking, I can't imagine not loving this restaurant. 
We did have the good fortune of having a corner table along the wall. The tables for two along the same banquette were pretty tight.

I like the idea of this place- farm to table, super fresh, local food. I wanted to love it but I it fell short. Went for a special occasion dinner and while the service was super good, detailed, and swift, the food was a bit blah as was the decor. In the end I couldnt understand the price of the farmer's feast pre-fix- 8 courses that left us feeling hungry and heading to The Lantern for a cheese plate after dinner. Most of the 'feast" were raw vegies on skewers and bites of proteins. I can now say I ate here but frankly was unmemorable.
This was one of the best meals I've ever had in my life. The Obamas came here on a date in 2009, and I can definitely see why.

Everything was special and extremely fresh. I look for something out of the ordinary and Blue Hill tried to do that with every step from the mini beet burgers that looked like they belong in a doll house to the roasted sunchokes to the pistachios in the Brussels sprouts. The goose egg sea urchin pasta blended together into a delicious dish. Loved the modern look the minute we stepped in, a real contrast from the street into the door, but we sat very close to our  neighbors which I liked but some may not. We wished happy birthday to the couple next to us.

I waited a few days to write this review because I really wanted to express how much I enjoyed my meal instead of just saying "it was really yummy". So we came here at 5:30 for my dad's birthday. I called the day before to ask if they could make my dish vegan and they said absolutely. When we got there, I looked at the menu and did not really see anything vegan. I asked the waitress and she went to ask the chef. This is kind of a side note but it almost feels as if there is a waiter for every table. They really do spend so much time addressing any concern you have and make you feel welcomed. Amazing service. Back to the food, so the waitress came back and told me there is one appetizer (a salad) and one main dish that could be made vegan. The main dish did not sound interesting to me and the appetizer was a salad which is honestly such an annoying thing to hear "you can have the salad" as a vegan.  The other option was a 85 tasting course that could be made vegan but I did not want to spend that much because I had no idea if I even want to eat there. I ended up picking and choosing several vegetables that I liked and they told me they can make me a grilled vegetable dish. I was so not impressed but though I was already agitated with Blue Hill, I decided not to make a big deal of it because it was my dad's birthday and I wanted him to enjoy. I was already thinking I would give this place 3 stars and just not plan to be back. 

My brother was the only one who did the tasting course. First off they give you an amuse bouche of these mini pork burgers. They brought me two radishes and at first I was kind of like "alright. a radish. great" but it has this green sauce on the bottom and it was just SO delicious. Next they brought out bread which had six different spreads. Three of them I tried and they were the Dill Salt, Carrot Salt, and Olive Oil. The oil was the tastiest olive oil I ever had. I also really liked the carrot salt. As my brother was receiving his meals, they made sure my dad and I had something small to nosh on. The next thing they brought out for me was a small butternut squash soup served in a 3-oz glass. It was very good. Next up was my grilled vegetable dish. It was really good. Every vegetable had its own sauce/seasoning and it was just so many different flavors. My favorite was the Jerusalem Artichoke. I could eat that all day. The second favorite was the brussels sprouts. I can not say this was some amazing dish that I could not get anywhere else. Yes, judging based on grilled-vegetable dishes, it was outstanding but overall it was just really good and unique and I really enjoyed it; I have nothing necessarily bad to say about it. 

After we finished our food, they brought out a plate of vegan brittle and truffle chocolates (no, not the mushroom). The brittle was not to my liking but the chocolate was so heavenly. I have never had such amazing chocolate (it does have honey in it though and they made sure to let me know). My dad and I split the citrus dessert. They separated the sponge cake and the assortment of sorbets so I can have the sorbet without the cake. 

We ended our meal at 830 so about 3 hours after we came here. It was amazing service, really unique food, and most importantly, my dad said it was the best birthday dinner he has ever had so it was truly a restaurant worth going to. I wish I could give it 6 stars so people do not think it is the same category of the other 5 star restaurants i have reviewed.
Not as good as I thought with the reviews.  Not bad, but more solid, I was not wow-ed by anything.  Some of the menu creations seemed a bit contrived.

I highly enjoyed my meal at Blue Hill and would highly recommend it to everyone! 

Most restaurants make the whole table do the tasting menu but at Blue Hill it was optional per guest. Therefore I chose the tasting menu and my friend was able to just order a la carte. 

Our meal started with these amazing mini beet and ricotta burgers on an almond bun that looked very similar to a macaron. 

Their fresh bread is brought to you warm and is accompanied by different types of butters and salts. 

My favorite dishes would definitely be "this mornings farm egg" and the  goose egg pasta that cooks the sea urchin into the sauce to give it more flavor. 

The meal was wonderful from beginning to end and our server was very friendly and helpful with the menu.

This must rank as one of the top meals I, and 3 guests, have ever eaten. The food was just simply fantastic, the service was excellent, and I would urge any visitor to Manhattan to experience this really gastronomic treat. We compared the meal with Charlie Trotter's Chicago, and Blue Hill came out ahead. Thank you for a wonderful evening. We loved it.

Really debated between a three and four star review. We ultimately had a very lovely evening with friends, but I left feeling really perplexed! I've had Blue Hill on my 'must try' list for years, and am not sure that we had an experience that matched my expectations. 

Highlights:
-Gluten free bread! I was able to participate in the bread course--excitement!  
-Really enjoyed the scallop appetizer. Beet "bolognese" in particular was an interesting and unusual addition. 
-The apple dessert was delicious! Not on the main menu, but was able to sub off of pre fixe due to allergy. No idea what it was called (as it was never really explained or presented), but ate every bite!

In between:
-Enjoyed but not overjoyed by my entre- the berkshire pig. Thought the combination of sweet potato, miso and peanuts was good, but felt some of the pork was well-cooked if not particularly interesting. The pork belly was probably my favorite part of the plate in terms of flavor. 

Low points:
-Our veggies on a fence were nicely dressed, but the lettuce was still a little sandy. Kind of shocking to have poorly washed vegetables at a restaurant of this caliber, especially when you're meant to eat the vegetables individually. When you pluck a piece of lettuce off a 'fence' point, you expect it to be a perfect bite of lettuce!
-Our waiter was helpful in identifying items that met a few individual needs at the table (a gluten allergy, a vegetarian, etc.), but the overall service was incredibly slow and lackluster. We were seated and then abandoned for quite a long time. And then after we ordered drinks, the same disappearing act. Perhaps it was because we were seated on the patio (which was otherwise very lovely), but it was very strange to have such sporadic service at this price point. 

I'm not sure we'd go back, despite having several nice courses and an overall very enjoyable evening out with friends.

The kitchen in this seemingly understated and nearly hidden West Village farm-to-table gem demonstrates the art of simplicity when fresh ingredients are put in the hands of a talented chef.

Not loud, actually surprising how small it is on the inside, but the food will just overwhelm you. Goat cheese fruit appetizer, lobster appetizer, gnocchi cooked to perfection, and make sure to get the chocolate bread pudding.

The service was wonderful, warm, and superb.  Our waitress was well informed about every dish and was not afraid to give us her opinions regarding her favorites plates.  Wines by the glass are small in number and very pricey, but beautifully chosen.

Portions might seem small but in truth are fairly and artfully sized.  You might clean your plate but you won't leave hungry.

Our entrée choices were lamb and pork. They were both exceptional, particularly the terrine and the sauce components. The fresh asparagus and fiddlehead offerings were perfect accompaniments as well.  

The lamb was hearty, perfectly cooked and rich with flavor and texture.  The pork had four distinct meat components, each delicious in its own way.  


Overall, farm to table excellence.

Went here last night on a date and it was seriously one of the best meals I have ever had in New York City. The bread and butter at the beginning of the meal is a nice rustic beginning to this farm-to-table experience, with real, moist, flavorful butter and crusty, toothsome breadsticks. The beet slider amuse bouche was delish, and I absolutely loved the wild striped bass entree. It was a little salty, but perfectly complemented the grapefruit garnish. At first the portion looked a little small, but the quality of each bite left me full and satisfied. For dessert, we had the chocolate bread pudding, which was divine, and the citrus plate with lemon ice cream, which was light and refreshing. The petit fours of caramelized pumpkin seeds and chocolate truffle were a wonderful way to end the evening. Great, friendly, accommodating, and attentive service, and a really great dining experience. I highly recommend this place for any occasion.

The warm atmosphere was the perfect respite on a frigid January night.  Table for our party of five was ready half an hour early, which was nice since the reservation was for 10.  Even though our table was right inside the door, we were not cold and the set up was perfect for our group and made for a great place to celebrate Julie's birthday.  The service was perhaps the best I've ever experienced. 

Four out of five had the tasting menu, and I ordered a la carte.  

Dishes consisted of:

Amuse bouche: mini roasted beet sliders, and a slice of charcuterie.  The beet slider was almost like a jam, which made it interesting and two non-beet lovers actually kinda liked it. 

A large, squat glass with thick bread sticks came with pork lard spread and butter, and two herb salt mixture: fennel and arugula salts.  The bread had a nice crispy crust with soft insides.  

Day boat scallops - least favorite part of the meal.  Obviously, since can't remember much about them. 

Little sausage balls.  Very yummy, although a little too salty. 

Pig's Jowl with speck, brussels sprouts and green apples.  The jowl was well prepared but a little boring, not enough porkyness.  

Pork belly with poached egg, was seared nicely on the outside.  The poached egg over it made a nice creamy sauce. 

Braised Hake with apple, fennel, and soy beans. The fish was well prepared, but needed the herb salts that were still on the table.  The soy beans were crunchy-ish which was a nice textural contrast.  accompanying sauce seemed citrusy and bit jarring. 

Venison with cranberries.  Venison was rare-medium rare and flavorful.  Everybody loved the venison.  

The wines by the glass list was rather small.  I believe they had 6 reds.  the Red Hook Cabernet from Long Island was fairly good, and the pinot noir from the Handlon in the Williammette was even better.

Wow! Food is awesome! Service is great! Restaurant is cozy! Absolutely recommended.  We did not have a reservation and sort of got in the last minute and the staff was soooo friendly.  They make the food from scratch and the drinks are awesome! It is a little pricey but for what you get, it is worth it!

Shockingly bad and incredibly disappointing. 7:30 reservation Sunday night. First time at the restaurant. 
Sat down on time but took an hour to get our appetizers. We were starving. I had a small vegetable salad, which was delicious and I ate it in two minutes.. A half hour later we still have no entree. So hungry. Finally we get our entrees shortly after 9pm and they are COLD. They are grilled venison so they are not supposed to be cold, but they are. And we ordered a side order of brussels sprouts, which was also completely cold.  Our server took the food away and promised it would be back hot in "two minutes". Fifteen minutes later, we still had no food )and are totally starving, so we got up to leave. At that pint the food returns and it is totally overbooked. They expect us to pay $35 per dish for overbooked, warmed over food? It didn't even look edible. 
So we told them we were leaving and as we were leaving, the hostess came up to give us our bill for our glasses of wine we had with our appetizer and said she was not going to charge us for our food. Seriously? They ruined my birthday dinner and she's not going to charge me for two mouthfuls of vegetables? How nice of them. 
And all she could say was "I don't know what to say..."  Seriously, they could care less. 
She's really going to need to think of something better to say, because I'm sure we are not the only ones who are going to having this experience.

Visited last evening, and it was nothing short of perfection. 

AMBIANCE: While the Manhattan location couldn't hold a candle to Stone Barns (c'mon, a working farm, how could it?), I really do love walking down those steps on Washington Pl., through the red curtain and being seated in a truly warm and cozy space. It's just plain welcoming. 

SERVICE: Like a beautifully executed ballet. The waitstaff moved quickly, yet gracefully between tables. We never wanted for anything; water, wine, bread, mini beet burgers .  Our female server made some great recommendations and really steered us in the right direction. 

FOOD:

Appetizers - Jerusalem artichoke soup was warm, velvety deliciousness; pure essence of artichoke, combined with the earthiness of mushrooms. The pork jowel was recommended by our server, and what a great call it was; crispy skin with tender and fatty jowel meet underneath. I could have eaten two! The amuse was the famous beet "burger". I could have eaten 10 of those and left a happy camper. 

Mid-Course - we shared the purple potato gnocchi with pork belly entree. We'd previously had a similar dish at Stone Barns, and this version didn't disappoint. Perfectly shaped small purple tubes filled with creamy ricotta, surrounded by bite-sized pieces of pork belly. Crunchy, salty, fatty, delicious. 

Entrees - The chicken was served as a sliced breast, and was as tender as could be (cooked sous vides); it was served with root veggies that gave the dish a bit of sweetness and nice crunch. The venison was AMAZING. A large sliced portion that was served with parsnip puree (love it, never gets old) and a dark coffee/cinnamon-like sauce that perfectly complimented the gaminess of the meat. 

Dessert - We had the "Citrus" dessert, which was very light, and the highlight of which was the lemon ice cream. We also had the chocolate bread pudding, which was rich and indulgent; a great version of the dish. They also brought us a mini slice of caramel cake, which was great.  Petit fours were caramelized pumpkin seeds and a kind of soft chocolate chip cookie with passion fruit gelee on top. 

What a great experience...

Best in class for farm-to-table American.  Make sure you can't get a reservation (you probably can't) before wasting time elsewhere.  It is a must-visit if you don't feel like making a pilgrimage north to the Farm.  Entrees are incredible, bar snacks/sides are worthwhile.  Otherwise lackluster.

Things that annoy me:
1) It's crowded.  Tightly packed tables.  I recommend going elsewhere if you plan on getting dumped at dinner by your significant other. 
2) Service isn't great.  Servers make way more than they should here given their attention to detail and effort.  Great example of NYC's social safety net in action for people from certain backgrounds. 
3) Kitchen is physically small - Food can take a while
4) Many of the appetizers and desserts are a complete waste of time and money.  I would avoid all together

Everything was exceptionally great! I had the extended farm feast tasting menu. Every plate that came out was delicious. The service was on point. The best dish to my liking was the Stone Barns Berkshire Pig. My girlfriend was speechless after she took a bite of the pork belly. Would definitely go back!

Ahh Blue Hill, my favorite restaurant in NYC.  Although if I had the bank account and time to go to the one in Westchester I would, this one definitely cures my longing for amazing farm to table food.  You just can't get a bad meal here. I love that you can order al la carte (did I spell that right? This is an iPhone review).  It's much less expensive then then tasting menu but same quality... So win win!  Everything is in season so no point in me going over the menu, since you will probably have a choice of something else.
