All of these other good reviews....believe them.  Service.....perfect.  Wine list...excellent.  Food choices...just right.  Presentation....as good as they get.  And actual taste of the food...read the reviews.  

Loved this place, and hope to go again.  Ate at the bar, because all the reviews said that reservations are real tough...and this was a Saturday night.  Would do it again just the same way.

So, if you are considering this place and can make it happen...do it.
One of my favorite restaurant in NYC, mainly for the understated simplicity of their dishes and their exceptional service/ambience.

Let's be clear: I'm not a foodie, I don' intend to practice as a food blogger and the day I went to Blue Hill was my birthday and I was in a great mood.
The service was impeccable and the food amazing. We had the chef's menu with wine pairing. Great value and outstanding quality.
And if you happen to go to the restroom, do wash your hands. The handsoap and lotion are great too. (they have their own brand)

What a disappointment, especially after all of the rave reviews.  We booked a Sunday reservation months in advance.  The day before, a friend from out of town was visiting unexpectedly, so I called the restaurant to see if they could accommodate a 4th person.  The answer was a flat no.  If we were going from 2 to 3 people, I could see how that could be a problem.  However, we had a reservation for 3 and were seated at a table for 4!  In fact, the service in general was poor.  Our waiter (Benjamin) was bored, supercilious and made it clear our questions were beneath him to answer.  We asked him to describe hedgehog mushrooms (having never heard of them before) and he didn't know what they were either, and didn't bother to find out. He also directed his answers and conversation in general to my sister's husband. Maybe he thought the man at the table was paying, but in fact, I was treating them to dinner.  

Even worse than the service was the food.  Our Christmas tree appetizer (a wire tree with various items such as kale chips stuck on the "branches") managed to be boring and pretentious.  The salads were the best part of the meal.  None of the other dishes we ordered (the farm egg with mushrooms, the bass, and the chicken) were anything but ordinary.  Desserts were actually BAD.  The pear and chocolate cake was dry and crunchy, the quince with ice cream was bland.  I think it was clear we disliked the desserts, because our waiter sent over a complimentary order of some type of fruit bread/cake.  At least that was moist, but since I can't even remember what it was, clearly it was nothing special.  At least the cocktails were good, so I'm giving one star for the drinks.  

All three of us agreed we would never go back or recommend it to anyone else.

The food is somewhere between three and four stars, but I thought the service is what really let Blue Hill down.  

Among the food courses, the veggies on a fence and pork (several different ways) stood out as awesome dishes I would happily order again and again.  Other items on the menu were good but clearly not memorable even several weeks later.  

As for the service, perhaps the waitress just rubbed me the wrong way - there was something about her that came off as haughty and seemed at odds with the positive, welcoming vibe other employees at the restaurant were giving off.  Bigger gripe is with respect to the door - it was one of those bitterly cold nights we had back in early December, and there was a brutal blast of cold air every time someone came or went (this coming from a group of diners sitting three tables from the entrance - my genuine pity to the two tables closer to the arctic tundra than we were). May be worth calling ahead to ask where exactly they're planning to seat you.

Im giving Blue Hill a poor review so I think I should explain myself with a short version and a long version.

Short Version: the food was quite bad and the place is stuffy. The fish was under cooked with no flavor, the venison was bland and the rest of the accompanying dishes were over sweetened. I came here based on the reviews but it was defanetly not worth the money. After my dinner and before dessert, I went to sit next to my date in the sofa seat across from me. I was asked by the manager to return to my chair. That's never happened before. Way too stuffy of a place if you can't sit next to your date for a moment.

Long version: Perhaps it's because I had high expectations based on reviews but overall, I was very dissatisfied with the food quality. Shortly after waking through the door, the experience went down hill very quickly.

One exception, the appetizer item named, "This morning's farm egg" with shiitake mushrooms was very good!!! This was all that can be praised.

The Octopus appetizer was ok "acceptable" but not for the price.

Our waitress was no help in deciphering the vague menu. Most places with a brief-description menu will have the table server explain or highlight some of the dishes. Nothing of the sort here.

Back to the food... the venison was flavorless. I ordered it medium rare as the chef recommends. Thumbs down! It came with collard greens and they were over sweetened. They appeared to be marinated in tangerine or orange juice but tasted like a soda pop drink. They could have been good with a subtle infusion of sweetness but the chef was drunk on sugar.

The fish, "Hake", was flavorless and was also too sweet, over-sweetened with preserved  lemon. The fish came on top of a creamy thick clam chowder that was supposed to have shrimp and clams. There were little bits of shrimp and some clams that were flavorless. The fish was under cooked.

As a side, I ordered the Pumpkin Cheese, Butternut Squash. It too was over sweetened, enhanced with honey or maple syrup. Way over done with sweetness.
 
In summary, poor food, stuffy environment, pretentious staff, and just to reiterate, poor food. Most of the clientele appeared to be over 60 so perhaps I'm missing something being a tad bit younger. But I've been around long enough to know good food, so I'm betting I'm dead-on with this review. Whatever people found good with this place seems to have left the building.

My second time dining at at Blue Hill, three weeks ago, I found it nearly impossible to decide what I wanted from the creative dishes on the menu.  The cocktails were very creative as well.  I ordered one featuring beet infused bourbon.  

Coming last minute without a reservation, a friend and I ate at the bar. 

As with my previous experience, the food was great.  Fresh, creative and (almost) perfectly executed technique. The ambience was romantically lit (although sometimes I wish I had a bit more light upon the plate to appreciate the food's presentation) and just the right amount of energy.  Sophisticated without being quiet or stuffy.  The staff was friendly and unpretentious, and the bartender was fun. 

For an appetizer I had a house-made pasta with sea urchin sauce which was fabulous-- perfectly cooked al dente strands that stood up to the creamy sea urchin.  While the urchin is not the star of the dish as its texture is somewhat lost, the flavor it imparted to the sauce was delicious. 

The only part of my meal that was not perfect was that the duck was a little more rare than I would prefer.  The slices near each end were exactly to my liking, but the central ones (over half of the portion) were so rare that they were almost difficult to chew.  I should have perhaps sent it back to be cooked slightly more to my liking, but everything else about the restaurant is so perfect I felt bad doing so.

Walking out, I saw a table eating the most dramatic presentation of brussels sprouts I have ever seen-- the stem roasted with the sprouts attached and presented erect as if growing from the plate.  Definitely left me wanting to go back for more. 

I will certainly return, as the quality of the food and ambience are superior and definitely a good value for the price. Definitely fit for special occasions.

As someone who recently started living on a grad school budget, I thought I had successfully sworn off my expensive foodie habit. "This is New York! I don't need to spend $$$$ to get good food!"

But then I had Blue Hill. Oh how my anti-expensive foodie facade has fallen. Their vegetables truly delight the senses. I've always loved sunchokes, but their sunchoke soup took it to another level in terms of complexity and general deliciousness. The pork (5 different  cuts) was also delectable. And the quince dessert was a party in my mouth. This restaurant is extremely vegetarian friendly, and I can't wait to come back with a fancy vegetarian friend to try the cauliflower steak.

tl;dr: You can really taste the freshness of the ingredients. Great food at somewhat reasonable prices.

Blue Hill really epitomizes the farm-to-table concept: one of our appetizers at the beginning (a "snack" as they call it) was literally some plain fresh vegetables stuck on a small picket fence. That was probably my least favorite dish, but everything else was pretty good.

Part of the reason why most of the dishes taste good is that they're actually fairly heavy on the flavor - possibly using a decent amount of butter (though it's the freshest possible butter, I'm sure). The fresh taste of the ingredients still comes out though.

For mains, the pork was very good, and the cauliflower steak also tasted great. I would probably suggest choosing a meat or vegetarian dish over the fish options, however.

And for dessert, definitely go for the chocolate bread pudding and the pumpkin souffle if you have the choice!

Expectations were high as we were comfortably seated in the quaint dining room.
Thankfully we were a party of four as the two seat tables against the wall looked uncomfortably cramped with no privacy whatsoever.

Service was polite, alert and accommodating all evening (so unlike the pretentious "Blue Hill at Stone Barns" up north).

Welcome to "farm to table" dining. 
Started with four complementary pill sized and tasty "beet burgers" served on a large plate (this was the norm all evening). The accompanying  bread was delicious.

Appetizers included Sea Scallops and "This Morning's Farm Egg" which included black dirt leeks, tuscan kale and hedgehog mushrooms. Fresh yes but we found both to be lacking in flavor. The Wild Striped Bass with almonds and pears was very good but portioned extremely small. Same with the Raven & Boars Pig entree. Sorry to say but - yes - size DOES matter. Especially at these prices.

For dessert we shared the "Chocolate Bread Pudding" which was exceptional.
The cheese dessert platter was excellent as well.

Terrific, Wonderful, Cozy, Accommodating, Fresh and Delicious!

Just some of the descriptive words for this gem.

We were celebrating my birthday and I've been dying to try this place. 
The ambiance was romantic and cozy and quiet and dark! 
Loved our waitress who recommended things for us and also got the chef to have duck made for my husband (which wasn't on the menu that night, but he asked about it)
I had a brussels sprouts tree with some dipping sauce to start. It could have been seasoned somewhat. It was paired with dipping sauce which was ok. Not my favorite, but fun to eat.

Scallops appetizer was really way too tiny. About 4 tiny scallops for over $20.

Entrees were a purple potato gnocchi and like I mentioned, duck for my husband with potatoes. HE LOVED IT and I LOVED my gnocchi!

Had dessert too, which we never do. A pear/chocolate brownie. Very good.

I want to eat here every weekend, but I'll wait for next year :)

My One Word: AMAZING!

Fact #1: All the servers were super nice, have a sense of humor, and sharp, my water cup was never left empty. They were just all so well trained! 

Fact #2: Large portions! Definitely go for the extended menu if your budget allows! Fresh ingredients for every dish! AMAZING to say the least. 

Fact #3: Their food tends to be on the saltier side.

My partner and I visited for an early dinner. 

We were seated in their back room: It's nice and cozy with a handful of other tables around, yet, well-spaced. (Upon leaving the restaurant, I noticed the back dining room was much less noisy than their packed front dining room.)

The cuisine featured fresh, seasonal and local ingredients (they champion their producers as Gods), and most importantly, all dishes were cooked very well. No unwanted surprises. 

Service was very professional with a smile. Wine list was thoughtfully put together, with many American wines to choose from.

One cannot go wrong dining here.

Without a doubt, one of the finest dining experiences to be had in NYC.

Step down into the simple, yet elegant dining area and you'll be transported into a culinary paradise, each dish more surprising and delicious than the last.

The chefs tasting menu is the way to go to get the most out of the seasonal fare offered at Blue Hill. I will admit to consuming more wine than I should have, so while the recall of each dish is a bit fuzzy, one thing that is certain is the complete satisfaction of the dining experience. 

The meals highlights included the poached country egg with milk fed pig ham, which was truly the best egg I have ever eaten. As a palate clenser, the dark chocolcate venison rillette was a tasty as it was creative.

From the food, to the wine list, to the impecable service, Blue Hill is a must try for any Locavore who appreciates the subtle flavors of seasonal cooking.

I don't know how anyone could give this place less than 5 stars!  We had the tasting menu with wine pairings, whcih I recommend!  Of course, we were on a special "Divinne Dining" deal through British Air VISA, where one price covers all including tax and tip, which MIGHT account for the special treatment.  (Only about 10 restaurants participate, and the deal ends end of November, probably so as to make it unavailable for the restaurant-busy Holidays).

Anyway, the food was exquisite, the wine divine, the pairings intelligent, the service and cozy romantic atmosphere inspiring!

This past Saturday was our second (wonderful) meal at Blue Hill.  The first was two years ago during another visit to NYC, when my wife and I got hooked.  

The previous night, we ate at Nougatine (John George) and had a wonderful experience there, having chosen the tasting menu, so it was easy to compare the two restaurants.  We chose the tasting menu at Blue Hill too, and while similarly priced, we found it to be nearly perfect, and better than Nougatine for numerous reasons.

But first, I'm puzzled by all of the recent lackluster reviews for Blue Hill.  It is so easy for people to be overly-dismissive in a review.  

Could the meals have been bad?  It's possible, but I doubt it.  

Blue Hill just won the James Beard award for the BEST restaurant in America.  It has a Michelin star.  Plus, restaurants as pricey as Blue Hill don't survive without regulars.   Regulars demand consistent good food and service.   The food and service is very good, period.  

Still, this might be lost on those who:
1.  Can't get out of their thoughts enough to sense, or enjoy, the food in their mouths.
2.  (Subclass of #1) Read lots of reviews and find that the experience fails to satisfy whatever perfection they had imagined.
3.  Think that culinary novelty and trendy interiors equals great food.
4.  Need large food portions to feel satisfied.
5.  Can't appreciate anything excellent because they lack humanity.  (too harsh?)
6.  Get bored unless bounced on the knee of a star chef.
7. Prefer to be impressed rather than moved.
8.  Are jerks.  (The staff is warm and nice.  It's nice to be nice to the nice.)

I enjoyed former food critic Frank Bruni's recent NYT article, "Familiarity Breeds Content."   He understands the interplay between our desire for culinary novelty and entertainment, and more soulful needs.  While writing this, I discovered Mr. Bruni's 2006 still relevant three star NYT review of Blue Hill, "Food You'd Almost Rather Hug Than Eat."   "What it presents," says Mr. Bruni, "is more like a hushed foreign film with subtitles. You have to pay attention and heed the nuances, and you can get only so carried away."  

I think that Blue Hill is worthy of much appreciation.  It is not trendy or flashy, but it is handsome, understated, and calm.  It isn't dated or threadbare any more than the venerated dining room at the Four Seasons.  Likewise, the dishes are refined and thoughtful, precisely because they possess flavors born of a wonderful chef using amazing Blue Hill Farm ingredients, and not culinary fireworks.  I think that the food feels good.  Really good.  

My review is this:  
I had a food-gasm.  Everything was sublime - the foodie cocktails, the fresh produce, the sommelier that picked an astounding wine to match the meal, the friendly attentive waitress, the warm romantic setting, the carrot sized baguettes with fresh made spreads and veggie-based salts, a tasting menu with courses chosen to best complement each other, the completely organic and scrumptious farm egg appetizer, the amazing melt in your mouth pasture chicken with lobster mushroom, the wonderful raspberry desert, the best dinner coffee in years.  Love Blue Hill.

Great room nestled in a Washington Square Park townhouse. Friendly service, attentive but not overbearing. Egg appetizer was outstanding as was the pasta w/sea urchin appetizer my friend enjoyed. Pig main course had different pork parts and was very nice, I'd give it 5 stars but for the wanting wine list. It was short and somewhat unbalanced. I'll certainly return for a farm to table fresh, well presented meal.

Just got back from dinner, and while the food was good, it's a bit over priced for what it is. Service was fine, although I was never asked if I wanted another glass of wine.

Appetizers: none looked particularly appealing, so we went with the potato pancakes based on our severs recommendation. They were good, but I wouldn't necessarily get them again.

Entrees: we got the gnocchi and duck. The gnocchi was better than most I've had (although L'Appicio's is better), but the duck was phenomenal. If you try anything, I highly recommend the duck.

Dessert: we got the strawberries and the chocolate bread pudding. This was the highlight of the meal (aside from the duck). 

Provided gratis were a mini "burger" of tomatoes and ricotta and an apple crisp dessert. Overall, I enjoyed the dinner but the appetizer choices are underwhelming and the prices are a tad high.
Loved location, decor, ambiance and top rate service. Had so looked forward to this meal but sadly disappointed - didn't stand up to the hype and the meal was not a stand out...sigh

Heard so many good things about this place even before I took the boyfriend for his birthday, and it didn't disappoint. 
Atmosphere: Cozy, romantic, dim lighting
Waitstaff: Very friendly, strikes up a conversation with you regarding preferences and checks up on you regularly to see how things are.  
 
Amuse bouche:  Tiny bite of what looked like a teeny burger bun w/tomatoes inside. Good and refreshing.
Appetizer: the emu egg pasta & the farm egg (with corn and other veggies) were great! Loved the farm egg, which came poached.
Main course:  Had the steak and the lamb, cooked med-rare.  Didn't seem like much on the plate, but the presentation was deceiving because we both walked out of there stuffed.  
Dessert:  Had the strawberry (lemon tart on bottom with creme fraiche, strawberry foam on top).  Loved this - I could've eaten the strawberry foam for days on end.  Boyfriend had the blackberry dessert which was alright - I liked my strawberry one better. 
Another dessert bite: there were three small petit four size dessert pieces that came out after everything was done - i think one was a small brownie bite with an espresso filling, a cake bite which i don't remember, and a toasted pumpkin seeds bite.

I had made the reservation online and noted that it was the boyfriend's birthday.  Without me even mentioning this on the day of the dinner, they brought out a small piece of caramel ice cream cake (at least i think it was ice cream because he inhaled it without me getting a second bite on it) with a candle for his birthday! 

Also, they can accommodate almost any dietary restrictions - a couple next to us had dietary restrictions (gluten free, and diabetic) and the waitstaff made sure it was taken care of without taking away from the experience.

I'm writing this review as a warning...this place is very nice but verging on ripoff. Pleasant but dull room, efficient yet robotic staff, fresh but bland food, and astronomical prices. 4 adults and two teens ordering off the standard menu came to $800. And we left unsatisfied and slightly hungry. Microscopic portions of weakly flavored food.  Not a bad place, but feels a lot like an SNL skit as you look at your giant empty places sprinkled with tiny bland vegetables. Would feel expensive at half the price.

This place is my new jam. 
Took my wife here for her birthday.  The service was excellent.  The food was delicious. 

I ordered the pig, which was several different cuts with a medley of different chopped veggies. It was awesome!

We also had the summer salad to start. Holy moly what don't they put in their salad? There were so many ingredients! It was amazing. 

Everything tasted fresh and delicious and I will definitely go back.

This place was just class and service from the moment we walked in. We were there for our anniversary and it did not disappoint. We had the tasting menu. But they do not obligate all guests to order it. They also allow substitutions, for example I can't eat fish, so they substituted one of their pricey appetizers, the potato pancakes. These were incredible. We also ordered the butter, pig lardo, tomato and corn salts that came out with bread, and the tiny, fresh from garden veggies on stick(this was a little weird looking) but still delicious. My husband's first course was a blue fish dish. Our second course was a far egg of the day, that was very lightly cooked over easy, and came with a spoon to pick up all the runny yumminess. Our main entree was various pork pieces, chop, tenderloin, and fat with beans. Our desserts were fresh yogurt with strawberries and honey and elderflower syrup. We then had apricots with ice cream. And they added a small piece of cake with a candle! Amazing. It was a perfect dinner. Great service. Great flavor. And if you're lucky, you will sit in the secret garden. I would recommend it. The tasting menu was 85.00 per person. Well worth it, I think. But you may want another appetizer if you're a big person, since portions were a bit small. Or eat the bread with the pig lardo. So good!

Great service and great food, farm to table type dishes. Everything was very well prepared. Décor and ambience was romantic, great lighting and the perfect noise level. Great downtown location, as well.

Maybe it was just an off-night but my husband and I were disappointed by Blue Hill... After reading all of the great reviews, and since we love farm to table cuisine, we decided to go to Blue Hill for dinner. Unfortunately, just about everything we ordered was sub-par. We started with farm snacks which left much to be desired. The portions were tiny, although that's not what bothered us. It was the quality. We ordered the ricotta and homemade butter, along with ahi tuna. The texture of the ricotta was dry (not smooth and moist as I was expecting) and the ahi tuna was a mushy tuna salad that my husband couldn't finish because of the bad taste. (This was a huge shock to me because he normally finishes everything!) Then we ordered "This morning's farm egg" as an appetizer. I've had farm fresh eggs before and this was nothing like the rich taste I was expecting. Farm fresh eggs have an orange yolk and a rich creamy taste. This egg had a pale yellow yolk and tasted like an average supermarket egg. My organic eggs at home taste better! However, the entrees were good. I ordered the risotto which was very flavorful and my husband ordered fish which he really liked. The portions were small though so it would have been nice if we could have enjoyed the appetizers before our dinner arrived.... After experiencing the food ourselves, we would not go back. We are going to stick to ABC Kitchen when we want a farm to table experience.

Can't argue with the freshness of the food.  They seem to be locked in to a long term rut that can only be explained as an attempt to challenge Gotham Bar and grill for longevity and operation.  I felt that the staff was knowledgeable but very uninspired.  Many of the captains seemed bored in there tasks and more focused on passing time than servicing their tables.  The décor is five years past due for an upgrade and with the resources that are behind the project I'm shocked they have let it get to the stage that you can barely open the door because it sticks on the ground causing the host to have to walk over to the door every five minutes to let the patrons in.  How can a restaurant at this level continue to be elevated to this status without merit or heart.

cracker trees and orchids fits the dark and quiet room... 

not impressed with the choices of the menu but we did our best....perhaps we should go with the chicken as i overheard recommended; oh happy days, chicken

nothing seemed on point, too many under-ripe cherry tomatoes garnishing many of the dishes..i know its tomato sauces but could anything be done to them besides halving them and putting them on a plate...if i wanted farm fresh produce with a simply cooked garnish i would have done it myself

High expectations going in and a little disappointed in the end...I felt the ingredients in the food were fresh, but the flavors could have been better.

Farm snacks: bologna, corn mustard...tasty and fresh, much better than a hot dog you would get from the super market, but am used to getting fresh bologna from the local butcher.

Appetizer:
I ordered "This Morning's Farm Egg sweet corn, shiitake mushrooms and homemade lardo"...this tasted very good...a lot of flavor in ever bite and the texture of all the ingredients mixed together was just right. My friend ordered the Chilled corn Soup shiitake mushrooms, chiles and basil...I'm not a big fan of cold corn soup, thought it was ok, but my friend liked it and thought it was refreshing.

Entrees: I ordered the stone barns pastured chicken crushed summer squash, ricotta cheese and basil...the chicken has good texture, flavor and was definitely fresh chicken. There was one piece that was a bit slimy and thought it wasn't cooked but the waitress told me it could have been the fat on the chicken...I don't think I can agree because that one piece tasted different than the others. the crushed summer squash, ricotta cheese and basil was very salty. The flavors were too strong. The waitress was kind enough to have the chef make a new batch for me, served warm vs cold...it was less salty than the first, but didn't really like the flavor of it...My friend took one for the team and ate it since the waitress was kind enough to bring out another one for me. My friend ordered the Stone Barns Berkshire Pig tropea onions, succotash, okra and chanterelle mushrooms, wasn't much on the plate, but he liked it overall.


Dessert: I ordered the layered strawberry with lemon, pancotta. It was good, not too sweet and refreshing. My friend ordered the Chocolate Bread Pudding salted caramel, pine nuts and cocoa nib ice cream which was very good, not too sweet and just the right amount of flavor.

Service: Our waitress was very nice and helpful....no complaints.

Ambiance: cute little place....good for dates.

Service, atmosphere and food were all done perfectly.  We chose to order a la carte instead of the tasting menu.  We were so happy we did.  I started with the tastiest tuna crostini ever then moved on to the stuffed eggplant as my main course.  It came with a side of couscous.  Both were light, fresh and tasted like summer.  My husband had the chicken as his main course and thought it was the moistest chicken he had ever eaten.  We shared the strawberries with lemon cake and again the fresh ingredients were bright and really did shine through.  We also loved all the little tastes of things that came complimentary.  Definitely plan on returning.

Staff: extremely knowledgeable and friendly. Attentive to food allergies (they brought out amazing gluten free bread substitution and replaced the amuse bouche with perfectly fried kale chips). 

Ambiance: surprisingly fresh and laid back for a white-tablecloth environment. We were there for an early Sunday supper, so we had a nice corner booth to ourselves. I can see how a normal dinner time would be too crowded for an intimate conversation though.

Food: Farm to table, fresh local ingredients, surprisingly delightful flavor combinations with complexity in depth and texture. I don't love fish, but I couldn't get enough of the grilled bluefish appetizer, and the lobster was delicious. Duck breast was perfectly tender and juicy, with crispy, tasty skin.

Overall: get the tasting menu. Perfect anniversary spot. Wish we could eat here every day!
One of our favorite local places to walk into and sit at the bar without a reservation.  We've been here many times and always had a flawless meal.

Quality of this place is outstanding. White tablecloth, each guest feels treated with over the top level of personal attention and detail. Took my girlfriend here for her birthday and we spent 3.5 hours on appetizer, dinner, desert and wine. Never once felt rushed by the staff, service was impeccable. Food was prepared very well. Mini cheeseburgers were unique (I mean one bite, size of a mint) great wine selection, location was nested below a stoop in Greenwich, felt very romantic and cozy inside. 

Not loud, actually surprising how small it is on the inside, but the food will just overwhelm you. Goat cheese fruit appetizer, lobster appetizer, gnocchi cooked to perfection, and make sure to get the chocolate bread pudding :)

Would definitely go back

I'm a little torn over whether to review Blue Hill after my first experience. I found the food to be great overall and the dining room very intimate, however the entire meal was hampered by the service. To be frank, the service was borderline painful the evening that I visited.

I actually took the bf here for his birthday dinner #3, on a Monday night. I was pretty surprised by how bustling the dining room was even on a Monday evening, mostly full of what looked to be business dinners and a whole lot of birthday celebrations. It actually shocked me to see more than five people celebrating birthday in the same room; a little scary, really. Anyway, the slow and inattentive service was particularly disappointing because we were celebrating a special occasion, so I was really hoping for a smooth meal. The one upside was that we were enjoying each other's company enough that we were both willing to overlook the lapses in service.

We decided to order a la carte instead of the farmer's feast tasting menu, just to get a few plates to share. To start, we had the bologna with corn mustard from the farm snacks section of the menu, which tasted fresh and pretty gourmet for a bologna. I was pleasantly surprised by how much flavor the bologna had, with a slight sear from the grill. The corn mustard was wonderful, a good counterbalance to the salty meat. This morning's farm egg was my favorite dish of the night, creamy and luxurious with a perfectly coddled egg swimming in a light broth of mushrooms, sweet corn, and lardo. The combination of flavors were delicate yet nuanced, with every element in perfect harmony. The summer bean salad was solid as well, highlighting all the fresh, in-season vegetables and fruits in an elegant presentation. The Stone Barnes berkshire pig was beautifully prepared and amazing, featuring many cuts of pork including loin, belly and other cuts all prepared a little differently. I swear the pig tasted a lot more "porky" than your average run-of-the-mill pork, they tasted like happy pigs that lived happy and fulfilled lives up at Stone Barns.The white eggplant, okra, and other vegetable garnishes on the plate tasted great as well, complementing the pork but not overwhelming the natural flavors at all. While I loved all the earlier salads and vegetable preparations, the vegetable side of sweet corn with basil and pickled ramps was a little underwhelming. Of course sweet summer corn always tastes good, even if eaten raw right off the cob, but the one we got was served cold and quite dull. The dessert menu is pretty interesting, again featuring seasonal ingredients in relatively straightforward combinations. We ended up getting the blueberries with toasted almond cake and buttermilk sorbet, and the kitchen sent out a mini mousse-like cheesecake for the bf as a birthday gift. I liked the simple blueberries and light, chiffon-like almond cake, I was yearning for more buttermilk sorbet just to tie all the elements together.

All in all, I enjoyed my evening with the bf, although I'm not certain I'll be returning very soon. Perhaps I'd have a better experience at Blue Hill at Stony Barns, if I can just make the drive out there.

The food is over-rated.  There is so much hype about this restaurant and consistently makes the top 10 list.   We had the signature chicken and pork dish, both of which were bland.  I understand the whole farm to table concept and wish more restaurants would do more of,  so I have to commend them for that.  The service was good, not exceptional for those prices.  The bartender was not on the ball.  

I cannot say that this is a top 10 restaurant.  You are better off going to another place.

Amazing experience. We went here for a special occasion and ordered al a carte. Every single thing we got was amazing and I would absolutely recommend coming here. The folks at James Beard know what they're doing.

If you want to know how to fall in love with nutrition this is the place to do it. Dan Barber is more than an amazing chef he is a radical thinker. It's impossible to overemphasize the importance of good farming for safe and nutritious food. He is a champion of this argument and wants to oversee the quality and sustainability of every ingredient he uses all the way down to the bathroom soaps.  Everything his restaurants' serve are as fresh and nutritious as possible. I am always amazed at the difference in taste that his vegetables have versus the ones I buy at the farmers market.

Perhaps an off nite - a VERY off nite, dissappointing especially on my birthday but the menu was underwhelming with limited, sparse selection except for the overpriced tasting menu, wines outrageously priced and the room cold and sterile - but a good match for the food. I get the freshness issue but portions tortureously tiny (which is ok given their tastelessness except for the oversalting). Braised hake was an unsightly tube of white steamed fish which had the shape of what it looked like - canned steam white fish. Accompaniment of "vegetables with shell fish" was really corn kernels, Lima beans (all nice and bright, seemingly fresh - all 6 pieces of thm) and the "shell fish" was a single mussel sans shell. That mixture mouth puckering salty but it took 10 minutes for any server to return and when she did advised I couldn't eat it, my date already half way thru dinner but she grabbed the plate and returned 5 minutes later with the half eaten fish and a new layer of succotash. My dates "pig" was dry, tough and without flavor. Plain Jane white ficelle bread on table - so much for farm fresh abundance.  Servers professional but cold and almost non human with vacuous expressions.  Again, good fit for the whole place.  I was here some years ago and was equally underwhelmed. Had my date told me where we were going ( a very serious mistake on her part) I would have suggested somewhere else.   As I started with - perhaps a bad nite, but even the menu was cold and sparse.  Overpriced, underwhelming.

I found the food good but underwhelming after all the hype and recommendations/reviews that lead to making this reservation. There was nothing to complain about except for the price, I expected more. The service was great: cordial and attentive. However, it was just the food that left something to be desired. I was also very upset at my fish portion. I assumed my one tiny piece was the normal entree size for something of this nature. However, during my dessert, the woman seated to my left was brought the same fish entree and she had double the amount of fish that I did. If this had happened while I was still eating my entree I would've alerted my server. As it was, we were weary of the cramped space and wanted to get out of there.

If U're a Gourmand that really appreciates good atmosphere and service ..A white table cloth candle lit  small restaurant awaits you..Please do make a reservation for one of my personal choices in Manhattan...Blue Hill ..Its a treat..
I hope they are able to maintain this quality for a long time. Its not easy , I've seen so many great restaurants slip away from their standards over time .
I have my fingers and toes crossed 
If  driving..I suggest you arrive early and wait 5-10 minutes for a spot to open up on the street itself.   works for us every time.
The restaurant is below street level, behind the red velvet curtains...

The food is soooo Good !  xxoo

"It can't just be corn!" Said I incredulously.

"It's special corn." Said friend wisely.

"It's corn with a few spices." Said the waitress mysteriously.

Well, I want to know what spices they used to make the chilled corn soup so damn floral/aromatic. Or maybe, it was indeed just special corn???

And who knew a runny egg, corn and mushrooms could taste so divine? Forget about recreating it at home... It's probably special egg and special mushrooms, and "a few spices".

Order their pig dish. Whatever pig dish is on the menu, just order it. Thank me later.

Absolutely amazing food.  Everything is fresh beyond belief.  Reservations are hard to get, so try well in advance.  You won't be disappointed at the attention paid to preparation and presentation and the highly attentive service.  I've been several times and enjoy it immensely.

Farm to table excellence.  We had been eagerly awaiting our meal at Blue Hill and it ended up being one of the best meals we've had in town.  

With the high quality and freshness of the ingredients, you really can't go wrong with anything on the menu.  The restaurant is small and romantic.  I've got to admit that it burns me up a bit when two tops stacked upon each other have to be pulled out for us to sit down.  But, I'll deal with that for good food and it's sadly become the norm for most places.  Our server was spot on and helped us out with describing dishes and recommendations.  

THIS MORNING'S FARM EGG
FIRST OF THE SEASON SWEET CORN, CHANTERELLE MUSHROOMS AND HOMEMADE LARDO

STRING BEAN SALAD
PEACHES, CUCUMBERS, FAVA BEANS, PURSLANE AND WHOLE GRAIN MUSTARD

MAHI MAHI
WARM TOMATOES, CUCUMBERS AND BASIL 

RAVEN AND BOAR'S PIG
HOMEMADE LARDO, STRING BEANS, TARRAGON AND ALMONDS

BEETS

I've fancied egg dishes lately, and this one was amongst the best.  I also very much enjoyed the pig that the waitress raved about.  I got to taste both the salad and fish that my wife had and those were fantastic too.  Beets were great and I managed to eat those without staining my clothes.  We finished with a cherry dessert that we devoured.  

Intimate and outstanding.  Blue Hill knocked it out of the park.

I have been lucky enough to have been here twice now, both at the recommendations of my long time NY'er EV friends. If you have the means and the money to order the tasting menu + the extended Chef's signature menu, the homemade pasta and a trio of pork are two additional entrees to this magnificent feast that you will not want to miss.

Then, accompany it with the alternative beverage pairing consisting of cocktails, beer + wine--and you've found your favourite meal in NY. It might not make the Yelp "top" list, but I'm certain it's b/c it's a low key locals' place where you have to be in the know. The additional tasting menu add-ons were the best part of the meal and although I rarely drink beer or cocktails, I would order this pairing again without hesitation.

Ensure that you reserve well in advance (about a month) and if the weather is nice enough, try to sit in the back patio area. Even many locals have told me that they didn't realize they offer a small, intimate patio and it makes your experience that much better. 

The hostess and server were  friendly and informative and the entire meal was intimate, tasty and wonderful. I have done many tasting menus in my time--especially in NY--and this was certainly the most unique if not the best. 

The only downside to this entire meal was the Southern transplant and her friend. They made the entire life stories known to everyone in the restaurant and I felt as if I was witnessing The Nanny Diaries, live.  Although their two unfortunate husbands were sitting closer to me, I did not hear these poor men's voices the entire time over the loud talk of their two entitled wives. The saving grace was that they opted not to order the tasting menu so were finished their meals before us. The entire patio including the server almost cheered upon their departure, since the air of relief was palpable. That was a funny part of this meal that I'll never forget and I thought that I should warn you about the potential "atmosphere". 

It was truly a wonderful bday and one of my top meals in NY, if not the top, even for my second visit. 
*Note* Some of the locals tell me that the Blue Hill upstate is even better which is almost unfathomable. Perhaps next time I will make the trek there, too.

The original blue hill restaurant, opened in 2000, it is hidden 3 steps below street level and occupies a "speakeasy" just off of Washington square park. The menu showcases local food from producers who respect artisanal techniques. Guests can choose from the regular menu or op for the Farmers Feast a five course tasting inspired by that particular weeks Harvest. Seasonal American is at its best here!

It's delicious.  Super fresh food not overly prepared.  The wine list is well organized.  Maybe some people are put off by the White table cloth decor, but doesn't this city have enough bare wood type places with the Stereo cranked up to 11?   As opposed to at Stone Barn I really appreciate that the menu here doesn't require several hours and a chefs tasting menu.   It's nice to be about to get an app, a main, and maybe split a desert on a random night.  Highly recommended.

Wow!  Wow!  Made reservations a week prior to surprise my wife for our anniversary. We flew out from sf just to eat good seasonal food. They made us feel very important, and the quantity and quality of the meal was second to none. We have ate at many nice restaurants around the world, and last nights experience was on top of the list. Amelia was our server, and she did an amazing job while teaming with the kitchen to bring out the dishes. The feast (10 or so special items) only took about 2 and a half hours to enjoy, compared to Manersa's 5 hour delayed out experience of 6 rich items. Worth the one day flight just to try this place.

I have yet to eat at this restaurant so my rating isn't exactly fair however, the customer service I experienced while trying to book a reservation was a bit lacking. I think diners should know that in order to book a dinner reservation at Blue Hill, expect to do so at least a month in advance. That is often normal for a popular New York City restaurant but you must also plan to call at EXACTLY 10:00am a month before you hope to dine - this is when their phone lines open! 

I attempted to make a reservation a few weeks ago for a date in August and was told they take reservations a month prior to the reservation date. That was all the information I was given - I told the host I would call a month prior and she told me that would be fine. 

I called at 11:00am, exactly one month before I was hoping to reserve a table and was told they were booked that evening! The host followed up by saying "our phone lines open at 10:00am." I certainly wish the host I originally spoke to would have mentioned that I should call back as early as 10:00am one month before I wish to dine. This would have been EXTREMELY helpful information.

I worked as a host and a server for over 10 years. I honestly believe that restaurant patrons underestimate the work that individuals in the service industry provide - they have very tough jobs and should be appreciated for all they do. When taking reservations, I constantly made sure my patrons got all the answers they needed regarding what they should expect. I wish Blue Hill would have done the same; first impressions are key!

One of the best meal I've had in NYC. The service is very friendly and extremely helpful with suggestions. The space itself is just so so in the main area (standard white table cloth) but a little more interesting in the small back area where we ate (and Japanese gardenesque). My friend had the cauliflower steak (delicious) and I had the pork (several types - some good, some too fatty for me). We shared several sides which were all fantastic, particularly the beets (best I've ever had). We had the bread pudding for dessert (okay, not special).
Another great NYC restaurant for foodies who like to shop in the Greenmarket. The quality of the food is amazing. They do a great job of letting the food "speak for itself".

5 stars for service for sure. These folks know how to keep you comfortable. The lowered rating is shockingly for their food. After all the hype the quality (not to mention quantity) of the food really fell flat. 
        A close friend had given my wife and I a gift certificate for our wedding gift. We wanted to use all of the certificate because we were leaving NYC. There was plenty on the certificate, yet we left very hungry. After arriving we ordered some drinks and a small starter, one that I'd heard so much about, the vegetables on a fence. It sounded much cooler than what it actually was. It's a giant wooden plank with nails driven into it and then on the nails are the most minuscule vegetables you've  ever seen. My wife hid her head in my shoulder because she was laughing, which caused me to laugh. The man next to us wasn't laughing though, because he had ordered the same thing. We both busted out in laughter as the man bit into a miniaturized piece of romaine lettuce, looked into the distance contemplative, and then shifted his head and explained "Delicious". Which made us both lose it!!!!!! My beer was another disappointment, they have a small beer list with very few good beers,  mostly stuff with around 70-85 scores on ratebeer (which isn't bad but isn't great either). My wife's wine was excellent though. The bread they served wasn't that good at all, I can bake much better at home which doesn't say much considering this is supposed to be a stellar restaurant. Our main courses were again miniature, it's not they weren't delicious or cooked perfectly it simply wasn't enough to fill two adults stomachs. Dessert was the high point, thankfully there was one. We shared the chocolate bread pudding which was very good, but once again I can cook it as well at home and there is something disappointing about eating at such a nice place and not receiving mind blowing food. As I mentioned service was never an issue, it's the food and portions I have trouble with. I understand and appreciate the nod to local providers and the use of fresh organic ingredients, but if you can't use all of that to create plates that will fill up healthy slim adults its all for naught.
        If you're planning a special occasion dinner I'd try places like Gothams, Bouley, Daniel, or some of the other high profile French/ New American places instead.

Blue Hill definitely did not meet expectations. I went here with a friend without a reservation so we ate at the bar. I definitely felt that because of our young age (mid 20s) and my being relatively underdressed (still presentable) we were given a lower caliber of service. The hostess did not greet us immediately, we has to remind them to bring a dish, and we were not doted on at a place as expensive and reputable as Blue Hill. 

Our appetizers and starters were great but our entree was mediocre. We ordered lamb and while it was cooked well the sauce and sides did very little to augment the flavored and texture. Give me a piece of farm raised lamb and a meat thermometer and I would have easily been able to replicate the best parts of the dish. 

The decor is stuffy and old-- not at all what you would expect from a farm to table restaurant. The staff also seemed to be lacking character and enthusiasm for their jobs. I love going to restaurants where wait staff love what they do and here it felt like it was just a job for them. 

I would go here again but only if someone else pays!

"Woah everyone is so old!" That was my first impression of Blue Hill. Ok now I'm in my mid 20's, but Blue Hill has got to loosen up a bit. With their farm to table style, I expected something more rustic and laid back--but Blue Hill is very much a white tablecloth kinda place. Nothing wrong with that, but I do think it contradicts their philosophy and attracts a more "mature" crowd. So points off for atmosphere. 

The food was great, however, it's hard not to have great food when you give talented chefs superbly fresh ingredients. I do think Blue Hill relies too heavily on letting the ingredients "speak for themselves." While the ingredients are fresh, I found the concepts behind each dish to be uncreative and kinda boring. For me, I left Blue Hill wondering "Wait...what did we eat again?" 

I'd go back if I was invited, but Blue Hill just didn't leave much of an impression on me.

If the Blue Hill prices aren't prohibitive, then definitely give it a try and try everything!  Everything is flavorful and cooked to perfection.  There were combinations of foods I would never have dreamed of (sugar snap peas, wild watercress, american cheese hazelnuts and pickled ramps) and who has ever heard of emu egg pasta, but everything I tried was perfect.  Seriously.

I'll make this quick: completely disappointing. Food just not that good, especially considering the hefty price tag, one dish was inedible and had to go back to the kitchen. Service good but not especially friendly. Don't waste your money, there are plenty other amazing restaurants in NYC where you can spend this much money and have a much better meal.

Blue Hill.... Thank You!     You are amazing.  Every aspect of the dining experience was impeccable.  Service was professional to the Nth degree.   (I'm sorry I forget the names)...   To the GREAT Bartender.  (tall dark-haired lady).  The Maitre 'D/Manager....and the the Chef who showed me the kitchen.....  Thank you all for an amazing experience.    To Dan....thank you for your vision and passion.  What you've created is A-M-A-Z-I-N-G !!!!!      Food, service, experience...ALL 5 STARS.

Been to Blue Hill NY twice so far. The first time was a few years back, before it got to be so well known, and I have to say that I remember it fondly. Everything was cooked to perfection and the flavors were impressive. Dined here again a few weeks ago and was a little disappointed. While service was spot-on, the dishes left me a bit underwhelmed. Everything was good, but I just wasn't terribly impressed. We've been to the Blue Hill at Stone Barns as well, and I think the same problem applies to both. While the ingredients are the showstoppers here, everything was just a bit too simply prepared.

We enjoyed the lardo with toasted bread, and the unique spices/salts that accompanied them. I ordered a fish dish for my main, and JB ordered a pork duo of some kind. Both were cooked perfectly, and flavored nicely. Somehow, though everything was good, we just weren't blown away which we were expecting given all the write-ups recently, and my first memorable experience.

Blue Hill is all about fresh ingredients - getting food from local farms nearby and using seasonal ingredients to create a brand-new menu every day. It's also pretty hard to get a reservation at a regular dining time, so my fiancee and I came here for a 5:30 reservation this past Sunday. It's got a very intimate feel given the relatively small dining room, the exposed brick, the low ceilings, and the slightly-below ground level location. That said, it has a modern air about it, and it's very good for low-key dinners with close friends and family. Our servers were very friendly, refilling our bread and water frequently, and giving us enough time between courses to savor each.

Although there is a seasonal 5-course (or an extended 7-course) tasting menu, we decided to stick with ordering an appetizer and entree, with dessert to share at the end. For appetizers, we went with the farm egg and the sage sausage. The egg is incredibly fresh - you can definitely tell the difference between an egg that was (probably) laid the same day and one that's been sitting in the grocery store a little bit. It tastes delicious poached, particularly with the morsels of bacon and the kale, which is a very plain vegetable on its own but works well with this dish. The sage sausage has a good dosage of herbs in it, but it's also freshly prepared, giving it a much better flavor than most sausage. It's also paired with a parsley-infused mustard, which helps add an additional kick to the plate. My fiancee got the duck for an entree, which is very well-done - extremely tender cuts of breast cooked just the right amount. The purple potato gnocchi is a cool twist on an Italian dish; the potato wrapped around the ricotta is very distinctive, but also light, which I appreciated. The slices of pork belly were delicious; it's extremely fatty and succulent, but the edges are slightly charred, giving it a nice, distinctive texture. We finished up with two desserts (even though we only ordered one - it was on the house)...strawberries paired with almond cake and buttermilk sorbet, and an apple cobbler of sorts (that was prepared more like a mochi cake). Both were really good and very light; in particular, I appreciated that the strawberries were real (i.e. they were the sizes of berries, not the oversized monstrosities you see in the supermarket), and the apple garnish with the cobbler was pure apple - no added sugar, just the rich flavor of the fruit itself.

To be honest, I would say that I've probably been to restaurants that get a little more creative with their food, but it's hard to get any fresher - and as a result, food that tastes really, really good - than Blue Hill. Everything is delicious, and you really do feel like you're eating something that came to you straight from the fields of a farm. I'd love to come back again, given that the menu changes every day based on availabilities.

I was so terribly dissapointed in this place that it saddens me. I was really expecting a wonderful joyful meal, but unfortunately that wasn't the case. My friend and I both had the tasting menu. At first I thought, "maybe I'm being too harsh," but then my friend confirmed that it was "obviously terrible." Neither of us liked a single item off the tasting menu. I don't know if they just changed their tasting menu right before we got there, but as the night went on, it just got worse. It could be that they were very busy, but not a single time did our waitress ask "how is everything," and we had to ask for bread 4x until it was finally brought out. Also the menu was never discussed with us, as usually does happen at Michelin star restaurants.

First came the soft shell crab which tasted like a deep fried crab with a slightly orangey flavor. I did not like the combination. Second came this almost raw egg in a green overly salty asparagus soup. Third was 1 small slice of lamb, most of it being fat and also too salty. (I have quite a high salt threshold compared to all my friends so if I say it's salty, it's SALTY). Fourth was a dessert which pretty much tasted like thinly sliced strawberries in a vanilla like pudding. Fifth was a small scoop of ice cream over this tangy fruit and goat cheese. I don't recall the exact fruit because as they were describing each dish, their voices were so soft it was almost inaudible. Each serving of food was SO tiny and took so long in between dishes. I became full despite the tiny amount of food because I waited so long for each dish, and during that time my stomach decided to tell my brain it was full. 

Maybe it was a stroke of bad luck, but my dining experience here was DEFINITELY not worth the HEFTY price tag paid. On a positive note, they do use farm fresh organic products.

If i had to pick between which was better, food or service, I'd pick service.
We started with bite sized asparagus burgers which were amazingly yummy, followed by Emu pasta and Tilefish with mustard greens.  Everything was creative and excellent!

Like everyone else said, expensive but very good. Portions don't seem very large but we walked out overstuffed. The chocolate bread pudding was incredible. The pig was excellent. The complimentary snack and dessert pieces were awesome. The service was perfect. Nice meal for a special occasion.

Love the stone barns view on food, fresh delicate and tasty.  I went here for a small graduation party held in the private back room (small but beautiful) food is delicious and you can tell yet take pride In the growing & raising of there produce and animals. It shows in the food.  Pricy but worth it for special occasions. Not much better then a fresh 24 hour old egg.
Must say the restaurant upstate is by at worth the trip. Still good but does not compare to tone barn at blue hill

Decided to take the Mrs. on a nice date for her birthday. This was most certainly a romantic and fun spot to go on a date. The staff was super friendly and helpful. The food was delicious. Great experience.

I dined here about a month ago with a group of friends. The farm to table concept is not new to me being a Californian, but they definitely got it right here. 

We started off with the veggies on the fence; I think it was called. It was delicious and had a cool presentation. For my entree I had the Risotto which was SO GOOD. Not too cheesy and heavy, just right. And the wine list was fabulous. 
This isn't a casual dining restaurant and the portion sizes are a bit shi-shi. But I didn't leave hungry either.

I've never liked chicken, but oh man the Hudson Valley Chicken dish here tastes divine!  It's incredibly tender, juicy, and silky -- it's what I imagine a unicorn would taste like.

Every single dish on the menu oozes freshness and delicate flavors. 

This is definitely one of my favorite restaurants in the city, and I can't wait to go back!

Blue Hill had been on my "list" for quite some time, and I had exceptionally high expectations. I was not disappointed in any way, everything about the meal exceeded my expectations.

We were seated in the garden room, which was preferable for me. It is brighter and roomier than the dining room.  

The amuse bouche was a beet burger on an almond bun, which was a delectable bite to say the least. I wanted another one...or three.  

We started out with "vegetables on a fence" as the appetizer. This cleverly presented course is served on a wooden block with nails presenting greens, radishes, carrots, cauliflower, and asparagus. Everything is mildly blanched. The lemon vinaigrette they use to poach the vegetables makes all the difference. The portion is small, but the flavors are huge.

Our entrée choices were lamb and pork. They were both exceptional, particularly the terrine and the sauce components. The fresh asparagus and fiddlehead offerings were perfect accompaniments as well.  

The lamb was hearty, perfectly cooked and rich with flavor and texture.  

The pork had four distinct meat components, each delicious in its own way.  

I had the Malbec at the urging of our server, who was attentive and very professional--but not overbearing. The gratis chocolates were dessert were the perfect ending to a truly transcendental meal.  

Blue Hill is top notch, across the board, in every respect. Five stars...

Perfect service. 
Cod fish head- taken off the bill because it was extremely salty 
The rest of the food was divine. The fresh greens were so sweet, so intense, so yummy!

It would be hard for anyone to write a bad review about this place.  I had one of the best meals I can remember here.

The server was friendly, helpful, and not as stuffy as I'd been expecting given the menu prices.  The food was great - not mind-blowing, mind you - but great.  I had the extended sampler dishes and got the beet salad, hake, cauliflower steak, risotto, pork belly, and gnocchi.  The pork belly was phenomenal; the others were "just" great.  The dessert was the best of all, though - it was a beer float with ice cream and, well I'm not exactly sure what else - maybe crack - but it was AWESOME.  If you go here and do not have this, you suck at life.

Note also that a meal here takes about 3 hours, which is probably why it took so long to find a reservation time.  I went at 8pm during a weeknight, so I was actually hoping the courses would come out quicker because I was starving.  

Now I want to try their brunch, which I've heard is one of the best in the city.

Fantastic restaurant, service is flawless, atmosphere is very intimate and romantic.  If you want to impress a special someone, take him/her here!

My husband and I ate here last Saturday evening.  We were 10 minutes late for our reservation, but they didn't bat an eyelash - totally fine.  Like I said, the service is absolutely flawless and not at all pretentious, all the good, and none of the bad.  Knowledgeable staff, perfect timing, answered all our silly questions and suggested an amazing wine for my husband.

We wanted to try what was good, and contemplated the farm feast tasting menu for $85 per person, but we remembered that Blue Hill at Stone Barns up in Tarrytown actually has a vegetable tasting menu so we asked if they could do something similar - to our delight, they could!  We started with a farm snack of frog legs (oh the irony!) which were tender and delicious, served with a green garlic sauce.  As for the tasting menus... welllllll... honestly, while the food was very good, we weren't THAT impressed with what was served to us.  The first dish was a pretty simple salad with a side of this green garlic (again!) soup.  The second dish was chickpeas and these crispy greens, with more green garlic (again!), and then we had a buttery grain/risotto type of thing with soy beans which was phenomenal.  I guess I just expected more innovative dishes, but that's not to say that any of it was bad.  We just probably should have gone with the regular tasting menu.  The desserts were awesome - candied pumpkin seeds and these dark chocolate hazelnut balls, then we had this buttermilk sorbet foamy type of thing (sorry, hard to explain), and then a beer float which was, hmmm, kind of interesting.  I didn't like the first two bites very much, but stuck with it and it grew on me.  It is what it sounds like - beer and ice cream with some bits of other stuff down in there - no complaints here though.  Their cocktails are AWESOME - I had a "noble bee" and was really pleased with it.

The only downer about the night was that there was a really obnoxious group at the table next to us.  They seemed drunk and were very loud.  There was a lady in the group who straight up screamed about her husband pissing on her in the shower which was pleasant.  I'm so glad she shared that with the restaurant.  We weren't the only ones annoyed, so I said something to the server, and a minute later the hostess came by offering us another table.  I explained that they were disturbing several tables, not just ours, and a few minutes later, I saw a gentleman approach the table and tell them to keep it down.  They left shortly after, and I could enjoy my conversation with my husband again.  The hostess later brought us a couple of glasses of dessert wine to make up for it, which was appreciated.  As we were getting ready to leave, another obnoxious LARGE group came through from the back - they seemed like young trust fund NYU students who were on their way to the meatpacking district and were stumbling around and yelling.  I know that the restaurant doesn't have much control over this, but my suggestion would be to avoid this place on a Saturday night, unless you can get a reservation before 9pm. 

The price was a little shocking, given that they charged us for a regular farm tasting menu - we expected it to be slightly less as it is at Stone Barns, but whatever, perfectly good experience and I'm glad I finally tried the NYC restaurant.  I still say Stone Barns is WAYYYYYY better though.  It's worth the trip to Tarrytown if you ever get the opportunity.

It's a little hard to write this review because I am afraid it is going to just sound like this:

"OhmygodSOAMAZINGohmygodDELICIOUSandPERFECTandGAHHH."

And that wouldn't be very constructive. So let me do my best and hopefully it'll be in English...but the food is good enough at Blue Hill to have anyone writing and speaking gibberish. Emma G. and I have been planning our Grad School Restaurant Reward Meal since late 2011, and after much deliberation, we settled on Blue Hill. The only reservation we could get on a Saturday was at 5:30 p.m. and  considering neither of us are crazy night owls, this suited us just fine. 

The restaurant is located just off Washington Square Park in a beautiful brownstone, on the ground floor. You step down several steps and then open a door and pull back the curtain to reveal a peaceful, simple, classy dining room. It's small, but not cramped. The hostess took our coats and we were led to our table. First off, the menus are beautiful inside and out. That's not some joke about inner beauty. They're actually gorgeous cloth-covered books that have a nice weight to them. (I never realized that this was something that mattered to me, but Blue Hill did it so nicely.)

We started out with glasses of champagne to toast our future status as Doctor and...Counselor? Esquire? Whatev. M.D. + J.D. what up! I don't like to pretend that I am any kind of expert when it comes to champagne, but even I could tell that this was a fine, complex glass. It was fragrant and fruity while still dry. We moved on to the Vegetables on a Fence, which was probably the best-presented item of the night. Seriously, this would be THE BEST way to get children to try vegetables. Push them onto a "fence" made of pins and a polished block of wood (and make sure they don't prick their fingers). All of the baby carrots and darling pieces of romaine and adorable radishes were so fresh and so good. This is what crudites are supposed to taste like.

We shared two appetizers - the first of the season spring vegetables, and the emu egg pasta. The former was good but somewhat unremarkable - lightly cooked spring vegetables sprinkled with lemon juice. But the emu egg pasta blew my mind. It was served with "immature egg", shittake mushrooms, and ramps. I learned from the waiter that an immature egg is the egg before it has separated into yolk and white, and they take that little egg and basically pickle it until it's hard, like a small round of cheese. Bear with me, since I know this sounds weird. The waiter took the little round and grated it onto the pasta, much like fresh Parmesan.   AND IT WAS DELICIOUS. It truly added an umami element to the pasta. The noodles were clearly hand-made, chewy and slightly sweet and delicious.

Then, the entrees. I got the Blue Hill Farm Pig served with rutabaga, pickled plums, and walnuts. Emma had the Grass-Fed Lamb with braised red cabbage, beets, walnuts, and wood ear mushrooms. Both dishes involved 4 cuts of meat. Let me just say that again. Each dish let you try FOUR cuts from the pig/lamb. Each cut tasted so distinctly different and was so flavorful and...clean. That's the thing. The meat was so rich and full of taste that it didn't need glazes or sauces to abundance. It spoke for itself. I guess that's part of what farm-to-table is about, and I like it. The platings were just gorgeous, too.

Now, I usually don't order dessert in restaurants, but the celebratory nature of this dinner called for it. She had the Chocolate Bread Pudding with Salted Caramel, Pine Nuts, and Cocoa Nib ice cream. It was chocolate-y and rich while still spongy and light, and the pine nuts complemented the chocolate flavor PERFECTLY. Now, not to take away from all of the dishes I've just described, but my dessert was not only my favorite dish of the night but also one of the top 5 desserts I've eaten at a restaurant, EVER. Yeah. I went there. It was a fromage blanc souffle with wild blueberry preserve, yogurt, and pink peppercorn ice cream. The souffle looked like a perfectly flattened circle of marshmallow, quavering atop a thin layer of shortbread. It melted in my mouth. It tasted like happiness and dreams and...okay, it was just reaaaaallly good. The sweet-tart blueberries were a perfect pairing, and that PINK PEPPERCORN ice cream really knocked my socks off. Amazing.

Blue Hill, as cliche as it sounds, can be as much of an experience as it is a meal. The wait staff and the chefs clearly take such pains to make it a pleasant evening for their guests, and we felt well taken care of. The amuse-bouche before the meal (a tiny little beet burger) and after (candied sunflower seeds and chocolate covered hazelnuts) just rounded out the experience and made us feel like we were someplace special.

Which we were. Blue Hill is pretty darn special.
One of the elite top-tier restaurants that deserves its sterling reputation.  Great ambiance, well-prepared fresh food, and consistent service.

I don't know how she did it but my sister managed to score a reservation at Blue Hill on a Saturday Night... that morning.

This restaurant isn't stuffy but it is definitely classy.  
What do I mean?  Dress and act accordingly but don't put too much pressure on yourself.  I felt a bit underdressed but the woman at the table next to us was fighting non-stop with her date about his terrible behavior.  ---Weird, but onto the more important things.

The service was wonderful, warm, and superb.  
Our waitress was well informed about every dish and was not afraid to give us her opinons regarding her favorites.  
Wines by the glass are small in number and very pricey, but tasty.

Portions might seem small but in truth are fairly and artfully sized.  
You might clean your plate but you won't leave hungry.

Food is not over salted or over seasoned which was wonderful!!!

The table next to us ordered side dishes of the risotto and a few other grain-based main courses.  If we had known this was a possibility we might have done the same thing.  I recommend asking if their is flexibility and ordering side dish sized portions of the grain-based mains like the risotto!!

Enjoy.  This will be a special meal and I know I would go back but only for a special occasion.  The bar was weirdly empty though the hostess told us that it is usually full.  It is an expensive meal though, to have sitting at a bar.


Food Specifics below:

Corn soup- not the most velvety, sweet soup but more of a savory, thin soup.   Enjoyable but not crazy outstanding.

Sausage plate- on the small side but sufficient.  Flavors were diverse and complex, loved, LOVED, this dish.

Chicken- my sister enjoyed the tender, juicy meat and ate her whole dish.

Lamb- best prepared lamb I have had in my entire life.  The lamb portion was more than enough for one person, and was outstanding.  OUTSTANDING.  The folks at the table next to us ordered the lamb and were in complete agreement with us.

Jerusalem artichokes, sunchokes- delicious,

Dinner at Blue Hill on Saturday, March 16, 2013. 

Blue Hill, New York, NY
Food: Seasonal American.
http://www.bluehillfarm.com/food/blue-hill-new-york

Overall: 7.0/10 vs. restaurants priced $$$$/5.
Ambiance: Good. 
Food: Very Good. 
Service: Exceptional.
Wine/Drinks: Exceptional. 
My rating scale: Exceptional, Very Good, Good, Ok, Needs Improvement, Terrible. 

Ambiance: Blue Hill hits on all cylinders elsewhere, but it falls short in the ambiance category. The restaurant at times feels slightly crammed. Don't expect any views due to it being semi-submerged. Blue Hill could stand to improve upon it's entry way, which is quite tiny and upon entering one feels thrust on top of the patrons at the bar. Also important to note, the curtain to keep out the cold doesn't really function and two diners asked to switch tables due to the draft and several others were clearly bothered by the cold, so sit away from the door. In regards to design, the interior is very well done in a modern style. An often underrated characteristic is comfort and here Blue Hill gets it right, the chairs are extremely comfortable.

Food: Elegantly displayed. Small portions. Some exotic selections available. 

Service: Top notch all around. The staff is very well trained, attentive, pleasant, and there are an appropriate number of people to make for an enjoyable evening.

Wine/Drinks: Exceptional wine list.

Overall comments: Blue Hill gets a high rating based on my criteria above, but I must admit, on March 16th it fell short of my possibly unfair high expectations. I've been to Blue Hill a few times before and it seems it's best during the summer months when the fresh vegetables from its garden in Westchester are in season; this is what really sets it apart from its competitors. I recommend Blue Hill for an elegant, quiet, one on one dinner; avoid large groups.

www.JustAGuyThatLovesFood.blogspot.com

I just don't get it. While the place is very nice and the bar tender helpful and passionate, once we left the bar to be seated the disappointments started. Vegetables on a fence? 3 slices of radish, a leaf of lettuce and 2 micro carrots on a block of wood and nails? Really? Well, my Berkshire pork belly app was coming so I didn't say much. Well the best way to describe my app was a 2 " piece of pure fat. How does that leave the kitchen? They graciously replaced it with emu egg pasta that was so salty I'm still drinking water 4 hours later. Next the BLACK CREAMY RICE LOCAL SHELLFISH, OCTOPUS, SHRIMP AND SQUID Came to the table cold. sent it back and the new one could be best described as what looked like an oil spill in the gulf with dead miniature crustaceans floating in a stringent black mess. I sent it back and just ate the great bread for dinner. At least the deserts were good. It's nice to have local food but they should consider tweezers instead of forks and substance and flavor instead of eclectic plating. My guests and I agreed that this was more of a mystery basket from Chopped than something you'd see on Top Chef.  HUGE LET DOWN!!!

n our week long trip to New York we wanted to do one fine dining experience. After looking at the amazing diversity and choices NY has to offer, we picked this little restaurant. Fresh produce, directly from the farm, nice for the wallet (nicer then WD50 and sorts) and the reviews were overall really good.

The restaurant is pretty small and the tables are close to each other. Since we had a late reservations the tables next ours were empty. Don't know about the dining experience when it's packed. Must be like sitting on each others lap.

The menu looked nice and the prices seemed kind. Wines were pretty expensive, but we're used to that in New York. We ordered a snack (as amuse), appetizers, an entree and cheese as dessert. For drinks we had half glasses of pairing wine.

The snack was nice, root vegetables stacked on pins with a bit of sour dressing. It wasn't special, but tasted good. Thing that ruined it a bit was the sand that was left on the vegetables. We told our waitress, and we got a full new rack of vegetables, which was top service to us.
As appetizer we had chicken and pork sausage. The chickenliver was undercooked for me, but the rest was really nice, so we didn't make the effort. The sausage was a collection of 3 different types. The portion was perfectly sized and the sausages were delicious. Unfortunately the horseradish looked like coleslaw, which gave a really hot and unpleasant surprise. Although it was mentioned on the menu, it would have been nice if they'd included this salad in the explanation of what was on the plate.
For the entree we had venison and pork. The venison was really good. Cuisson was spot on and the beet root sauce delicious. The pork was a little bit disappointing. Tasted good but was drowned in horseradish (again) sauce, lacked finesse and needed a bit more vegetables.
The cheese was really good and the tawny port was a very good chose to go with it.
Wines were the best we had in New York and the paired perfect with the food. 
Service was really good, but with 11 people walking around 11 tables was a bit of an overkill. 

If the prices were a bit cheaper this could have been the place to go. But since they are pretty steep, you tend to expect more. Also there could be a bit more creativity and finesse in the food for our standard. We've had a wonderful experience though, especially since our (first) waitress was genuinely kind and service minded.

My neice took me here while I was attending NYFW (2/10/13), getting a table here was tough, and its even tougher to add in 2 more people.  My neice is in to organic foods and all the foods here came from Blue HIll farm.  We had a great table for 6 in the middle of the restaurant, the waiters were ok because we didn't complain there.  Most of the entrees were organic vegatables, a lot of pork, & chicken dishes, 1 veal dish & maybe 2 fish dishes.  We had 6 people so we ordered like 12 different appetizers and entrees, plus 3 desserts, so we tasted pretty much all the dishes there.  When the appetizers came out, we all noticed that the food was very very little for the $15-$20, example the cabonara, there was less than an ounce of noodles, it looked like a little hummingbird's nest, lol, the beet sliders were 3 little buns with beets instead of burgers, and they were the size of a quarter, not even your average 2" buns.  The entrees was a little more food considering the price is in the upper $35-$55, but its still very little food, my veal dish had about 8 thin slices of veal on vegetables and even the vegetables were tiny portion.  I don't like chintzy, tiny portions.  Most of the entrees regardless if its pork, fish, veal, all had this brown sauce very very salty, don't get me wrong I like asian foods so I'm used to salt and sauces but their brown sauce was almost too too salty not edible.  But I have to give them credit for cooking the chicken, fish & veal to perfection, downfall was too salty sauce.  Don't order the roast pork, the skin was so tough and hard, it will cut your gum, they don't have it down like the crispy skin roast pork in Chinatown, and you are paying 5 times more.  The atmosphere was dark & dim, and nice, maybe the chef was just heavy handed that night.  I don't know if i would come back here.
