Words would not do this place justice. I personally recommend the the extended Farmers Feast, which adds two additional savory course and it's worth every cent. I can't give you an idea of what you would find on the tasting menu, as it changes often, as it the idea of Chef Barber. All I can promise you is an experience you won't soon forget and a night you'll only regret if you don't come with an open pallet.

I wasn't sure what to expect upon walking in to the minimalist interior (clean and simple), but it was a fantastic experience from the customized customer service, attentiveness, and fresh, delicious, artistic / artisinal, seasonal, and creative dishes. Eating here has enhanced the way I think about and make vegetables in my own kitchen. Eat here if you want a completely new and fresh take on veggies. The menu was completely customized to my likes, dislikes, and sensitivities, and it was excellent. The only place they could improve is on the dessert - the apple tartine was good but not great. All of the small dishes that came in between the big dishes were delectable - especially the vinaigrette veggies on a fence (what this place is known for too), mini beet burgers (that looked and tasted like delicate macarons), vegetable salts, and other special details.

I came here on a date with the woman the day after Valentine's Day to avoid the overpriced menus that most restaurants peddle out on V-day.

I'll start out with the positives which are many:

-wine selection, we thought they had a unique wine selection
-The chef selected mini courses in-between our appetizers, main course and dessert which were unique and complementary to what we were about to eat.
-The best breadsticks or mini baguettes we have ever had.

On top of that, below is the list of appetizers and main dishes we ate and the stars we would give them:

-Chickpea fries (4 stars): Loves the display and the sauce, wish there had been more of them.  A unique take much like the other dishes we had later in the meal.
-Chicken wings, hearts and livers (4.5 stars): The livers were like the perfect pate and the hearts had the texture of grilled calamari although I would admit that eating a heart feels primal.
-Morning Egg (3 stars) Really liked it, but wish there had been more lobster.
-Hake (5 stars) Perfectly cooked, very light flavors
-Pig (5 stars) 3 different cuts all with unique texture and taste, all seemingly better than the last.
-Chocolate bread pudding (5 stars) A refreshing twist on a predictable option. 

An easy 5 stars for me given the strength of the main courses and the unique take on otherwise predictable sounding dishes.  In terms of new American cuisine, I'd have to put it below the slightest notch below Gramercy Tavern simply because we did not have a muffin to take home with us :).
Great food, service, at reasonable prices. Good for dates, casual or romantic. Great for conversations. Attentive and friendly service.

Best meal I've had in the city.

Venison
Pig liver terrine
Fromage blanc souffle

All MUST orders

Get:
~chickpea fries (5 stars): with smoky aioli. Came in a log stack of 6, beautifully presented. Perfectly crispy on the outside, creamy on the inside. $8
~anything with pork belly in it: we had this as a component of a dish on the tasting menu, and it is the best pork belly I've ever had. Skin was (again) perfectly crisp, and the rest just melted, with so much pork flavor.
~chicken wings, livers, and hearts (4.5 stars): wings were cut up with (again) perfectly crispy skin and tender juicy meat. Livers were seared and melted in your mouth, no graininess at all. Hearts were grilled and were possibly the best chicken hearts I've ever eaten. Paired with a sauce of hazelnuts and pickled vegetables. $18
~venison tartare (4 stars): just chunky enough while still melting in your mouth. Paired with crisped toast, mustard, mushroom "pate," and couscous. Also came with pickled vegetables, which I loved. They're just briny enough while letting the vegetable flavor to shine. $25
~chocolate bread pudding (4 stars): one the best chocolate bread puddings I've every had. The top was crispy (running theme here), with a surprise center of salted caramel and pine nuts. I don't normally order something like this, but this was exceptionally delicious. Paired with tonka ice cream. $12

Skip:
~tasting (4 stars): don't get me wrong, the tasting was very lovely. But there are so many other components of the menu that I would love to try! It was a great way to get to know Blue Hill, and it definitely makes me want to return.  Highlights included the pork belly and apple dessert. $85 for 5 courses

Drinks:
~we opted for the non-traditional pairing with the tasting (4.5 stars), which included wine, beer and a cocktail. Overall they all paired extremely well, and it was a really fun way to explore their drink menu. $60

For free:
~bread: warm, came in a glass.
~spreads of lardo and butter, both amazing.  I couldn't decide which I liked better!
~salts: of beet (my favorite), celery, and carrot.
Be careful, because these were all so tasty that I almost filled up on these in between courses!
~amuse 1: mini-beet sliders on cornbread buns. Couldn't get enough.
~amuse 2: coppa. So smoky!

Service:
5 stars. Napkins were folded within 10 seconds of one of us leaving the table! Even though the place had gotten pretty busy by the time we were mid-way through our meal, our glasses were always full. When one of our courses came a bit after the paired drink was poured, our server came and topped it up.

Would not hesitate to come back! Perhaps we can make it one day upstate to their farm.

I was so excited to eat at Blue Hill, but it was horrible.  The food was sub-par and the presentation was stupid.  Our waitress was so horrible, it was humorous.  She brought the wrong entree out, then confessed to having never have tried it in the first place, and suggested the worst wine I had ever tasted.  The worst part had to have been the argumentative waitress, however, whether or not we were forced to eat food we did not order, it was horrible.

We came here for a special occasion and Blue Hill did not disappoint.

We started off with two farm snacks: 1) potato balls, toasted seeds and nuts and 2) Lardo, bell pepper-flavored butter, dill powder, and carrot salt. The potato balls were good, but nothing special in my opinion. By contrast, the other farm snack was extremely tasty and memorable. I actually saw the four colorful components on small white square plates on many other tables, so I inquired about it with our waitress and added it to our order. Again, this is highly recommended, especially with the delicious bread.

For appetizers, we ordered farm egg yolk carbonara. I was more than surprised when I realized that this dish did not taste like pasta at all. I learnt the lesson that carbonara really referred to the sauce only, and it was served with celery. The dish was good, but my disappointment did not allow me to fully appreciate it. Plus, the portion was tiny.

For main courses, we opted for boar's pig I and boar's pig II, which was as good as expected. Pig I was primary cuts, salsify, walnuts, and lardo. Pig II was secondary cuts, root vegetables, Brussels sprouts, and horseradish. Both dishes were very tasty.

We concluded our meal with the Bosc pear dessert, which consisted of an olive oil cake, brown butter, and toasted almond ice cream.

Altogether, we had a pleasant experience here, the ambience is elegant, and service has been friendly and efficient.

Hands down the best restaurant in NYC and, thereby, America.  The only better place might be Stone Barnes, but it's all one.  I've been so many times and there is so much I could say - if you care about fresh farm food, you won't find any better.  Especially the vegetables.  Amazing!  Just go!

This review is for Blue Hill at Stone Barns in Pocantico Hills. 

My boyfriend and I had a 9pm reservation at Blue Hill at Stone Barns on a Saturday night. We were surprised to find a last minute reservation on open table for such an ideal time. When we arrived, the valet gentleman asked our name and parked our car complimentary. The short walk to the restaurant was gorgeous. Dim lit lanterns and bare trees lined the walk way. Once we entered, the front desk immediately took my coat and asked for our names. Without checking the reservation book, they mentioned they were expecting us and sat us immediately (nice touch). We expected at least a 30minute wait at the bar, even though we were on time. I suppose the meat packing district has us jaded with wait times. We were located towards the back of the restaurant, with a full view of the venue. The building is European, without beams in the middle of the room. Our little booklet like menus were waiting for us on the table as we sat down. The booklet was more of a description of their seasonal vegetables, and sketches of the landscape rather than a menu. The menus were actually a sheer piece of paper (post it size) that simply contained the prices of the different courses. There is a 5 course, 8 course, and 12 course option with or without a wine pairing. We chose the 8 course without a wine pairing. The waitress discusses dinner options with you and gains insight on what you like/don't like. The chef then prepares a menu exclusively for your table. The portions were small of course but we were SO stuffed by the end of the meal. There were a lot of little extra appetizers that were provided as well. I never had to ask for another drink, and our table was always clean. Overall the experience was fantastic. My boyfriend and I travel to Vermont often for farm to table faire. Blue Hill is now our new go to place as it's only an hour away. Their menu changes with the season (as it should) so we're excited to return in the Spring. When we were finished with dinner and ready to leave, the front desk was awaiting with our Jackets in hand and our car out front. Nothing was needed on our end to make them aware. Attention to detail, fresh organic food, and consistent genuine service make this venue a must visit!

Blue Hill is my favorite restaurant in New York.  I haven't been to all the greats, but I've been to a lot of them and this is my #1.

The reason is that this place is the whole package.  Ambiance, service, creativeness of preparation and most importantly the quality of the ingredients.  It just doesn't get much better, particularly for the price, which I find to be a bargain relative to many of the other high-end restaurants in the city.

Blue Hill, the pre-eminent farm to table restaurant in Manhattan.  Difficult to get a reservation during the slow seasons, impossible to get into during the busy weekends.  Somehow by g-d's good graces, with just three weeks lead time we got a reservation at prime time Saturday night.  

 There are a lot of expectations that a restaurant has to live up to when it has a reputation like Blue Hill's.  It's perennial listed as one of the top twenty restaurants in Manhattan.  It's a leader in local and organic cuisine.  It has it's own farm just an hour outside the city, which encapsulates farm education, year round greenhouse growing and raising it's own animals from pigs and chickens all the way to bees.  One is going to this restaurant expecting to have their taste buds blown off their tongue.  Unfortunately this was not the case for the six of us last night.

 Overall, the experience was good, not great.  The room itself is small, but cozy and not overly loud.  Conversation was easily had without listening to the people at the next table.  Our server was incredibly attentive and there was a lot to pay attention to.  Between six people, we had a gluten allergy, a pescatarian (who does not eat shellfish), and a 'kosher-style' eater.  Our table had a question about every single dish, that our server was able to easily answer and accommodate.  She even picked up on the fact that it was my mother's birthday based on the conversation at the table.  

 Unfortunately, the service fell short during the pace of the meal.  People at a table should never be sitting around, wondering when their food should be coming out.  There were awkwardly long periods between the farm snacks, appetizers and main courses.  Our second bottle of wine was specifically ordered to go with the appetizer course, but was drained well before the appetizers arrived.  The only plus side to the waiting time was we got to gorge ourselves on warm baguettes and creamy butter.  When the main course arrived, some of the plates were lukewarm, while other were piping hot.  These issues made the meal feel out of sync.

 The food was not up to the level we expected it to be at.   From the outset, the menu lacked variety.  Pork is the hot meat in the country, but it is overkill to put it in 50% of the dishes that you offer.  The only meat alternative to pork was venison, everything else was fish or a vegetable dish.  A tight menu in a restaurant is fine, but repetitiveness on a small menu strikes of poor planning.

 There, however, were several highlights on the menu one would not want to miss.  The Farm Egg Yolk Carbonara, composed of celery root cut to replicate thin noodles looked and tasty wonderful.  The Sprouted Mung Beans, were cooked to perfection, mixed with pistachio nuts that added a welcome bit of crunchiness and salt to the plate.  Unfortunately, the Bacon and Pickled Peanut Tart fell short of the mark, being less of a tart and more of a crostini.  

 The mains suffered some of the same inconsistency as the aforementioned appetizers.  The venison was perfectly cooked, but slightly over salted, and unfortunately served cool..  The secondary cuts of pork was bursting with flavor, but some identification of the cuts presented would have been helpful.  The deserts on the whole were rather tasteless, with the crime of only one chocolate offering on the entire dessert menu.

 Overall, the experience did not live up to the high expectations we had at the outset.  We expected four stars across the board and received a solid two star experience.  It was an enjoyable and memorable night, serviced well by the restaurant, but not enhanced or elevated by the restaurant.

4.5 stars

I came here last night with my boyfriend and had a delightful experience. We loved our server Neil. He was so friendly, accommodating, and helpful.

We both got the Farmer's Feast. I substituted the scallops for the pig's liver and venison terrine, which was a mistake because I ended up liking the scallops and thought my substitution was the low point of the meal. The fresh farmer's egg was absolutely amazing. It was served with lobster and caviar--couldn't have been more perfect for us! The next course was lamb with vegetables. Delicious! I expected the portion of this to be slightly bigger, but I ended up being full by the end.

The dessert courses were fresh yogurt with honey and bread pudding (we asked for this because we heard it was so good.) Both desserts were good, but not exceptional. 

We also enjoyed our drinks very much.

The bread was amazing and I loved all the spreads and salts so much. Overall, it was a wonderful time and an excellent date spot.

This was my first experience at Blue Hill . My friends had gone to the Farm in Westchester and wanted to see what the NYC location had to offer. 

I had the Pig and Raven I and it was pretty amazing. I like my food to be on the heavier side of spice so I enjoyed the peppered seasoning. The hit to me though was the crispy pork belly. The flavor of the belly combined with a crispy skin gave me a Kool-Aid smile. 

My friends had the Striped Bass and the Raven and Boar's Pig II. The striped bass was perfectly cooked, light and well seasoned. The Pig and Raven II my friend has in my opinion wasn't as good. It also was not presented as elegantly as the P&R1.  It was more of a "hearty" type of presentation. 

In all if was a good restaurant, especially if you like organic, sustainable food.  Keep in mind if you choose to  go to this restaurant their whole concept is simplicity. Let the ingredients speak for themselves. I was told however the farm location in Westchester is far better. I guess I'll have to go and find out.
The most innovative, satisfying, and brilliantly flavored meal I've ever had. On par with 11 Madison Park and Per Se.

Blue Hill. Not that impressive. Yes it was fresh and pretty good, but I like the blue hill at stone Barnes in westchester a lot better. We ordered the pair and parsnip soup and it was excellent.

I ordered the pig and raven II because the portions were supposed to be more flavorable according to the waiter. It was so overwhelmingly saturated with pepper it was more like pork with peppercorns as to a pork dish with a light seasoning. Not thrilled with it. 

My friends had the stripped bass which was just ok. They blacken the fish to mark it on the grill leaving a charcoal cross pattern on the fish like a ny strip steak. Not a good idea because it leaves a overwhelming charcoal burnt taste to it as the dominant taste as opposed to a nice fresh fish dominant taste. Feel like why bother. I Did not like it.

My other friend ordered the pig and raven I so we could share. It was a little better then mine with the pork belly in a bigger portion but once again a disappointment . 

Ok  for the synopsis: good to great veggie dishes! But just good to better than average meat and fish dishes for the price. zagat gave it a 27. i would not argue with that but a 26 could be more fitting. Will not return to nyc location and would recommend it for veggie appetizers.

Ambience 8/10
Service 8/10
Food  7/10

My favourite restaurant of a week of eating at the best restaurants NYC has to offer including EMP, Atera, Le Bernardin and Marea. 

Every single dish we had was amazing (other than the blue fish toast which was not mediocre). The ingredients and flavours of every dish worked amazingly together. I think I had the best tasting beans I've ever had here - almost potato like in texture. The testa (fried head cheese) with homemade mustard was delicious. The ricotta served in the bread appetizer was one of the best fresh cheeses I've had.
The food was very good and the restaurant exceeded my expectations. Everything about my experience at Blue Hill was better than Hearth.

The menu is seasonal so I won't go overboard with describing a dish that you may never get to sample. In a nutshell, the food was whimsical and delightful--like my fiance and I needed a moment of silence after trying the pork belly appetizer delightful. As someone who has waited tables, I always appreciate good service but my expectations are generally just be nice, efficient and get the order right. At a place like Blue Hill, I had higher expectations and the service exceeded my expectations. It was professional, knowledgeable, friendly and spot on from the hostess, server, food runner, and manager. All stellar. My fiance and I went here to celebrate my birthday and as we were walking to the restaurant, we passed a pizza parlor. He said, "So this is where we'll go after dinner, right?" He assumed that the portions would be tiny and expensive. We had an appetizer and farmer's snack to share, an entree each and dessert and left quite satisfied. No pizza needed.

To beat the crowd, we had a 5pm dinner. We had a cozy corner booth seat. Everything and all the bites in between were top-tier. We were happy they allowed one of us to get the tasting menu, and the other to order a la carte so that we can try all different things on their menu (not all high-end dining establishments are OK with that). I got the a tasting menu. Some dishes included braised hake, "This Morning's Farm Egg," Berkshire pork that's cut/cooked five ways, and a sorbet. Some hors d'oeuvres included beet burgers and coppa. The bread they give is memorable mainly because it comes with lovely sides of lardo, homemade butter, ricotta, and carrot salt. We ordered the "Lady Apples" doughnut dessert with hazelnut ice cream, and I enjoyed it as well. It was a wholesome experience knowing that our food came from local sources.

This was my second Blue Hill experience, my first one being at Stone Barns a few years ago to celebrate my birthday. This time we were celebrating our engagement, and it was just as amazing. I absolutely love Blue Hill. Everything is perfect - ambiance, service, and food. Now on to the food. 

For starters, we had the vegetables on a fence and the chicken wings. The chicken was crispy and had a nice flavor. For our first course, Dan had the Cheese Pumpkin and Butternut Squash Soup and I had the Grey Mullet per our waiter's recommendation - just slightly seared with a smoky lemony flavor - delicious and a fish I had never actually tried before. Dan chose the Duck and I had the Venison (3 cuts) for our entrees. The Venison was prepared exactly right and the plate had so much flavor and depth. I tasted the Duck and it was also delicious, but I was too focused on my Venison to take note of much else.

We ended the meal with chocolate bread pudding, scotch and a cappuccino. The perfect meal for a very special occasion. Hope to be back soon!

Blown away. One of the best dining experiences in NYC so far - mouth-wateringly fresh seasonal ingredients combined in in the best possible manner. We started out light with some greens shiitake shrooms, then went on to a delectable porgy sprouts hazelnuts, and finished strong with farro quinoa venison risotto. Perfect climax, and the waitress was so kind to portion everything out between the 2 of us so we did not have to mess around at the table. Wine list is impressive and very much on the pricey side, but our $76 pinot noir was perfect and we got to taste it beforehand so we knew where we were going. Service was amazing too - fast, friendly, personalized (not supply chain style, as often happens). Perfect spot for a romantic date.

The food here literally melted in my mouth. Start with the egg for an appetizer, and get one per person (it's a little messy to share, and you're not going to want to). For the main course, we had the Raven + Boar's Pig, and the Apple. The name is confusing... it's not really a $45 Apple. In fact, it's an older cow that was first a dairy cow, and then a meat cow. You receive 3 different cuts of meat, and each is soo tender and flavorful. Our waitress was a complete gem, and we loved the sommelier; the entire experience was absolutely lovely.

My second experience at Blue Hill was just as amazing as the first. Food was exceptionally fresh and tasty, my parents were so impressed!

The vegetables on a fence had such a cute presentation, although it did feel a bit pricey for the amount of veggies we got. The grilled duck hearts were so tasty, that even those on my table that don't like offal enjoyed them! Chicken wings had a really nice flavor.

Can't beat the farm egg as a first course, but the Hudson Valley chicken liver was a nice alternative. For entrees, I loved both the boar and the duck. Both meats were cooked very nicely and I loved the sauces. I couldn't decide between them, so am glad that my dining companions were willing to share!

Chocolate bread pudding is definitely worth it if you aren't stuffed full by dessert. We got one for our table of five to split and we polished it off in just a couple of minutes. Everyone protested that they couldn't possibly do dessert, yet we somehow all managed a few bites!

Our waitress, Julia, was amazing and we were definitely impressed with the level of service, as well as the sheer number of staff working at an establishment so tiny. The thing about the service that stands out to me is that at the end of our meal, Julia handed me a copy of the menu since she noticed that I took a photo of EVERY course that came out. It's the little gestures like that which go a long way. Needless to say, I was really touched by her thoughtfulness.

No flash photography allowed and it's a pretty dimly lit restaurant so you'll need to bring the good low-light camera if you want good food photos.

There were a few dishes that had surprising/good elements. Otherwise, the experience was unexceptional.

Tiny beet hamburgers simulated the hamburger experience incredibly well. Juicy beet with a hint of pickle up front, then a substantial 'bun' experience even though the portion is tiny. The highlight of the meal for me.

The farm fresh egg was good. My favorite part was the salad that had a dry dressing with cilantro and salt.

The black dirt carrot steak was full of umami. The brussel sprout side was burnt too far. The sunchokes in the sunchoke and potatoes side are high in inulin, a prebiotic indigestible fiber that gives many people gas.

The Raven and Boar's Pig was good but nothing stood out. The grey hake was ok.

The service was very friendly and low-key but attentive. Overall, it was good, but I don't need to go back. I've had fresher-tasting food at Print Restaurant, not sure why.

I came here last week to celebrate my bf's birthday. We both had the farmer's feast tasting menu and were anticipating the best meals of our lives. Although it didn't quite meet that expectation, our overall experience was good.

Our tasting menu consisted of:

1) Braised hake (shellfish with apples, fennel, and celery): 4/5

2) This morning's farm egg: 4/5

3) Berkshire pig: 5/5

4) Granola and yogurt sorbet: 3/5

5) Bartlett Pears (olive oil cake with almond ice cream): 4/5

Everything was delicious, with the Berkshire Pig being the real standout. My bf made a good point that 2 of the 5 dishes were desserts. This was great for me because I love dessert but he was looking for more meats. We decided we'd come back but would not get the farmer's feast now that we had a better sense of what Blue Hill does best.

For drinks, we got two specialty cocktails. They were both strong and delicious.

I personally love the concept of Blue Hill. To top it off, they had great service. The ambiance was swanktastic to say the least.

Farm to table food, delicious, but unimaginative simple favors.  Pumpkin butternut squash soup was sweet, fatty pork dishes 1and 2 by design, chicken dish  with root vegetables.  Subtle, natural food tastes. Unconventional wine listings.  Overall it was missing something.

Impeccable Service, excellent and innovative food. Ordered the chef's tasting and it was a party in your palate :)

Highly recommend!

Return ? Yes 
Frequency ? Occasionally

Unfortunately didn't flip over the food here or the experience as I did at Stone Barns. 
What I will say is this place seems less formal, the staff less stuffy, and they sure come around a lot with those (good!) baguettes and butter.

My tilefish entree was a bit too fishy, and well, blah.  Think it was $34 - don't understand that price tag at all for such a disappointing dish.  Bf liked his dish but it looked totally unappealing to me so I didn't even try it.  Also thought his appetizer of pork was good, which I tried a bit of and it was pretty good.

The menu bored me, and then so did the food.  I would go back to the other Blue Hill but this one left me wishing we (sorry dear bf, you meant very well, I'm going to get in trouble for this) spent my birthday meal someplace else.

This restaurant is about the ingredients and not the ego of the chef, which is a marvelous refreshing experience. FRom the start i got a beautiful surprise with a snack suggested by the waiter: veggies on the fence, each a beautiful, tasty and fresh miniature, visually attractive and delicious. I had a veal-quinoa plate that was also great.

Utterly fantastic, particularly the vegetables (the vegetable fence is both delightful visually and delicious).  My reluctance to award the fifth star stems from: (1) the restaurant's insistence it could not expand our reservation from 3 people to 4, despite half a dozen or so four-tops that remained empty throughout our meal; and (2) the rabbit entree was just too much rabbit and not enough . . . anything else.  Still, a top-tier restaurant that does just about everything flawlessly.

OUTSTANDING!!!  Could not get a reservation, but was told to show up and hope for a seat at the small bar.  Walked in around 9:30 or so on a Saturday night and got lucky... we actually preferred the bar to the tables.  Cozy but not cramped, elegant but not stuffy, classy but not pretentious.  Everything was absolutely perfect.  My new favorite restaurant in the city, and probably the best meal I've ever had!

We enjoyed this restaurant before the great storm of 2012, literally two days before so I do not know how they fared in the storm but I do know that we  fared well here. The restaurant is smallish which is perfectly fine with me. If you enjoy great service then this is the place to go. Very attentive and accommodating. I had the Duck Pate and the Stone Barns Berkshire Pig. While the portions for the Pig were small, the flavor was huge. The Chef doubled my Pate order as I was jones'n for pate. Our dessert was wonderful. As we left we noticed that a another famous chef was dining there - name I cannot remember - so this must be a chef's type of place also.

I probably shouldn't even write this review because our experience was non-typical - and we ate at Blue Hill 13 months ago. But the experience was so lovely that I might as well share.

The long and the short of it: I went with my sister, who's friends with a chef was who filling in in the kitchen at the time (he's cooked at Lambs Club, Per Se, Del Posto, Alinea, Charlie Trotter's, etc). He whipped us up a ridiculous custom tasting menu - with a few dishes that aren't on the menu. We got a great table, and since we had the hookup in the kitchen, our service was literally perfect (shoutout to the terrific waitresses!), and we got to thank the staff in the kitchen afterward (which really was the perfect ending to such a memorable few-times-in-a-lifetime meal). Blue Hill is a cozy little joint and feels intimate without trying to. Probably because it's below ground so there are few windows and less to distract you (ie, no watching pedestrians passing by). The noise level was just right; my sister and I never had trouble hearing each other (and never had to shout). And the crowd was very well dressed. Blue Hill just feels like one of those classic New York dining establishments where you get the quintessential New York amazing dining experience. 

Again, because this all happened so long ago, some of the details are fuzzy. But the presentation at Blue Hill is a big part of the magic. Every dish is a work of art. I especially loved the selection of tiny vegetables and fruits served on a funny little fence (which was one of the first courses). Kale chips were executed perfectly and flavorfully (and the best part of eating kale chips in a restaurant is not having to stink up your house making them yourself!). There was a refreshing tomato-ey gazpacho-type dish bursting with all manner of cool deliciousness. There was duck. There was fish. There was a poached egg (and I'm not a poached egg kind of girl, but it worked so well). There were clouds. And there was snow. I like having weather and assorted atmospheric phenomena on my menu. 

I look forward to dining at Blue Hill again and having a straight-up, run-of-the-mill experience. I'm sure it will live up to the bar they set for us last fall.

I think what I absolutely loved and adored most about Blue Hill is the impeccable and friendly service!  Probably the best I've had in a very long loooong time! We had the veggies on a fence (or on a torture rack?), which were almost too adorable to eat, the farm fresh egg (without speck), a vegetarian version of the quinoa entree, the cauliflower steak (amazing! I love cauliflower) and a vegan peanut butter ice cream+ choco cake combo complementary from our awesome waiter/restaurant! Everything was lightly flavored, which I loved, as I could appreciate the flavors of the wonderful veggies. They were also very accommodating about our dietary restrictions (I am vegetarian and my husband has been vegan for three months), which was really superb - we felt welcomed into the warmth that is Blue Hill!

My husband and I were so stuffed, we could barely waddle out of the restaurant (so I totally feel like we over-ordered based on folks feedback about portions being small - they were big/filling for us). 

I will most certainly go back!

Great service to match with the wonderful food at this cozy GV mainstay. I'd been wanting to try Blue Hill for awhile and it did not let me down. The menu had a lot of great sounding dishes so it was difficult to try to narrow it down, but my friendly waiter was very personable and eager to answer any questions and offer his opinions.

They have added a new section to the menu calles Farm Snaks. Basically little bites that are priced at $8 each. Unfortunately, I was suckered into ordering the butter, lardo, ricotta, and fennel salt from this section of the menu. I usually dont order something like this as I feel its a waste of money, but the lardo is what really got me. The butter was a very good quality, the lardo was whipped with smoked paprika that really overpowered it and you couldn't pick up the lardo flavor, the ricotta was nice but just a little dollop in olive oil, and the fennel salt was just very overpowering but I am not a huge fan of fennel. From what I have read in previous reviews, they used to give you this complimentary as a a free treat with the bread but I guess they figured now they can charge for it. To be honest, I'd advise against ordering this and focus on the main menu.

I decided of three courses. For my appetizer I went with this morning's farm egg, mid course of ginger and oat pasta with mushrooms and sea urchin, and finally I went with the Tilefish after strongly deliberating between that and the duck. I asked my waiter which he would recommend since I love duck but was more in a fish mood. Of course he said both were great, but he preferred the duck. Even so, I stuck with the tilefish as I wanted something lighter since I was doing 3 courses.

This morning's farm egg with spinach, mushrooms, and speck ($18)- Yes, $18 for an egg. I know, it sounds ridiculous and it probably is. But I knew this was one of their signatures and wanted to try it. The egg was lightly poached, set on a little bed of spinach and mushrooms with a piece of speck draped upon it. Good? Yeah definitely, but again nothing revolutionary or mind blowing. I think this was something considered "original" when Blue Hill first opened but now everyone is doing eggs on the menu. For $18, I'd choose something else.

Ginger and Oat pasta with mushrooms and sea urchin- The pasta was perfectly cooked al dente. It was basically spaghetti shaped, and while I was wary of the "ginger" label since I'm not a huge fan, I was happy that the ginger flavor wasnt too pronounced. You could taste it but it didnt hit you in the face. The sea urchin I think was blended into the sauce because I didnt see or taste any pieces of it. The only critique is this could have used more mushrooms, but overall I really enjoyed this dish as it was light and the perfect portion size as a mid course.

Now is when something funny happened. Remember I was deciding between duck and tilefish? Well when it was time for the main course, the duck came out. I stared at it for a second, looked up, and told the server I had actually ordered the tilefish. She was very apologetic and offered to take it back to replace, but honestly the duck looked great. I am a stickler for duck and like it extremely rare but with a crispy skin and that is exactly how this looked. It was set on a bed of creamed broccoli rabe and spinach, with pickled onions. I told her it was no problem that it looked great and I'd keep the duck. Boy was it delicious.

Of course, the waiter came over and said he "mistakenly" must have told the kitchen I wanted the duck since he subconsciously wanted me to try it. But he said no problem I would also get the tilefish!!! Wow, what an amazing gesture. I'm not sure if he really made the mistake or if the restaurant was just going above and beyond to allow me to try both. I'd love to think it was the latter.

The tilefish was served with brussel sprouts, hazelnuts, and little bits of apple in an apple balsamic like sauce around the plate. This was incredible. The fish was fresh, light, perfectly cooked and I loved the flavors. It had so many complex textures and flavors- bitterness from the brussel sprout leaves, crunch and nuttiness from the hazelnuts, acidity from the sauce, and finally some sweetness and crunch from the apples. A winning dish!!!

As a side, I got the puree of blue hubbard squash which was fantastic. I could have eaten a whole bowful as it just sang fall. Reminded me of mashed sweet potatoes on Thanksgiving baby.

For dessert, I got the "Apples", which were two nice size beignets filled with apples, dusted with cinnamon sugar, and topped with a milk jam ice cream. A terrific way to end the meal.

Overall, I really loved Blue Hill and it was money well spent. Extra points for "mistakingly" giving me the extra course. 

The only mini qualms I had were with charging $8 for the bread condiments and the fact they didn't give any petit fours with the check which I thought was odd. Nonetheless, a very tasty experience and a quality meal

Did you know they have an ice cream machine in the back, so kids can choose their flavors and whip up their own ice cream for dessert?  One of a few things that surprised me about Blue Hill.  
 
I came here with a small group of friends for my birthday, and at the end of it was glad I went with this spot.  

Love the feel of the restaurant -- it's small & intimate, cozy without being cramped, and elegant without trying too hard.  

The waitstaff deserves mention.  They were helpful, enthusiastic, and unpretentious.  They answered our numerous inquiries about the menu and (this is a reflection of the whole restaurant, not just the waitstaff) were extremely flexible with letting us substitute courses from the tasting menu.  

Our group  of 4 went with the tasting menu, which was decently priced at $85 for 5 courses.   Unaltered, the menu was:

1.  Marinated Bluefish
         - very light and refreshing - I don't remember tasting the sesame or basil but it was among the lightest dishes I've had of its kind.  

2. This Morning's Farm Egg 
         - everyone raves about this dish, and rightfully so - it comes with chicken and pickled veggies, something about the combination of flavors was really amazing.  The grilled leeks were a good add to this.  Much more complex than expected for a dish called farm egg.  

3. Stone Barns Berkshire Pig
          - They give you multiple cuts of pork with different ways of cooking the meat, and each type brought out the flavor in a different way.  Not a huge pork chop if that's what you're looking for.  This is much more about the different flavors you can tease out of pork meat in one dish.  Accompaniments of corn & mushroom with some bacony flavored sauce were all awesome.  

4. Blueberries - Granola, honey & yogurt sorbet
       - A really nice palate cleanser, simple clean delicious.  

5. Plums - Elderberries, ginger cake & toasted almond ice cream
         - Sour plums make for great desserts if you like tart over sweet - the ginger cake was well done, really great way to end the meal.

They top it off with a cute touch of blackberries dipped in sugar.  

The bread & spreads deserve mention.  In the beginning of the meal they bring you bread with not just butter but a collection of different spreads.  Despite a pending 5 course meal, we all kept going back, especially for the lardo.  

I got the tilefish and my friend got the halibut instead of the Berkshire Pig.  Now I read in another review of someone who regretted ordering something that did not grow on a farm, since this place does farm-grown items very well.  I would agree with that -- the seafood was very well done, I especially liked the corn that came with the halibut, but the Berkshire pig was the entree that really stood out.

What really gives this place 5 stars and not 4 is the tasting menu that's fairly priced at $78, $145 including wine pairings.  And the wine is generous - one person in our group got it, and at some point he had 4 glasses in front of him as they brought out new ones with the courses.  The white wine pairs were the best -- some really great unique wines.  

Blue Hill is an understated, elegant place to celebrate any occasion.   The best part, besides the delicious food, was the service.  I was made to feel like I could bring anyone here from a good friend to my mom, and be made comfortable.

This place is amazing! Everything we got was delicious, and luckily, I got to try what everyone else was eating. 

The staff is super friendly, but mellow. They don't rush you so it makes for a really lovely evening. 

We got:

-sea urchin pasta
-pork liver
-braised bacon-super super yummy
-veal
-hake with manhattan clam chowder 
-gnocchi
-raspberry
-chocolate bread pudding


Honestly, everything was really delicious. The portions aren't huge, but you'll leave satisfied. For me, the appetizers and entree were much better than the desserts, but everything was fantastic-really. The table that we sat at in the back was lovely and not super loud.

Arrived a few minutes late on a rainy night.  Were seated in the back garden room, thankfully so, as we had a private quiet corner booth and it was quite stuffy in the main dining room what with the low ceilings.  Would definitely recommend requesting a table in the back.  

I had the farmers feast tasting menu with wine pairings.  This consisted of lardo, bluefish, this mornings farm egg, the Berkshire pig and chocolate tart.  My wife had the pig as well as the chocolate bread pudding. 

Everything was wonderfully prepared and the service was delightful. Recommend highly.

Really expensive but...amazing above & beyond service.  I'm a vegan & actually left full.  Lovely food.  Simple understated romantic setting.  Not only did they ask when I made the reservation (you really need reservations) if we were going for a special occasion but  they remembered and surprised us at the end with a lovely birthday candle and free little appys & after treats.  Great for an upscale special occasion.  Very quiet with warm lighting.   Decor is sort of businesslike.   Doesn't make you want to look around the room at anything....but if you are there for the company and food experience, you will have a nice time.  Be prepared to spend $200 with only 1 drink each and no wine.

My boyfriend decided to take me here because I've always wanted to go, and it's now one of my favorite restaurants in the city. Mostly, that's because Blue Hill is one of the few places where I'll eat lots of greens because they're delicious!

I wasn't as WOWed by the service as other Yelpers, but the waiter was very nice and helpful. I loved the fresh farm egg, and the green apple mustard accompanying the pig terrine tastes like an apple Jolly Rancher (in a good way).

My chicken reminded me of Hainanese chicken -- it was incredibly moist and I even finished all my vegetables. Wish that every piece of chicken had come with skin -- very crisp and tasty. 

Boyfriend's duck was also perfectly cooked. For dessert we ordered the chocolate bread pudding. It looked a lot more dense and decadent than it was -- it could have been as dense as a brownie, but it was light-ish (didn't make me feel overly guilty after finishing it), and paired perfectly with the ice cream and caramel.

I loved the ambience at Blue Hill. The room is cozy, well lit, and very intimate--a great spot to impress that special someone. The service wasn't overly friendly, but all were polite, knowledgeable, and attentive. 

The food is--as advertised--very fresh and very tasty. Portions aren't huge, but I certainly left the table satisfied (this isn't Applebee's, kids). My entre, featuring a variety of succulent pork was prepared to perfection. The bread pudding is astounding.

Note that the snacks (at least all of the ones we tried) are served with some kind of bread. So if you're limiting carbs and/or gluten, you may want to skip the snacks.

If you're in the West Village, looking for a quiet & charming spot for a date, and you can get a reservation, give Blue Hill a try.

Favorite restaurant in the city.  Food tastes SO fresh and they prepare dishes very uniquely.  Waiters and sommelier are very knowledgeable...you feel like you got a bit of a lesson after eating here.  It's not cheap, but all the extras you get make it worth it.  I've also eaten at the upstate venue, which is stellar, but the village definitely gives it a run for the money.  If I had one complaint (minor) it's that the village location does tend to feel a little bit "stuffy" and doesn't have a very "fun" vibe to it...probably due to the clientele at this stage in their restaurant life.

It wasn't on top of my list so when my baby suggested taking me here I was a little skeptical. However, I was very happy with the food and ambience overall. The vegetables were extremely fresh and tasty and the egg appetizer might have been my favorite of the dinner. I never thought an egg could be that delicious! The tilefish wasn't the best but since this isn't a seafood restaurant, I won't be too critical. We shared the pear for dessert (with ice-cream, caramelized pear and olive oil cake) and it was truly amazing and aesthetically pleasing. The only complaint was that it was too small. 

It's definitely a great romantic date place and I am glad I got to check it out.

Went here for a dinner for two on a Wednesday night, early evening...

Interior is great, very calming, subtle yet sophisticated. There's an entire team waiting at the entrance to do everything from check you in, check your coat, etc.

We had a nice table in the corner of one of the large booth areas. Our server presented us with our menus and then left us to figure out our food options; she did give us quite a bit of time and answered all of our questions. While we were waiting for our starters, they gave us an amuse-bouche, but I forget what it was; it was decent.

We started with:
White Eggplant Spread: tangy, creamy spread served on grilled slices of bread; very nice!
Last Chance Heirloom Tomato Salad: not my favorite, there was an odd warm, cold element to this salad. Some of the fruit was warm, which was just plain weird to me.
Smoked Oat Pasta: one of my favorites of the night; excellent smoky flavor (almost like a barbecue sauce, but not nearly as strong or sweet), perfectly cooked pasta, delicious mushrooms. 

Entrees:
Potato and Ricotta Gnocchi: like little pillows of cheese! There was another hint of smoke in this dish, and it paired well with the other ingredients, especially the salami.
Raven and Boar's Pig: I was really disappointed with this dish. Pork served several ways including pork belly, blood sausage, center cut and shoulder. Overall the pork was tough and chewy, and not very flavorful. The best part of this dish was the pork belly, which had a super crisp layer to offset the fattiness of the cut.
Roasted Potatoes: super good! Small potatoes that had a great "snap" when you bit into them but still cooked through. Served with what tasted like a vegetable broth reduction.

Dessert:
Strawberries: a wonderful dessert served with fresh wild strawberries (the little ones), a sorbet, a bit of chocolate cake and caramelized white chocolate. Really good.
Chocolate Bread Pudding: wow, this was a spectacular dessert! Served like a square piece of brownie, with candied pecans and a very nice vanilla bourbon ice cream.

Overall, the meal was good except for my main, which is why I wasn't sure if I should go for three or four stars. However, the service was great and non-intrusive, we had a great spot in the restaurant, and honestly the prices aren't that outrageous, so four stars it is.

Also for any white wine drinkers, the Domaine De Chazette Sauvignon Blanc was superb, and paired well with our choices.

I have been coming back to Blue HIll in Stone Barns since 2007. Since I love the one in Stone Barns, I decided to try this one as well.

We ordered Farmer's Feast Tasting Menu. I love that they truly understand their customers' needs. My boyfriend told them that I am vegan, and they made changes to my menu. We also received a nice card and surprise gifts! Their food might be very different from what you would expect if you are a frequent diner at Daniel or Per se. (When we first ventured out to Blue Hill in Stone Barns for the first time, it was a bit of surprise) But if you are a vegan/vegetarian, the chefs here is a lot more flexible than those.  

My only complaint is that the romantic atmosphere you can enjoy in Stone Barns is not here.

The space is intimate and packed full of people. 

I was excited by the concept of local foods and whatnot,  but the execution is lacking. The food was just okay - not great, not especially flavorful or interesting. The dishes came out about as good as I can make at home. 

Overall, a food needs to be more than local and sustainable for me to be interested. Sure, the carrot's from over there, but that doesn't make it taste any better.

This was a wonderful experience, recommended by our local Farm to Table Chef.  The recommendations by Franc, the GM, for both food and drink were spot.  He and his staff made us feel most welcome.  Would recommend this to anyone looking for a delicious and personal experience.

Got the Farmer's Feast tasting menu.  Good value and love that they let you sub anything if you're not into one of the dishes.  Flexible kitchen.

The space is a bit - cozy.  Can be a challenge as a party of 2 to get privacy you're looking for.

Food was very good but definitely hit/miss.  Out of 6 dishes, two were really exceptional.  Definitely the late harvest/last chance tomato/handmade ricotta toast is a must have.

They work with Hirsch to source a blue hill exclusive Pinot - get it even though it's expensive.  Big fan of the vineyard and this is not a disappointment.

Overall a great experience but left wondering if the wine + feast for two was worth the same $400 I could have spent half as much for at ABC Kitchen or pay not too much more for a life changing dinner at Eleven Madison Park.

Very good, but perhaps my expectations were too high. Was the food incredibly fresh, local, beautifully and cleverly presented, and simply prepared? Yes. But, honestly, I was a tad bit bored at times.
We started with the vegetables on a fence (tiny vegetables like mini slivers of summer squash and zucchini presented on a bed of upright nails). The presentation of the dish really forced you to take in the taste of each vegetable. I really liked the crostini with goat cheese as well.
For my appetizer, I had the famous morning farm egg.  I really enjoyed this dish and recommend it. I also enjoyed the oat pasta. It had a nice nutty flavor to it.
For my entree, the grilled wreckfish had a decent broth, but I found it be rather bland and the texture was a  bit tough. It really needed some seasoning or spicing. My husband was not blown away by his pork either and kind of just picked at it.
For desserts, the strawberries with caramelized white chocolate and milk ice cream was pretty to look at and tasty to eat. The blueberry dessert was also nice.
Overall, the dinner was fine, but not particularly exciting.  Blue Hill has an excellent wine list, including a nice selection of dessert wines. And it is nice to have a cocktail before dinner as well.  The dining room has a romantic atmosphere, but the tables feel way too close together. I would come back for sure, but I do think it might have been a bit hyped up. It is one of the first farm to table restaurants in the area, but I think it also has some pretty good competition now.

Amazing!  I loved every minute of this meal.  My husband ordered the hake and I ordered the grass fed beef so we could try both - so good.  The server recommended really wonderful wine pairings.  Despite the fact that I was full by the end of the meal, I couldn't resist the chocolate bread pudding.  SO good I had to resist the urge to lick the plate.  It's been awhile since I was here last but everything was so fresh and, well, perfect, it felt like a totally new and exciting experience.

I have to say that it's not RELLY fair to compare when its not the SAME season but I took my BF to the upstate Blue Hill for his birthday in February...and dont get me wrong it was AMAZING...but 6 months later when the season is in peak and the options are abound...(and you know the chef and mait'rd) you get excited by the options...AND...VERY well taken care of and that is what happened this night...we saw NO menu the chef said he'd like to cook us what he thought was fresh and boy did he.  Delicious meal of various meats veggies and desserts...oh and the pours the pours!  One better than the other...no way...both delicious!

I had wanted to try Dan Barber's cousine ever since watching his presentation on TED.
http://www.ted.com/talks/dan_barber_how_i_fell_in_love_with_a_fish.html

Luckily, my husband took me to celebrate my birthday with friends and family in the garden room @ BHNY. After recent ventures into molecular gastronomy and unusual flavor combinations, it was pleasant to enjoy food the old fashioned way where the star of each course was the ingredient. 

We started with the summer bean salad: dried peaches, cucumber and ruby streaks. I was amazed by the peaches and unusual greens they chose for the salad. 
This was followed with braised hake with corn and clam chowder (we removed the bacon) and a chicken entree that included cuts of white and dark meat. The unusual texture of the hake was pleasant and allowed for a refreshing way to devour the fish. I loved the crispy skin on the chicken and was impressed by the grain it was served with. 

I usually get full quickly so i stayed away from the bread & still managed to fill up.

Wow.

I don't give out 5 star reviews very often but this place was very good.

Here is what I ate:
1. THIS MORNING'S FARM EGG: STONE BARNS SPECK, BUTTERBALL POTATOES AND GREENHOUSE GREENS
For someone who loves eggs as much as I do, this was amazing.
 
2. GRILLED WRECKFISH: WARM TOMATO GAZPACHO, BASIL AND CUCUMBER
Love the seasonal part of the menu.  Dish was perfect / I love fish.  Our server compared wreckfish to seabass if you're wondering what wreckfish tastes like.

As for wine, I am no wine connoisseur, so I asked the server for a sweeter white, and brought me a glass of a wine that was perfect for my palette.  And, to top it all off, I got it on the house!

We were too full for dessert, but our server brought us blackberry lollipops to top off our meal, again, on the house.

Again, wow.

The bread was warm and served with semi cold butter. Started with the pig liver terrine, which came with greens, shallots and cocoa nibs. The terrine had excellent flavor and the addition of the shallots and cocoa brought out a richness in the flavor of the terrine. Also tried the farm egg which was served with speck, potatoes and greens. The egg was delicate and fresh and had a wonderful taste.

For the meal I had the Berkshire pig, which was served with tomatoes, beans, and parsley. The pork was perfectly cooked. Also tried the grass fed beef which was served with corn and cherry tomatoes. Ordered the meat medium rare and it came out that way. The corn was sweet and the tartness of the tomatoes helped balance it out. The sides didn't seem to fit that well with the beef, though.

We sat in the garden in the back, which was not really outside but close. The service was excellent and they had a decent wine list. Overall, a very nice place to have a meal in Manhattan.

Blue Hill was lovely - a beautiful space with amazing service and incredible tasting food. There's just one problem: there's not enough of it. 

I know. A serious foodie shouldn't express portion complaints. I should be squealing about the delicate flavor of the poached quail egg, rejoicing over the refreshment of my snap pea cocktail, and expressing awe over the tender, flavorful nibbles of boar. And it was all beautiful, but I possess a certain arbitrary non-foodie nexus of food quality and quantity, and Blue Hill was just a little too sparse for me. 

As a Pacific Northwesterner, I felt surprisingly at home at a NYC farm-to-table joint with service so nice, a New Yorker would scarcely recognize it. But things were just a little too precious for me. If I leave a place hungry after 6 courses, it's not the place for me.

Yes they are in major need of an update on the interiors but it's the food and service that really counts and it;s mostly spot on.
Our server was exceptional, very knowledgeable about the menu, very attentive. Our Sommelier was less  knowledgeable about the wines, I was very surprised about how she couldn't answer a few of my questions. 
We took our time with ordering and enjoyed cocktails and wine, no rushing here. The food was farm fresh and cooked to perfection, from beginning to end. A very enjoyable evening.

Far and away one of the best restaurants in the city. They're farmer's feast is an semi-annual tradition for me, and every time i get it i am never disappointed.

Service is spectacular and they do a great job of post-visit follow up through opentable and email. 

I highly highly recommend their premium tasting menu (7-8 courses, plus wine flight) to anyone who goes there. It may be pricey, but it will be one of the most memorable 3hr meals of your life.

The ambiance: Dimly lit, classy, but sort of like a hotel restaurant, if you know what I mean. The 2-tops in the back, where we sat, are a bit cramped. 

The service: No complaints.

On to the food. The bread is great! Warm sourdough mini-baguettes with soft, salty butter. I had a cocktail (meh, and overpriced), while my dinner companion indulged in a glass of fancy French sparkling cider (only $5, but then again, it tasted essentially identical to Martinelli's, which is like $2 a bottle). We were served an amuse bouche of "mini pea sliders": some poor cook had prepared teeny tiny brioche buns -- complete with sesame seeds on top -- which were filled with a coarse puree of almond and snap peas. I have to say the concept was a complete failure. They tasted like peas alright but the overwhelming flavor was the sweetness of the bun, which was itself not particularly good in taste or texture (spongy). 

Not  hungry enough to get the $85ish tasting menu, we ordered a la carte. It's nice that this is once fancy NYC restaurant where it is still possible to do so.

For an appetizer, I had the corn soup. While not worth $18, it was very nice. Cool, corn-y, with nice textural and flavor contrast from some little pickled things floating on top. My companion had the $20 egg dish. To my taste, the egg flavor was overwhelmed by  unsubtle flavors with which the egg was served: crab, bacon, lots of veggies. I believe restraint is key for eggs, and I think the epitome of a good egg course may the 5 minute soft egg with caviar at Momofuku Ko. Blue Hill's egg did not succeed along the restraint axis. Also charging $20 for this is insane. But the bacon was a pleasant surprise, and in fairness my companion enjoyed the dish a lot. The servings on the appetizers were quite generous as well.

For a main, I had the duck. This was cooked perfectly and served a top a smear of blanched fava beans smothered in bright green pea- and tarragon-based sauce. (There was probably some other sauce element on the plate that I don't recall.) The plate was visually arresting with all the green, but not really that successful presentation-wise. The beans tasted pretty good, though. Tarragon can be an overpowering, assertive flavor but it was held back just enough. At $38, not the best value for a well-cooked duck breast, but then again, such things are not necessarily so easy to find. Let's summarize by saying I was satisfied but not blown away by my main course.

My companion had the (braised, if I remember correctly) hake, served as two generous blobs of *medium rare* (! -- on the chef's recommendation, via our server -- !) white fish, over diced vegetables and a bright yellow saffron-scented sauce. Comparing the appearance with that of my duck, it was quite clear that the chef's visual sensibilities are informed by aesthetic sympathy with the abstract expressionist movement. I quite liked the sauce -- the saffron/fish combination reminded me of eating bouillabaisse in Marseilles, and the color was  beautiful. I would not say hake is a particularly great fish, at least as prepared at Blue Hill. It seems to be related to cod and haddock, and it is roughly as boring as those two. I bet it would be quite serviceable fried up and served with chips at a UK pub, or dyed orange and made into imitation crab meat, but why serve a fillet of a less-than-delicious fish for $35? The portion was (too) generous, but why not serve less  of a more expensive and tasty fish?

For dessert, we shared the peach dish. This featured ginger cake, fromage blanc ice cream, and pine nuts, in addition to the obvious peaches. I was not too impressed. The fromage blanc ice cream, in particular, just tastes like vanilla ice cream gone horribly wrong. I'm all for less-sweet desserts, and I think creme fraiche or sour cream could have worked well here. But *cheesy* tasting ice cream just seems wrong to me. I did like the subtle effect of a few leaves of fresh herbs sprinkled atop the dish. Also the peaches, which should be singing their deliciousness in this kind of preparation, were just average. If you can't source perfect ingredients, don't serve such an ingredient-centric dish!

With our check we were served some very nice caramels, but they were no Jacques Genins. 

Reflecting on the whole thing, I'd say Blue Hill is just OK. It's overpriced and it underperformed. But it is a fairly classy joint and it is especially vegetarian friendly for a fine dining restaurant. The sort of place to take out that vegan art history NYU grad student chick you're trying to impress, and right in the neighborhood. Also ever so ever so ever so ever so sustainable, I'm sure. Is it utterly delicious? Not really.

Dinner here was lovely. The ambiance is relaxed and intimate. I love this place's concept of bringing farm fresh ingredients straight to the table. The farm egg, salad greens, beef, duck, and veggies were all amazing dishes. The dessert also did not disappoint. I would highly recommend ordering the beef or duck with a side of greenhouse greens. The dishes here are well thought out with each one having a complex and well balanced flavor to it.

Blue Hill is truly a gem not only in Greenwich Village, but in all of New York City. They exemplify the farm to table concept better than any other restaurant in the area, and for good reason. All ingredients are sourced fresh and locally so that diners can really experience and taste the difference. Inside the restaurant, you can also find a great atmosphere. It's not very loud, so everyone can hear what's being said at the table; but at the same time, you can hear the subtle background noise of other conversations, and they all seem to be saying one thing -  how good the food is.

Blue Hill gave me a great impression right off the bat. Our waitress was very attentive and knowledgeable about each and every detail pertaining to the menu. The bread they served was terrific. It was slightly warm with a crunchy thin crust on the outside and a small chew still on the inside.

Our amuse bouches started with beat burgers garnished with caper leaves.

Next, we had some lightly salted kale chips with a nice crispy texture that still retained a strong taste of kale. The presentation of the kale standing tall on a wooden slab was nice too.

To finish off our amuse bouches, we had a small platter of charcuterie consisting of salami and pork shoulder coppa.

To accompany our bread and amuse bouches, we were also given special housemade butter, lardo, and fennel salt, in addition to the normal butter served at the table. Our favorite was the really rich and flavorful lardo.

For our first course, we had this morning's poached farm egg with asparagus marmalade, bio char red onion and greenhouse greens. The egg was undeniably fresh in taste, as the yolk slowly oozed out of it's egg white casing when cut into. On the lighter side, the dish was a nice start to the rest of the meal. This course was paired with a crisp minerally wine from northern Italy.

Next, the second course was a purple potato and ricotta gnocchi with shitake mushrooms, hazelnuts and stone barns coppa. The colorful presentation really complimented the earthy and nutty taste of the dish. This was paired with a nice crisp white wine, also from Italy, that brought out the earthy notes even more.

The third course was a Hudson Valley duck with Charleston gold rice, asparagus and lamb's quarters. The duck was seasoned well and cooked perfectly so that each bite was tender and juicy. A medium-bodied red wine blend of Grenache and Syrah from France was paired perfectly with the duck. It brought all the components together well and had a great clean finish to top everything off.

The fourth course was a strawberry and red wine soup with pink peppercorn sorbet. I wasn't the biggest fan of the flavors in this dish, but the spiciness from the peppercorn really cut into everything else and stole the show, adding another interesting dimension.

The fifth and last course was a steamed goat cheesecake with poached rhubarb and yogurt sorbet. Each deconstructed component of this dish was amazingly delicious. The soft creamy texture of the cheesecake married perfectly with the crunchy fresh granola. A sweet moscato from Italy balanced well with all the components of the dish.

We finished our meal with a couple chocolate bites, a blood orange truffle and a honey chocolate. The truffle had a nice hint of orange flavor that balanced the chocolate. Needless to say, on the opposite side of the spectrum though, the honey chocolate was incredibly sweet.

Overall, Blue Hill meets its expectations as one of the best restaurants in New York City and deserves its Michelin star award. Not only is all the food fresh and delicious, you can really feel the effort that goes into each plate, starting from the ingredients to the cooking and finally to the presentation. Service is excellent throughout the meal, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. I simply cannot wait for my next meal at Blue Hill, or maybe even Blue Hill at Stone Barns.

http://knockrz.wordpress.com/

Best service I have *ever* experienced.  On point in every conceivable way.  Had the bread pudding (every bit as good as they say), chicken (incredibly tender), and gazpacho - all delicious and so fresh.  Loved the complimentary breadsticks and tasty butter as well.  Atmosphere very pleasant and romantic.  It's pricey but worth every penny.  The Obamas were smart to go there.

Decor is hohum. The service is exceptional and very helpful. The apps were good but very overpriced. $18 for pea soup? The entrees were good but again they were ridiculously expensive. I could have bought the whole flock of chickens for what a sliced up breast of one cost here. The pig is very tasty and well prepared and the bed of beans was fresh. The steak was tender and well prepared. The deserts are really outstanding and were the highlight of the meal. 

I am not sure why this uberchef cant make great food with these fresh natural organic ingredients. It is like saying one cant make beautiful clothes with natural fibers. I think that this is a place that is like Vermont- politically correct in every way but generally not successful in delivering on its potential. Spend your money elsewhere (and at this price any place in NYC is a candidate)  and get much better value.

The entrance to the restaurant is adorable, and inside itself is very cozy. You WILL be sitting very close to other customers, however you may feel about that (doesn't bother me one bit). Had the Berkshire Pig 1, very juicy, flavorful, perfectly prepared. The tasting menu is also worth trying - it will really highlight what a huge difference organic treatment makes to flavor. Standout, seamless execution of service. Thank you to my server Erin and the managers for your warm welcome. Next time will definitely try the pre-fixe menu. My only regret is not having tried the wine pairings. A Do Not Miss in New York!

Closer to a 4.5 :-)  Went a few nights ago on a short tript to NYC and we will definitely return.  It comes short of a 5 because not every bite merits a rave review and, yes, I found it overpriced, even at its most excellent. Lastly, I found the physical place uninspiring, as many have noted. It lacks any discernable character and is a bit bunker like. But my husband liked it. Then again, he prefers taupe and all the other "REI" colors, so if a dimly lit blank canvas of whites and taupes appeals to you, you may like it too. 

Now to the excellent:

1. The service was excellent, friendly and will bring me back. 

2. The foods/plates that were good were outstanding. The best thing called chilled pea soup I'll ever try, I am sure of it. I don't even like peas. But I loved this. 

3. Similarly, you can have your chocolate for dessert, nine out of ten times I'll try the other thing, but my husband's chocolate bread pudding dessert was out of this world. I keep imagining the texture of that pudding...how was it achieved? when will I ever be able to have something like it again?! man oh man

4. I had the daily farm feast. I would do that again, at least as a first-timer. No, not every teeny-tiny (and they are tiny) plate was extraordinary, but the opportunity to try many things was a good one. The farm egg with bits of bacon on a bed of greens has to be the kind of thing that put this restaurant on the culinary map; it was just so improbably good for what it was. I mean it was an egg people. And yet it wasn't just an egg. :-))

If you are curious about $, we spent approx $260 for 2 persons for one daily farm feast for one person and then one appetizer/one entree/one dessert for the second and three glasses of wine; this total includes tax and tip.

4.5 stars. The backyard is fantastic. The servers are fantastic. The wine list is fantastic. The prices, for the experience, are fantastic. The food is very good. The vegetables and the simple preparations are really excellent. The meats are quite good. The food seems to lack the finesse that the rest of the establishment has, but it's still very enjoyable. I can't wait to go back and that's really the best thing you could say about a restaurant. Especially in a city like New York where you would never have to return to anywhere a second time.

I've been saving this review for when I had a couple reviews under my belt since I'm a fairly new  yelper..

My boyfriend brought me to Blue Hill to celebrate a special occasion. The concept here is amazing and really unique. The menu changes heavily based on what's in season. We had the Farmer's Feast and it really was incredible. The bread came with asparagus salt which was a really nice and tasty surprise. We also had baby carrots lightly seasoned with some type of vinegar. Honestly, I'm more of a meat person but I would have these carrots over a burger any day. They were just that good. I couldn't believe it was a vegetable. Also, the Morning farm egg was fantastic- you can really taste how fresh it is. We had the duck as an entree and it was so incredibly tender and delicious. The crowd is slightly older and its definitely not a place to go with a large group. 

Overall, we had a wonderful experience, the food was absolutely incredible, and Blue Hill is definitely one of my top favorite restaurants in NYC.

Had the vegetarian version of the tasting menu.  delicious!  no issues at all with substituting the standard entree for one of the vegetarian a la carte entrees..  

The food is outstanding and feels extremely fresh and crisp.  Cocktail (with some rooftop grown herbs or so) was great - very creative and perfectly executed, not the usual stuff.  

Loved the laid back and nevertheless refined atmosphere.

great restaurant!

I had been looking forward to this night for a while, anticipating great flavors with an emphasis on farm to table dining.  

We arrived for our 5 o'clock reservation 9 minutes early and were "greeted with a very curt; "We don't open until 5."   We said we could drink at the bar,  and the response was; "We are going to have our staff meeting and aren't serving at the bar until 5."   We then said we would be okay with just sitting at the bar.  Well this seemed to upset her as well, though there was no way out of it for her and we took seats.

We then watched as someone tried to make a reservation and was just as curtly treated as we had been.  Not a great first impression, but I wanted to dine here so we looked past it.

The room is dark, the decor is lots of grey cushions on the wall, which soundproofed the room well, but there was nothing to brighten the room's atmosphere.  Except for the cheerfulness of another tables waiter, the energy in the room was fairly restricted and heavy.

The waitress was slightly friendlier though aloof and pretty much just an order taker.  I ordered the duck, roast potatoes, and the sun chokes (artichokes).  The complimentary mini-burgers arrived and were delightful and the bread was delicious.  The meal itself was a large disappointment however.  Everything was so heavily seasoned and sauced that, except for a little bit of artichoke flavor, I couldn't taste the actual item on the plate.  The duck, though cooked perfectly to MR, was the same.  I love duck and order it everywhere it is available, but when you can't taste it, what's the point?

I thought I had found a wonderful treasure and was wrong.  I won't go back and now I won't go out to the Blue Hill at the Barn restaurant either.  Why travel that far if this is what defines them.  Sorry guys.

This is, by far, my favorite special occasion restaurant in the city. The food, the atmosphere, the service, the drinks. . . everything is perfect. A friend took me here for my 30th birthday, and our meal was incredible. We enjoyed three courses, were never rushed, and the chef sent over free samples of some appetizers and desserts. The fact that the food is local and organic makes the experience even better. I wish I could turn 30 every year so I could celebrate here!

There was a lot I liked about this restaurant - and very little I didn't. The atmosphere was not my favorite. Dark with a low roof. I guess they were going for romantic but for me it came off as dull. I don't think it is a very romantic place - if that's what you're looking for. 

I was looking for a place with local, organic food and I really loved that about this place. The vegetables were all top notch. I heard that the pig is fantastic - I wish I had gotten that instead of the duck, which was still good. 

It seems to me that the Farmers Feast is the way to go.  For the price and what you get, without a doubt. I was continually jealous of the guy next to me who got it. I heard the words bacon marmalade. Yep. 

So overall I wouldn't go again, but it was a pleasure to be there.
The service was very good and friendly, the bread was great. All the rest not impressive at all.  I cannot recall even one dish that we enjoyed.

I gave it four stars due to the fabulous service, not the food.  I came here and did the full tasting menu and wine pairing.  They brought out several starter courses and one being the Kale Chips.  They are really good however, be sure to take a trip to the bathroom afterwards since they get stuck in your teeth...not sexy on a date!  Everything was fantastic however, it was too much food and we actually asked to skip our dessert course because we were so full.  I think for the price, the food wasn't AMAZING.  I would prefer having the full tasting menu at Brushstroke then this place.  The service was fantastic and we had the nicest waitress.  But, I wouldn't come back, overpriced and a bit of a stuffy atmosphere in my opinion.

It was amazing.

I had the Farmer's Feast and it was fantastic. The first thing that came out was the smallest burger I have ever been served--The Beet Burger with ricotta cheese. Then came 2 slices of meat. Ok. Bread was served with salted cream butter, fennel salt, and lardon butter. 

Items on the Farmer's Feast included This Morning Farm Egg, a white fish that was served with a watercress puree and almonds (this was my favorite), Hudson Valley Duck, there was a sweet red soup--I think the server said it was a red wine soup? It was very sweet, chill, and delicious. The dessert was somewhat interactive...it was a a sweet goat cheese (with the consistency of cheesecake) in a jar with a side of granola and jam. It was very good. 

After the feast, I also got 2 chocolate truffles. The bill followed. 

Overall, the Farmer's Feast was one of the best culinary experiences I have ever had. Would I do it again? Yes.

Had an absolutely fantastic experience at Blue Hill this evening, from the moment we walked in the door. Simply the very finest food and service - Amelia was a terrific waitress. Every dish was unique, special and FRESH. Probably falls into my top ten dining experiences ever.

I've long had Blue Hill on my NYC hit list, and this past Sunday after a Tribeca Film Festival screening, we finally had our chance to check it out.  The setting is understated, and they definitely achieve a level of serenity that they are clearly trying to attain. 
 
On to the food.  The breadsticks, freshly baked, crispy on the outside and basically perfect were a good start (and probably the best part of the meal).  The amuse bouche of beet burgers was cute, but seemed to undersell both burgers and beets.  For app I had the chicken wing and heart dish, which was beautifully presented with pickled veggies, and really rocked.  My fiance had the morning egg app, over shitakes, morels, and asparagus, which to her disappointment had a green soupiness to it - diluting the yolky goodness she signed up for.

My main course was listed as a duck dish, but it seemed a lot more like a chickpea dish with again, a green 'sauce' and several mini duck slices (not sure if they come from mini ducks, or the chefs just have little knives) that were well cooked, but not overly satisfying.  The one saving grace was the fiddlehead ferns, but for $38  I'm sure I could buy a big ol' basket of them at Union Square (and get a smoked duck breast or 4).  My fiance had the hake and grilled squid entree, which was a rather large and unmanageable hunk of poached fish that seemed to lack both seasoning and flavor.  The dish needed a broth to liven up the fish, which I recall the waitress mentioning, but never did appear.

Overall I would consider myself underwhelmed, and this seems to be the moment for us, as my fiance said, that farm to table jumped the shark.  Selling appetizers that are billed as lettuce for $18 a pop is more about wanting to feel good spiritually than it is about having a taste for the world's greatest lettuce.  If yelp let me give 2.5 stars, I would have, but in the end this was closer to a disappointing meal than a satisfying one.
