Got their soft shell crabs, Berkshire pig and the parsnip steak. The crabs were only decent, not really that impressive. I've had better in little china town hole in the walls. The Berkshire pig was really good, it was a selection of 3 cuts from a pig. I'd say the pig belly was the best part. The parsnip steak was the most interesting, not to say the best but good and interesting. It was presented as a sliced steak was but had a really nice texture and flavor. Something worth trying.

I wasn't blown away by this place. Everything was good, but nothing was excellent.  It's not that I'm not complaining - I think the restaurant was OK, but I left feeling very underwhelmed. In that price range, there are many other restaurants in NY where I've been more impressed with the food. 

The meal:  
-Beet "sliders" as an amuse. They were tasty, but a bit heavy despite their small size.
-Appetizer: Beetfurter with pickled vegetables and house-made mustard.  The sausage was good and the fusion of pork and beet flavors worked very well, but the garnishes were disappointing. I thought the pickled vegetables would pair well with the sausage, the way sauerkraut does, but it wasn't so. They were somehow too pickled to eat together with the sausage and mustard and we were left with the impression that there were two distinct dishes on our plate, neither one quite complete and neither one complementing the other. The mustard was somewhat disappointing as well - I love a good spicy mustard with sausage, but this one just wasn't very good.
-Entrees: Pan-seared fish with ramps and fiddleheads. Everything was tasty but again nothing amazing. Ingredients were fresh and everything tasted OK, but nothing was inventive and the flavors didn't pop.  My girlfriend had the chicken with lamb and pancetta, which was also quite good, but, you guessed it - not amazing. Most disappointing were the ramps and fiddleheads on both plates - two veggies we look forward to all winter, and their flavors were somehow lost in these dishes.
-Dessert: Apple beignets with vanilla ice cream. This was probably the best course of the meal, and I'm not much of a dessert person. The flavors melded together really well and everything was perfectly executed. The beignets were warm and coated with the perfect amount of sugar and cinnamon.

Our overall impression was that the meal (other than dessert) was one we would have thrown together at home after a trip to the farmers market. I want restaurants to "wow" me on one level or another - to bring out the very best in the ingredients they use or to use the ingredients in novel ways. I wish I could give them 3.5 stars - I liked the meal - but, the restaurant doesn't deserve 4 stars, either. I won't go back.

My new favorite restaurant. So fresh. So tasty. Pleasant ambiance. 

Exquisite service--unrivaled attention to detail. Four examples: First, I asked if the artichoke soup was premade with the bacon, and the waiter asked if I didn't eat meat, so I responded that I don't but do eat fish--every other server who brought us an amuse bouche (there were several) mentioned whether I could or couldn't eat it because I was a pescetarian; Second, two amuse bouches and a little smoothie with olive oil cake were part of the Farmer's Fesat (tasting menu), which only one in our party ordered, but they brought them for all 6 of us; Third, when the waiter served the smoothies, he brought my grandmother a different one without alcohol because he noticed she hadn't had any wine; Fourth, my father must have looked a little cold or uncomfortable and the manager came over immediately and asked if he should turn up the heat. 

My only potential qualm would be that it was quite a long meal, around 3 hours, but just be prepared for it.

I loved what I ordered: goose egg pasta, beet salad, and Brussels sprouts with pistachios. The appetizer portions are quite large compared to most high end restaurants. Wait for them to bring out their homemade butter before you dig into the bread. The chocolate bread pudding was divine--more like one of those molten chocolate cakes. Other dishes people enjoyed were the artichoke and bacon soup, wreckfish with spicy fruits and vegetables, the chicken, and the pork (basically all of them). Can't wait to go back!

What am I missing here? I was so underwhelmed by the food that I was tempted to give this 2 stars. The food did not stand out at all. In fact, it was a place I would not think twice about going back to. To start, the egg yolk carbonara was about the size of my spoon. Literally the smallest portion I've ever seen. It tasted ok, but for close to $20 I was amazed at how small the portion was. I forget the other appetizer we go. For main meals, we got the chicken and the pig. The pig was tough and really not that good. The chicken was average. Maybe it was an off night but I would not recommend. We didn't even finish both entrees and portion size was not the issue.

This restaurant reminds me of the fine dining we have back home in Durham-Chapel Hill area of North Carolina. Everything on the menu is based on seasonal and more importantly LOCAL ingredients. The cooking is thoroughly American and very tasty. They give you plenty of bread--maybe too much! The bread is nice--tube-shaped, light and crunchy with some good chewiness. 

We had the beet burger as the amuse. the cornbread "buns" were very moist and buttery. They left "imprints" on the stone slab they were served on. Next i had the fruit and lettuce salad. It was very well seasoned and reflected well on the season and the freshness of the items. My sister had the Jerusalem artichoke soup which was good but not special...there was a strong acidic bite. However, my sister appreciated the texture added in the soup since many soups in NYC are just purees or have nothing to "chew" on. Next i had the venison which was 3 different cuts served with chickpeas. The venison was cooked perfectly! My sister's hake was cooked well but i think she would have preferred a different preparation (it was poached). For dessert, we had the fromage blanc souffle...which in fact is not a souffle. i was somewhat disappointed. It was mainly like a buttery pastry/ graham cracker crust with some meringue/marshmallow on top. The quenelle of ice cream had the "fromage" and pink peppercorns. 

The restaurant is located underneath someones town house which is kinda of interesting. Our waiter was nice and the crowd is a bit older. Also everyone here orders wine, the waiter kinda of pushes it and that's somewhat annoying for 2 people who don't drink.

Good food, but skip dessert.

My boyfriend and I went there for our valentines day celebration on Feb 15th.  We arrived at 7 and didn't finish till after 9.  We had the tasting menu along with the wine pairing.  Everything was DELICIOUS.  The best combinations of flavor and texture.  

This dinner is going down in the books as one of the best....

Oh my! were do i even begin from.. 

As i walked towards Blue Hill i couldn't contain my self i was so excited I've heard so much and expected even more. We walk in and what appeared to be the FH manager nicely approached us and asked for the name of the reservation. He then took us to our table a cute little corner table, privet, but you could still see the whole dinning room. As we receive the our menus we look through it and close it after like 5 seconds... our server comes up to us and said "I'm guessing you don't have any questions about the menu"... I'm like NoP we want The Farmers Feast! :)  she told us that she loved the feast of today and what a great choice we had made.(she was really nice) We ordered their 2 cocktails which were really good i cant remember Eddies but it was really fruity and delish. I had the Salt and Pepper which is made with the pickling liquid of their house made pickles and the black pepper gives it a little kick... loved it!

Then our food starts arriving!!! (we really didn't wait for food it just kept coming!)

We first get the really cool mini veggies plate (the little veggies are soooo cute) they are really fresh and tender and coated in a light dressing. Don't be afraid just use your hands to pick the veggies... i tried with a fork next thing you know I'm chasing my mini radish around the table.
Soon after we receive mini beet burgers (also soo cute), Kale Chips and mini romaine lettuce wrapped in some sort of cured meat...mmmmm!

Following we got bread and spreads... OMG! lardon butter... if you cant get enough PORK like me now there is spreadable pork!!! i really couldn't get over it :) and they kept refilling the lardon butter too...in love!

So after all of that deliciousness! The good food starts coming...
1st course- Grilled scallops with razor clams and baby bok choy and a squash puree (exquisite!)
2nd course- Polenta with a soft boiled farm egg and sauteed spinach and a bacon    relish on top( Im such a sucker for soft boil eggs)
3rd course- (this was a gift from the kitchen) Purple potato gnocchi with ricotta and braised pork and mushrooms... it was heavenly! 
4th course- Was the whole PIG... small pieces of all the body parts of the pig including the snout served with herb spetzel Brussels leafs and jus.... i was soo happy how much pork this menu consisted of!

Our dinner was followed by a little citrus salad with Meyer lemon sorbet, to clean the palate. Dessert was a salted caramel chocolate cake and cocoa nib ice cream (to die for) and to finish an AMAZING dinner a chocolate covered hazelnut and a blood orange truffle... i really cant erase this blood orange truffle from my mind! if only i could have a box of them.

In all its glory Blue Hill is an experience on its self if you what to have a meal that you will never forget come here!!!!!


Love and Food = Life... come on' enjoy it!

Last night was a New York moment for us......!!
Blue Hill is exceptional. The staff great...our waitress explaining in detail every little thing on that menu with  passion and knowledge . Egg Cabonara Pasta....legendary, Venison, Pork all great....A tad $$ but hey ho so worth it.....loved every minute of it.

Lives up to the hype!  

I came here for dinner on a Saturday night and was treated to amazing food and service.  

We were seated at a corner booth (request this way in the back) and this gave us a view to see every other dish that we didn't get to try trotted out to other tables.  Everything was so pretty and well presented!

Memorable dishes:  I can never say no to duck and that was superb!  Also the uni pasta was delicately flavored and came with noodles which were perfectly cooked.

The menu changes seasonally so coming back will be fun even though I probably won't get to have the same dishes again, I can say I look forward to the next time!

The wait staff are nice and gave good wine recommendations.  They also did not rush us through our meal even though it was Saturday night - kudos for that because in NYC that is hard to come by even at the nicest places.

When is a technically superior experience at a restaurant disappointing?  When it's just that; only technically superior...

I have been sitting on this review for a few weeks, because I walked away from my meal couple of weeks ago with a "meh" feeling...but I couldn't put my finger on why.

There was nothing specifically wrong with the experience.  The service was friendly and spot on, the wine was great, the cooking was expertly executed; but out of an amuse, two apps and two entrees, the flavor was only WOW worthy on two things...the amuse (for all practical purposes a beet macaron...may sound weird, but was delicious), and funny enough (beets again) the beet salad my brother ordered.  It was one of the best salads I've ever tasted.  The beets were magical.

The rest of the food was...to put it simply...boring.

My first experience at Blue Hill was anything but; so this expectation may have led to the letdown.

In my original review from 2008, I said..." with all of the great options for fine dining in NYC, I would definitely make this a place for a return trip."

In 2012, I'm not so sure.

Guys. Hey, guys. Guys, I ... guys! Listen, guys. 

This was one of the best meals of my life. 

That's right. One of the best meals. And I've led a well-fed life. The ambience isn't anything special. But they brought out a mini beet snack on almond crackers. Here's the thing. I HATE BEETS. But it was marvelous! So I was off to an intriguing start. It only got better from there - I got a tilefish with "spicy fruits and vegetables". I have no idea what was in the spicy sauce, but it was downright magical. Same for the apple cider beignet. Loved it. Enthusiastically recommended.
My favorite restaurant in New York City. They can take the mundane and make music.

My wife and I went there for our fourth wedding anniversary.  Everything about this gem is low profile.  From the entry to the decor to the simplicity of the menu...everything until you get a taste of the food.  

We were tempted to get the Farmers' Feast tasting menu, but opted to go a la carte instead.  Before our appetizer arrived they brought out mini-beet burgers, and we immediately knew that this meal would be a rare treat.  We got the Beetfurter for our appetizer and loved every morsel.  We both ordered venisen for our main course, I ordered KLAAS MARTENS' EMMER AND QUINOA and my wife ordered HALLORAN FARM VENISON.  For our vegetables we ordered the marinated beets and brussels sprouts and pistachios. Every bite popped with fresh flavor.  I entered this meal believing that I didn't even like beets and left with the realization that I just never had them prepared properly.  For dessert we had the CHEESE PUMPKIN SOUFFLE, which was light and delicious.  

Needless to say Blue Hill was just the sort of special meal you want for such a special occasion.  The food was tremendous and the service was incredible.  Our server really went out of her way to make sure we had everything we could want and that it was prepared just the way we would want.  Right up to subtly accommodating my wife's pregnancy needs.  An absolute complete experience.

what can I say...believe the hype...I actually ate at the bar, which you would think at  a place this small wouldn't be that easy.  My friend was a little late so we missed our reservation...but since we were already at the bar...we said what the heck.

Egg Carbonara - gotta do it.  I had the Milk Fed Pig...4 cuts on the plate...and not too much food.  Yes it is expensive, but worth the money.

Rocky the bartender - cool guy.

Perfect!  If I could afford it I'd eat here weekly.  Great food, great service, perfect for real foodies.  And they keep bringing out great amuse-bouches between courses.  This is what all restaurants should emulate.  I'll be back soon (well, as soon as I can afford it).

*Shhhh!* It's a secret.
 In fact it's so secret that this culinary classic's sign is hidden behind a well-sculpted shrub. Only the gleaming "A" on the door suggested that something delicious was happening, down a darkened flight of stairs.

It is no secret that the staff and well-lit spread of wall-lining booths and tables create a warm atmosphere that is friendly, relaxed and refined all-at-once.

The five-course Farmers' Feast is a great menu for that special occasion.
It's not really possible to describe the food as I might in other establishments. The selection of plates are very much a story - a food journey.  I can't just write, "I had the gelato". Although the gelato was the feature of the plate, the champaign jelly and pomegranate seeds built the full flavor experience.

So, with that in mind I'll fumble through some of the other highlights of the evening...

- Marble sized burgers of shredded beet.

- Towering, paper-thin sheets of crispy Kale, served up-ended on a horse brush (untested at the farm.)

- Oven-hot bread sticks paired with a variety of butters and tallows. 

- Pâté, sandwiched between delicate dark chocolate wafers served on slate.
  (Peanut butter cups have some competition...)

-A firm scallop that was so fresh, it could have been someone's  pet.

-The golden orange farm-fresh egg was proof that 
  "breakfast any time"can be life changing.

-The rest of the herd is still looking for the medium-rare venison plate. "Bambi come home!"

I cried into my omelette at breakfast the next morning. 
Everything had changed,

We dined here New Years evening. Blue Hill is in Greenwich Village right off the main path. At first I was not sure I had arrived at a restaurant as it does not scream the obvious.  We stepped down a few steps from street level to enter.  We were seated at a stand alone table with a stationary wall booth seat.  Tables were too close together and seating was too tight. Our neighbor rubbed against our table when getting up even though they had moved their table aside to scoot from their seating.  Also, because seating was so close everyone seemed to be talking in hushed tones to their dinner partners.  It was not a lively atmosphere or particularly enjoyable. Since it was New Years evening, I am assuming the preset menu is not their standard menu. We enjoyed various sushi starters, soup, the rarest duck I have ever eaten but also the best I have ever had, and multiple chocolate delights for dessert. The food was fabulous, small portions with nice presentation, wine was good. Good service as well.

Ten stars if possible... Every single aspect of this dining experience is incredible.The eight course meal and wine pairing was the ultimate experience! This is hand's down the most elegant and amazing dining experience- the farm to table excellence, knowledge of the wonderful servers and managers, and presentation are absolutely devine. Be prepared to be wined and dined, and know that it is pricey but totally worth it. Words cannot express the quality and ambiance, definitely an experience to check off of the "bucket list"! Indulge and enjoy!
This is by far my favorite restaurant in NYC. You get full and simply do not want to stop eating - it's that good.

Wow - 6 stars. This place is so much better than wd-50, not that they can be compared but we just went there last night and it was such the disappointment that we were craving a perfect dinner that would make up for last night. And Blue Hill did the trick, and then some! They welcomed us with freshly baked warm bread (i love bread that's warm; it shows care in the complimentary items) and soft butter, followed by an amuse bouche of mini-beet burgers. We recall the buns were made of ricotta and almond but don't quote me. I had the venizon with dirty carrots. IT was SO good, not overly salty, flavors went so well together and the meat was close to perfect in color & taste. Finished off the meal with a cheese plate. The only thing I'd recommend is to change the tea selection...we really don't like Pursuit of Tea brand and oddly that's the brand every top restaurant seems to offer :( 

oh, I forgot to mention..we also had an app of *fruit and vegetable salad* that they generously split for 2. It made me want to eat my veggies! that's always good. It was a pretty unique mix of vegetables. The cool thing was that it was not all raw...I don't know if it was a blanche or what technique they used but it was not overly crunchy and certainly not mushy. Served on a beautiful slate...mmmmm

Our total including 3 glasses of wine, app, 2 entrees and dessert was about $150. Normally, we'd do the tasting menu but I wasn't feeling two of the items and after such a great meal, I'd happily return for full portions anytime! YAY for great service, exquisite ingredients, and a warm/romantic venue nestled in the Washington Square area. Blue Hill is on the north side of the street and if you're not careful, you can walk right by it.

I've been anticipating a meal at Blue Hill for some time and it saddens me to say that I was disappointed.   

I had such high hopes of a delicious birthday meal but alas Blue Hill left something to be desired.  I will say the service was excellent.  Our server was very knowledgeable of not only the food but the wine as well.  I did enjoy my appetizer, a beat salad, that was very fresh and beautifully presented.  However my entree of striped bass was  lacking.  I will say it wasn't horrible nor inedible, just lacking in flavor.  The description of the dish also included bacon however I tasted no beautiful pig flavors on my plate.  My friend also said his entree was bland as well so I don't think it's just me.........  

For the price point of Blue Hill I do expect a fantastic meal.  Again the service was exceptional just not the meal as a whole

We were the youngest people there. Very old crowd. But food is great. Would I go back after my mandatory three tries? Most likely not. Not really memorable but I recall it be good but no real stand outs.

Excellent food, subpar service. Basically, the food here is amazing but the wait staff needs to get over themselves.Came here with 2 of my girlfriends and we were ignored for about 10 minutes.. and then we finally had to ASK our waitress if we could order wine.. to which she says, umm ok. I love Dan Barber and I SO want to love this place, its totally up my alley foodwise and I love the concept, but Dan.. please.. get more pleasant wait staff!!!

Part 10 of a Series: The PMD Chronicles (How I Fell in Love with a Murderer)

When your murderer beckons to the server and asks, "Do the chefs cook while wearing straightjackets? Because the food's crazy good!" you know you're eating somewhere special. Our server, a lovely young woman who appreciates dining and madmen, divulged to us the secret behind the "bio char." We're not sharing it with you. You'll have to find out by booking your own reservation. 

That a restaurant can serve you tiny vegetables impaled on tines for an amuse and you're grateful: this is the majesty of Blue Hill. I could trot out all the key buzzwords: "farm to table," "locally sourced" and "organic" but you can't eat words (trust me, I've tried). What you can eat are the egg of the day carbonara and the milk fed pig. Though the menu offerings vary based on what's available, these two are spectacular (our other selections were no slouches either), leaving me and my murderer stunned. It was at this moment when one of the chefs wandered past our table and my murderer flagged him down.

"Are you responsible for this?" my murderer demanded, mouth still full of pork and bio char apple.

The chef, an awkward, lanky man, shifted anxiously. "Partially."

"My god, you are a genius," my murderer exclaimed, heartily shaking his hand. "Thank you."

The poor employee beamed proudly before scurrying away.

Don't scare the staff like we did. Just eat and make a solemn vow to return repeatedly.

I really recommend going to Blue Hill at Stone Barns. Not the one in the city.

The experience was beautiful. food was exceptional. playful and creative. 
I tried the 5 course tasting menu and it was honestly so much to eat. I recommend the tasting menu for sure if you have never been here. Reservation is pretty hard to get so plan this in advance!

Blue Hill has received many glorious reviews. I don't know why. 

I invited my two friends Stephanie & Armand to dinner.  We each started with a glass of wine. Stephanie had soup ($15), Armand had the cod head ($16) and I do mean 'cod head', which he pulled apart with his chopped sticks, and I had roasted fennel ($16). For our entrees Stephanie had the turkey ($36). The turkey looked like it was pressed turkey, beautifully arranged as if it were novel cousine. I would have rather had turkey in a New Jersey diner with mashed potatoes and cranberries for $10. I had the tuna ($34). It was beautifully prepared and probably the best tuna I have ever had. Armand chose to have the vegetarian dish. 

When I was outside waiting for my friends to show up, I looked at the menu. There was only one dish I didn't understand what it was. That dish was the cauliflower steak. A cauliflower steak turns out to be a slice of cauliflower about 1/2 inch thick, sauteed or grilled, for ($32 freakin dollars)! I said to the waitress that it probably costs only 50 cents to make it and she said, "Sir, you're wrong." To me, this entree was an insult to good value in a restaurant.  

We had two desserts. The total bill with tax came to $234.08 before tip. I tipped $48 dollars which brought it up to $282.08! Yes, President Obama has eaten there, but has he gone back? I don't plan to go back.

http://woobyworld.com/

Blue Hill managed to exceed my high expectations.  I was originally drawn in by the farm to table concept, but will keep coming back for their excellent handling of my gluten allergy.  The server was extremely knowledgable about the menu items and double-checked everything with the chef to confirm it was safe.  They brought out gluten free bread and a special GF amuse-bouche for me when the rest of the table was enjoying fresh-baked bread and beet burgers with brioche.  My appetizer, entree and dessert were all gluten free without modification and all delicious.

Blue Hill does not live up to its billing as a top New York restaurant. The farm-fresh gimmick apparently makes it okay to charge fine dining prices for ordinary food. I also found the staff surprisingly aloof. 

My girlfriend and I both ordered the tasting menu, and we were surprised by the poor execution. We were either waiting longer than we should have between courses, or one was put on the table before the last one was finished. 

The dishes were neither inventive nor particularly remarkable, although I will say that everything was fresh and well presented. Nothing stood out except the mini-burgers at the beginning, which were notable for being tasteless and sponge-like.

The restaurant has a nice atmosphere, but the staff does not cultivate a friendly, welcoming feeling. Our waiter was absolutely distant. When I arrived early and waited at the bar, the bartender stood around chatting with the waitresses rather than seeing if I wanted to order a drink. 

Bottom line: If you're going to set high expectations in the marketplace, you have to deliver. Blue Hill does not. It is not a good value or experience for the money. There are many other restaurants in New York where that money would be much better spent.

.

This restaurant is as good as it gets in terms of food and experience. I wish the table for 2 were a little more private, but that is about the size of the restaurant not the people running it. The servers were very well informed. I did the tasting menu and really enjoyed it.

Before I get lynched, let me just say, if you had blindfolded me and asked me to rate the food, I would definitely NOT have guessed that it was from a 5*, $$$$ place. Took the visiting parents here for their first dinner on the town, and was generally underwhelmed by the food. The service was great, except that our waitress was not terribly helpful about the menu; when I asked her what the difference was between the two lamb dishes, she hemmed and hawed before muttering something like, "well the lamb belly is... rich." Oh well, you were nice so you get a pass. Bread and butter come warm at the table (and keep coming if you like) and is delicious.

We started off with fried kale/collard chips, which were too salty, then the tiny beet burgers which were ok, braised cod head was fishy (ok, my fault perhaps for ordering fish on a Sunday) not to mention a b*tch to eat and super salty if you merely touched any part of the salt garnish on the side; egg carbonara was good but way too small for $18; the seared tuna from the tasting menu was quite good; lamb belly was kind of tough to get through and yes very fatty; mullet (fish) dish was nothing special; beef strip loin was done medium rare like I prefer but left chewiness in your mouth. Dessert was yummy, we shared the braised pear and the apple dish -- I should mention that you could probably totally forgo the dessert menu, since you'll most likely be served a complimentary mini dessert plus a chocolate truffle pop at the end. 

In summary, for ~$80pp all-in without drinks, I was underwhelmed. Notice the lack of descriptiveness of all the dishes -- that's because the food was merely good, not memorable, and I can't recall any specific tastes that excited me. Sure the ingredients were fresh (and I appreciate locally-sourced), but I won't be getting in line to come back, too many other worthwhile places to try. I have to regrettably give this place an "OVER-HYPED" stamp.

I'm definitely a fan of the whole farm to table movement.  Dan Barber's Blue Hill has been on my restaurant to-do list for a while and last night, we finally got there.  The evening as a whole was a memorable one. 

We started with an amuse bouche of beet burgers on a tiny brioche.  The sweetness of the beets was expected but, the flavor in the brioche was the real surprise.  It lingered a little after the beet had gone and made me wish I had more.  

For my cocktail, I had the Salt and Pepper.  Now, I'm a big fan of gin, especially for the bright, juniper notes.  This was right up my alley.  With pickled green bean floating as a garnish, the Salt and Pepper had enough brightness and contrast to make you think, not just imbibe.  

We shared a few appetizers.  The fruit and vegetable salad was subtle but, also surprising, a trail of very mild vegetables and fruits dotted with a wonderful sauce to drag them through.  The fennel appetizer, by contrast, was bolder and more straight forward but, still delightful.

We all tried different entrees; the Hake, Chicken, Turkey and Pig.  I had the pig with apple and cabbage.  It was dotted with specks of bacon and an apple glaze.  The meat was cooked perfectly and the combination of all the elements on the plate worked really well together.  Our sides were squash and brussel sprouts.  Both were spot on.  I did get to sample the other proteins and they were prepared very well.  There's just not enough to make a fair comment about them.

Finally for dessert, we decided on the chocolate bread pudding and the apple beignets.  One of my party went to town on the chocolate bread pudding.  What I could get for myself, I thoroughly enjoyed.  The beignets were still hot and deliciously covered in sugar and cinnamon.  

I have only a few reservations.  The portions border on meager.  These plates are not fore sharing which, would be fine but not at these prices.   The bartender did seem to get in the weeds pretty easily.  

Overall, they really know how to contrast tastes and textures at Blue Hill.  They definitely prepared some outstanding cuisine.  The restaurant is spotless and the staff is endearing.  It's worth making an event out of your locally grown food at Blue Hill.

A couple friends treated me out here and it was good but nothing mindblowing.

Maybe because earlier in the week, I was at the Modern, Gramcery Tavern, and Sushi Yasuda so my palate was spoiled.

The ambiance was dull and plain with a hint of farmhouse. A gripe I have is that the tables were way too close to each other but I did enjoy the unpretentiousness.

The star here is not the cooking, but the ingredients. Nothing was exceptional but everything was fresh and delicate.

Amazing passion fruit souffle dessert!

Come here for a healthy alternative to fine dining for a nice, unfussy night.

Classy yet unpretentious, fresh, quality, yet inventive, indulgence without the guilt, Blue Hill scores very high on my favorite restaurants list. The space is small, elegant, and cozy, with a comfortable noise level and kind service. They welcome the average walk in wearing sneakers as well as the couple celebrating their 50th anniversary with the same enthusiasm and grace.

Perry L. treated me to an "early Christmas present" at Blue Hill last week and I was blown away by the freshness of the food and the presentation. We chose to partake in the $78 tasting menu:
-  beet burger
-  braised copa
-  bread with arugula salt, pepper lardo house butter
-  beet salad
-  poached egg arugula salad with pancetta
-  lamb belly (for me) and pork medley (loin, tenderloin, belly) for Perry
-  yogurt sorbet amuse with apple granita
-  dark chocolate balls filled with apple cider

Blue Hill absolutely deserves its Michelin star. I'll be back!

I visited Blue Hill on Sunday the 27th of November.  We were seated near the back against the wall.  If you haven't been here before, you'll find the two-top tables incredibly close together, which is not untypical of NYC dining, but even more at Blue Hill compared to its peer restaurants.  It very much felt cramped and hard to concentrate on your own conversation whilst within accidental spray-range of your neighbors mouths.

That said, all the comfort issues went away once the food started arriving.  Which, was fairly quick after ordering.  The bread was warm and the butter soft.  The amuse bouche of "beet burgers" was a hit with me, they should have served four instead of two, but that's just me being greedy.

The apple and fennel soup had a nice flavor with, if I recall, a slight kick in the pants.  This morning's farm egg served was served with a Yukon gold puree and mushrooms and the egg (which was a chicken egg), was succulent and soft and melted in your mouth.  That's what a 45 minute bath at 140 degrees will do to an egg, btw.

The trio of milk fed pig was, good - but I wouldn't say it was great.  The artfully plated on a bed of sauteed greens.  The duck, however, was great and certainly glad I got to share in it.

The apple cider beignet's were delicious, but be careful - just like McDonald's apple pies (not making a comparison at all), the filling is hot!

We had a glass or two of the Tempranillo, fyi.

Would I go again? I would.

The apple and fennel soup with almond slivers had wonderfully complex flavors, though I could have done without the apple bits.  The duck with brussel sprouts had a perfect combination of flavors and textures.  The duck was soft and succulent, the brussel sprouts slightly crunchy and the sauce (not sure what the ingredients were) was creamy but had a slight tanginess that complimented the duck beautifully.  The pumpkin cheesecake souffle was so-so.  My favorite was actually a free appetizer that they served before our meal: a mini bun made of almonds with a "meat pattie" made of beets.  The flavors worked unexpectedly wonderfully well together.

My wife and I celebrated our 2nd Wedding Anniversary on a Menuless Monday several months ago at the height of the summer bounty and I am still wistfully recounting several dishes... 

I wont recount them for you. There is no point.  They have since moved on and I am certain even tonight are serving dishes that pop just as brightly with flavor and inspired combinations.

It is a very small space, not stuffy at all.  Depending on your style, it is quite suitable for a special occasion... you may be seated quite close to others... 

Not many restaurants, especially after an omakase or tasting menu make it back on our ever growing restaurant list.  We'll be returning to Blue Hill annually. It is excellent.

Rating: 4.0, Date Dined: 11/22/2011

Two years after experiencing a private lunch function and a guided tour at Blue Hill at Stone Barns, I wanted to enjoy the city location of Blue Hill for a relaxed but special evening with a good friend.

Service & Atmosphere
The atmosphere at Blue Hill is not fitting of a Michelin-starred restaurant. I understand that it probably wants to be sparse to fit with the rustic theme but it is neither warm nor welcoming. The décor looks to have been pieced together haphazardly. It's confusing as the setting doesn't match the quality (nor the prices) of the food. Having been to Blue Hill at Stone Barns, I was definitely disappointed upon entering the dining area. If you are sitting on the banquette, you are definitely in tight quarters with the adjoining tables. The lights could be dimmed a little to create a more relaxed tone. Thankfully the service we personally experienced was across the board genuine and attentive. 

Food & Drink
The amuse bouche of baby beet burgers on sweet, tiny buns were delightful. The ficelle bread was so delicious. Chewy yet crusty on the outside. Unfortunately unlike the array of spreads we saw on other tables we were only offered butter to accompany our bread. We had the Nantucket Bay Scallops to start. Each of the ten plump nuggets was seared but rare inside, tender and sweet. I chose the Hudson Valley Duck as my main course and it was heavenly. The skin could have been crispier, but the tangy whole grain mustard sauce really amplified the taste and stood up to the rich duck flavor. It was sprinkled with crisp, blanched Brussels sprouts leaves. My friend had the veal schnitzel, two small triangles of breaded veal, also with Brussels sprouts and served with a side of roasted potatoes. The meat of the veal was masked by all of the breading and the portion size was miniscule. Thankfully he enjoyed it because I thought the duck was the better entrée. As a side we had the blue Hubbard and butternut squash. As other Yelpers described, it's pureed with pumpkin pie spices. It wasn't my favorite and given its runny consistency, it was difficult to eat with a fork and knife. We had the wholly satisfying Apple Cider Beignets (a chewy-crispy exterior stuffed with apple filling) and the Chocolate Bread Pudding for dessert. This was by far the fanciest bread pudding I've ever encountered. Not too sweet, formed into a perfect square, but the star was the vanilla bean ice cream on top. The chocolate lollipops filled with calvados were presented in a small glass filled with cacao nibs. Lovely.


Side Note on Celebrity Fawning
Before making a reservation at Blue Hill, I read many Yelp reviews to decide on what to order so as to maximize my limited stomach real estate. I came across a Yelp review discussing the inconsistencies of what was provided to the tables and I can sympathize. Halfway through our meal, a celebrity I did not recognize and his wife sat down at the table next to us. From that point on the service staff started to fawn over them to such an extreme degree that it made me uncomfortable. The waitress started off by saying "I don't want to embarrass you but Chef Barber and the staff are HUGE fans of yours and wanted to start you off with some free champagne". Afterwards, lots of complimentary dishes started coming out as the couple looked at their menu. Once again, banquette seating is tight, so you're experiencing everything whether you like it or not. The celebrity's wife then proceeded to proclaim loudly that they were "semi-vegetarians" and "wouldn't mind having chicken or fish for dinner" but "certainly NOT the veal or the duck". Awesome as my friend and I were in the middle of eating our veal and duck entrees as she was announcing this. The waitress quickly agreed they'd never be served anything like the veal or the duck and went off to inform the kitchen. The whole situation was odd and off-putting. For a restaurant that gives the impression of being exceptional yet subtle, the commotion caused by a single celebrity (based on the reviews this is not the first celebrity to dine at Blue Hill) seemed out of character and embarrassing.

An appetizer, two entrees, two desserts, two beers and a glass each of champagne and red wine brought the bill to around $230. Thankfully half the price of my Stone Barns experience with similar to possibly better food ... and no commute to Tarrytown!

I wanted to give this place 5 stars but it was not going to happen tonight. The 4 star rating is solidly endorsed by the food, of which the scallops and duck were memorable. The docking of one star is because Blue Hill is missing an intangible element that would have made this dinner a phenomenal overall experience. As I am writing this review, I am still full from lunch at Le Bernardin two hours ago. I can honestly say I am aching to go back to Le Bernardin, but I am not aching to go back to Blue Hill any time soon.

Had my first dinner here last night.  Was definitely excited, as I love local food.  But was very disappointed.  Not a whole a lot of positives so I'll focus on what I disliked in this review:

- the decor was fine, but the tables are so close together.  I know it's NYC, but it's a bummer to get dressed up to go out on a date and have 6 inches on each side separating you from all the other couples along the wall, men on one side and ladies on the other.  It's impossible not to hear everyone else's conversations, or avoid watching them eat their food.

- the food was pretty but disappointing.

- ordered the cod head appetizer.  sounded interesting on the menu.  when it arrived, looked disgusting.  actually looks like a dog's head.  it was braised, but not quite enough so it's very slimy.  mild and slightly salty taste, but nothing special.  it was certainly a memorable experience, but not one that i would want to repeat.  comes with a side of greens, which was probably the best part of the whole meal.  i wish it was cooked more thoroughly and with more seasoning - any seasoning.

- this morning's farm egg appetizer - pretty on dish, forgettable in taste.  lightly poached egg so yolk spills out on touch, so this dish is difficult to share.

- entree 1 - lobster.  probably the winner on the menu tonight.  but portion was quite small, and i would prefer a steakhouse lobster or luke's lobster roll any day of the week.

- entree 2 - chicken.  the waiter convinced us to go for the chicken - he said it's often overlooked but is a real standout on the menu.  i wish we had gone with our gut and selected the duck or the veal schnitzel.  but we didn't.  the chicken was sous vide in buttermilk.  maybe i am not edumacated enough to enjoy it, but it basically was a very mild tasting, mushy piece of chicken that seemed undercooked.  actually i think it was prepared 3 ways, with one tiny piece being roasted (which is the only piece we enjoyed) and another piece being braised (?).  very forgettable dish.

- sides of squash/hubbard and brussel sprouts were good.  desserts of bartlett pear and chocolate bread pudding were also tasty.

- booze was a decent value for this kind of establishment.  good selection of bottled beers (no draft), wines by the glass starting at $13 or $14 with generous pours.

- service was ehh.  our waiter was polite enough but was MIA for the last half of the meal.

Lovely intimate atmosphere.  The food is very fresh, which is what it is known for.  The presentation and service is very good. Food is well prepared and very good, but not terribly exiting.  The This Morning's Farm Egg Yolk Carbonara was good, with the sweet corn being the best part.  The Grass Fed Lamb grilled radicchio, cherries and pistachios was also good.  It comes medium rare without asking.  The Chocolate Bread Pudding with cocoa nib ice cream followed by petits fours was a great end to the meal.  I always like some  petits fours at the very end.  A fine finale.

Have been here once before, meal was good, this time it was fantastic!
Cocktail-called Autumn something, perfect Autumn drink.
Bread is great, comes with homemade butter, arugula salt and bacon and paprika butter.  My combo was the homemade butter with the salt.  I did not like the bacon one, way too strong of a flavor for me.
They brought us out some baked(?) kale, presentation was wonderful, I could have eaten it all by myself, salty and delicious and happy to be eating my vegetables.
App.-Fennel...OMG was the best app I have ever had, huge roasted bulb in amazing sweet sauce, Apple/Pickled Onion/Coppa salad on the side.
Also tried the smoked Tomato soup-so smooth, buttery, amazing, I went in for another taste and it was gone. 
Other people at the table got the Scallops and were in love, melt in your mouth.
Entree-Chicken, best chicken I have ever had, sauce was sweet and there was a lot of it which I like, dirt carrots were the best carrots I have ever had (like someone else here wrote). 
Tried the milk fed Pig-wow, especially loved the bits of Pumpkin.
The rest of the people at the table got the Duck, they all finished every bit on their plate.
Side Dish-Squash,do yourself a favor and get this, honestly it was more like a dessert, went with the Chicken, Pig and Duck.
Dessert-I ordered the Apple Cider Beignets, wow, warm apples in caramel, toasted almond ice cream was amazing, wished it was bigger.
Tried the Cheese Pumpkin, thought it was bland, liked the pumpkin seeds and sorbet it came with but I was happy I didn't order it.
End of the meal we were brought  Dark Chocolate truffles filled with Calvados, apple caramel...goodness....wow.

Overall an amazing meal!!!  My entire table did not leave any food on their plates for any course. Cannot wait to come back, a serious special place.
Some problems-drinks took a long time, waiter spilled a drink, special butters were brought out 15 minutes after the bread, long time in between courses (on purpose?).
I gave this place a 5 because the food is amazing and the service issues did not affect my experience.
Had an amazing anniversary/birthday dinner here a few weeks ago. Service was impeccable and the food was absolutely divine. Definitely recommend it for a lovely dinner or special occasion.

My husband and I received a gift certificate to Blue Hill as a wedding gift, and we had high expectations based on the length of time we had to wait before we could even make a reservation. Unfortunately, we both left feeling a little underwhelmed.

Throughout our meal we noticed that several surrounding tables were receiving beautiful small bites compliments of the chef, yet we only received one of the four total things we saw delivered to other tables. Maybe it's because we are young, or it was our first time, or just a mistake, but it left us feeling like we were not getting the same service that most (if not all) other patrons were receiving.

As for the meal, the morningsfarm egg was very good. The table bread was warm and fresh, and we really enjoyed it. We would have loved to try one of the tasty looking spreads we saw on other tables, but we weren't offered any (see above). My husband's chicken with vegetables were amazing. My hake was mediocre to bland. It took on much of the flavor of the Brussels sprouts paired with it, which were roasted and almost too dry. The side of hubbard and butternut squash was by far my favorite--a pureed blend of squash, butter, and spice. Finally, the desserts (beignets and pumpkin soufflé) were delicious. We did actually receive the chocolate lollipops that other tables received, and we were excited that we didn't miss that. These were filled with apple cider and delicious.

Overall, we had a good experience, but had such high expectations based on all the hype that Blue Hill receives. We absolutely love the idea of farm to table and were really looking forward to this meal. Sadly, it left us both feeling like it's a little overrated and that we've had better experiences (food and service) elsewhere.

I live in SF but my girlfriend lives in the City.  I went expecting Blue Hill to be a romantic wonderful evening of California style food, but was very disappointed.   While the ingredients promised to give rise to a wonderful dining experience, it did not.  The chef botched what he had to work with into a relatively tasteless set of food.  But what made Blue Hill the biggest dissapointment was the service. A number of the reviews state that the staff was not pretentious, but we had the opposite experience.  We arrived at 5:30 because we did not have a reservation at opening.  One of the staff said that we could have a table for two but then another said "no- they are all taken, they have to sit at the bar."  We really wanted to try the food so we did.  We wanted to try the appetizers first and decide on the entree afterwards, but were told by the bartender that she we had to order it all at once.  She was extremely rude to us and others throughout the night. Since it was supposed to be a special night for us, we wanted a photograph, but were told "no pictures in Blue Hill."  In the end, we spent nearly two miserable hours in Blue Hill and when we left the table that should have been ours still sat empty along with others that had been empty since we arrived.  Blue Hill, spend more time on flavors, less time on ingredients, and most of all get over yourself and be polite.  Alice Waters would never have tolerated her staff to behave the way the Blue Hill staff behaved.  If you want to really be California Cuisine, get over yourself and just be nice.

Wife took me here for a 30th birthday dinner.  Well done by her!

I would love to give this place five stars, but a few things conspired to keep it a 4.  Also, we had 5 dishes (two apps, two entrees, cheese plate) of which only 2 were extremely good.

First, as we entered the restaurant, a mouse was scrambling inside under the door.  This is NYC, so I'm not above a mouse sighting (hey, it wasn't a rat), but we did choose to point this out to the greeter.  When we told the greeter, she implied that it was a reality of the city and they tried to keep it in control.  Fine.  But a few minutes later a manager came by the table and said in her 3 years at the restaurant she had never seen a mouse... Not sure why the discrepancy between the staff, but it was odd.

Second, the wait staff laid down the incorrect dish in front of us for EVERY COURSE.  This wasn't just putting the wrong dish in front of the wrong person.  One of the appetizers wasn't right, both entrees were wrong and taken to another table, and they laid down 2 desserts even though we ordered a cheese plate.  For the entree course, my wife's wound up sitting in front of her for 5 minutes while they scrambled to bring mine out.  We honestly thought they must have had some table mislabeling issues; the waitstaff was completely confused every time they laid food on our table only to find out it wasn't our order.  Bizarre, because these quirks rarely occur even at much lesser restaurants.  Even more bizarre, they didn't really apologize or try to make amends.

Anyways, moving past this, the food was quite delicious.  The tomato soup is simply amazing, just the perfect iteration of this classic dish.  The lamb entree outshined the pork.  I'm a big lamb fan, and I can't remember I had lamb this tasty, executed so well.  The egg appetizer sounded better than it tasted.  Cheese plate was a strong showing .

I would give Blue Hill another chance on the assumption that we caught them on an off night - obviously the place has a great reputation.  But they didn't do themselves any favors on this night!

Awesome neighborhood hole-in-the-wall that deserves a lot of recognition. Let's just say everything tasted top-notch and was all naturally grown on the restaurant's farm in Massachusetts! One of the mushroom dishes was a bit on the salty side, but nothing untolerable. The freshness and deliciousness of all the other dishes far outweighed that! The wait staff were all very friendly and down to earth, and they even took the time to chat with us and explain the preparation of some of the dishes. The amuse bouches were always welcome and a very nice touch. 

For the appetizer, I ordered the grilled peaches and green beans. You wouldn't normally think of putting these two ingredients together, but it worked amazingly well. 

I had the crispy skin mullet as the entree and it was prepared exactly as I had imagined it would be -- with a crispy crunch on the top and soft, tender fish beneath, all the way to the last bite.

Really wished this meal didn't have to end!!

I'm torn between 3 and 4 stars.  This was a lovely meal.  Was it 5-stars lovely? No.  But lovely nonetheless. 

To start, I had the heirloom tomato salad.  It was definitely fresh, and the presentation was hands-down beautiful.  Was it the best tasting tomato salad I've ever had?  No. But it was good. 

Boyfriend's tomato soup was delightful; probably more so than my salad. He finished his bowl. 

Moving on to entrees, I opted for the milk fed pig.  If I were to do it again, I would choose differently.  The dish came with several different cuts of the pig.  I learned from this meal that I am not a fan of pork belly.  As an aside, why don't they just call it "pork fat", as opposed to pork belly?  At least this way expectations would be appropriately set.  In any case, I was not a huge fan of this dish.  Disappointing, as I typically love pork chops so figured I'd love Blue Hill's pig. 

The roasted potato side was WAY too salty. Boyfriend agreed. 

Dessert was chocolate bread pudding.  From what I recall, it was fine.  Perhaps wiser diners would opt for a fruit-based dessert, seeing as how chocolate does not grow on a farm.  Sometimes, a wise diner I am not.

Service was impeccable, our wine was excellent and I enjoyed my pre-dinner cocktail.  Perhaps the highlight of this meal, however, was sitting a table away from Kelly Ripa, who happened to be celebrating her birthday with husband and friend, the night I was there.  If the food had been mind-blowing, I probably wouldn't have cared.

Blue Hill is fine dining in a not too stuffy environment. And man, is this food fresh and good. They source their produce, fruits, meat, eggs from local farms, i.e. Stone Barns. 

It's not as expensive as 11 Madison Park, but it's right up there. However, it is definitely worth a splurge for a special occasion.

I did the tasting menu. They did not have to modify it to make it gluten-free! Even the almond cake was made with almond flour and no gluten flour! ANd they don't use flour to thicken any of their sauces. 

It really will be a delectable meal. Trust me!

So it looks like I am going to be one of the few 3 stars and it pains me. I had been looking forward to going to Blue Hill for months and snagged a late evening dinner reservation only to see that the place was completely empty when we arrived, so naturally we were confused as to why they couldn't take us earlier? anyway, we decided to stay off the tasting menu and each got an appetizer, heirloom tomato salad and cold corn soup. Both were awesome and the corn used in the soup was extremely fresh and sweet, the cheese used in the Heirloom salad was to die for. We were excited to get to the next course however were extremely disappointed. I ordered the pig and my husband the chicken. Both entrees were clearly quality and tasted okay, however they lacked creativity and there was nothing amazing about them. The plates basically all used the same ingredients and the proteins lacked any real flavor or spice. I have been to multiple farm to table establishments and i had to say that this was the least exciting. Then we went to dessert expecting something spectacular, we got the chocolate bread pudding that the waitress recommended. When we got it, it tasted like a molten lava cake that you get from any restaurant and it resembled a microwaved brownie, nothing special about it. I was possibly expecting that the ice cream on top used local herbs or flavors, but nothing. Just standard ice cream. I have made better at home. 
At the end of the meal they also gave us some mini sweets, based on the quality they should have just not given them because there is nothing worse then leaving on a bad note. The sweets had this wierd mint flavor that just didn't work with the chocolate and the other sweet had this odd raspberry jelly on top of an extremely dry cake. Bummer.

Anyway, we will not be going back to Blue Hill as there are less expensive and far tastier options in the city, the green table in Chelsea markets is less well known but hands down better quality and more creative dishes.

really wanted to love this place.  must have hit it on an off night...but it just was not that special.  i feel like there are a dozen places in san francisco (where I live)  where you can get better ingredients more creatively prepared.

cool space and quiet room.

i trust yelp though, and i will give it another shot.

Menu-less Monday was full of amazing seasonal summer fruits (watermelon) and vegetables (tomatoes, lots and lots of tomatoes) in a tasting menu style.
The highlight was the curry egg dish. 
The chicken was tender and melty in my mouth deliciousness.
Several gripes - because it was menu-less Monday, you simply state what you won't eat (in my case it was lamb) but because of that, my husband who LOVES lamb, also got served the chicken. I felt really bad about this (however the chicken was really freaking good - he said he didn't mind).
I also was really hoping for the roasted veggies on the sticks - but didn't get that - perhaps it was for vegetarians only?

I was expecting so much more...  ordered the chilled corn soup which was ok, the chicken dish my wife ordered was done sous vide and I have to say, what a poor choice of technique... resulted in a gamey, and somewhat undercooked bird.  I had the duck that well executed but the accompanying sauce was some sort of curry tagine that did not accent the duck - I was actively trying to avoid it!  Very attentive service, just ok space...  could not even get excited to try dessert.  Very Meh - cannot recommend...  if you like well executed duck head over to Craft.

Recently came for a nice dinner with the Mrs.  I am all about farm to table and had high hopes for blue hill.  While it was good, it just didnt quite live up to the hype and hyperbole.  


We started with the pan fried egg with fresh corn app, which as others have described is simple and yet perfect.  It was the highlight of the meal for us and something I would order again.

For mains, we had the duck which was cooked perfectly and served with some fresh veggies.  It was solid, but not transcendent.  My wife had the veggie entree which featured quinoa.  It was actually quite creative, fresh, and great tasting, but its presentation left  a lot to be desired (it was just all heaped messily onto a plate).

For dessert, we had the passion fruit souffle with fresh raspberries which was a great way to end the meal.  it was tart with a hint of sweetness and perfectly done.

We found the wine list to be decent with slightly high prices (would you expect anything else).  Our service was good without being overbearing and although the room is cramped/loud we felt comfortable at all times.

Earlier this year I had one of the top five best meals I've enjoyed in the last decade. Every ingredient is unbelievably fresh (that's what farm-to-table is all about), and allowed to express itself fully in delicately balanced combination with creative pairings. The staff was warm, accommodating and helpful.

My husband and I went to Blue Hill last night to celebrate our 4th anniversary. We ordered the This morning's farm egg as appetizer. It was quite good! My husband got the Hake and I got the pig for entrees. Both entrees were good except they were both too salty. I found that quite unacceptable when I was paying $35 per entree to get salty food + both of them had the same problem! I'm not the kinda person who likes food that's blend...Trust me! I love food with lots of flavor, so when I said the food were too salty, it's quite objective! The fish and part of the pork were a little raw and you can tell they had to be very fresh in order to serve them this way! We also ordered the eggplant as a side, but we didn't recevie it. We got the ginger cake with peaches for desert. It was also quite good, but not that special. I had better desert before. The qulity of the food wasn't bad at all! The only problem I had with this restaurant was the service! Our waitress was polite, but she had this poker face the whole night...I smiled at her and thanked her everytime she came by us to serve us and all I saw was her face with no expression. And what pissed me off the most was this manager asked us not to use flash to take photos...Number 1, the restaurant was dark. it's hard to take good pics without using flash. Number 2, if i take good pics and post them on Yelp, that can only help their business. Number 3, this is a $50-70 per person price range restaurant, not some ridiculous $300 per person restaurant...You really consider your restaurant that HIGH class? Really?!

i went here a little over a week ago, and while i remembered the food to be quite good, i have to pause and think for a few moments about what dishes i actually ordered.  i guess that sums up my feeling about the restaurant - definitely worth a try but not necessarily the most memorable meal i've ever had.

Have you ever been to one of those places where every ingredient listed on the menu has it's source listed with it: West Virginia Ham!! Terhune Orchard Tomatos!!!! SERIOUSLY!! TERHUNE!!!! and then the food comes out and it's completely ordinary? Blue Hill is the opposite. They list things like "Chilled Corn Soup, Chanterelles, Pancetta" and then it comes out extraordinary. The info is there on the website for those that want it, but it's not shoved down your throat.

Blue Hill takes farm-to-table to a whole new level. The thing that is so wonderful about it, however, is that they do this without that whole hipster-pretentious thing that has become such an irritating part of the dining scene these days.

I've had several meals at the New York branch of the Blue Hill trio of restaurants and never have I been disappointed. The food is always beautifully prepared, the ingredients the freshest and most seasonally  relevant that you can find in NYC, the wine list is extensive, and the service is better-than-good. It is also not terribly expensive, for an expensive restaurant: it'll cost you more than your average place off the street, but not tons more.

What makes Blue Hill unique is the degree to which they are willing to emphasize the freshness of the ingredients. Can you imagine going into Daniel and receiving a carrot as an amuse bouche? A Carrot? Really? And yet at one trip to blue hill, that is exactly what I was given: a carrot, served in an ice-cream cone holder. At any other restaurant this would be absurd, but at Blue Hill, it works. It matches the style of the restaurant perfectly, not to mention it was the best damn carrot I ever had.

And that is the kind of place blue hill is. Every course is a testament to the restaurant's commitment to using fresh, seasonal ingredients, prepared lovingly, and with great skill so that each ingredient is complimented by the preparation, rather than being overwhelmed by it. It is absolutely unique in New York City: other fine dining restaurants don't do what Blue HIll does, and other "farm-to-table" restaurants are just poor imitations.

The only real drawback is the restaurant itself. Blue hill is small, in a basement, loud, and the tables are too close together to be really comfortable. It is always packed, so these last 2 things are particularly troubling. The dining room seems to be in stark contrast to the food and the philosophy of the restaurant, in fact. 

Anyway, go to Blue Hill. It will give you a new appreciation for your veggies.

From the amuse bouche to start, to the cocoa-dusted truffles to end, it was the best meal I've had all year ... enjoyed the tilefish, and the duck is excellent too.  The potatoes are so far from the run-of-the-mill potatoes. Also the marinated cherry tomatoes (side dish) are not to be missed. Small space, lovely staff. Do make this a special occasion venue. 
Also - must add that we sat at the bar, and really enjoyed the conversations with not only the bartender, but especially the various friendly patrons.

A great dinner is more than excellent fresh ingredients, a gifted chef, attentive service and atmosphere; it is all of those ingredients mixed with skill and a delicate touch.

Blue Hill NYC is as good as it gets for American Nouveau.

The atmosphere is intimate and tasteful.  The service is personal and dedicated without the pretentious edge that some hot spots can develop.  The menu is inspired.

The pan-fried hard boild egg appetizer is so unexpectedly wonderful it's top on my list of "dessert island" foods - and I don't even like eggs.

You can't go wrong if you're with foodie friends and want a memorable night.

Came here for the first time after several meals and a wedding at Stone Barns.  Food was just as delightful as at Stone Barns.  Service was warm and friendly.  We are always amazed by how great the simplest dishes and ingredients taste at Blue Hill.  Like super enhanced versions of themselves!  

One tip - get the 5-course farmer's feast!!  It costs about the same as a 3-course a la carte but is a WAY better deal with a lot more variety and all sorts of amuses and little extras thrown in.  Both tables next to us ordered a la carte and kept looking over to us and mentioning how they should have gotten the farmer's feast instead.
Most overrated place in NYC. It is decent food in a decent setting. That's it. Peaked several yrs ago. Move along. Nothing to see here.

Dining at Dan Barber's Blue Hill is comparable to an expensive introductory course to New York's green market. To be sure, dinner at this low-profile yet Michelin-starred West Village restaurant is a classy affair. But unfortunately the food itself is unexciting and therefore fails to provide a memorable dining experience. 

Dan Barber's penchant for all things home grown is well known. Partnering with his family he opened Stone Barns in upstate New York and the menu at his restaurants feature the week's bounty from their farms and barns. The menu is therefore constantly changing and one would expect Barber to take advantage of this and showcase his creative talents but his dishes are rather unremarkable. The morning egg yolk carbonara, for example, was quite a disappointment. With a watery sauce that felt more like corn chowder and over cooked pasta, to call the dish carbonara was practically sacrilegious. The entrees fared better. The Stone Barns chicken with ricotta stuffed zucchini, broccoli rabe, and pine nuts highlighted the meat's versatility by utilizing both dark and white meat in two different preparations. The vegetable side was a nice contrast but the dish over all was a little too salty. The Berkshire pork is an impressive plate but mostly so in quantity. Various cuts of pork are served along with sweet corn and shiitake mushrooms but the nuances of the dish ends up being lost. It's too much meat and very little variation in flavors. Desserts, on the other hand, were excellent. The chocolate bread pudding topped with cocoa nib ice cream is every bit as rich and decadent as it looks. And the passion fruit soufflé with raspberries, lemon, and thyme is heavenly. The layers of flavors are highlighted through the wonderfully airy texture and it's the kind of dessert that is neither overly sweet nor too heavy and thus perfect for ending a hearty meal. Over all, the menu's shortcomings can be attributed to Barber's over emphasis on the ingredients. Certainly he is to be praised for using only the finest and freshest of ingredients but for a dish to elicit excitement and be memorable it takes technique, which Barber has, and creativity, which Barber seems to be lacking of.
Close my eyes, and I would think I was on Shattuck....different vibe as after all this is NYC, but perfect no the less.

I feel like this place may be too sophisticated for my uncultured palate.  The food was extremely well prepared and innovative, but no amount of tomato sorbet is going to cover up the fact that the appetizer was just a big slice of tomato.  A damn good tomato, but still just a tomato.  I think what killed my experience was the chicken, which I had a hard time finishing.  That plus the price makes me think my time and money are better spent at other places.

"they told me to go to Blue Hill and I said NO NO NO....." so here is our review:

we are originally europeans but we have been living in NY for over 21 years, we love this city, this country and we LOVE  to eat out.

after looking to soooo many good reviews we thought we should give it a try;

- table clothes...yes, presentation is important, but when you are charging $34 for an entree, you can take your table clothes to wash and dry and not place any plastic white paper on top of the table...looks "cheap" or maybe "green" for some people....not for us, please, let us feel your super clean white table clothes sometime.

- server: cold as the winter in NY...not very welcomed, she didn't explain any dish. nothing additional to the menu. we just saw her when we order our dishes and when we got our check. 

- appetizers, beware...and this is why my comment about no explaining any dish. We love fish and we ordered braised cod head. You will get the all head. basically the only thing missing is the eyes. Pretty impressive for a first dish (please staff, beware of that for people that are not used to it). I'm saying this because from  our next door table there was a lady who was almost feeling like throwing up. 
I loved it...but I guess because we are grown up with that experience...we are used to eat pig legs...fish heads, full rabbits....etc...

-Can you please ask how do we want our meat to be cooked? Here is for our server again.
No matter what type of animal piece you are cooking.. do it well and as per the customer will. We were not eating steak, where the BASIC rule for most of the cuisines in the world and stomachs is that the only rare meat  to be cooked as rare is steak, nothing else. I ordered pig, which was as hard as my knife....but there was blood all over the plate!!

-The wine list seems to be done for tourists, very typical description way to say NOTHING,  bright, round, fruity, lean, spicy, aromatic... uh? am I in a wine tasting? no....I have no idea of wine, neither what bright, lean.....means...and I just want to drink a good wine that I can enjoy with my meal. I still wonder if the sommelier was in the restaurant.
We heard another server in another table saying how special was Rioja....uh...so special like what? can you tell me the grape variety? can you tell me how it tastes? can you tell me how the winemaking is done? where Rioja is located? 

- conclusion: NEVER AGAIN

I know, I'm the only person in the universe slamming the place, but...

I had foamy, soppy, drippy watermelon with fatty, thin bacon on top.  Due to the foam and the watermelon juice, the bacon was wet!  And cold!  Eating that cold, wet, foamy bacon, my friend, was exactly as unappetizing as mounting a wet dog and riding him all they way to a land of never-ending Old Country Buffets where all they serve is wet Purina Beggin' Strips Dog Treats.

My chicken was underwhelming.  It was very tender, but it lacked flavor. 

I was wholly disappointed.  I swear I'm no foodie, but I can't believe how unsatisfying my meal was!  I didn't even want dessert, I was so "meh" about the whole thing!  

The stars go to the excellent server (he tried to deny that it was "foam" on our wet bacon appetizer; he characterized it as a "moist cloud."  Why, isn't that delicious?), the great hostess, the ambiance, the butter served with bread (I could eat it with a spoon, let's be honest) and the summer vegetable appetizer with thinly sliced lardo (it was like rice paper!).

One of the best restaurants in the world.  Loved everything about it.  We were here for my mother in law's 70th birthday.  She was expecting an amazing experience (the Obamas had just eaten here, it's in the newspaper all the time, etc.).  We had two children with us who were at the time ages 7 and 11, and who are far from adventurous eaters.  My sister-in-law is a vegetarian - who doesn't like most vegetables.  All kinds of things could have gone wrong given that combination of people!  I was hesitant to bring kids here (and to be honest, it isn't worth it to bring your kids), but my mother-in-law insisted and it was her birthday dinner so...

The interior is very small, beautiful, more modern than I expected given the "farm" element of their food/marketing.  We waited a tiny bit past our reservation but were made comfortable with a glass of wine at the small bar (where you can also eat if you want to try to walk in). Our table was round - perfect for a group of 6.

The food was amazing.  We had mini carrots and radishes to start.  Superb.  Sweet, tasty, served on an interesting sort of dish with greens still attached.  

The adults all had the tasting menu - I think it was called the Farmer's Menu.  The kids had pasta with butter on it.  That is not on the menu, but when we asked they had zero problem making it up for us.  They also made a piece of broiled chicken for our older son.  At no time did we feel like our children were a bother (and thank goodness, they were well mannered too).

We all tried different desserts and each was amazing.  The menu changes frequently and seasonally and I cannot wait to go again.

Man this place is good. It's Fresh, local and well-executed. Magically my expectations were met, and they were HIGH.

The restaurant itself is much smaller than I expected, but this only added to the feeling of intimacy when you walk down the stairs, and into the restaurant that is tucked below a painfully quaint Greenwich Village brownstone. The lighting is dim, the walls, chairs and booths are all colored a neutral grey stone, with warm wood accents. The mood is relaxed, cozy and elegant (in that minimalist kind of way).
I went with a party of four, and we each chose our own entrees and apps, and to our delight, one of our guests chose the Farmers Feast, which basically meant that we were exposed to an entirely different menu, with a few additional courses. With this meal, the palate cleanser before the dessert is shared with the entire table, so instead of having one serving of blueberries in home made cream, we had four, which was a nice treat.

Our meal started with an amuse bouche that was a Barbie sized "hamburger" made with corn bread buns, and a sweet tomato paste center.
We were then treated to a trio of spreads that accompanied some fresh bread. Home made butter (like churned-on-the farm home made), bacon spread (yup, made with bacon, like an elegant version of the stuff that ends up on the bottom of the frying pan you make your bacon in), and tomato infused spread (mild and satisfying). 

For my app, because I must always choose eggs on a menu that celebrates farm fresh eggs I had:
THIS MORNING'S FARM EGG YOLK CARBONARA
PANCETTA, ZUCCHINI AND CORN

For my entree:
STONE BARNS BERKSHIRE PIG
SWEET CORN, SHIITAKE MUSHROOMS, TITAN PARSLEY AND ALMONDS. This was so great because you got three different cuts of pork on your plate, chop, belly and third that I was less familiar with. All of which paired perfectly with the other items on my plate, and with different pork pairings, different aspects of the dish were highlighted. It was so simple, yet so complex in both taste and execution.

This restaurant is a five star experience, without the pretentiousness that follow some of the City's five star restaurants. I will definitely be returning when I have the money.
Perfect!  Imagine wonderully prepared fish and meat with vegetables exploding with flavor.  I can't imagine a better meal.  Go!

This place is a foodie's dream.  Fresh ingredients that are well prepared in a simple, understated fashion.  Blue Hill is a unique hotspot because it's a no frills place that simply focuses on the food.  It doesn't care about being a scene or having the latest Phillipe Stark inspired avant garde decor.  The fresh ingredients are the star here, and nothing else.  I recently had the farm egg as an appetizer and the wild sea bass.  The aroma and flavors will simply captivate you.

Blue HIll is a great litmus test for your relationship.  If your girl likes it, she has good taste and cares about subtle flavors and good company. If your girl doesn't like it, she's a golddigger that only cares about being seen at a place she once saw on Sex and the City.  Leave her.  Life is too short.  Enjoy.

This place is fantastic!! I'm vegan and they went out of their way to accommodate me on Menu-less Mondays.  We told them ahead of time that I was vegan and they made sure it was a great experience.  Every time they brought out my food, they made sure to tell me "it's vegan, we promise!" and described all ingredients. 

DELICIOUS!!!!  My father loved his (non vegan) dishes and the waiter we had was so nice!

It's very rare that I am 100% happy with a restaurant, but I was 100% happy here.  I went home feeling the perfect amount of full - not too full that I felt sick, but full enough that I felt content and refreshed.
This has long been the splurge meal for my wife and I. Never had a problem wiht the service and the food has us talking about moving into a car so we can eat there more often.
Excellent! Good environment, beautifully presented food. Very tasty. Great for a special evening

If you're not a veggie lover, Blue Hill will definitely turn you into one by the end of the night. And then you'll be sad when you try to make veggies at home and they don't taste anywhere as fresh or delicious as they do here.

I took my boyfriend here last night for his birthday, and lucky for us, it was Menuless Monday, an approx. 2-hour-long meal where you have no idea what you're going to eat until it's put right in front of you. Chefs at Blue Hill must be overjoyed on the second Monday of each month. Instead of cranking out the same tired dishes night after night, they finally get to play with that day's freshest ingredients and let their imaginations run wild. 

Here's what we got:

Started off with a shot glass of chilled tomato water. Light orange in color with a crisp, full tomato flavor. Very interesting and refreshing.

Amuse-bouche:
*Tomato burgers with ricotta and almond bun:  These were the most adorable things, and definitely one of the more memorable foods of the night. Imagine a quarter-sized "burger," no more than an inch tall, with a savory tomato spread and a dab of ricotta, wrapped in a light airy "bun" that tasted more like a cookie. It was even topped with little sesame seeds. 

*Grilled padron and shishito peppers:  Deep green peppers charred to perfection. The waiter warned us that 1 in 9 of the peppers is spicy; turned out the largest shishito pepper was the one that had that kick. Awesome flavor.

Bread came out next. Warm breadsticks that were crispy on the outside, chewy on the inside... perfect. They came with an assortment of homemade ricotta, rendered pork fat spread sprinkled with paprika, homemade butter, and spinach salt. All of them were excellent but the boy liked the ricotta the best, while I loved the butter... it was so light and the right amount of saltiness for me. The spinach salt was good, too... looks more like powder and has a very subtle taste of spinach. Rendered pork fat, as you could guess, was pure fatty goodness. We probably ate more bread than we should have.

Savory courses:
*Summer fruit salad with gazpacho vinaigrette, grilled bio-charred peaches, and straciatella cheese:  Wow, who knew salad could taste this good? The gazpacho vinaigrette definitely hit it out of the park, and the peaches were oh-so-juicy. The salad was filled with every kind of summer fruit and veg you could imagine, from cherries, to plums, to sugar snap peas.

*Wild Alaskan sockeye salmon with sofrito tomato and cucumber:  I felt so healthy eating this. The sofrito was a perfect complement to the fish, and the cucumbers we got weren't your run-of-the-mill cucumbers. They were small in diameter, but plump, almost like pickles.
