*Variety of cuts of Berkshire pig with side of corn and various beans:  This, unfortunately, was the most disappointing dish of the night. Not only did they pile on way too many slices of pork (I think it was about eight slices), but there was nothing really unique about the flavoring. It was very simple, as was the sauce that was drizzled on it. The corn/bean side was tasty, though.

Our palate cleanser was a sour cream sorbet with honey and red currants. I wish I got a huge bowl of this. 

Desserts:
*Poached peaches with sliver of almond cake, golden raspberries, milk jam ice cream, and chamomile foam:  I bet you're salivating now just reading that. Words cannot describe how amazing this dessert was. The flavors blended beautifully and my only complaint is that the portion just wasn't big enough. Big props to the Blue Hill pastry chef. And they remembered it was my boyfriend's birthday, so they even added a little candle to his plate :)

*Caramelized flaxseed and blackcurrant chocolate cake:  These sweet little bits came at the end with our check. The flaxseed was in the shape of a little mound, and it reminded me of Korean sesame candies I love eating. The blackcurrant chocolate cake was moist cake with a thin layer of blackcurrant on top. Great way to end our meal.

Our server was great and very attentive. If you're not too much of a picky eater, you like surprises, and you want to taste the real Hudson Valley, definitely check out Menuless Monday on the second Monday of each month. If you have allergies or if you absolutely refuse to eat certain foods, they will accommodate and whip up something else for you. Blue Hill's not cheap (what Michelin-starred restaurant is?), but I'd say Menuless Monday is definitely worth trying at least once if not for the food, then at least for the fun and unpredictable experience.

We ordered a la carte from the menu as we felt that the tasting menu was way too much food. 

The food was good, however, I have had the same quality of food in other restaurants and for a better price. Maybe the tasting menu is way better, I wont know, but this place is not worth the hype!

For a chef that is all over TV etc I expect complexity and more flavors than simple char grilled fish cooked to perfection!!! This is where chefs like these fall short of people like Jean Georges and the like!

I didn't know eating straight out of the earth can taste this good. Blue hill somehow transforms food literally pulled right out of the garden (okay farm) and prepares it to tasty perfection. It's also one of those places that you leave feeling full but not gross, since the food you ate was not only delicious, but also actually healthy and fresh. Easily a "I will come back" place (very important in my book). 

I went with the Farmer's Feast tasting menu - June 22, 2011 (yea I know I finally have time to write a review on the same day haha) 

First came a few baby carrots served... pretty much as is with a light citrus dressing. They were still served with the leaves which made me want to eat them bugs bunny style but in the interest of dining at a fairly fancy restaurant I refrained. Standard carrots served raw; crunchy and complimented with the dressing in harmony. 

Then came the mini asparagus burgers... the asparagus pureed into small pieces and sandwiched between two buttery buns. Tasty little bite. 

Charcuterie - two thin slices of pork shoulder was a nice little addition to lead the way into the actual meal... 

First Course - First of the Season String Beans and Grilled Peaches - Homemade pancetta, Fennel and Cucumber: Let's just say, I'm not really a veggie eating kind of person, and I vacuumed it all up. Maybe it's because the waitress brought out the actual fresh string beans prior to the meal (a mixture of green beans and wax beans), maybe it's the light citrusy seasoning that made the salad flavorful yet light, maybe it's the perfectly grilled peaches paired with the pancetta. One of my favorite salads ever. 

Second Course - This Morning's Farm Egg - Morel Mushrooms, Snow Peas and Lamb's Quarters: Gooey goodness. The slow cooked poached egg blended in creamy harmony with the chopped sweet snow peas. And always a fan of morel mushrooms. Yum. 

Second Course (Swapped one of the tasting menus for a Cod Head) - One of the best pieces of cooked fish I've ever had. A must try for those who come. We inquired about the preparation and was let in on how.... but out of respect I will not disclose any details. Although let's just say it takes lots of love to get that eyeball-less cod head to taste like perfection. The texture was almost crab like... just melts in your mouth. Minimal spices needed as the fish goodness takes center stage. 

Main Course - Hudson Valley Duck - Fava Beans, Garlic Scapes, Peas and Almonds. Nom nom. Once again the beans and pea were fresh and delicious (and I hate peas)... somehow the slivered almonds played in just fine and provided some texture omph. The duck was tender and tasty and the portion size was just right. The best duck I've ever had is still at Alinea but this is fairly close. 

Dessert Course 1 - Blueberries - Stone barns honey, yogurt sorbet - a tasty blend but nothing to call home about. 

Dessert Course 2 - Strawberries - Caramelized white chocolate, Milk Jam Ice Cream - this was the tastier of the two; the caramelized white chocolate was deliciously paired with a little slice of chocolate cake and ice cream. 

We ended the meal with a piece of little brownie that fell apart in my mouth, and a passion fruit marshmallow that was very passion fruity (in a good way). 

Service - wonderful. Passes the 30-second napkin folding test (actually happened within 10 seconds of leaving the table). I spilled some sauce and dipped my napkin into my water to clean my dress and the waiter immediately brought me a new cup of water... impeccable attention to detail. Thumbs up! 

All and all, a wonderful dining experience and one of my best overall.

I feel like a wet blanket here, but wow, worst service ever. Blue Hill has a reputation to live up to ... and they don't. Our waiter was incapable of answering any questions about the menu - he finally sent over another server who was moderately helpful.

When we asked to speak to the sommelier about wine pairings, she came over with two bottles of wine and poured full glasses while explaining that it went with our entree choices. No discussion, no taste, no mention of what might match with our starters. It was startling. I've never seen wine service handled so poorly.

There were many other missteps, but the piece de resistance occurred at the table next to us. A woman was served the chicken entree without the chicken. 

The food we were served was very good - but at those prices, they're selling an experience. I hope they were just having an off night, but it was pretty egregious.

i love blue hill, and can't wait to go back. went with my boyfriend, the food was incredible, service was excellent, and really couldn't find anything wrong with it. can't wait to visit blue hill at stone barns.

This is the Blue Hills in the city. It is more accessible, but I would dine in the one in Stone Barns in upstate NY in a heartbeat.

Don't get me wrong. This is really good too. Just that they serve out of a menu instead of the surprise menu at Stone Barns. So it is not as fun. And it is also more fun when you are up there in the country, seeing all the happy chickens and cows and pigs running.

We shared a farmer's feast and ordered another appetizer and one main course from the ala carte menu.

Everything is all seriously good. My favorite, hands-down, is the duck, which is perfectly perfectly seared and so very succulent, with a crispy skin.

I truly believe that the quality of the produce is what makes the difference. Dan Barber is hands-down the coolest farmer around. Do watch his TED talk on ethical foie gras and be blown away.

Blue hill is one of my favorite restaurants... It's great for a special occasion or romantic date night.

It's a fancy restaurant, but the ambiance is really cozy.  But what I love most is the concept of farm fresh food, and they executed it perfectly.  You could taste the freshness, and they brought out the true flavors.  Presentation was great with each dish, and the taste was even better, from start to finish.  I even enjoyed the raw vegetables they that playfully presented to each table.  It's an overall wonderful experience!

It's 8:30 on a Wednesday night.  I'm at a friend's apartment for an impromptu housewarming glass of champagne.  She says "Let's go and eat somewhere close by".  I say "Great idea - let's yelp it".  Blue Hill comes up tops so I phone and work the "I have a foreign accent" angle with the hostess.  It works.  We get a table for 9:15.

I had no idea what awaited me.  I think that made the experience even more special because it was so unexpected.  

First of all, I was completely unaware that it was a fine dining establishment and I arrived in my usual work attire.  Some ladies were in cocktail dresses.  But it didn't seem to matter in the slightest.  We were treated to excellent service just the same.

We had fresh salads followed by fish.  I'm sorry I'm not being more specific here.  I can't recall the actual fish I chose - but we all had a different one, and we all thought they were heavenly.  Light, fresh and balanced.  I think ramps were involved somewhere.  Or fiddle-heads?  What is this obsession with obscure green thingys?

But here's the bit that really sticks in my mind.  Dessert.  Cappuccino.  But not just the usual cappuccino, no, my friends.  Some inspired cheffy person - some godlike woman/man in white - has taken the essence of cappucino-ness and turned it into a dessert that delights.  Layers of soft light coffee-flavoured ricotta cream, interspersed by layers of a firm, clear espresso jelly (jello not jam), topped by a fluffy-as-a-cloud foam layer.  *sigh*

Go here!  Go here now. Go here now with lots of cash. (It's not an inexpensive meal but its definitely worth it)

Food:   Insane.  The cod- head!  Absolutely amazing.  As usual, we ordered many dishes, and the server cautioned us that it may be too much... every single dish was perfect.

Service:  Incredible.  I hate making reservations, so we are always a walk-in.  They handled us appropriately, told us that a table was available but that they would need it back... No problem, had that same thing happen at an amazing restaurant in Tuscany (Italy) once.  

Ambience:  The back room was absolutely perfect.  The only slight problem was that on our left was a baby (kinda crying) and a couple trying to figure out their cell phone ring.  

Will be back this weekend.  Will have the cod again.

Every dish had an interesting range of flavors.  You can taste hoe fresh the food was.  The service was great. They replaced part of a dish that had goat cheese that my dining mate doesn't like.  It's expensive but compared to others in that range much better.

We had the chef's tasting menu with wine pairings. Top notch on all counts. 

The idea for each dish is carefully thought out and honed to perfection with good and sometimes unusual flavour combinations and textures but all successful. 

Miniature baby raw vegetables served up on a simple wooden stand, excellent bread with a variety of accompaniments such as arugula 'salt', duck pate and other varied items. A deliciously fresh cold vegetable soup which was zingy with fresh, green flavour. 

Carefully poached poussin followed by roast belly of lamb which was a bit like pork belly and just as delicious with perfect balance of meat and fat. A pallette cleanser of honeyed, orange zest jelly and some wonderful minature deserts to follow. Wow!

The restaurant is entered down a few steps from street level and has an understated clubby ambience with very freindly staff and service. Just feels very comfortable and cool.  Sophisitcated and very New York at the same time. A real treat to eat here.

This restaurant is the epitome of class, sophistication and fine-dining. 
The chef is beyond brilliant. I have never tasted food so fresh nor come across staff so knowledgeable in the menu items.

Speaking of menu items, I ordered one of EVERYTHING. I am not exaggerating. I have heard amazing things about this restaurant and I did not want to miss out on a single dish. 

I loved the warm, elegant decor.  I love the friendly staff. Most of all, I love 
the food. 

Just a warning, the food is expensive.  No matter how good, I couldn't justify paying $18 for one egg. (Still an amazing egg though)

The only thing that could've topped this experience is if I was dining at Stone Barns.

Compliments to the chef.

The food, atmosphere and service could not be more perfect. Upscale in every regard Blue Hill is hard to disappoint. Everything on the menu is beyond fresh and cooked to perfection. Great wine list and menu. A refreshing New York restaurant.

Overall, I felt the experience very enjoyable.  Dinner lasted about 2 hours and we started eating at 10pm.  It was the only time we were able to get reservations.  It was a very intimate experience.  I ordered the tasting menu ($78) and my boyfriend ordered a few items from the appetizer so as to match my tasting menu.
Appetizer: Gazpacho, Asparagus soup, morning farm egg, spring vegetable salad.  It's tough to compare which soup is better: gazpacho and asparagus.  Both were really good and very different.  I would say the Gazpacho had more complex flavors (pickled strawberries and lots of greens and some sort of cheese to make it creamy).  My favorite favorite was the morning farm egg (sunny side up with a sauce).  both my bf and I ordered it as there was 2 different types of sauces.  I preferred mine.  Blue Hill knows how to make English peas taste amazing.  My bf had the egg with an onion sauce.  I absolutely loved this dish.  So simple yet so complex. Would def return just for the egg.
Entree: My bf ordered the Quinoa and I had the braised lamb.  We both thought the dishes were a little more salty than we like it.  However, we both loved our respective dishes.  The lamb was melt-in-your mouth goodness.
Desert: we split my strawberry sorbet something.  We're not huge desert ppl but we thought it was ok.

We were extremely full after the meal.  They had little appetizers, breads, dips, chocolates, palate cleansers in between the courses so it was more than enough food.

But, if I could pick my meal I would choose: Gazpacho, morning farm egg, Lamb, and try another type of desert.  However, would I go back?  Not sure. I think it's a good one time experience.  I think of all my "fine dining experience," I really enjoyed Thomas Kelly's Ad Hoc in Napa Valley $50 for the tasting menu.  I felt that was more reasonably price, for what you got.

I have to say Blue Hill in the NYC was a mixed bag of emotions.  On one hand, the food was great and the wine was tasty.  On the other hand, the service was terrible.  Waiters dropped serving trays, messed up orders and only paid attention to elderly NYC socialites. 

The duck was delicious and the coffee and creme dessert ended the night perfectly.  However, the $16 sunny side up egg was a bit of a mistake - it's really just 1 egg.  My boyfriend had the cod head which was accompanied by a rice soup.  It appeared good, but seemed uninspiring.

The duck and the pork were delicious, but the service definitely left a bad taste in our mouths.

I have a feeling if you went to StoneBarn, you won't be disappointed with either the food or the service.  Or if you do plan to go to the NYC one, dress up like a rich socialite (or Skeletor's mom).  The entire Blue Hill waitstaff will kiss your ass and continuously give you free wine throughout the night.  

YOU the average guest will be ignored and your order will be messed up.

This place is amazing!  I would come here every single day if I could afford it.  The food is so fresh and seasonal.  Everything is so creative. I never thought that you could get this creative with vegetables. The poached egg appetizer was so amazing that I still dream of it. I never thought you could elevate eggs to this level. The service is really good too and the place is nice and cute.

This place has a wonderful menu because it is seasonal. It is was a very nice and 'fresh' experience and I love that you can go back and have a completely different menu tasting (may seem scary for those who like static menus). Regardless, good ambiance, good food, very knowledgeable waiter, will return in the Summer.

Excellent food with distinct clean flavors that delight the palate.  The quality of the ingredients (many sourced from their farm adjacent to Blue Hill Stone Barns) is inspirational.  The service is as good as it gets - professional and helpful without being too invasive.  And, the wine list always has excellent wines at reasonable prices that I have never had.  And, I love their bread and their desserts and cheeses.  I could go on.

Loved by foodies (and apparently Obama), Blue Hill delivers fresh and delicious food and quality service.  I had the opportunity to dine here, when one of my faculty friends came upon a generous gift certificate and needed a dining partner.  

We were seated in the back - we gave each other a look as we walked through the kitchen to get there - but boy were we happy with our location.  The front - although perfectly nice - feels more formal and "stuffy," while the back room feels like you are dining in a backyard or garden.  When we sat down, we were almost immediately served these mini-beet "sandwiches."  I popped one into my mouth and thought I was eating a little bbq sandwich - don't know how they got beet to taste that way (vinegar and mustard, perhaps?), but it was tres bien!  

We started with the eight row flint corn soup and first of the season greens.  Hats off to the chef for the corn soup!!!  This beautifully flavored soup is enhanced with black trumpet mushrooms and homemade pancetta.  They knew we were sharing, so brought the table "already split" two bowls.  The greens were also fresh and tasty.  

Next, we ordered the veal and lamb.  Both cooked perfectly - super tender and juicy!  Warning, we were originally going to order the lamb and cauliflower steak, until we were informed that the steak was indeed cauliflower - weird.  

We ended by splitting two desserts - why only split one!?!?  We got the chocolate bread pudding and pineapple dessert.  The chocolate bread pudding was warm and rich with flavor.  The pineapple dessert was a real surprise - hard to describe but excellent!  In addition to the dessert we ordered, they served us two mini desserts - marshmallows and mint-chocolates.

Probably more like a solid 4.5 stars but while the experience was great it simply paled in comparison to Stone Farms, which is a must do.  Nonetheless, the locally grown produce was earthy and vibrant and the other three at our table had the silky and sweet corn soup.  Wow!  Our entrees were generally really good though mine fell a bit flat (the "pig").  The evening was very pleasant, the service was charming and my gluten needs were easily managed.  I do recommend Blue Hill but do yourself a favor and make your way to Stone Farms.

I just left after what is now my 9th time at Blue Hill (2 times @ Stone Barns and now 7 time in Manhattan).  The food is incredibly accessible.  If you have a friend or family member (or child) who has yet to experience fine dining, this remains the absolute best place to take them.  Yet, it remains exciting for even the most jaded among us (something about picked that morning carrots and freshly prepared pea burgers turn that frown upside down).  

Each course is a celebration of the main ingredient:  that days farm egg makes you wish you lived on the farm, the chicken makes you wonder what kind of bird every other restaurant is serving because if this is chicken you won't want anything else, the deserts, too, are both simple and exciting.  

I wandered in on a whim this evening on the way home from work and had a few hours of total enjoyment.  

This is a restaurant absolutely worth the trip.

Worth the hype.

I'm not the one to really enjoy vegetables, but everything I ate here was really, really good. Got the tasting menu and do not regret it.

I would readily recommend this place to anyone. And after all, who is not a fan restaurants focusing on local ingredients? Definitely am coming back to try other dishes in the future.

My fiancé and I have been wanting to go to Blue Hill for a long time and finally managed to eat there last night. We've been excited about these reservations for awhile and pretty much knew before we walked in that we were going for the tasting menu. Let me start off by saying that the service was fantastic. We actually had reservations several months ago but due to a problem with their boiler, they had to call us and cancel. They must have noted it on their computer because as soon as we sat down, the hostess came over and apologized once again (after they apologized on the phone) and gave us each a complimentary glass of champagne. Whether they do that for everyone or not, it was still a very nice way to start our dinner. Once we settled in, drank a little champagne and got comfortable, we started noticing the people around us and the general atmosphere of the place. We were both surprised at how stuffy it was. Some other reviews mentioned that it wasn't stuffy, but I completely disagree. Let me add that it wasn't because of the staff there, they were all easy-going, friendly and extremely knowledgeable, but it was the people around us. I felt like I was dining in Midtown or the UES restaurant rather than a place in the West Village. We weren't expecting a "hip" restaurant, but it took us both by surprise. Women in pearls, men with sweaters draped around their shoulders or in uniform type business suits. And I'm not talking about a few, I'm talking about 80%of the place. Me walking in with red pants and a leather jacket and my fiancé in jeans, felt a bit... inappropriate? I'm not saying anything is wrong with that, just not our cup of tea.

Now, on to the food - first, the breadsticks. One word... amazing! I noticed that everyone around us had these scrumptious looking breadsticks and I started to get worried when 10 minutes passed and we didn't get any yet (oh no! did they forget about us?) but then I saw them come out of the kitchen on a tray (ahh..excitement!) with 3 little dipping additions, which is heaven for me. The butter was clearly made by some very special ingredients and the BEET spice, was one of the best spices I've tried. We were slightly obsessed with it and it was a challenge to refrain from eating the 2nd serving of breadsticks since we finished the first. On to our tasting menu, first came the matzo ball soup (since it was Passover, which I thought was very clever) and it was simple and delicious. Would I order it if it was on the menu, probably not, but it was very good. Then we got a serving of a pasta dish with little pieces of bacon, which was incredible. I wish there was more. I understand it's a tasting menu, but give us some more to taste! Then came the veal which was some juicy, tender and just plain delicious! Easily one of the best pieces of veal I've had and everything else on the plate complimented it perfectly. After the veal and before our dessert, we got a citrus and champagne dish which tasted like an orange creamsicle. I wasn't blown away by it, but it was tasty and refreshing. Dessert was something chocolatey and it was good, but I also wasn't blown away by it. 

All in all, the food was excellent, but I do wish some of the portions were just slightly bigger. I understand it's a tasting, but for $78 p/p, it would have been nice (total bill with 2 beers and tip was $235). If we didn't have all of those breadsticks, there is no way we'd both leave completely full. Our last tasting meal was at Degustation, which is one of the most incredible meals we've ever had, so it was hard not to compare (although we completely understand they're 2 totally different types of cuisines!). The service was great but the again, the ambiance was not for us... so we're happy we ate there, but agreed we wouldn't return. Perhaps we're jaded New Yorkers with expectations that are too high? Who knows but we're excited to try Eleven Madison Park next. Hopefully we wont be disappointed.

You need to go here now! I eat out very often and love to find new places but most establishments don't impress me very much. They're often good but not "excellent, I need to come back here again". However Blue Hill is the first restaurant in NYC that I've been to in 4 years that as we were eating the meal, we were planning the next time to come back. Reservations for the prime dining times need to be made 1 month in advance. I'm sure when Obama dined here he didn't need to wait for a month but heyy we all can't be as special as the pres.

On to the dining experience:
We had reservations but still had to wait about 15 minutes. We got the tasting menu which I must say was delish! The food was fresh and succulent. I didn't even notice I was eating mostly vegetables. Kale chips were amazing, even the butter they had was unlike any butter I've ever had (probably because it came right from the farm like all the other ingredients). If you're deciding to order a vegetable dish here or a meat dish, hands down go for the vegetables! It's unfortunate that American restaurants always focus on meat. Blue Hill will open your eyes to how veggies should be cooked. Oh and for dessert we got this apple dessert with ice cream, forgot the name, but it was so good we were tempted to get another one but refrained. I will be coming back!

We had a great time here.  The food was amzing as fresh (as always) and the waiter was helpful and knowledgable about the menu.  I had the buttermilk chicken and it was full of flavor and very smooth.  My husband had the vension and it was so delicate and soft, he really enjoyed it.  The place was a little crowded, but what you would expect from a sucessful restaurant in NYC.

Truly an experience.  Been here once at the end of winter.

Their whole thing is an ever-changing menu that reflects local foods that are in season.  So pretty much every dish had either beets or fennel bulbs involved in some way, without fail.  Beet bloody mary, beetfurter, roasted fennel, you name it.  Granted this is the best preparation and presentation of winter veggies I've had in recent memory but let's be frank, does anyone REALLY like fennel?  When dessert came we were cracking up, waiting for carmelized fennel bulb with sweet beet reduction.  Aaaand, lo and behold, fennel cononut ice cream.  Pretty sure our delightful and knowledgable waitress picked up on our amusement as when she brought out the desert I'm 90% positive she said, "And here is the fennel course of the evening."  Supertroopers anyone?

Speaking of dessert, I almost never eat it.  That said, every single dessert here was a masterpiece.  There was some sort of carmel with apple balls that I tried and my heart might have stopped for moment.

Sort of doing this backwards, sorry, but I had the tasting menu with wine pairings.  Most of my eating companions were not so adventurous (read: picky).  The Hudson valley chicken was unbelievably tender and delicious.  Wasn't in love with the hake appetizer, and I thought the farmers poached egg was very salty, though that's not necessarily a bad thing.  I wasn't crazy about any of the wines that were served (would not order them again at a wine bar), but each was perfectly paired with their respective serving.

Ambiance is comfortable and tasteful but nothing really exceptional (as it is slightly below street level there is not a view to speak of).  Would be appropriate for a wide range, everything from business dinner for six to casual meeting of friends to a romantic date.

In short, figure out what is locally in season before you go and make sure you're into it.  Whatever it is will be well prepared and you'll have a great time.

My first visit to Blue Hill was with someone doing their senior thesis on sustainable food.  She grilled the waitstaff, and they were unbelievably knowledgeable about everything on the menu.  Was really impressive.  (the food was unbelievably good too)

Went back again and got a vegetarian tasting menu, and it was great.  Since they only tend to use things that are in season, veg menus in winter can be a bit challenging, but they pulled it off.  

One of my favorites.

I made a reservation a month before the actual date to celebrate my friend and my belated birthday. Because of the a month difference, I was slightly surprised when the waitress brought out two bowls of ice cream and candles. 

I had tasting menu and my friend ordered the tilefish for entree and scallops for appetizer. The tilefish was slightly unpleasant since it was cooked rare and the waitress did not ask us how we would like it. Other than that The food was one of the meals I had in NYC. You can taste how fresh everything is. 

From the tasting menu, I had slightly smoked sturgeon, today's egg, berkshire port (bread and fried), fruits (mostly citrus), and caramelized apple and white chocolate ice cream.

My favorite part of the meal is the dried kelp we had before the appetizer and also one of the bread butter-like spread. The spread is made of pork fat. It was delicious!

We arrived early and took a seat at the bar where the bartender prepared me the most fabulous rosewater mocktail I have ever had. The Speakeasy Book Store, (which specializes in vintage cocktails) in Bethlehem, PA has since tried to reproduce this drink for me without success. Our experience at this bar was memorable; relaxing and super hospitable.

Our table was ready on time and we were greeted by the maitre d' whom was polite, professional and quite honestly, a bit blue-blooded. Everyone on duty; men and women alike, wore pristine matching suits with ties; perfectly groomed, well-spoken and very attractive. I couldn't help but wonder about the recruitment process for getting a job in such a discerning place.

When we sat down we obviously expected  to receive dinner menus, only to learn that Blue Hill does not offer menus. Rather, you are given a complete list of all fresh ingredients that are available on that given day. You are asked to circle the items on the list that you do not like. For example, if you do not like mushrooms, you circle mushrooms on the ingredient sheet and all of your food will be prepared without mushrooms, and so on. The items that you do not circle are the basis for your entire meal, all courses. You will only be served the food that you want; this is ideal for anyone with specific dietary requests. The ingredients are then gathered from the farm after your selections are made. Yes, your food is literally prepared through a farm-to-fork process and you will most likely never forget it.

And then there is the acclaimed egg basket. Shortly after we were seated, a server visited our table with a wire basket of brown eggs resting on straw. As Dee would say, "It was very Vanna White-esque." Her hands swaying back & forth, in a loving motion as she told us the story of their cherished chickens and how the eggs were collected within the hour and that they could be prepared as an appetizer.  If you have watched any episode of Portlandia, you will appreciate this.

Regardless of how many guests are at the table, all food arrives at the  same time; multiple servers, each carrying one entree only (other hand behind their back) as each plate touches the table in absolute accord with the other. The table next to us had 12 guests; 12 servers, each carrying one service.

The food kept coming and coming, overflowing; it was out of this world; creative, organic, earthy, dreamy and absolutely delicious. I haven't had anything quite as good since and doubt that I will for a long time.

The service was ludicrous, in a good way. I giggled at the royal treatment which was seriously exaggerated at times. For us, a table of two, we had over eight servers and longed for nothing from the time we walked in the door until the time we left, almost six hours later. Every move we made was monitored closely by employees and when I gave the slightest notion that I would leave our table to visit the ladies' room, a server was at my side, within a split second, to escort me. She slid out my chair, made certain that I knew where I was going, waited and then escorted me back to my table.

So it seems I could go on all day about Blue Hill. Dining here was a really fantastic, first-class and celebrated experience. Quite expensive, but worth every penny.

We had dinner here about a week ago, fresh ingredients make all the difference. We had the tasting menu and it was paired perfectly with wine. 

It was our seventh time here and as usual, it did not disappoint. Our only complaint is that sometimes it gets really noisy.

Probably more of a 4 star place then 3, but the service we received knocked it down.

We were one of the last reservations on Friday evening and our waitress did not seem very happy that we were sat in her sections.  When she came over to ask about drinks and my wife asked for a club soda, she seemed put off.  Well sorry my wife is pregnant!!  This just seemed to set the mood for the rest of our dinner.  She did not explain any dishes or give any suggestions.

My wife had the cauliflower "steak" and i had the braised pig.  The cauliflower dish was amazing, very fresh and the flavors went well together.  The pig dish was 3 cuts of a pig layered upon some type of beet relish.  It was just ok.  We also had appetizers, this mornings egg and scallops.  Both very good, but given the choice for only one we would choose the egg.  Dessert was the chocolate bread pudding, also very good.

The decor is muted and goes nicely with the vibe this place is promoting.  You are seated very close to other patrons, and when one has had too much to drink--as we encountered, makes for some interesting conversations.

I recommend this place and would love to try again, giving our server the benefit of the doubt.

I just ate here last weekend and I gotta say the tasting menu was just ok. I had heard from several friends and other yelp reviews that this was an amazing dining experience. Not so much.

The best part of the meal were the free breadsticks, which were served warm with arugula salt and paprika lardo. Yum. 

Onto the tasting menu....

Hake fish dish had a nice flavor and good portion size but was cooked to weird level somewhere between a steam and sashmi....imagine stringy undercooked fish.  

The second dish was misleading...labeled Steak and Eggs on the menu it was really a fried egg, salsa, 3 tiny coins of butternut squash, and a super tart/bitter cranberry sauce. I am all for playful interpretations of recognizable dishes but throw a pair of quotation marks up there or something to tip us meat eaters that we should expect a veggie dish.

The veal cutlets came next served over a bed of savory spaetzle...very tasty but the breading on the cutlets was a little soggy. Could've been a great dish...

The two dessert dishes that followed were ok. Nothing spectacular.  Sorbet was forgettable...I actually had to look online to remember what the fourth dish was.  The maple butter ice cream with candied apple and milk jam was good, but I think I was too disappointed in the meal to give it a fair chance. 

Pre-Dinner cocktails were ok. We ordered a glass of pinot with dinner and they served it chilled.  I understand the whole "cellar temp" or room temp argument but the glass was sweating with condensation.  Kinda killed whatever flavor I imagine it had before being chilled to that temp.

I think the quality of the food and service was good so I'd be willing to give Blue Hill another shot and just order off the regular menu.  Sounds like the Stone Barns location is where it's really at....maybe it's time for a drive.

I really feel badly for those who had a bad experience here. I highly recommend to go again and give it one more try. They won't be sorry!

cons: this little joint can get super loud! not exactly helpful when on a sexy date

pros: EVERYTHING ELSE

now, please don't walk into this restaurant with ridiculous expectations, as that will only lead to a let down. No, the wine does not taste like an angel-baby cherub's tears of laughter and no, you won't be envisioning yourself romance-slow-dancing a perfect night away with ___insert_dream_dude/dudette_you've_been_lusting_for_since_G*od_knows_how_long_yes_including_imaginary_people_and_celebs_too__ every time you close your eyes after a bite and a chew of the entree. However, do expect amazing service, something delicious that had a lot of care and attention put into it and great drinks. 

why is it missing the 5th star? 2 reasons.
1) this is the first time i ever saw this happen, but apparently, its not uncommon. Our reservation this time was at 6:30 and a delivery was being made and ALL the chefs, cooks, workmen and handlers came through the kitchen, walked through the entire dining room and out the front door to pick up the groceries, all while opening the door and letting in the incredibly icy biting cold winter air into the restaurant. Uh.... one reason why my final bill is so high is because I paid for ambiance. Please give it to me. 
I then overhead a waitress explain it to a patron that this happens all the time and is totally how they do it here. uh.... please dont do it that way anymore. 
2) this one is more of a matter of opinion, but the boyfriend and I just werent blown away by our entrees. We were deeply impressed by the appetizers, cheese plate and desserts. Yes, the egg rocks. and dude, that marshmallow soup was savory and sheer decadence. Dessert? awesome! that pumpkin one was so good, i was tempted to order a second one. Cheese plate is allllmost worth the heart-attack fats it delivers. The boyfriend is from out of town, and i was determined to show him that US local foods, cheeses and fruits are just as good as where he's from (N. Europe). The cheese plate sure proved my point. ...However, for some strange reason, the entrees just werent doing it for us. It just... wasnt kickin'. im sorry I cant explain better, but yes, they were delicious, but no, they just didnt have the same level of amazing excellence as the other dishes had. you try it yourself. Its still great food though.

is it worth it? YES (duh!)

will i return? duh!

90% of "New American" restaurants have the same menu. Tell me if this looks familiar: marinated hanger steak, pan seared arctic char, pan roasted free range organic chicken, free range Colorado lamb chops. You will not find any of these things on the menu at Blue Hill. Their menu is seasonal, original, and a great representation of the simple (but exquisite), faithful preparations of the best of American produce.

When I went there, there were two dishes I remember vividly. The first, a gnocchi with guanciale (aka pork jowls or "face bacon"). Just perfect. Guanciale is pretty much my favorite thing in the world, and the gnocchi were rich without being chewy. Better than any Italian place I've ever been to. The other was venison leg and loin with winter root vegetables. First, the venison, rich, tender, perfectly done. But the vegetables were like crack. I could have eaten a giant bucket of those. I think it was some kind of squash, possibly carrots, maybe parsnips, carmelized in a pan and dusted with uncut Colombian cocaine. My mouth is literally watering while writing this. Sweet, but not sugary. Rich, but not heavy. I really never thought my favorite component of a meal would be the vegetable garnish served with my precious red meat, but I must say, the vegetables under the venison that night were the best thing I have ever eaten.

You should not now be thinking about IF you should go to Blue Hill, it is a matter of WHEN. That's easy: just go to opentable and grab the next open reservation. Enjoy it. Thank me later.

I've been dying to go to Blue Hill for a while and finally went recently for my birthday dinner. It was a perfect evening!

When we walked in we thought it was going to be stuffy, but I was totally wrong.  The service was both friendly and impeccable. The food and wine was as good as it gets. Expensive (my husband had a $17 egg), but worth every penny for the perfect evening. 

We'd love to go back in the summer try the magic that they make with all of those wonderful local summer foods.

My friend and I very much enjoyed our meal at Blue Hill. The ingredients are unique, fresh, and artfully prepared. We ended up sitting at the bar which worked out grate as the bar tender was very knowledgeable about the wine and food. 

We share the grilled mackerel appetizer, venison entree, and chocolate souffle. All were out of this world. 

The restaurant is intimate, tucked away on a West Village side street. My friend's last comment was "how soon would it be appropriate for me to return?"

Rounding out my 20th 5-star yelp, the honor goes to Blue Hill. Truly delicious, it was a beautiful evening of fine dining. They gifted us with quite a bit even before the meal began, from crisp and interesting bread sticks, to an amuse bouche of petite cranberry/turkey bites, and dipping salts of parsley herb, red pepper, and some buttery fat.

Of our party of 4, 3 opted for the Prix Fixe Menu ($78pp) which I'll detail later.

I was the 1 who chose a la carte, just so I could taste a little more variety.

I started with the Butternut Squash Soup ($15) paired with 3 plump marshmallows, topped with caviar. I also got a kabob of marshmallow and squash on the side. Absolutely creamy and delightful, I loathed sharing spoonfuls to my bf.

My main was the Hudson Valley Duck ($34?) with a nutty pistachio puree and roasted brussel sprouts. Cooked perfectly, my duck medallions were tender and juicy with nice crisp skin.

Dessert was Chocolate Bread Pudding ($12). This is a slight misnomer. It tasted more like a dark rich brownie topped with vanilla ice cream. Have to say it was good but really it's a brownie sundae.

On the Prix Fixe side, there was some interesting items: 
- Appetizer: Of note, was the Pig Snout Bacon Combo. Sliced so it wasn't a recognizable snout (luckily), the pig nose was crunchy. Not bad, just more psychologically disturbing. The pork belly bacon that accompanied it was delicious though. So much flavor. And paired with the trumpet mushrooms and hazelnut creme, it was fantastic.

- Intermezzo: Scallops in a light cucumber consomme, this was super refreshing and palate cleansing. Ah so good. I was jealous of not having a full shell filled with scallops.

- Main: Choice of duck and some others. Everyone chose the same duck as mine, just smaller portions.

- Dessert: I have to say I preferred the Stewed Apple with Milk Jam and Maple Ice Cream. Delish. The textures and amount of sweetness was perfect. Absolutely delicious. A deconstructed apple pie of sorts.

Great service, knowledgeable staff, romantic ambiance, fantastic food. It's good.

Pains me to write this...

I love the Stone Barns location.  Probably my favorite restaurant ever.  But, NYC, a let down.

Granted, i visited in winter, when the farm isn't sending it's bounty down.  But, if you're paying for the Blue Hill experience, dial 7's and make the trip up to Pocantico Hills for the real deal.  

The room is eh, the back "garden room" is a joke.  

Ok, the lamb and the venison were good, but got lost in the sea of fine NYC dining.  

That said, can't wait to head back up to Blue Hill Stone Barns this summer!

I love going to Blue Hill. They somehow manage to balance a bit of pretension with a nice conviviality. It's in a basement, basically, so friendliness happens. Also, everyone is so happy, because the food is really so good. The appetizers can be anorexic portions, so it's one of those places you want to hate. You want them to just get over themselves.
But if I can't get over them, then how can they? Also, I think it's reasonably priced, so it's all well worth it.
We had the venison with hedgehog mushrooms and carrots and the veal with braised salsify, hazelnuts and gingerbread- ohhhh. But the pumpkin seed cake with  with fromage blanc sorbet was unbelievable. It was only $12. You'd be hard pressed to find a better $12 experience. The almond cake with milk jam and maple ice cream was not bad either.
It's just always fresh, reasonably priced and never fails to impress.
Go!

I love Blue Hill Stone Barns, so I had high expectations for the Manhattan location.  But given its ambiance and price point, I was disappointed.  We participated in the "Menuless Monday" dinner, which is 5 courses for $95. I should start by saying the food is excellent.  The preparation and the ingredients are top notch.  The scallops were cooked to perfection.  Also, we don't mind that the restaurant cooks what they want for us.  Obviously we have preferences, but we were happy to try out their little venture.

My issue is with the price point: $95 for 2 relatively small proteins, a large-format entree, a sorbet dessert intermezzo, and a small dessert.  It's not a ton of food.  I've eaten at many nice places, and I firmly believe that after paying $95, I should not even think that I could head across the street to McDonald's to have a cheeseburger.  I should be full!  Considering: Alto is $88 for four courses, Le Bernardin dinner is $112 for four courses, Marc Forgione is $75 for six courses, Babbo is $75 for eight courses, The Modern is $98 for four courses, Jean George is $98 for four courses, etc etc... and from all those, I've left really stuffed!!  I've only EVER left one prix fixe hungry (Momofuku Ko), and we've never gone back.  So that is strike one.

Strike two is the ambiance.  I understand that the coziness of a NYC basement has its charms, but honestly the decor is boring and bland with really terrible (fake?) flower arrangements.  I could be anywhere, in any city, at a nice basement bar/lounge.  Certainly it does not in any way connote a one star Michelin restaurant.  Although with only one small window and a pretty deep room, I'm sure it's pretty easy to secure gov't VIPs like Obama.

The last strike is for the patrons.  The average age is somewhere around 50, and it's really not a lively place.  I suppose that is to be expected at a nice restaurant which focuses on the genre of folks who like farm-to-table, but (and maybe I'm just being snarky here) I feel like the women who come here dress like mumsy fuddy duddies.  I wouldn't come here on a non-married date, that's for sure (go to Daniel!).

The no-menu prix fixe format works better at their Stone Barns location because for the price you pay, you get more amuses, the same quality of food, and a gorgeous, significantly nicer surround (a renovated old barn with vaulted ceilings and a wonderful view of the grounds).  It's a real treat.

Went here on a date with my wife on a Tuesday, loved it.  Quaint little place that is sort of hard to find, which I love.  The retaurant is small and intimate.  People seem to really appreciate the food and it was packed but not crowded.

Started with a beer and cava. Had a few glasses of a Pinot Noir. Very nice.

Our server brought us piping hot mini loaves of bread with extremely soft butter.  A nice start.  Then followed complimentary mini beet sandwiches, bun was heavenly and the flavor was vibrant...I don't like beets, but I loved these.

Next up we ordered lamb and venison for dinner.  Venison cooked rare, to perfection, lamb medium rare and there was just a slight difference to the degree of doneness...this is how the chef recomends both and they were both cooked to perfection.  The meats melted in our mouths, were seasoned beautifully and came with delightful sauces...very, very rich and full of flavor...mmmm.  The plating was nice but nothing out of this world...good to keep it simple.  There are minimal accompaniments with the proteins, so you may want to order a vegetable or two.  We ordered the sunchokes ie jerusalem artichokes, they were in full effect with their natural sweet nuttiness, crisped on the outside and buttery inside.  For desert we had the citrus, very fresh...fit the theme of the night which was just that, fresh.  Crisp citrus explosions, tasted better than normal, over a light cake with a very small amount of lemon ice cream that was divine.  Closed with a deep and enchanting coffee with wonderful steamed milk and complimentary speariment chocolates and complimentary hot chocolate.

Overall, portions were modest but perfectly sized.  Food was as advertised, prices a bit high but were worth it, given the extremely high quality of ingredients and powerful display and excellence of the foods full flavor.  Service was good, and more than met our needs.  Give the place a try.  It is a unique restaurant and farm to table is a fantastic, worthwhile concept.

Yowza. Delicious. Started with the braised fennel. Yum. Lady friend had a white fish, I forgot which one. I had the venison. Both were amazing. Side of brussel sprouts and roasted potatoes were dominated. Dessert of apple and citrus were great finishers as well. Fantastically fresh food. I would slot it after 11 Madison on my personal list of must try but it's definitely on the list.

Had dinner here recently and everything was superb. We had the chef's tasting course with wine pairing and the food was great. It's very small in portion but after the 4th course I was pretty full. Presentation was also beautiful.

Ambiance is great, server was amazing and put up with my questions about the obama visit.

I had really high hopes for my dinner here, but unfortunately it was a bit of a disappointment.  Although I love the concept of the restaurant as well of the presentation of the food, I was not impressed with the flavor of the dishes.  I found everything was waaay over salted and didn't think much of the seasonings or ingredient combinations.

This place indulges your every food fantasy.  The only place better is the actual Blue Hill at Stone Barns restaurant in Tarrytown.

Go.  Indulge.  Fall in love with your plates of bliss.  

I mean, Obama eats here.  Come on.  It's effing good.
Love the farm to table concept but will have to come back for a real tasting before I can give it a more comprehensive review. Enjoyed the decor and the service.

sub level new york 4 star dining shootin on all cylinders every night with their front and back of the house brigade. great tasty meat and veg done to perfection. BEST FAVAS....I ate there in the summer. service a lil stuffy but good. would eat there again for sure.

It has been over 2 years since I've been to Blue Hill, and I still have such fond memories. I went here to celebrate after taking an exam, and it was everything it was hyped up to be. 

Food was delicious, I was even more impressed with the little tasters that were brought out (which we did not order) than the dishes we ordered from the menu. And I also didn't feel it was crazy expensive for what it was. Fresh food, tasty, very good service.

I went here a shortly after eating at for the second time at Blue Hills at Stone Barns.  It was very different Stone Barns is a more convention style and the NY Blue Hill was more adventurous.  The dishes were uneven and flavored unusually for me, but inventive and interesting.  Some came together, melded and blended, while others never worked. The wines were very good and the service and decor professional. 

I like the atmosphere, skills and creativity.  Given the prices, I expect restaurants of this level to get it right.  Maybe, it was a bad night.

Best meal I've had in New York...  ever.  

Wow.  What a special restaurant.  We had a group of 12 for a birthday.  They accomodated us in a private room in the back, which allowed for us to laugh, and let loose on the special night.

Enough about that.  The food is simply remarkable.  I could go on  about everything I tried, but don't need to.  Check out their menu, Read about their philosophy on food.  Then book a reservation.

One of the best meals I've ever eaten. It's obvious somebody in the kitchen cares deeply about my dining experience. The toasted quinoa with a poached egg nearly made me weep for joy. And I don't even like quinoa. The attention to detail was spectacular--even the sorbet was a symphony of flavors and textures. Our server was friendly and knowledgeable without being either invasive or aloof. Lovely, intimate atmosphere. A++++
Pricey, but worth it. Excellent food, good service. Wine list is lovely. The changing menu and creativity plus the access to fresh food via their own farm makes this place worthy of 4 stars.

A truly wonderful place for a special evening, Blue Hill excels in every category. 

A small, warm dining room greets you as you walk down the steps. The service is first class, with a gracious host, knowledgeable waitstaff and attentive bussers. 

The menu changes daily with inspired dishes featuring Stone Barns farm-fresh ingredients. The wine list isn't cheap but we found a delicious Rioja at a reasonable $60 which they also offered by the glass. 

The food is beyond amazing!! I had the venizon which blew my mind. The rest of the party ordered pig, cobia, halibut, etc and everyone's dishes were outstanding.

The bill was $450 for 6 people which is to be expected at such a phenomenally executed restaurant and I will hopefully be returning soon for  Valentine's Day, Birthday, or any special occasion!

Great farm to table find ; ended up eating at the bar due to last minute reservation and despite the swirls of wind from when the door opened, it worked out just fine. 

I started with the This Morning's egg with lamb quarters which was quite tasty (though every egg I have I now compare to Momofoku's Ko rendition I had there) but a little too soupy for my liking. My wife's smoked tomato gazpacho was spot on flavor wise....simple and fresh, just as promised

The entrees were great. My duck in particular was truly one of the best I've had, and the portion was quite large. Cooked slightly under medium rare, the flavors came out beautifully, and the sear on the outside combined with perfect seasoning, hit this one out of the park. My wife's braised haddock dish was also served medium rare, and the lemon-cilantro ish sauce that came with it, along with a side of pea shoots were a perfect match. Had the haddock been served alone; probably a bit boring, but all together, it was a success. 

Wines by the glass were enjoyable, and the cocktails made by the bartender looked delicious as well (salt and pepper, with pickled garnishes - works in my book)

Besides the duck, nothing was so unbelievable that it deserves a full 5 stars, but a solid 4.5 for great execution and a reminder the food can be simple and still taste amazing. 

All in all, a great experience, and after seeing Julia Roberts dining amongst the packed restaurantt, I imagine we are not alone in that opinion.

Highlights:

1) The Duck - The best duck I've ever had. They'll even split the dish at no charge if they notice that you're sharing with another person. 

2) Stone Barns greenhouse greens with local mushrooms, - This salad is beautifully prepared and has just the right amount of pesto sauce underneath. The mushrooms are earthy and delicious as well. 

3) Service - The service is noticeably friendly and far superior to other restaurants. They're always polite and they happily take their time to answer any annoying questions. 

I'll definitely be back to try their tasting menu!

Blue Hill epitomizes farm-to-table cuisine.  Most of the ingredients are sourced from the Blue Hill Farm and Stone Barns, or any number of other farms and ranches within a 250 mile radius.

The restaurant itself is easy to miss.  We actually passed right by without noticing it.  This makes sense since this space used to be a prohibition-era speakeasy.  Once inside, we were immediately greeted and taken to our table.  The dining room is warm and intimate with a definite casual feel.  The lack of pretense at a restaurant as well regarded as this is refreshing.

Each dish we had was simply prepared, placing an emphasize on the high quality ingredients.  Great care and precise cooking allowed these excellent, fresh ingredients to shine.  For the record, we started with the smoked tomato soup and the roasted and braised fennel.  The entrees were a chicken (which I think was poached) with shelling beans and shiitake mushrooms and a Hudson Valley pan roasted duck with wonderful root vegetables and chanterelle mushrooms.  Our sides were roasted beets and brussels sprouts with pistachios.  Dessert consisted of a chocolate bread pudding with cocoa nib ice cream and poached Honeycrisp apples with honey ice cream and caramel sauce (referred to as "milk jam").  

I'm not sure I've had beets that were so bright or carrots that tasted so deeply earthy.  It is a real treat to eat food that was probably picked that morning.  The proteins also had a deep, real flavor that is simply lacking in factory produced foods.

Service was quick, but never intrusive.  We were allowed to linger over our food and never made to feel as though we had to hurry.  Our waiter was exceptionally friendly and genuine, sometimes a rarity at higher end establishments.

Although certainly pricey and perhaps not a place I would go to again because of that, I highly recommend Blue Hill for their commitment to seasonal and farm fresh food.

Ive been dying to go here. Finally got a table. Love the Farm to Table concept. The ingredients are top notch. We had the tasting menu and every course was perfectly prepared. They all looked great but tasted even better. My favs were the tomato burger, this mornings egg in the pea soup, the raviolis, and the suckling blue hill pig. Incredible.

The food here was so fresh that it did not need much favoring. Very vegetable centric though. I would have preferred more meat dishes.

My rating system:
Taste: 7.5/10
Presentation: 4/5
Creativity: 4/5

Total 15.5/20

This restaurant did not disappoint.  The service was excellent and friendly. The food was impeccable. We had fluke which was done perfectly.  
The seating was a bit cozy but acceptable.
We can say that it was the best meal we had in NYC during our 5 day stay.

Italian food cannot get better than Blue Hill! We went here last year after my husband proposed to me. The ambiance of the restaurant is very romantic-A very good place for dates. The only thing is that its a small restaurant so its hard to get reservations, you have to call a couple weeks in advance to get the reservation there. Highly recommended!!!

I started eating here long before it was well known or stared winning awards.  It remains one of my favorite places to eat in NYC.  The food, the athmosphere, and the service are top notch.  I cannot recomend it highly enough.

Maybe my expectations were too high, but I just wasn't impressed.

Went here for dinner recently and was so excited.  First, I will say that the service was great and deserves 5 stars.  But I found the atmosphere to be pretentious (much more than I expected, bc I did expect a little bit of it) -- primarily the older couple sitting to the side of us.  The close proximity of the tables was a turnoff as well - I could hear both of my neighbors entire conversations.  There is no music playing in the background, so voices carry far...

As for the food, it was good but not outstanding.  Nothing blew me away; presentation was nice, however.   I just can't seem to justify the prices for what you're getting.  My boyfriend & i eat out quite often, and we both decided that we could've had the same quality of meal for about 1/3 or 1/2 the price elsewhere.  Live and learn.  

the wine list is lengthy, and the average bottle was around $150.  

I've heard great things about the farm outside of the city, so maybe we'll give that a try, but I won't be returning here.

My mother and I took a short gourmet vacation to New York and Blue Hill, while great, was the least impressive of our meals.  I loved the intimate atmosphere and contrary to my Yelp-constructed expectations, service was friendly as well as efficient.  I never looked at an empty glass for more than a second, and our meal was over within two hours.

We went with the Farmer's Feast, which was $78 for five courses.  We split a wine pairing for an additional $45.  Right up front, we were presented with amuse bouches and bread.  First came tomato burgers and a little bed of tiny farm vegetables - carrot, turnip, and tomato.  The savory bite-sized "burgers" consisted of a savory tomato marmalade on buttery cornbread buns and the miniscule veggies were crunchy and fresh.  Next came some great rounds of beef and pork salami.  I would eat many a sandwich made with those.  The bread was also wonderful, great tall rustic sticks of white bread served with whipped pork lard, housemade butter, and fine tomato salt.

Our first course was braised hake with coco beans, tomatoes, Titan parsley, and local shellfish.  It was kind of salty, which I didn't mind but my mother disliked.  The shellfish was great, and I'm not sure what it consisted of but the texture was like clam or abalone.  There was also one oyster that was really special, lightly cooked and just gorgeous.

Next came the strongest course of the night, this morning's farm egg with an English pea "redux," pistachios, and face bacon.  This was a soupy dish with some great al dente peas and nice crunch and salt from the bacon.  The egg was spectacular, with a creamy, silky texture that was almost like tofu.  Everything together was simply delicious.

After the egg came the chicken, Stone Barns pastured chicken with Tuscan kale, homemade pasta, Mountain Magic tomatoes, and foraged mushrooms.  Like the dishes that came before it, the chicken was very salty, almost like cured ham.  It was also supremely juicy and moist, with perfect texture.  The tomatoes were also some of the best I've ever tasted.

The fourth course was a palate cleanser with plum, elderberries, yogurt sorbet, and honey.  This was tart and refreshing with a stripe of sticky sweetness courtesy of the honey.

The nectarine dessert that followed was less enticing.  It came with nectarines, pistachios, and lemongrass ice cream, and while it was tasty enough it nectarine dessert tasty enough it lacked cohesion.

There was one last dessert as well, a little pot of housemade yogurt with blueberries and graham cracker crumbs.  This was simple but compelling, and it might have been the best of the sweets.

The wine pairings throughout the meal were pretty good, though not very well explained.  I did, however, get a hand-written list of the wines at the end of our meal on request.

Overall, I enjoyed Blue Hill.  I loved the concept and use of top-notch ingredients, and the intimate vibe of the small dining room.  The food had some great moments, but the meal didn't amaze me.  I would recommend Blue Hill to anyone, but I don't know that I'd go twice as a tourist.
Amazing!  Sat next to where Obama ate.  The food lives up to the hype.  Perhaps the closest thing to Chez Panisse you'll find in NYC.

The food at Blue Hill is good, but not outstanding or overly creative.  Their ingredients are super fresh.  The service is spotty and not up to par for the price.  The tables are a little tight for a high-end dining experience.  Good food and nice enough, but I wouldn't hurry back.  There are better choices for the price.

Blue Hill was outstanding.

Great dishes and I loved the unique presentation of their micro veggies pinned one by one.

Had the tasting menu and it was phenomenal. I loved the combination and balance between seafood and meats.

Funny enough though, my favorite dish was the "This Morning's Farm Egg" sitting on a bed of greens.

If you're on a budget and still want to get a taste of Blue Hill, go a la carte. It's fairly reasonable.

Great service, romantic ambiance, and beautiful presentation. Was not impressed by the desserts though, that was the only downside. very mediocre desserts. Everything else was top notch =)

Having also been to the Blue Hill Farm, I've now collected a set!!!

At this location we finally get to enjoy the fabulous food and drinks without the drama and theatrics. (Don't get me wrong, I loved the experience at the Farm, it was just... different.) Well, this time, it's all about what you put in your mouth.

Without the giant herd of staff maneuvering around you and not being in a huge open space, we didn't get distracted and finally got to focus on our food. Every course was excellent and extremely delicate: taste and appearance. Service was excellent - subtle yet attentive, 2 qualities that I appreciate the most when balanced well. Since it was a romantic birthday dinner for two, I was so glad that everyone left us alone most of time and let us enjoyed our time together privately. When they provided us with service, they did it ever so silently and out-of-the-way that we didn't even realize.

It's a very small, closed and intimate place, but that might have just made the food taste better.

All it's cracked up to be.  The food is wonderful but what stood out was the service.  Waiter detected on his own that we were there for a birthday and added a candle to the dessert (in a discrete not cheesy way).  We got one dessert and one glass of dessert wine and he split the wine into glasses.

Food wise, as close to perfect as you can get.  A few dishes maybe had one too many ingredients on the plate but that's a minor complaint.

Dined here along with three others. We sat in the back of the restaurant in an enclosed outdoor area. The tables were pretty close together, maybe 5 in all and I always noticed as soon as there was a break in our conversation...*Crickets. Im not sure if this was because the other patrons were not as enthusiatic or inebriated as our party, but i almost felt guilty enjoying myself.
A majority of the dishes were accented with tomatoes or corn probably due to it being in season. Everything tasted light and fresh and was overall pleasant. Not sure if Id be back anytime soon, but thats only because there are so many wonderful restaurants to try in the city.

I'd been hearing/reading about this place for a long time and we finally went on a Sunday evening for a 6:00 dinner a few months ago. Being the first seating for dinner we were seated promptly and quickly helped.

Every course we had was delicious, fresh and looked perfect. 

This is somewhere you come on a special night, anniversary, birthday, etc. because it is not going to be kind to your wallet!

I guess I will be the only one to give such a review to Blue Hill but this is just my opinion. I feel that no matter how fresh the ingredients are, no matter how perfectly the meat/fish is cooked, there has to be a flavor to the dish. This I found lacking at Blue Hill. It could be that I ordered the wrong dishes (I went with the recommendations). The poached farm egg was inedible due to the lack of flavor even though the egg was poached to perfection. The fish was the best cooked fish I have ever had, but alas there was no flavor, leaving my senses with a "blah". The chicken again cooked perfectly with vegetables whose freshness you can taste but would you be happy with such meat and vegetables alone and a little salt on them? But then again I keep doubting myself, there has to be something to it if everyone thinks it is an amazing place. Dessert was the better part of my experience there though not exceptional. I finish this review apprehensively as I feel maybe I missed something...

It seems to me that restaurants of this strata are either food-centric or service-centric, but rarely both.  Blue Hill is definitely the former.  (I'm not knocking the staff, I'm just saying, it's about the food at Blue Hill.)

Food:  Our dinner delivered some of the better dishes I've had in New York.  The starters are especially inspired: farm egg with crispy pork belly and marinated green beans -- this thing elevated.  (I have to confess, I'd had pork belly for lunch -- Oops!).  Even my wife's tomato salad seemed blessed by the saints in heaven.  The menu always changes based on the best-of-the-best ingredients available to the chef, transforming what would be wonderful someplace else into extra-inspired and scrumtrulescent.  The main courses were also pretty stellar.

Now the deserts...  Just get one.  Or two.  It doesn't matter which.  They take everything wonderful about a particular fruit, and add everything wonderful about pastry chefs, and that happy offspring is the dessert at Blue Hill.  I would go back just for dessert.   

And the wine was pretty good.  Get the Cote-de-Rhone.

Staff:  Finally, I want to reiterate that I'm not knocking the staff.  Our waiter was superb: he took good care of us, and obviously cared a lot about what was happening with food and wine.  I'm just saying it wasn't one of those 4-Star, army-of-synchronized-back-waiter-type places.

Complaints:  Nothing worth mentioning.

Great spot - I'd say it certainly lives up to the reputation that it has as a small, very high quality dining experience with a focus on fresh / local produce that is expertly executed. The only reason I am going with 4 vs. 5 stars is (the admittedly slightly unfair reason) that I'd just recently eaten at Blue Hill / Stone Barns (the original farm / restaurant about 1 hour out of the city) and the experience there was just unbelievable, and so I'd say my expectations were probably a bit more inflated than is fair...

Other than that, the ambiance, service and food preparation were all top notch. The attention to detail is always impressive - they serve you little amuse bouches and pieces of absurdly fresh and robust local fruits and vegetables as they warm you up for your orders. This is one of the more unique aspects of the dining experience here - and definitely a reason to try it out. The menu is great - I appreciate that they focus on simply, well executed dishes with extremely high quality local ingredients vs. the indecipherable dishes that many top quality NYC restaurants have (i.e. entrees with 17 ingredients, of which you only recognize 3, etc.) 

I'd definitely recommend it as a great date or occasion place - just make sure to go with a foodie!

Sigh, I think expectation is what precedes and explains most reviews.  

I just thought, this should be the best of the best.  In a place known to be excellent there is no reason any dish should be actually bad.  Rubbery, undercooked, terrible chicken.  

We also had an asparagus appetizer that was limp, with little flavor, and overcooked.  For a place that is seasonal I expected the asparagus to be amazing (this was at the peak of the season.)  

I went with my parents and a friend, and we shared everything, as we do.  All the other dishes WERE excellent.  But expectation, expectation kills.

I will say that it is a bit over hyped. I am a farmer and have the same access to the food that they do for the most part. I was expecting more but was not disappointed.

They had a gnocchi with hen of the woods mushrooms that were out of this world. The Chocolate Bread pudding is a great dessert. Overall there are better places for you money in NYC, but you wont be disappointed in what you get.

This isn't much of a "review", more like another vote in favor of this excellent restaurant.  I love blue hill's combination of farm fresh ingredients, simple preparations, and lack of pretension.  I love the fact that they made produce exciting in march.  I love the fact that while not cheap, it is well-priced for what they are serving.  I love that if I choose I can have a (local) beer with my meal without being looked down upon.

This is a restaurant for people who like simple food, done well.  If you're the type for whom every dinner needs to be an "experience", look elsewhere.

I have to say that this review is highly skewed.  1. I've been wanting to go to this restaurant for a very long time.  2. Finally had the opportunity to go here as my boss generously took over the entire restaurant for our Christmas party.  Thus, I was able to sample everything without worrying about the cost. The staff were probably on top of their game because this was a special event.

The food is organic, simple yet & artfully presented.  I thoroughly enjoyed everything.  What I love is how well they were able to bring out the full essence of each food so perfectly.  Something as simple as vinegared carrots tasted so good.  It was really a treat for us!  The chicken we had was moist and flavorful (one of the best my hubs as ever had in fact)  I had the fish of the night which I loved as well.

I hope to visit the Farm one of these days!

My cousin visited me a while back, so I chose Blue Hill as our nice restaurant. (Note: I'm a little rusty on the food.) I was taken to a smaller room in the back, which had about six tables. I think this room was mentioned as an example in a Times article on bad tables in a restaurant, but I liked the intimacy of the room, and hey, no playing eye tag with the server(which was irrelevant here).

My cousin called me, and after playing the "I'm at the bar" "I don't see you" "I'm at the bar next to [more and more detailed description as the exchange goes on]" game, it turned out that had turned up at the right restaurant on the wrong day. After giving her some direction, I waited about half an hour, but I got to chill with my drink and watch the other two tables. I knew things were going to be great when I saw the server offer to bring out the herb another table asked him about when ordering. When he noticed me not-so-discreetly peering at him, he brought the plate over and explained what it was to me. He was also super cool when I apologized and told him my cousin was going to be late.

The food's such that you can taste the freshness of the food. No unnecessary flourishes to show off the chef's skills. This is the place where the food comes first. The bread "basket" had ficelles, baguettes, and something sort of crisp bread. It came with sea salt and fresh butter, an idea that I've been able to take to my kitchen. It's always unfortunate when the bread is yummy, and you know there's going to be even more delicious food coming later. For a starter, we had This Morning's Farm Egg, which was good, but not particularly exciting. It's worth getting though, since it's one of the dishes Blue Hill is known for. For our entrees, I had the lamb and my cousin had the hake. I'm not fond of lamb, but thought I'd give it another go at a place where the food's great. As it turned out, I still don't like lamb. However, I loved the Brussels Sprouts with Pistachios, and I'm like a little kid when it comes to Brussels Sprouts. Our awesome server did not lie when he said that even those who don't like brussels sprouts like Blue Hill's take. My cousin and I LOVED the Poached Hake, which was light, flaky, and not fish. She said it was the best dish she's ever had, and she normally doesn't like fish. I don't remember dessert, besides that it wasn't mind-blowing, but still pretty good.

However, the highlight of the meal was near the end of the meal. I had been talking to my cousin about how I wanted to take her to a speakeasy bar later that night, but didn't make it through in making reservations at PDT. Our server, who was friendly, knowledgeable, attentive without being overbearing, came by and told us he couldn't help but overhear us talk about PDT. He had asked around for someplace else we could go to, and told us about Little Branch. We'd already discussed Little Branch (we'd probably stand around forever outside, then inside at the bar), but that act bumped him up from our pretty awesome server to our f'in awesome server. When we left, my cousin and I both agreed we should leave a great tip(~35%). As we were leaving and near the front door, he came up to us to give us our change. When we told him that was the tip, he protested, and after we insisted, he thanked up profusely and told us the next time we came back, we'd get a round of drinks or something on the house. 

We never did get to go back, but I know my cousin holds Blue Hill as dear to her heart as I do. When I visited her in Toronto, we went out to eat and talked about how, though the restaurant we were at was supposed to be pretty good for Toronto and similar in style in Blue Hill, the service and food couldn't compare to the best of New York, especially Blue Hill. And even if there's more exciting food in the city, I love Blue Hill's style: homey but nice and professional without being too distant. Case in point: the postcard Dan Barber sends out to everyone who's dined at Blue Hill.

When I heard that the Obamas went here for date night, besides geeking out and being excited I'd been in the same space as them, I thought, "Smart man."

Wow!  We just had dinner here Friday night, and we thought it was amazing.   The food, sevice, and wine, were perfect.

The waitress was outgoing and very helpful, the food was amazing, I had the chicken and my girlfriend had the pork with the cherry and pistachio.  The food was very fresh, the preparation was well done, and the wine recommended by the waitress was a great fit.

I wanted the portions to be a little larger but they were certainly adequate, check it out next time you are in the Village.

Almost every night, when my furry personal trainer, Mr. Barkypants, is taking me out for my evening stroll, I pass by a little pane of glass, nearly level with the ground. I can't help myself from voyeuristically peering in at the simple, pleasant dining room on the other side. Even traveling by at the speed of dog, some of the food has been beautiful enough to catch my eye: here, a blur of pink radish against a bed of vivid green; there, the yellows and reds of glistening jewel-like tomatoes. 

It'd been years since my last meal at Blue Hill at Stone Barns, so it was only a matter of time before I succumbed to the near daily reminder of Blue Hill New York. I am so glad I did -- and I'm so glad I did so at the height of summer, in the midst of our great season of bounty. 

Yes, Blue Hill does do farm-to-market, locavore food so well that it starts making you think in terms like "great season of bounty".  I'm not always a fan of the genre, in truth. I find Market Table kind of dull and uninteresting. Green Table in Chelsea Market has the nicest service, but the food always seems to be heavily oversalted these days. And frankly, I think Alice Waters is rather irritating as a public persona. Blue Hill redeems all these bad associations to a great extent. 

We had:

- This Morning's Farm Egg served in this season with a sweet corn, almonds, lardo and new potatoes
- Summer Bean Salad with new potatoes, purslane (both the greens and a few of the delicious flowers), melon and green gazpacho vinaigrette
- Wild Striped Bass with string beans, currants, curry and pine nuts
-  Berkshire Pig with braised and grilled radicchio, pistachios and smoked cherries
- A few glasses of wine, including a really nice, crisp Albariño that was not on the menu, but went nicely with the striped bass

I thought the farm egg would be the better appetizer, since I am probably clinically obsessed with very fresh eggs. The egg was very good, but the accompanying soup / garnish overwhelmed the clean, pure flavor and texture of the perfect egg to some extent.
