I may be in the eccentric minority, but I think I would've preferred to've had the egg all by its lonesome. Still, the dish was quite good and if I can believe my eyes, all those vegetables were diced by hand.

Surprisingly, the bean salad was even better, though not really for the headline ingredient of green beans. The bed of purslane underneath the green beans was the truly remarkable component, fresh, perfect... and so very VIVID in flavor. It was as intense as a strong childhood memory of a taste -- perhaps the first taste one ever had of apricots or ice cream or something you like very much -- magnified by time. This salad has inspired me to plant a bed of purslane in my garden next year. 

I was a little bit skeptical of my striped bass at first, in truth. I don't often like dishes that are labeled as "curry" at European restaurants or restaurants of European derivation. Too often, gringo versions of curry involve untempered "curry powder" and the acrid flavor that results is an abomination. Thankfully, Blue Hill's curried green beans, served with a nicely cooked, fresh square of striped bass, were not that at all. There was a slight hint of sourness that was somewhat reminiscent of a Thai curry, but the unlikely addition of pine nuts and a few currants made the dish its own thing, completely. The flavors mostly worked. My only complaint about the dish is that the green beans in it were mushy and overcooked. 

I didn't try any of my SO's pork, but it came as what looked like small medallions of tenderloin and a slice of pork belly with a smear of what tasted like toasted pistachio butter. He loved his dish. I loved the lick of pistachio butter I stole from his plate. 

Whether it was because of the heat or the portion sizes or just the fact that the courses took a long time to come, we were pleasantly full by this time and didn't really want to stick around for dessert. Despite our less spendy ways, our gracious waiter didn't change his attitude at all. He was, in general, very helpful and on the ball. Earlier in the evening, he'd brought out three wines for me to taste after he found they were out of the original dry Riesling I'd ordered. The Albarino was his recommendation and a very nice substitute. I was even more impressed by the fact that he really took the time to chat with a single diner sitting by himself a few tables away. 

It is true that the kitchen (and therefore service) are a bit slow -- but I've read that the kitchen is also remarkably small, which helps to explain things. I'm not sure I'd be able to sit through an entire tasting menu, though the glimpses I caught of it as it went to an adjoining table looked like fine art. 

Very enjoyable meal, overall. I can't wait to try more of the menu.

Has anyone had the maine crab appetizer with avocado squash and strawberries? I did not like this dish at all. I figure it's just not my personal taste but was fairly surprised because I do like the individual ingredients.

The veal on the other hand was very tender and I loved the mushrooms and corn that was served underneath. The bf had this morning's farm egg and the pork and could not have been happier with both choices.

The pork was served 2 ways. The shoulder on one side of the plate and 2 impossibly crispy slices of the belly on the other. Served on top of red rice, this dish was insanely rich..a pork lover's dream! 

For dessert we shared the chocolate bread pudding and raspberries. I wasn't a huge fan of the raspberries dessert as a whole although the raspberries themselves were very nice. The bread pudding was probably one of the best chocolate deserts i've had in a restaurant. 

All in all it was a lovely meal although I would suggest to skip the crab and I should have listened to the server when he suggested the peaches over the raspberries. It's generally best to listen to the server's recommendations!

If it's good enough for Barack Obama, then it's good enough for me to celebrate my promotion, right? 

Blue Hill touts one Michelin star - this is quite evident by the use of the freshest ingredients that I have tasted. My family and I decided on the 5 course tasting menu with wine pairing for such a special occasion. The sommelier was extremely knowledgeable and frequently asked us of our thoughts on the pairings. 

The service started out at warp speed. Our three amuse bouches came out WAY too quickly and the first course of mackerel was already arriving at the table. We asked our server if she could slow things down a bit. The presentation of one of the amuse bouches, a little rack of baby vegetables, was adorable. They were lightly salted - but I was still able to taste the freshness, earthiness, and crispness of each. The hot baguettes (bouche 2) came with two different types of butter and tomato salt. This tomato salt was phenomenal, you'll want to eat bread all evening because of it! Three tiny green pea burgers were brought to our table and these were not only extremely cute, but extremely tasty! We also received small slices of cured pork - also very good. 

Each of our courses used very simple ingredients to create complex flavors, compliments, and contrasts. The best example of this was the Blue Hill Farm Egg. Served in a subtype dish, there were small chopped up greens and corn. Once you broke the yolk, it was truly a refreshing dish that made the syrupy wine it was paired with taste a bit drier. 

My family agreed that by far, our favorite dish of the evening was the eggplant three ways: pureed, marinated then roasted with mushrooms and heirloom tomatoes, and marinated with duck. The eggplant with tomatoes was very simple concept, but its preparation made it the star of the evening. 

The palate cleanser consisted of elderflower and fresh strawberries - so refreshing on a hot and humid summer day. For dessert, we had a cherry and chocolate dessert, served with a cherry ice wine. Once again, this sommelier really knew her stuff. Paired with the dessert, the ice wine was the perfect balance of sweet and tart. 

What was best about the meal is that although there is a lot of food, my stomach felt content, balanced, and not disgustingly stuffed. (Plus, mom and dad picked up the tab so my wallet was spared.) I am truly grateful to have experienced such a fantastic meal to commemorate one of the first defining moments of my career. 

My family is already talking about giving the Westchester location a try!

I would like to undercut Buo Z.'s rating by .25 stars.

The fine dining scene in Greenwich Village - Blue Hill is arguably the zenith - is a paragon of civilized living, evoking a good-natured English country nanny. There's modest exposed brick and a prim outdoor space; the whole place rosily encourages stuff like the taking of tea in a tea-length skirt and white gloves without any sense of foolish irony. 

It won't judge you when you show up with gym bag and accounting text books in hand, but rather usher you in (you poor dear) and feed you nice, wholesome meats (we chose veal, grouper, mackerel and calf liver), and fresh beets, peas, strawberries, rhubarb, cream, and the like.

Even though I certainly enjoyed myself, I suppose I prefer a grittier scene - like a single mom nanny with a dirt bike. I walked away feeling that everything was fairly vanilla - with the exception of the vanilla itself - a tapioca and coconut puddle under poached meringue and stalks of rhubarb. That one was excellent, and reaped the reward of an uncivilized consumption.

I didn't know what i signed up until i got there. With few yelps it was a good girls night out. But i am not too impressed with the food here. Although this is a very well-known restaurant. The place is nice and they have a cute a little garden. Perfect for date. 

I think this is a one time experience for me, i don't see myself being a regular guest here. If you get some good deal like restaurant week. I would say it's ok to give it a try,

Went in and sat at the bar for some amazing food. Ended up downing a bottle of Oregon Pinot at the bartenders suggestion and it paired nicely with my entree of rabbit. In all, a good meal that I enjoyed very much.

The  food is fantastic!! Elegant presentations, fresh and simple flavors and amazingly delicious! Flavors are not complex the chef allows the fresh garden ingredients to speak for it self.  Dessert is well done. The wait staff is extremely friendly.  Your hard earned money is worth it.  I hope to be back, however there are so many fantastic restaurants to try out in the city and this place it one of them.

My best friend brought me here for my birthday and it was one of the best meals i have had in a long time. I had wanted to come to blue hill since trying Dan Barber's other restaurant Stone Barns. It is difficult to make reservations so do it early. You will not regret coming here. 
The dessert wine was absolutely delicious, i could finish a whole bottle myself. (Moscato D'Asti).

My husband and I were lucky enough to snag an 8:30 reservation at this amazing place...and we weren't disappointed.  

First of all...the atmosphere is so warm and inviting.  It's like descending into a little den of goodness...the bar is smack dab in front of you when you walk in, but somehow, there were two seats available, and we took them to wait for 5-10 minutes while our table was being prepared.  We sampled some of their hard cider and beer selections, which were diverse, interesting and delicious.   But no time for more, as our cozy little corner table is now ready.  

The tables are close together, but in a charming way.  It reminds one of dining in Europe, where people aren't so afraid of sharing space on a night out.  

The food was great...I won't go into too much detail....you should experience it for yourself.  But the Amuse was a highlight...the Sweet Pea burger...served on a miniature almond bun.  Wow.  Yummy.
And the dessert--if you like chocolate, have their "old standby;"  a chocolate bread pudding, which sounds very unsexy, but the little surprise that flows forth will change your mind.  

All in all..a wonderful "experience" of an evening.  We can't wait to go back.

Wow.

I'm here in the city for a week, and immediately found it's not so easy to get into Blue Hill.  Luckily, tonight it rained.  And I got in.

Immediately, the ambiance.

Within seconds of that?  A team ready to serve from every direction.  Seriously, I was alone, and throughout the 2-hour tour de force, I had no less than 5 people tending to me.

When I was first approached, I asked to have "the experience of my life."  They delivered - nothing short of a feast.

At her recommendation, I enjoyed a green garden gazpacho, followed with grilled wreckfish (surrounded by peas and pistachios.) Next up? Hudson Valley duck with curried beans.  The meal ended with blueberries with yogurt sorbet.  (I'm grossly oversimplifying this menu - there were bits and bites coming from every direction.  The ones I'm listing are part of the whole.)

Seriously, whenever I fall in love with a place, the 3 stars of ambiance, attention, and fine cuisine must align.    Blue Hill achieves all 3 stars, then multiplies them times a hundred.

I think I just had the culinary experience of my life.  

Run, don't walk, to Blue Hill.

3.5 Stars.

Going to both of Dan Barber's main restaurants (I kind of want to visit the cafe to complete the trilogy) within a week was quite the experience. The Stone Barns one is clearly classier and more sophisticated (think Prince William), while the BH near Washington Square Park is the younger wilder casual sibling (think Prince Harry). We were seated in the "garden" which is essentially an enclosed back yard (very cozy, only 6 or so tables, and very quiet compared to the main room). Sadly there was no orchestration of placing the dishes on the table. This place has an a la carte menu, which is exactly what I needed since I've been scarfing down way too much food lately. Overall I'd have to say this restaurant has much better dessert than the Stone Barns location but the Stone Barns location wins hands down in almost every other category except perhaps the amuse bouche. 

The must-try girly drink here is the Elderflower Royal -- pretty sweet but oh so good. Dan Barber's restaurants have the best girly drinks.

Amuse bouche (clearly better than the upstate BH) - Sugar snap pea burger - I couldn't believe the incredible mixture of flavors. The sugar snap pea mix was sweet while the tiny bite-sized buns tasted almost like cake or some other pastry goodness. 

Rabbi Bob's Calf's Liver (very lightly seared, almost raw) - I couldn't eat more than a couple slices of this one as I kept thinking about how I'm eating raw liver. It was definitely good, but too much of a good thing can be bad. 

Mackerel - delicious and fresh. 

Grouper - tender, fresh, and wonderfully seasoned

Rabbi Bob's sliced veal - mediocre dish but the meat was tender and the peas and mushroom were a nice complement. 

Side of beets - pretty good

Side of creamy broccoli rabe - very good but nothing special 

Strawberries with Blue Hill Farm milk jam, almond cake, and ice cream (I substituted the almond ice cream for lemon ice cream) - the milk jam (think condensed milk) went very well with the strawberries and I really believe the lemon ice cream is much better than having almond ice cream on top of the almond cake

Rhubarb with poached meringue and tapioca in coconut milk - my fave of the night. The coconut milk tapioca tastes exactly like my fave Chinese dessert "xi mi lu" which also normally adds taro or some other fruit. I couldn't get enough of the coconut milk tapioca part. I could care less about the poached meringue. 

The cherries dish also looked quite delish but I didn't get to try it.

Very few restaurants in New York City are worth the hype. Blue Hill is one of those restaurants. 

Courtney P. recommended it, so I knew it would exceed expectations for her birthday meal.

Get the five course tasting menu with the wine pairing.

Don't forget your wallet and reservations.

If Yelp could take half-star ratings, I would give Blue HIll 3.5 stars for great service, good food, and nice ambience.

The dining room is comfortable and intimate.  The front of the house was very direct, borderline rude, but our server was excellent.  She made great recommendations and was very friendly.  

My friend and I started our meal with a Fuji apple and ginger soda made by Brooklyn Soda Works.  This is hands-down the best soda I've ever had, and I've had my fair share of sodas!  They seem to be doing a trial run at Blue Hill, so be sure to try it out while you can.

The amuse was a sugar snap pea and almond burger, which was delicious; the almond burger had a very intense flavor without being too sweet.  We had the calf's liver and grilled mackerel as our starters.  The mackerel was excellent, and the accompanying soup of rhubarb and fennel was very flavorful and complemented the fish well.  The calf's liver had a strong, gamy taste that lingered somewhat unpleasantly after finishing the course.  I personally am not a big fan of liver, though.

For our entrees, we had the chicken and the potato and ricotta gnocchi.  
Part of the chicken dish had an off-putting slimy texture and did not have a distinguishable chicken flavor.  I'm guessing this may be because it was prepared sous vide without pan frying afterward.  The rest of the chicken on the plate was delicious, though, especially the cripy skin.  The shiitake mushrooms were very flavorful.  The gnocchi were pretty good, but were not particularly special.  The pork's jowl was extremely fatty, which I can't say I was fully prepared for.  The morels on the plate were excellent.  We also shared a side of beets, which were extremely sweet.  I've never had beets with that strong of a taste, which I thought was a bit overpowering and cloying after a few bites.  But I'm sure they're very highly quality beets.

We had the rhubarb and strawberry desserts, which were both okay.  The milk ice cream on the strawberry dessert was a standout.  The petit fours were very good, particularly the coconut marshmallow.  

Overall, I thought the food was pretty good, but the amuse and the amazing apple and ginger soda were the standouts for me.
Phenomenal food. Amazing staff. Be prepared to enjoy a 2-3 hour meal. Meals are created around the table's willingness to be adventurous. Enjoyed 8 courses along with education around each course.

Blue Hill, a "farm to table" restaurant that serves vegetables raised on their own farm and meat and seafood from artisan farmers and fishers, has high ambitions, with complex and unusual preparations. At its best, Blue Hill approaches the level of a three-star Parisian restaurant like Alain Passard's L'Arpege. Unfortunately, Blue Hill doesn't reach that height very consistently. Our Sweet Pea "Mini-burger" amuse bouche were delightful, but sligtly marred by over-sweet bread as was the gnocci/ravioli by one element that was too heavily salted.   However, other elements of the meal were excellent, and the attention paid to the sauces and presentation of the plates was exceptional.  The cheese course for dessert was a real treat, with some New York cheese that tasted straight out of the best of France.

In addition, the service was excellent: attentive but not fawning, and friendly but not over-familiar.  The wine list was expensive, but provided good range, and the staff was knowledgeable about it.

Blue Hill did not reach the pinnacle we perhaps expected, but it was very good, and I would try it again

Decided to follow the hype and make a reservation after I read about the Obama's dining experience here.  Not sure what the hype about this place is all about. Food was decent, but definitely not spectacular.  Maybe i'll need to take the trip out to the farm to have a better experience.

We had a really wonderful dinner here as part of my birthday celebration.   Very nice decor with a good bar area that several guests were eating at.   

A lot of guests around us seemed to have picked the tasting menu, but we both decided to pick from the a la carte menu.  I knew which dishes I wanted immediately, while my boyfriend needed recommendations because every entree sounded so good.  

I had the Buty Beast Cabernet Sauvignon, which started out slow but grew on me.  We started with a nice amuse bouche - mini sugar snap pea burgers (mashed peas in a cornmeal like bun), as well as warm bread.  My appetizer was the broccoli rapini and asparagus, with hackleback roe, "immature egg" and spiced almonds.  This was excellent.  Fresh and delicious.  My boyfriend also enjoyed his spring vegetable salad, which had seasonal greens, edamame, pickled radish and spiced pistachios.  

For entrees, I ordered the Hudson Valley Duck, which was seared medium rare and very tender, served with soft radishes and diced sugar snap peas, and spiced pistachios.  I absolutely loved both the duck as well as the vegetables.  Another excellent dish. 

My boyfriend ordered the Berkshire pig with peas, red rice, chorizo.  It was spicy, and I didn't care for the taste.  The pig was also rather chewy and sinewy.  This dish was only okay. 

For dessert, we had the strawberries dessert, which was strawberries with jam, almond cake and ice cream, with something like dulce de leche.  Everything tasted great except the strawberries, which were a little too jammy.  We finished the meal with chocolate passionfruit truffles on espresso nibs that came with our tab. 

We were very impressed - an excellent experience.

This was the rare, perfect NYC experience. Our waitress was incredibly knowledgeable, patient and unpretentious (especially compared to Stone Barn, which is beautiful but snootier). The pace was very leisurely--yes, it's expensive, but unlike so many others in this price range, there wasn't a rush to turn over the table (being there on a week night helps).  I recommend anything with the farm fresh egg, the ricotta ravioli, the bread pudding and the (seasonal) strawberry dessert. The vegetable salads are a little unadventurous and rabbit-y. Mostly, though, you can't go wrong. Even the bread was delicious.
Wow! Vegetables actually have good flavors!

I took my husband here for his birthday on a Thursday night.  Because of previous reviews, I was expecting our dinner to be 3-4 hours but we were in and out in less than 2.  Granted, we didn't get the tasting menu but we ordered a good amount of food.  Everything tastes very fresh and the service was exceptional.  I have to say that when you go to places like this, you have to assume that the portions are small.  I personally like small portions so that I am able to try as many dishes as possible.  My overall opinion is that the food is very good but not mind blowing.  

Ambiance:
Very small restaurant with low ceilings.  The tables are too close together.  It could be romantic but it didn't quite fit the bill for me.  I felt cramped. 3/5

Service:
I don't recall our servers name (she looks like Angela Bassett) but she was very warm & attentive.  5/5

Drinks:
We drank wines by the glass, Pinot Noir & Sauvignon Blanc.  They have ice wine on their menu but unfortunately they ran out.  Bummer, since it would have been my first time trying it.  4/5

Amuse Bouche: 
Mini (Mini) Asparagus Burgers - Cute presentation and pretty good.  4/5

Bread:
Very hot and fresh.  No variety but it doesn't matter.  4/5

Appetizers:
Blue Hill Farm Egg (X2) - I thought the egg was cooked perfectly.  Good flavors but not spectacular.  3.5/5

Soft Shell Crab w/ Watercress, Hazelnuts & Asparagus - One almost microscopic crab but it was delicious. 4.5/5

Entrees:
My husband had the lamb w/ broccoli rabe & mini fingerling potatoes.  I hate lamb but I tried it and it was very juicy and had lots of flavor.  It wasn't 'gamy' which is always a plus for me.  4.5/5

Purple Potato & Ricotta Gnocchi -  It's hard to find good gnocchi.  This was almost a winner but not quite there.  4/5

Desserts:
Strawberries, Almond Cake & Ice Cream - The cake stood out in this trio.  3.5/5

Chocolate Bread Pudding - Better than the strawberry dessert.  4/5

This was the perfect amount of food for us. We left quite full.

Went last night was dinner and was a bit disappointed.  I am normally not one to complain about service, but restaurant was packed and it took us an hour to get our first course, and a total of 3 hours to get the five courses of our tasting.

Wait aside, most memorable part of the meal for me was actually the bread - their butter is heavenly, and was so good I took it home with me.  The kale chip amuse was also stellar.  Unfortunately, the entres were good but not great, and one (think it was the blue hill farm egg) was unpleasant and had a generally slimy texture with all the ingredients.

Everything was very fresh, but did not excel in taste versus other restaurants of a similar caliber.  On the plus side they accommodated my girlfriend, who was a vegan.  Her food was probably better than mine, in particular her desert (the apples desert) which is probably the best apple dish I've ever had.
Wow...A *must* go-to.  I think Sai S. covered everything perfectly.  Absolutely one of the best experiences I have ever had.  I will be back again and again.

Cocktails= yum

Food= pretty damn good. I did not realize how much I love me some ramps.  I went with two appetizers and could not have been happier. GRILLED SPANISH MACKERAL
DANDELION GREENS, RAMPS AND PRESERVED MEYER LEMON

SPRING VEGETABLE SALAD
STONE BARNS LETTUCE, SPICED PISTACHIOS AND SOYBEANS

Momma was happy.

Service= slow as hell but,  I forgive you guys.  We closed this place down and not on purpose! On a Monday night no less.  Reservations at 8..we didn't get out of there until way past midnight.  Longest dinner service ever but the food was great so, I can't complain.  Looking forward to heading Upstate to their farm this summer.

5 course tasting menu, $72

I expected an older more stuffy crowd but not tonight. Plenty of young couples, a very good looking crowd I must admit. Although the crowd was not exactly a bastion of cultural diversity.

At the start (830am), I mentioned my 2 hour time limit due to another event. I was worried given the other yelp reviews of 3 to 4 hour dinners that this wouldn't happen, but I was in and out in 2 hours (with 15 min to spare). And I never ever felt rushed at all. Well done. 

On to the food!

Amuse
Salami + mini asparagus burger + spring vegetables. Neat presentation, looked like they were just plucked from the farm. Super fresh. I could have had 50 of the asparagus burgers, very nice.

Bread
2 butters with 2 salts (arugula and carrot). Nice touch. The butters were insanely fresh. 

First course
Block Island Tilefish. Tilefish with a green sauce made of wild onion and garlic. Un-real!! So good, so fresh and the green sauce made me want to lick my plate. 

Second course
Blue Hill Farm Egg
Wow, did not expect an egg to taste like this. The texture, flavor, gentleness was outstanding. I liken it to the tofu at a Michelin rated Japanese place versus your daily tofu --- both are called tofu but they are night and day different.

Third course
Farmer's Cross Pig
So succulent! Tasted "healthy" the way they cooked it. I never ever order pork as my main as I generally am not a pork fan but this plate was incredible. So well cooked! Simple yet brilliant. 

Dessert amuse
Rhubarb
Seems to be in these days, got something similar at Sho. The ice cream was perfect and the rhubarb was fresh and excellent. The syrup soup was sweet but not overly so like at Sho. 

Dessert
Flourless chocolate cake
Flavorful and not overwhelming. Very nice. This coming from someone who doesn't really like chocolate too much.

After dinner sweets
Coconut covered marshmallow and an incredible orange truffle. I wish I had more of the truffles!

Service --- very down to earth (unlike that of most higher end places), attentive, friendly. Perhaps the best service I have had in a long time. If I even made a funny face after a bite, he would come by to make sure it was ok. In between the 2nd and 3rd course, after it had been 20 or so min, he came by and said "let me check on your entree". He even asked twice to see if I felt rushed. Attentive in the best possible way. 

And at $72, the Farmer's Feast is an absolute no brainer. Don't bother ordering a la carte. Bravo Blue Hill, clearly worthy of 5 stars and now I am just debating if this will be my #1 fav amongst the Michelin's in NYC or at worst, 2nd or 3rd.

I was very excited to dine at Blue Hill and they did not disappoint. Was made to feel very welcome upon entering the restaurant. We were there for an early reservation so the place was fairly empty but it filled up by around 7pm. All of the dishes were excellent, one nice surprise at the start of the meal were these asparagus sliders that were some of the most delicious and interesting things I ever tasted. We shared the pasta appetizer, which was small, but when you want to try so many things on the menu, this is a good thing. For dinner, I had the tilefish, which was cooked perfectly and sitting in a divine sauce. The chocolate bread pudding for dessert is amazing, and definitely more like a rich chocolate cake. This is a great restaurant for a special occasion, tho I wish I could dine there more often. Will definitely have to go to the farm upstate one day.

Blue Hill served me an absolutely fabulous meal replete with some of the freshest ingredients I ever tasted.  This observation is counterbalanced by the fact that Blue Hill has the slowest service of the more than 35 Michelin starred restaurants I have been to in the city.  Fortunately enough for Blue Hill, the food is worth the wait. 

Our table of six was split evenly between partaking in that evening's tasting menu or ordering a la carte.  It was with great fortune that Blue Hill will allow both types of service at the same table -- a rarity.  I opted for the 5 course tasting menu ($72) along with wine pairings ($42).  

Amuse Bouche 1:  a rack of baby spring vegetables with greens attached.  Whimsical, folksy, and delicious.  Adorned only with salt, these vegetables were excellent and obviously freshly picked.  The signal was clear for what lied ahead.  

Amuse Bouche 2:  Bread.  First served with butter (seemingly freshly churned) and then again later with a selection of powders and spread.    Functional but not particularly special.

The waitress then visited our table and informed us that the first course of sea bass had run out.  One of the three of us would have to settle for cobia.  We all looked distrustfully at each other and asked to share the sea bass instead.  The request went unheeded, and I wound up with the sea bass (and a complimentary glass of rose from the Loire Valley).  This was probably because I was the only one doing the wine pairing.  

First Course:  (looks at watch, we are 1 hour in at this point).  The much touted sea bass served with ramps, green garlic, littleneck clams, and squid ink pasta.  A perfect dish!  The sea bass was perfectly cooked with lovely texture -- delicious.  The ramps were in season and especially tasty.  The green garlic had an important note in the dish, and the clams were great.  The squid ink pasta was served as a handful of bowties, so soft, so lovely.  What a resounding start.  

Second Course:  Blue Hill Farm Egg served with dandelion greens, pancetta, and Stone Barns spinach.  The egg was resplendent.  It was centrally perched with arms of dandelion greens emanating from it along the plate.  The pancetta added a surprising note of heat to the dish.  The egg was so beautiful, I didn't want to break the yolk.  Breaking the yolk though, brought the components of the dish together, and it worked wonderfully.  Again, another success.

Third Course:  Farmer's Cross Pig served with grilled asparagus, pickled ramps, and hazelnuts.  The ramps, while a repeat ingredient, were welcomed due to their inherent freshness.  The pig boasted a lovely color and was remarkably tender -- so delicious.  The hazelnuts served as a simple adornment atop the pig.  To the side the two spears of asparagus were placed as an "X", and there was the bonus inclusion of pork belly.  Pork belly?  I was in heaven.   Another lovely dish.

Fourth Course:  (notices watch, we are 3 hours in at this point).  With the service so noticeably slow, the kitchen provided this course to all six members of the table rather than just the three who ordered the tasting menu.  The course was rhubarb and lemon thyme soup served with a fromage blanc sorbet.  I know, it sounds dubious, and I never intentionally ordered rhubarb before.  Too bad, because the dish worked and rhubarb can be quite good when it is fresh.  The course worked well as a palate cleanser and boasted a refreshing, clean flavor.  

Fifth Course:  Flourless chocolate cake served with chocolate, rum cream, and cocoa nib ice cream.  Again, this sounded dubious, and again I was wrong.  Yes, another great dish.  I will spare further words of praise.

All of the wine selections worked especially well.  I was even pleased to have a lovely dessert wine.  At the low price point, this was probably the best wine pairing in the city -- a much better bargain than ordering individually.  

We asked for the bill and wound everything up after 4 hours of service.  We were the last table left in the restaurant, so we literally closed the place down.  Leaving at 12:30am on a Monday night was a bit more than anyone bargained for.  Clearly there was a problem or three in the kitchen, but I am happy to report that the food did not suffer in the least as a result.  

What was so remarkably special about this meal was the simplicity of the effort and the high quality of the ingredients.  The chef has a sure hand and can quickly sum up what adds to a dish and what detracts from it.  The farm fresh ingredients are the backdrop that makes every dish pop and stand memorable.  It is a lament that we can not all eat like this every day.  Highly recommend.

Dan Barber kept me up all night the other night.  O geez, that came out wrong... let's try that again.

As everyone is likely aware at this point, Dan Barber's Blue Hill restaurants represent a force of good in the fight against the commercialization, commoditization, and dumbification of what our nation shoves into our gullets.  His point-of-view on locally sourced, sustainable, organic, farm-to-table has been rightfully critically acclaimed, loved and imitated by the nation's dining public.  However, during a recent visit to Blue Hill, I'll add an additional and perhaps unintended platitude - 'slow food'.

I'll get negativity out of the way - our dinner was beleaguered by alarmingly slow execution of food.  While I couldn't determine if this was a lack of oversight of service or if the kitchen was at fault, from entry to exit, our meal approached the 4 hour mark and well past most of our self appointed bed times.  I'm still internalizing if the food was 'worth the wait', but it certainly was choice.

Starters and amuse's of asparagus and almond tarts as well as Dan Barber's signature crudités plate initiated the meal.  The crudités, a swath of baby spring vegetables on a spiked bed, was borderline genius and borderline pretentious.  Most diners should get the point of the dish - simple revelry of fresh vegetables at their most tender and flavorful stage.  Diners will also revel in the bread basket, which interestingly was one of the highlights of the meal.  Fresh, crusty, buttery ficelle's completed with local butter and a pinch of complimentary carrot or arugula essence'd salts - just awesome.

Blue Hill's signature dish, a softly poached farm egg, which was allegedly laid within 24 hours of service, again highlighted the merits of simple and rustic food.  Flavor-wise, it was superb, but lacked textural intrigue.  The real star of the show was the grass fed loin and belly of lamb.  Perfectly medium rare, subtly flavored, and completed with fingerling potatoes, sautéed greens and plump fiddlehead ferns, it was perhaps the best lamb dishes I've ever tasted.

I'm told that Mr. Barber and his crew can sometimes be found in the Union Square greenmarket, collecting fresh produce for that evening's service.  Therefore you might find me stalking them near the rhubarb section, so that I can properly thank them for the delicious meal... and perhaps a little chastising for keeping me up all night.

Dan, I left my number next to your bed stand.  Call me. xoxo

L'amuse: asparagus & almond brioche. Looked like a macaron. Inexplicably, it was sweet.

Bread came piping hot, crusty and soft, accompanied by addictive carrot salt and arugula salt. *We could not stop eating the bread.*

Architecturally displayed assortment of teeny spring greens that had been very slightly blanched w/salt.  Absolutely delightful.

My wine pour was heavy,  at least 30% more than average.

Excruciatingly long wait between courses. (Exceeded one hour in one case)

We did appreciate that they did not require the entire table to participate in the tasting menu.

Spring vegetable salad - pleasing variety of textures and flavors, especially thanks to the nuts. A subtle, unusual, thickly creamy green dressing.  The roasted fennel was so sweet and mild it reminded of an artichoke. Fiddlehead ferns! luv

Probably the mildest, softest, most delectable lamb I've ever had.  Greens too salty (what is with the oversalting everywhere these days?) but just perfectly cooked. The fiddlehead ferns (again!) still had a hint of a bite.

Mignardises: coconut marshmallows (non-gummy texture, chilled, the coconut toasted just right), chocolate-passionfruit truffles (a passionfruit bomb of flavor ideally balanced by the bitter chocolate). 

The room is tight, and did not have the chill ambience I'd been told to expect.  Not down-to-earth, and certainly not farmhousey.  French service.  And I thought they were famous for the friendly service?  The person who answered the phone when I called to confirm was irritable.  Not snooty, just irritable, sounded annoyed that I had called.

The food is a 5 all the way, but I can't give 5 stars to a place that takes 3:40 to serve dinner while not being a 12-course Ducasse-style epic opera.

Heavenly!  Every bite was perfect, one of the most delicious dinners ever.  I had the grilled mackerel appetizer - perfectly grilled just on the outside, and of course extremely fresh.  I wanted lamb and it wasn't on the menu - I asked about it, and they made it for me anyway!  It was excellent - half the dish was leg of lamb and half was lamb loin.  Succulent and perfectly done.  The other person with me wanted the gnocchi and the veal but couldn't decide - they happily agreed to serve the gnocchi as an appetizer instead of an entree.  Service was impeccable.  We had the pineapple vanilla rice pudding and the chocolate bread pudding for dessert - both couldn't have been any better.  I want to go back every day.  Mmmm.....!

i'm giving this place 3 stars for the location and ambience. fancy and relaxed at the same time, that's the west village for you. the food was disappointing, not flavorful and overpriced. spend the dough elsewhere.
Follow-up handwritten postcard from the barn, can't beat it...Just makes me wanna travel around the northeast to all their hotspots.

Came here for my husband's birthday dinner. We loved the small touches of the tasting menu although we found some flavors to be hit-or-miss (might be our particular taste). As a vegetarian, I feel like I missed out on some things, but my husband claims it was some of the best food he's had in a while. Outstanding warm bread and fresh creamy butter almost overshadowed the entrees! Definitely not the kind of place you will leave hungry! Every time you think it's the last plate, there's something else-- down to the final homemade marshmallow.

Great wine, great service. Glad I wasn't paying the bill! Overall a great place for a special occasion. Make sure to plan way in advance for reservations

Wow...we got the nice quite room in the back called the garden room!! Intimate with limited seating!! If you are looking for some "privacy" make sure you as for that room in the back!  The food was so fresh and cooked to perfection.  There was another table seated where we were and ordered the Tasting Menu.  Every dish that came out had a beautiful and creative presentation.  Next time I'm doing that... :(  The sides are excellent as well!! The chef sent us some extra sides on the house!! Soooo nice!!

Sometimes you go someplace with high expectations and you expect that they won't be able to meet your expectations. And then sometimes you go in with high expectations, and they somehow meet and exceed them. That's what happened at Blue Hill. Everything we had was really really good - lovely to look at and consistently good to eat. I loved the plating of the food, the use of white/blank space, the FOOD!

 I had the pig. Not to be confused with pork. This was Blue Hill pig. And it was really really yummy. I started with the root veggie "burger" and ended with the citrus dessert. My boyfriend had the fruit and veggie salad, the venison, and the rice pudding dessert (I think). Even the wine our waiter helped us pick out was the perfect complement. No it was not cheap. But it was totally worth it.

This place didn't live up to the hype for my wife and I. The food was definitely fresh and very tasty, but the portions were obscenely small. My wife got the tortellini appetizer, there were 5 tortellini, yes, only 5!! I couldn't personally tell you how they tasted, since there were so few of them I didn't have the heart to eat 20% of my wife's appetizer.

So, from the beginning, we got there at 5:30 for a 6:00pm reservation. Were hoping to get a drink at the bar, but 5 or 10 minutes went by before someone came to serve us. Not sure if that was the bartender or a waiter, but the bartender wasn't very welcoming.

The bread was excellent, bread should be hot and come with butter as this did, very, very good.

For appetizer I had the scallops, they were incredibly tasty, 2 of them , not too big, but a more satisfying appetizer then my wife's.

For entree I had the chicken, my wife had the striped bass. My chicken was good, the skin was excellent. The sides around it were very tasty. My wife had the striped bass, it was good, not great and there was limited sides on the plate.

We passed on the dessert, wasn't about to take our chances on tiny, overpriced dessert. So we headed to Perilla, got a seat at the bar , had a couple of drinks and dessert there. My wife loves the chocolate glazed donuts so thanks to Harold and Perilla for ending our night on a positive note.
Amazing food, really good service. Go for the wine pairing.

We went to both Blue Hill and the Blue Hill Farm.. both a great experience restaurant!
It's expensive but so worth it once in a blue moon or of course if you can afford often! 
I love the Blue Hill farm... is just an extraordinary experience and the food is the best I have had so far in my 30 yr life!
If you are like me learning about where the food comes from.. you will love the Blue Hill farm because they explain where the ingredients you are about to eat came from. I couldn't recommend any other restaurant with organic , natural , green and healthy food than this one! Must try!

I had an outstanding dining experience here.  It's a beautiful space and everyone who works here is very professional and friendly; excited about service, the food and the wines they chose for the menu.  And the food is really incredible; made with fresh ingredients, flavorful and perfectly executed.

wow...I am still speechless after an evening at Blue Hill in NYC. This is really as good as it gets in the city. I went to Blue Hill at Stone Barn Farms last summer and that is the only other place that is better than this because the food is literally just outside the back door.
But in the city, it is still outstanding. You will drop a lot of cash but it is so worth it. The staff is so attentive and anticipate your every need. At Stone Barn Farms they pull the table out for you if you need to go to the restroom!
This is food at it's finest and get there as much as you can.
Follow up: You guys, they sent me a postcard thanking me for dining with them.  Who does that?!  They have a fan for life.

I had a lovely birthday dinner at Blue Hill NYC. For such a celebrated restaurant, I was impressed by their low-profile location below street level. 

The amuse bouche we were given at the start of the meal were two lightly seasoned whole Sun Gold cherry tomatoes and some crispy wafer cookies. Very simple and cute.

I hear their Stone Barns location, on the old Rockefeller estate, can possibly be one of the most beautiful dining experiences you can imagine. If the food is as exceptional as our meal at the NYC restaurant, I would definitely eat there if I am ever in the area again.

Word on the street is that President Obama ate here.

incredible. perfect service and presentation, but not fussy. just a lovely place for a lovely meal. the food is so simple and flavorful.

they have wonderful cocktails, too! i had the best ginger-beet martini here.

Went in on a Tuesday night without a reservation by myself - while the place was busy, they found a place for me at the bar. While I would have preferred a place not behind a massive plant, beggars can't be choosers... The food was most excellent - I was meeting a friend later and so just ordered a couple of appetizers - the charcuterie platter and the swiss chard tortellini. Even though I only ordered appetizers, I was most impressed that they went ahead and brought me an amuse bouche of the "beet hamburger", which was interesting if not awe inspiring. The charcuterie to be honest was very similar to others that I have had in Houston, and was probably behind Poscal in that city in flavor, but was high quality and well made. The tortellini was excellent, my only complaint being a slight overcitrused element that probably was just a matter of taste. 

I LOVED the accompaniments to the bread - the lardo was easily the best I've had, and the salt with dehydrated arugula was just so interesting that it seemed I was continually willing to oversalt my food just to get at the flavor - that would be my thought - is it possible to do a version that allows you to access the flavor without oversalting? 

The decor was warm and inviting, the staff very nice, especially given that I didn't have a reservation and was just wandering in. Overall - loved it!

I can't wait to go again. I can see how people fall in love with and in this restaurant.

I took S here and we couldn't get a reservation until 10PM on a Friday so we trekked empty-stomached to the W Village that cold wintry evening ... we walked into a romantic, warm, and absolutely charming space - inconspicuously hidden in Greenwich Village. By the way, I've never been seated at a restaurant at 10PM and felt like it was still 7PM, packed and bustling but with dining decorum.

We started with Brussel Sprouts with Pistachios, which was far too salty but delightfully flavorful when it first came to our table. I usually do not ask for a dish to be re-done, but I felt comfortable enough here to catch the eye of our waiter and make a slight unhappy face, begging his question of "oh, is something off with this dish?" Without hesitation, he took the dish back and smiled as he re-introduced the Brussel Sprouts. It was perfect the second time and his attitude added to our enjoyment of the dish.

My dish was the Poached Hake (with pressed carrots, almonds and warm vegetable vinaigrette). I've never had Hake before but Blue Hill's fresh Hake has whetted my appetite and elevated my expectation bar for my next encounter.  S had the Hudson Valley Chicken, which was so soft and juicy that I wondered what they fed their farm animals...couldn't have been just the way they cooked it. 

The bread... mini tangent: I'm particular about the bread offered with any meal. I think it speaks to the attention to detail of the restaurant. The perfect bread is warm, toasted to crisp perfection on the outside but when bite into it, there is a minor fluffy pillow-deflating effect that reveals a soft and chewy interior...one that breathes the temperature of the oven it just left. Blue Hill's country bread is about as close to perfection as I have encountered thus far.

When we paid, I wrote a "thank you" on the receipt and on their customer feedback card. A week later, I received a handwritten postcard that thanked me back for my visit. I love old-fashioned charm.
Had dinner here with friends. Amazing food, staff and presentation. I'd like a repeat~
Wonderful fresh from the farm food! The vegetables app was amazing! Fresh food and amazing service. It's definitly worth the price.

In NYC for a night, my foodie friend and I went to Blue Hill and had a pretty amazing meal. We arrived early and out table was waiting for us! How often does that happen in NYC? For apps, I had the Spanish Mackerel (with fennel, soybeans and green apple) and it was wonderful. The perfectly cooked fish went surprisingly well with the other items. Very tasty. However, the Klaas Martens' Emmer and Quinoa (with blue hubbard squash and pancetta, stone barns berkshire pig's shoulder and jowl) was off the chart fabulous. This dish was so good, I wanted to lick my plate. You have to try this if you like pig, and I do! Wonderful entree! 

Place is kinda small, so gets loud. Pricey compared to restaurants in NOLA, but we were in Manhattan, after all...highly recommended!

Excellent dining - I cannot wait to go back!

What I ordered:  app: This morning's farm egg - Creamy and lovely. It was perfect. As my entree: Venison - incredible, delicious, amazing ...it was even tenderer than the pork my mother ordered.  Last but not least, the chocolate bread pudding - If you are a chocolate lover, this will not disappoint - maybe one of the best desserts ever.

The space itself is very cozy and for being considered a high end restaurant it was not stuffy - to me that's a huge plus.

I was so excited for my meal here. The service was shaky at first -- when we first got there, the waitress plunked down a wine list yet no cocktail list -- when we asked her for one, we found they had 3 interesting seasonal cocktails on there. I had a spiced apple cider with allspice which was amazing.  

My gripe, surprisingly, was the food. We did the tasting menu (with wine pairing, which was impressive. Complex and well-described bottles). Our first dish, a sea scallop atop golden beets was good but nearly cold by the time it got to our table. Next there was their take on a bouillabaisse which had ISSUES. The poached hake was fine (just fine) but the mussels were tough and inedible. Also the black chickpeas (which I was excited to try!) were undercooked and chalky. When none of us finished even half the waitress listened to our critiques and appropriately brought us out a replacement, a fabulous gnocchi with seasonal mushrooms. Our entree, a veal chop, was well prepared and flavorful. And dessert was great -- bread pudding. 

But I was really just disappointed because I expected the execution to be perfect! Hopefully it was just an off-night.

I went with a friend this past Sunday.  It's so hard to get a reservation at this place and every time I got one and made plans with someone, I had to cancel the reservation.  So this time around, I made sure I went!

While Blue Hill was decent and the service was wonderful, I am not sure if it is worth the hype or if it was what the restaurant had served for this week that did not particularly "wow" me.

My friend and I ordered the following:

 Maine Sea Scallops
citrus marmalade, endive and whole grain mustard
(we shared this and though they were tasty, you really can't go wrong with scallops.  nothing that really stood out.  presentation was nice.)

We shared a side of the brussels sprouts and pistachios and that was the best part of the meal, hands down (and the least expensive!).

I ordered the Berkshire Pork (pork shoulder and pork belly served on top of shiitake mushrooms, curry sauce, and some type of bean (forgot).  Curry worked well  with the pork, but certainly not worth $35.

My friend ordered a chicken dish (breast and leg cooked sous vide) served on top of chick peas and some type of sauce.  I was really impressed with the texture of the chicken - so smooth, silky, melt-in your-mouth.  But then again, I had higher expectations for the sauce and was not wowed by that.

We did not see anything on the dessert menu that we could get elsewhere but noticed that there was a lot of fruit and cheese.

I had to use the restroom  (the one on the right side) during the meal and upon entering the restroom was overwhelmed by the scent of old urine.  That was unsettling.


Good things:
1. I enjoyed the service - very attentive and courteous.  Water and bread bowl were always filled throughout dinner.
2. They offered this "macaron-like" amuse bouche - some type of ricotta cheese/beet jam thing.  Not bad.
3. After dinner, they gave us home-made coconut marshmallows and these chocolates on top of cocoa nibs (very good).

I was really excited for this meal.  A coworker of mine was finally finishing up on our project after a long 8 month stint and we were trying to end on a high note.  Plus, this was going to be my 25th Yelp review (a small feat, but a feat nonetheless) -- rather than review something in my current town of residency (Philadelphia), I wanted to explore Dan Barber's cuisine in my hometown for the momentous occasion.

It started out great -- arriving early, a colleague and I were seated and given a well thought out wine list with lots of affordable bottles from around the world.  My only criticism is that there were only 2-3 bottles from NY State, which has produced several strong wines over the last few years.  Given the farm-to-table image, I wanted more opportunities to be as locavore as possible.  Fantastic bread was served and refilled promptly.   For amuse, they served little beat and goat cheese "sliders" on almond financier.  Very tasty but a little under seasoned.  I'm not a huge salt person but a sprinkle of sea salt would have brought this together.

Appetizers arrived and were beautifully plated.  Two of my colleagues enjoyed the poached egg with mushrooms and quinoa, although said the equivalent dish at Eleven Madison Park was much better.  I went with the Winter Vegetables, which was a beautifully presented assortment of lightly marinated fruits and veggies of the season.  This time, I would have liked a tad more acid, although the soybean based dressing did provide a bit of tang.

If I've learned one thing from Top Chef, it's that your main should be served around 5-10 minutes after your appetizer is cleared.  Five minutes went by.  Ten. Twenty. Thirty five.  No mention from anybody.  Finally, I ask our server, who mentions the kitchen was down two people and is doing it's best.  Now I understand stuff happens -- but set that expectation upfront.  This way, when I'm waiting 30 minutes, I'm prepared for it -- not fidgeting.  FI-nally, our food arrives.  The manager informs us he's comping our sides for the wait, which is very much appreciated.

Across the group, all of us were very impressed with presentations, vegetables, and sides.  Across the group, we were all disappointed with our proteins.  Veal fared the best -- those who had it enjoyed it even if it played second fiddle on the plate (and frankly, I personally believe it's not a bad thing when meats are second to veggies). My two coworkers who went with the pork thought it was okay.  The chicken appeared almost sous vide -- it was still pink in color and had a spongy texture, although I'm positive it was brought to proper temperature.  There was something very off-putting about this dish.  

And then there was my dish.  I pride myself in being satisfied with my choices in a restaurant.  Maybe I create self-fulfilling scenarios; maybe I make great choices.  Who knows.  I asked our server to describe Wreckfish to me, as I was unfamiliar; to which she mentioned that it was a fatty bass.  So I assumed that given the "high fat content," it would be relatively soft and oily (like a salmon or black cod). No -- this was meatier than a monkfish and nothing was done to tenderize it in the process.  Basically my plate was a $32 plate o'rubber.  Honestly, I really needed a steak knife.  I should have sent it back, but it was very late and I was content to eat sides, which, coincidentally, were the standout of the meal (the spinach and spaetzle barely beat out the brussels sprouts in my book).

In terms of dessert, we enjoyed the apple and pear desserts (although they were a little too similar for my liking), but both me and two colleagues felt the bread pudding lacked character and flavor.  It's a pretty dish, but the chocolate is very uni-dimensional and the dish lacks the texture of the homemade favorite.  Petit fours (a mint merangue and a sesame cluster) were okay but nothing special.

All in all, while I really enjoyed the freshness of the veggies and their true-to-character preparation, Blue Hill lacked great, inspired cooking.  Lucky for them, great ingredients get you most of the way there.  I am back and forth between two and three stars, but I think I'll give them the benefit of the doubt and stick with 3 for the ingredients.

The space is tiny; the crowd is loud; the wait is long; the service is spotty-- the food, however, is AMAZING.

GO!

I went to the one on the farm and the experience was wonderful! The staff was probably the most attentive staff I have EVER encountered. We brought our purses and had no place to put them, when were were about to place them on the floor, the wait staff rushed over and gave us a small bench to place them next to us. The presentation of the food was excellent and the ambiance and room was beautiful. It WAS pretty expensive and not a go to every day to, but we have been there 3 times and love it. Would go back again!

My taste buds tingle just thinking about this place. My West Coast friend has quickly become a hard core New Yorker and made a reservation for us with great anticipation. We were walking down a residential street and as I looked down into a cozy room with diners conversing intimately over delicious looking plates, I thought 'What a great little restaurant; looks ideal!'.  Thirty minutes of wandering later, I realized that was our restaurant. Funny how those things work.  
They have done well with the small space - a large room down from street level with a bar on the right and intimate tables throughout.
I loved the wine recommended by our waiter, was equally impressed with dinner, and of course, just HAD to try dessert.
And what is even better is the concept of the farm, and the fresh ingredients and the simplicity of wholesome local food? It can't get much better than that.
Elegant, understated, delicious, fresh, and easy.

Excellent!!! I went this past summer and sat in covered patio/garden in the back. The food is soo amazing. They change their menu often and at the time I had grilled octopus to start and the Venison for my entree. Both were excellent. They have possibly the best brussel sprouts you will ever have in your life which are served with pistachios.

I have been here a few times and will keep coming back!

Try to get seated in the covered patio in the back, it is initmate, warm and a great dining experience. Not sure if they open it in the winter time though.

Sometimes things just fall into place.  I needed to celebrate my last GMAT class and i didn't want my reservation for blue hill to go to waste, so i combined the two occasions and what resulted was one of the best meals I've ever had.   We arrived on a Tuesday night and were promptly seated.  I was glad I had asked to be seated in the main dining room because "the patio" area looked chilly and it was freezing outside.  Our waiter was informative but not as personable as I usually like.  The sommelier on the other hand had a certain florish and didnt push overpriced wines. We shared the Maine crabmeat appetizer which was a great dish to start with- full of flavor, expertly seasoned and very light.  I usually stick with fish for my entree but my friends had been pushing me to get the lamb so i succumbed.  She got the veal and we went halfsies, which is how i like to roll in general.  I prefered the lamb, i thought it had more flavor and I love mushrooms, but she loved her veal so everyone was happy.  We didnt want dessert, but after overhearing our debate, our waiter said we couldn't leave without trying the chocolate bread pudding.  Really one of the better desserts i've had, and different from anything I've tasted before- I don't know what i'd do if i had to eat another molten chocolate cake.  It was rich but remained fluffy and wasn't too dense.  I left completely satisfied, not in a food coma, but on a food high.  If only I could eat like this everyday, makes me want to live on a farm and work the land.  Shout out to the bartender Rocky, I promised i'd mention him.

If you can get a reservation. . . A new favorite.  It's not fussy but it's sophisticated with only the best ingredients, mostly local.  Some of the preparations are unique and wonderful, like the Westchester pig, but they also have a few  old standbys, including the best striped bass I've ever tasted.  How did they make it so wonderful?  There's a good wine list with wide variety and pricing, a sommelier that is helpful and doesn't up sell, and a knowledgeable and professional wait staff.  But it's a small restaurant and it's definitely been discovered.  Book early.

If I could give this place 6 stars I would, but Yelp stops at 5.  Every single year I eat here on my birthday, and every single year, I leave incredibly happy with the staff, with the food, and with the decor.  It's simple, traditional, and healthy. 

This past year (12/7/2009), my girlfriend and I ordered the Maine Crabmeat (Poached Quince, Marinated Fennel and Tapioca), and Swiss Chard and Ricotta Ravioli as appetizers.  For our entrees we ordered the Tamworth Pig (Shelling Beans, Curry, and Shiitake Mushrooms) and the Venison (served rare with baby carrots) and split Brussel Spouts and Pistachios.   And we were both full and left happy with the food and service.

My only suggestion is that when booking the reservation, specifically ask to sit in the front dining room.  On 12/7/2009, we were seated in the back patio, beyond the kitchen which would have been nice on a spring or fall day.  But the weather was extremely cold, and the 2 space heaters simply did not keep that back patio warm enough.

Before we left, I noted that the patio was a little chilly on the comment card, and the waitress came up to me while I was getting my coat from the coat-check room.  She wished me a happy birthday and was genuinely sorry that the patio wasn't comfortable.  I told her that it was quite alright and that Blue Hill was still my favorite restaurant in the city.  She quickly spoke with the maitre'd who also came over and assured me that the next time I dined at Blue Hill I would be seated in the front dining room.

But regardless, this place is still my favorite restaurants in NYC and on my short list of restaurants I recommend to friends, family, and colleagues.  Skip Babbo and walk over a block to this restaurant... you won't be sorry.

Ate here about a year ago... 

It was sooo good I'm STILL speechless...it was the best experience of my life... 

I still drool whenever I talk about it... 

I tell anyone and everyone about this place... 

DELICIOUS FOOD. WONDERFUL SERVICE.

*YuMMm*  ^.^

Simple, elegant food made with subtlety and care. The vegetables are fresh and crisp. Everything is obviously straight out of the garden.  The meat dishes sing with a balance of richness, sweetness, and sour notes, while the fish dishes are extremely subtle and complex. Everything was cooked to perfection. The atmosphere is casual and laid back, unusual for this level of cuisine. The service could have been a tad better, as our waiter seemed overly nervous and not very knowledgeable about the wines. Small service hiccups aside, thank you Chef Barber. We had a wonderful evening.
Delicious!  Blending of flavors with simple, healthy ingredients is amazing!  Great for taking someone special!

I've been to Blue Hill a few times and i think it is a top notch restaurant. I would have given it five stars the first time I went but this last time I didn't have as great of service and it was little too loud. That said, the food was great and I would definitely come back, however probably on a slower night. It seems like a lot of people have their birthdays here.

Nice staff, atmosphere,  and better than average food.  However, I don't get the hype.  The ingredients are definitely fresh, but not particularly more flavorful or fresh than ingredients I've tasted in other high end restaurants.  I also found the seasoning bland and not particularly creative.   Although I appreciate simple pairings as much as complex ones, nothing stood out, except the wine, and bread & butter.  3 stars compared to restaurants of the same caliber.  I honestly feel the prices could be reduced by a 1/3 to 1/2, and they should call it a bistro.

Blue Hill has a charming atmosphere, and a great service, yet those two attributes don't justify such bland entrees for $30+ each. I wasn't impressed with food at all. I got venison, it was cooked medium, but still a bit tough, nothing special regarding preparation, marinade, or sauce. A side of braised Brussels sprouts with pistachios was more interesting and tasty.  As far as fancy places go, there much better restaurants where for the same price you get outstanding creations. For a similar fare, atmosphere, and service, try Red Cat or Harrison, and you will not feel you butthole hurting after cashing out.

It's not too late to take a trip to Blue Hill StoneBarn and enjoy a day in the outdoors. Fall in NY is beautiful.
For more reviews visit my blog.

Will be going to Blue Hil NYC soon...

Nasanna:  "Wanna walk or take the cab home?"

Dustin:  "Meh... If I was fat, happy and couldn't move I would take a cab, but I'm not so let's just walk."

We originally wanted to go to Blue Hill Farm outside the city, but it's a bit further, so we went to the restaurant in the city for our 1 year anniversary.  

I'd give it 3.5 stars.  

Price, service, décor was good.  Food was nothing to rave about.  My husband and I found their dishes to be more on the salty side.  

For appetizer, we had This Morning Farm Egg.  It seemed like one big blob.  The one we had at Babbo, Warm Lamb's Tongue Vinaigrette is MUCH better.  We also had Klaas Martens' Emmer Wheat Pasta, which was a bit salty.  For entre, my husband had the Rabbi Bob's Veal and I had the Rabbi Bob's Veal.  Both were good, but nothing to rave about.    The execution of their food in general was good.  But seasoning wasn't there.  It was something to try, but we would not go back again.  We would however, still try to make a trip out to Blue Hill at Stone Barns 

One thing that is worth mentioning is that my husband apparently enjoyed the Salt and Pepper drink a lot.  It's got a spicy kick and flavor.  They infuse Thai chili with I believe Square One organic vodka.  But their mixed drink menu is not huge.

I believe a restaurant sets the tone for its patrons immediately when they step foot in the door.  Every imaginable visual and auditory element formulates an impression on them that is constantly shaped and refined as the evening progresses.

From the other wait staff serving you and greeting you, to the simple yet classy white table cloth that covers your table, an experience with each of the components of the venue shapes the dining experience.  

Easy lighting, soft voices and muted conversations enable each guest to participate in what is sure to be a remarkable and enchanting evening.  

The amuse bouche presented to our table was cauliflower prepared in 4 different ways, each one spiced to showcase Blue Hill's command of one of the simplest vegetables in the produce aisle.  

For an appetizer I had the Maine crabmeat served with poached quince, fennel and tapioca was fresh, perfectly seasoned and an eye-opening first dish.

My main course of grass fed lamb exceeded my expectations, perfectly cooked, medium rare, tender, and complemented with roasted potatoes and string beans was a joy to look at and eat.  

Conversation at dinner began to slow down as each course was presented to the 5 of us, the tomato soup, the ravioli, the grilled cobia, a unique sampling of all things fresh and organic.  

For wine I asked the sommelier to recommend a bottle $100 and below to complement all of our choices.  He came back with the Giorgio Odero Frecciarossa Pinot Nero Ottreno Pavese 2006 from Italy.  $72 bottle of wine that impressed all my dinner companions.  Thank you!

I will say that my review should also include a small mention of my dining companions.  The only male present amongst 4 women, 2 redheads, a blonde, and a brunette made dinner much more satisfying.  I must apologize to the tables around us, our laughter, discussions of dildos and vibrators must have been distracting.  

I recommend that your dates in the future do not wear short skirts and low cut blouses, it distracts from your ability to focus on the food at hand.  You should advise said dates to keep all activity above the table.  Talking amongst your friends becomes a concentrated effort.  

To end the evening, dessert was the chocolate bread pudding with vanilla ice cream.  A classic combination that melted in my mouth and left me speechless.  

Hats off to our server Steven, he was fantastic throughout the night.  
I'm coming back in the very near future, perhaps in 2 1/2 weeks when I'm back in NYC.  

Bravo Blue Hill!

Flawless food, creative presentation, and white-cloth service in a romantic and intimate townhouse setting. 

There is a certain respect for the food here which clearly is evinced in the thoughtfully prepared dishes. Blue Hill encompasses all the trendy culinary buzzwords to date: local, seasonal, sustainable, and humane. There is some comfort in knowing that my swine came from a biodynamic farm and "this morning's egg" is well, literally from this morning!

For appetizers we started with the fresh egg and lamb quarters along with the smoked eel and chicken liver terrine. Fresh eggs are worlds apart from the regular dairy farmed eggs you can pick up at the Duane Reade across the street. Delicious, golden yolk oozed out of the slightly translucent white, infusing the delicious savory broth and enhancing the delicate lamb. The chicken liver tasted so fresh and the eel provided a shart contrast against the gamey flavor. For entrees, I opted for the emmer and quinoa - buttery pork jowls and shoulder atop pancetta and quinoa. My boyfriend chose Hudson Valley duck, seared to a perfect medium rare accompanied by roasted vegetables and broccoli rabe. Simple food, abundant flavor.

We sat in the back patio, tucked away from the bustling main dining room. I swear, if I looked hard enough, I could see Stone Barns right outside the window.
what a fantastic restaurant with fantastic service, fantastic food and a  fantastic neighborhood love the veggies and mini pea burger

Impressive place. Fantastic food, presentation, and a concept I can stand behind. I like the idea of knowing the source of my food and shortening the food chain, I wish I could say that for more restaurants in NYC. However, for the price, I doubt I'll be back for a return visit, but definitely worth checking out once.

I was looking for the perfect restaurant for my boyfriends birthday.  With all of the great restaurants in the city, I had no clue where to start.  I stumbled upon a website called eateryexpert.com.  I emailed them and they came back with a list of 3 restaurants that would be perfect for a special bday.  Blue Hill was first on the list and boy am I thrilled that I took their advice.  EVERYTHING was perfect - The food, the service and of course company.  I've heard that the menu constantly changes, but try the buttermilk chicken if you come across it.  I never thought I would describe chicken as melting in your mouth, but it did.  The white meat was perfectly adorned with veggies in a yummy warm buttermilk sauce.  The whole experience was to die for and I HIGHLY recommend it to anyone and everyone.  Be prepared to spend some money, but it is worth it!

I have been dying to try Blue Hill since I saw Blue Hill at Stone Barns on Top Chef a couple of seasons ago. Every time it occurred to me to go - it would be booked solid (2 weeks in advance). Finally, I put in a call a month in advance and scored a table (options were before 6 and after 9). 

The menu was mouthwatering. To start, I had the corn ravioli - it was interesting - a little dry but still flavorful. My mom had the summer bean salad - which was freshness on a fork (and huge). Will had Maine crab meat which was also tasty (and I didn't know that avocado squash existed). 

We couldn't decide on our entrees so we arranged to have separate dishes so that we could try as much as possible. I had pork belly with sweet corn, summer squash and zucchini. The vegetables were all diced small and mixed together in a lite but creamy sauce - it was superb. Mom had bass in clam chowder - the bass was served on top of a bowl of New England style chowder with really fresh, fulsome clams. Will had the veal - very lite and flavorful - and he was able to request his preferred cut of the veal. Each entree was large, flavorful and packed with delicious vegetables. 

For dessert I had the "Strawberries" - which was served in a glass and layered with nuts, cream, sorbet and diced strawberries - it was both sweet and tangy. 

The wine list is extensive and a bit expensive. The waitstaff is friendly and patient. The restaurant is dimly lit and the design paired with simple decor allows for you to focus on your own table. 

I can't wait to get a table at Stone Barns!

Great place, amazingly fresh food, beautiful presentation, nice wine list, good service.  But this place is hilariously terrifying! First of all, we came a week or two after Barack & Michelle Obama so there was still buzz in the place about it, almost to the point where you start to hate who they're talking about because it's enough already.  This is the guests, not the staff, the staff were very discreet, but who the hell goes out and asks what someone else ordered, like if you completely suspend belief and eat what they ate you can go around telling people that by the transitive properties you ate with the president and his wife!  Freaks.  

Second, they placed on the table this thick heavy wooden block with sharp, dangerous spikes coming out of it, each one holding something random, like a piece of lettuce or a snow pea.  And radio silence, no commentary from the person who dropped it off, cant find our waiter.   So we're staring at it for a while asking each other if we should eat it or if it was meant to be a centerpiece and finally we decided that we should eat it.  Then my friend being so "klassy" starts to cut it with a knife and a fork and at that point the waiter must have decided he was done laughing his ass off at us and he told us we could just use our fingers to pluck the veggies off the spikes which was a relief!  

The menu is great, how fun to order "pig" instead of some overly descriptive item with every ingredient listed out.  Love it!  The food was incredible, a great experience but pricey of course, this is not an everyday meal kind of place.  

Oh and my friend slipped and fell down on the way back from the bathroom which was entertaining (for me at least) since the whole place got a good view of it!  Luckily, she;s a good sport about these things! :)

I heart Blue Hill.  After dining here on date nite with my man-friend, I have new found respect for the meaning of a memorable meal.  Service, atmosphere, menu - impeccable!
Chef Dan Barber is a genius - I love his concept of bringing 'farm to table', practicing the use of the freshest and in season ingredients to this seasonal and ever-changing menu.
Would return again, and again if I won the lottery.  Next destination is Blue Hill at Stone Barns.

It was good but TINY portions.  The eggplant main course is miniscule.  And too sweet.  The veal was excellent.  Just quite quite small portions.  imaginative and fresh but you have to go out for dinner afterwards.
Very cute, nice wine list.   But just ... for the $?  The portions should be bigger. Esp for the eggplant which was basically eggplant parmigiana for around $28- but, seriously, 4 two inch pieces of eggplant.  Seriously.  Go to Murray's up the street and go to the farmer's market and make it at home.  And I don't like big portions!  That's how small these were, babe.

Let me preface this by saying that the meal was great.  It was delicious and imaginative, yet not overdone.  The freshness of the food was really able to speak for itself.

But, I honestly had one of the most bizarre dining experiences of my life the night I ate at Blue Hill!  Just  to get rid of the laundry list, first off the dining room was randomly obscenely hot.  Like, my-butt-is-stuck-to-my-seat hot.  Second, our waiter MAY have forgotten to take his Paxil that night.  So, so sweet, trying so, so hard, but SO, SO NERVOUS!  Also, his descriptions of the dishes and the wine didn't really resemble reality.  At all.  Third, I LOVE close seating.  I am an unabashed eavesdropper.  However, occasionally, this works to your disadvantage.  Like, say when you are seated a few tables down from a woman going through a bitter divorce who is wailing (with tears) into a bottle of wine.  Ha, okay that last part was pretty amusing.  But, weird.

So, I say all of the above and yet I had a great time.  Besides the sweaty butt.  We had a late reservation, but the place was packed and only began to empty out towards the very tail end of our meal.  

As an amuse-bouche, our waiter brought out a selection of cherry tomatoes.  Plain and simple and ballsy.  I loved it and it definitely made a thematic statement to the diner, that freshness and simplicity were the raison d'être of the restaurant. 

As an appetizer, I went with the watermelon tart, which was delicious and surprising.  The watermelon was lightly grilled and complimented perfectly by the goat cheese and tomatoes.  My only suggestion would be more face bacon.  But, then again I am a bacon fiend.

For my entree, I went with the veal and quinoa.  It tasted wonderful, there were bits of pancetta (that's like ALMOST bacon, right?!) mixed in with the quinoa and emmer.  Every bite was savory.  However, it looked a little like baby vomit.  There just has to be a more pleasant presentation for that dish. 

For dessert, the table went with two choices, the blackberries and cheesecake and the peaches, hazelnut "daquoise," and rose hip ice cream.  The blackberries and cheesecake were delicious little bites accompanied by POWERFULLY strong berry ice cream.  Like, so strong and tart as to make you suck in your cheeks.  Now, we had no clue what a "daquoise" was - not even our fluent French speaker.  So, we asked our waiter.  His response was that it was like a meringue.  No.  It is not.  However, the rose hip ice cream, was fantastic, light and refreshing, in no way overpowering.  It was quite a treat.               

Honestly, I was stuck between a three star and a four star review.  It was a delicious meal, but not the best I've ever had.  It's a terrific example of the "slow food" movement and worth the trip, just to have that sort of experience and I'm not talking about the butt sweat.

FRESH!!!!

It is amazing the pure flavor that comes from food that has not been trucked thousands of miles.  This was our second time at Blue Hill and they have impressed us both times.  

First time we ordered off the menu making a couple selections from the appetizer menu and an entree.  This time we did the Farmers Tasting Menu.  Both times we paired with wines.

The Chef sends our several one bite dishes that "Show Off"  the skills of the farmers, and locally produced meats and sausages.

Each dish was true to the base ingredients and relied on that natural flavor coming out.  The food is not simple but taste pure and not over powered.  This allows each bite to be enjoyed and different from the next.  

The only down side to Blue Hill it has become a tourist destination.  Too many times we over heard "Where did the Obama's sit?"   Come for the food.  Not because the president ate here.  

The most shocking part of the meal is when the check comes.  VERY reasonable for the quality of food, service and wine selections.  Restaurants that hit on these buttons are usually twice the price of Blue Hill.

We loved this place! The food is incredibly delicious with beautiful presentation. An extensive wine list. And the service, our waitress Elizabeth, was excellent. 
Definitely recommend getting the Maine crabmeat salad yummy! My bass with lentils and beans was very nice. My husbands lamb was very tasty too. And for dessert the cheese plate and the berries with cheesecake were perfect to finish off the meal.
Highly recommended!
