The food here was solidly good but I was ready to be much, much more impressed.  For one thing, their restaurant at Stone Barns blew me away and remains one of the top meals I've ever had.  I just wasn't as wowed by Blue Hill, sadly.  The service was superb, though.  I didn't finish my chicken (it was fine, nothing wrong with it, just didn't love it) and they wouldn't let us pay for it.  Impressive.

After reading about Blue Hill on various web blogs we decided to give it a try on Friday night.  One of the reasons people enjoyed going there was because of the various tastings they provide you before your meal.  We read about the 3 different types of butter, the various vegetables and their presentations. So we were a little surprised when we received 4 tomatoes in a bowl and 1 pat of butter.  Perhaps the restaurant changed since last week when we last read about it, but we kept seeing beautiful tomatoes go by on wooden stands w skewers and carrots - but not at our table. Hmm. Then a single diner sat down next to us and "Keith" our server became enamored with him. Lo and behold the beautiful tomatoes arrived at his table, as well as, 3 types of butter and a wonderful explanation but why stop there next comes beautiful an array of meats along with their own presentation. We were an after thought to our servers dating life. Food was delicious and the ambiance was very cozy and romantic. But you go to a restaurant like this for the full experience which includes impeccable service. We did not sadly experience that and would not return or recommend it to anyone.

My appetizer was the Maine crabmeat and entree was the Klaas Marten's emmer and quinoa.

The crabmeat came in a green garden gazpacho and was topped with a yogurt sorbet.  The crabmeat was fresh but a little bland.  The gazpacho was cool and refreshing, as was the yogurt sorbet, which had a slightly tarty flavor.  Both were a nice contrast to the quite flavor-less crabmeat.  

The emmer and quinoa came with Berkshire pork, peas, corn, and pancetta.  The Berkshire pork came as a sausage, loin, and...shoulder??.  The pancetta was mixed in with the emmer and quinoa, which was almost like a risotto.  The Berkshire pork itself was ok, the sausage and loin were moist and tender, but I prefer Berkshire pork at other places. But the emmer and quinoa itself was very tasty!  A unique dish I'm glad I tried.

highlights and lowlights of my 3 hour dinner 

my friend made the reservation 30 days to the dot. when another friend wanted to join us, they said it wasn't  possible to change from 3 to a 4 person reservation. how odd i thought. imagine my dull surprise when we were seated at a 4 person table anyway. 

we had an unbelievable amount of food. started off with 3 appetizers and 2 complimentary tasters. 
1. tomatoes (taster) - 6 tiny tomatoes, juicy and sweet. perfect start. 
2. fresh greens - the leafy greens were salty but could not taste the granules of salt. the sauce and mushrooms layered on the bottom were fantastic. very meaty wild mushrooms. 
3. farm fresh egg - the egg had a very large yolk. not exactly poached. very silky, warm, mm. great. 
4. shot of house v8 (taster) - reminded me of pulpless salsa. 
5. tomatoes - a variety of tomatoes, but i could have gone without. the taster was enough. 

did i mention whipped butter? always a plus. 

entrees 
at least one person at your table needs to get a pork entree. right now there's 2 - the berkshire pig and the klaas marten. the berkshire pig is much leaner, and the klaas marten is richer. both come with these thick slices of tender bacon with crisped skin. it reminded me of a popular shanghainese dish (equally tasty, though much cheaper). we all liked the klaas marten the best. the other entree was the lamb, which they gave us two columns of slices. my friend kept mentioning how curiously small the potatoes were, but clearly enjoyed it. all the entrees were generously portioned. it was just very on the salty side, maybe being pork and all, but i tend to eat salty anyway so i don't know if ppl with more neutral taste buds would mind. 

side dishes:
swiss chard - simple, good contrast to the heavy pork dishes.
complimentary succotash - very colorful, balances, and clean.

dessert:
chocolate bread pudding - freckled vanilla ice cream over a crisp layer over the brownie like pudding. melted chocolate inside. it was good but not terribly exciting. 


overall impressions: they overlap the ingredients a lot. the meaty wild mushrooms, tomatoes, pork etc made several appearances, not that we minded. they have an emphasis on what's in season. if you're lucky, get the line of impaled broccoli veggies haha. they also offered us several complimentary dishes that we really enjoyed. it was almost as if we had done a tasting menu but literally paid half the price. 

it wasn't perfect, but i enjoyed it. :)

So for my 400th review - I have to write about the absolutely amazing Blue Hill.

I wanted to come to Blue Hill ever since I heard that the Obamas went there - yes, i know - it's lame - but I am definitely an avid (and open)  player in 'follow the celebrity'.

The ambience in this hideaway is super posh, elegant, and romantic. 

We decided to order the tasting menu, since almost every yelper has raved about it, and it certainly impressed!

Our waiter let us make some changes to the menu so that we could try everything we wanted.  One change was that we wanted to get 1 chocolate bread pudding and then one of the listed dessert, which was a blueberry and ice cream type dish.  Another change was that, since I'm a pescatarian, I wouldn't be able to eat the pork entree - so the chef prepared a fish entree for me instead.  They also mentioned that if I was vegetarian, they could have easily adjusted the menu accordingly - which is great to know!

So now the meal!  The meal starts with warm toasty bread served with 3 different types of butter.  One they get from a farm in vermont, the other is a pork-based butter (nice way of saying lard..haha), and the final is a butter they make in-house which is creamy, soft, and was my favorite of the 3.

As we were waiting for our food - the waiter asked if I wanted anything to drink.  I was planning on having just water so I could enjoy the food completely, but he finally insisted that I have either champagne or apple cider b/c 'there should be some sort of alcohol on the table' - so I opted for a complimentary glass of wonderful champagne.  Service here is IMPECCABLE.

Then, we received several amuse bouches (sp?) - a line of fresh farm grown veggies on little sticks appeared - and each tasted as if it had come straight from the ground - so fresh!  The snap peas and radishes were my favorite.  We also got mini green peppers and 2 mini pea burgers.  Everything was so cute and small and delicious!

Then, came our first course (yes - all of the above was just the introduction) - which was a fruit and vegetable medley - consisting of the sweetest baby tomatoes and grilled peaches. There were other veggies in there too - but these are the ones I remember best.  So fresh, and the marinade was just perfect.

Next, was our sea bass dish - this dish consisted of almost raw (sashimi-like) sea bass.  It was done in a great creative way - and I'm not a big fan of sashimi unless there's rice with it - but the flavors of the sauce, veggies, and fish mixed so well together I just enjoyed it all.

So, in addition to the tasting menu - we also wanted to try the popular egg dish.  This dish is a poached egg, that's been poaching for over 12 hours, on top of a curry like sauce.  To be honest, this was probably my least favorite dish.  I didn't get the appeal - and whereas everything else on the menu had light and fresh tastes, the curry in this option just felt heavy and spicy and not in sync with the rest of our menu.

Then, we got our main courses.  By this time, I was already quite stuffed!  My dining mate got something similar to porkchops, and i got the haddock.  This fish was again amazing.  Not oily or greasy - just the right amount of sauce, and baked(or broiled?) to the perfect amount.

After this, we had a small bowl which consisted of some sort of champagne, sorbet, and fresh raspberries.  This was probably to cleanse the palate - The fizzyness of the champagne combined with the sorbet and tartness of the raspberries gave a great mix of flavors.

And finally, it was time for dessert.  The chocolate bread pudding was basically like a classy brownie sundae.  It was crunchy on the top layer, and warm and oozing out chocolate on the inside.  A scoop of ice cream lay on top giving the perfect hot-to-cold ratio.

In comparison, the blueberry dessert was a bit lackluster.  It was basically a sprinkle of blueberries on a plate, with a tiny scoop of ice cream in the middle.  There were hard caramel-like shavings on the ice cream and the dish also had a sprinkling of popcorn(?) which was odd.  The popcorn combined with the rest of the dish didn't really work for me - but the berries were fresh and the caramel like sprinkles tasted nice.  For me though, I'm never satisfied with a non-chocolate dessert.

We left completely full - and yet - my stomach wasn't aching due to over-processed fatty food.  The food here is fresh and oil/fat is used within reason so you feel clean after eating.  That's not to say, I wasn't in a deep food coma...b/c i definitely was.  But it was from a really good wholesome meal.

After 399 reviews of a multitude of restaurants, I have to say that Blue Hill is the PINNACLE of my NYC restaurant experiences.  Amazing service, food, ambience, everything was perfect.

Is it expensive?  Yes.  Is it worth it? oh my goodness YES!!!

No wonder the president took his wife here! :-p

Blue Hill is absolutely fantastic. I was cautiously optimistic about eating here, wary of the hype surrounding the restaurants and farm upstate but excited to try Dan Barber and crew's (James Beard award winner) culinary creations. We splurged a bit for my wife's birthday and did the tasting menu and wine pairing. We started with fresh picked vegetables, sugar snap pea puree mini burgers, a trio of chorizos, multiple homemade butters with tomato salt and fresh bread, a summer vegetable and fruit salad. All accompanied by perfectly paired wines. We moved on to a beautiful Mahi Mahi dish and then an main course of Ossabaw Pig, cut after cut of the most savory pork I've ever tasted. Dessert consisted of homemade frozen yogurt and raspberries followed by a corn ice cream with corn flakes and fresh blueberries. Our server was kind enough to include a small candle on the last dish for my wife's birthday. The service is impeccable, the food is beyond fresh (and as someone who spent some serious time in a farming community I can attest to just how fresh this food is) and organic which without question adds entirely new dimensions to the food's flavor. The restaurant's ambiance is perfect for a romantic dinner and the overall atmosphere, while fancy, is very relaxed and unpretentious. Support this restaurant and treat your palate to what will be, perhaps, one of the best dining experiences of your entire life.

I can truly say i've never had a better meal and i cant wait to visit their Westchester farmhouse to see if they can outdo the experience we had in New York.

I've never been to the great and powerful California restaurant Chez Panisse which sets the standards for  ingredients-focused restaurants, but I adore the principals that they embody and visit restaurants that adopt those principals (like Blue Hill!) whenever I can.  Sure,  I love and respect chefs who use creative and unique recipes to create their flavors but I much prefer flavor that comes from a combination of exceptional quality ingredients and impeccable preparation.

Blue Hill undoubtably provided the best Panisse-esque experience of any restaurant I've ever visited.  Can you imagine a restaurant so focused on food that even a single snow pea can taste like heaven?  

BP, you won me over with a snow pea, then knocked my socks off with tomatos that tasted like you expect a tomato to taste (think garden of eden-- yes that good!), and had me reeling when they served three types of butter with their fresh warm bread.   If that last part of the sentence excited you, get ready to drool-- one of the three butters wasnt butter at all, but more of a pig fat, whipped up into a bacony smokey delicious seasoned spread. 

Dont expect wild crazy dishes, everything is simple.  Fish with vegetables, a salad of summer fruits, a pork loin and a pork belly-- but every dish is created with the goal of maximum flavor.  And everything looks and smells just as beautiful as it tastes-- a true feast for the senses.  

Do the right thing-- get the farmers feast, which will allow you to taste a little of everything delicious.  And if the pork tenderloin is part of your menu that night, EAT THE RIND!  F'ing Fantastic!

My ultimate 5 star test-- did i get food drunk?  YES!!!!!!  I actually walked out wobbly knee'd without drinkiing a drop of alcohol.  In fact, with food this good, I highly recommend sticking with sparkling water, so that nothing competes with the flavors you will be served.

Is there anything bad you can say about Blue Hill?  Sure.  Its a NY restaurant, and its small so yes, you will encounter  the dreaded row of tables for two, close enough to cuddle up with the other patrons.  And yes, I agree that this is not the best environment for enjoying this type of meal....but...if thats what  I need to do to get food this good and this fresh without leaving NYC, then so be it.  If you close your eyes (and dont lean too far to your left or right) you'll be convinced you're sitting at a farmhouse table upstate somewhere.

Oh one more thing--- go with someone who appreciates deliciousness as much as you do.  I think I'd cry if i ever found myself sitting across such a from some grumpy droopy downer of a guy while trying to enjoy the Blue Hill 'Experience'.

Great meal. We ordered off the menu. My wide and I split apps and dessert. Everything was superb. The "pig" on top of my mixed grains was totally amazing. Wines by the glass were great too as was the dessert. The price was reasonable given the impeccable - but not stuffy - service and the tremendous food.

Wonderful! And, yes, we had our reservation set here before the Obamas dropped by, so we felt like cool kids for being (slightly) ahead of the curve. 

They brought some wonderful fresh vegetables out to start (radishes and snap peas with an interesting light tangy glaze).I had the farm fresh egg and the lamb with emmers and quinoa, which was prepared sort of like a pesto risotto, and I added a side of the marinated beets. The boyfriend had the basil ravioli and  the veal. The farm fresh egg was my favorite thing, but everything was delicious. Our server's wine recommendation was also spot-on and pretty reasonable.  Unfortunately we were on our way to a show and weren't able to linger or grab dessert, but the service was fantastic and they made sure to get us out of there on time. 

I definitely hear the comparisons to Chez Panisse, but it also reminded me very much of Plumpjack in San Francisco. Same cozy setting, interesting but not overwhelmingly fussy food, and extra-delicious bread and butter. Break out the multiple types of volcanic salt and they'd really seem like kindred spirits.

Fabulous.  Had the Farmer's Tasting Menu, which they made vegetarian-- it was excellent.  Warm, subdued decor; attentive but not oppressive service.  The strawberry cannoli is one of a kind.  Highly recommended for vegetarians; I enjoyed the big servings of rich, filling veggie entrees.

I bookmarked Blue Hill (at least mentally, but maybe not on yelp) several years ago.  When the opportunity arose to try it last night, I was delighted.  Coming from Berkeley, it's hard not to think of Chez Panisse when you walk in.  Blue Hill has the same focus on local organic ingredients that Chez pioneered decades ago, and it seems to create the same kind of interactions between guests and staff that make everyone feel completely at home when they dine at C.P.

The personnel at Blue Hill were clearly very busy.  The staff members float around to wherever they're needed, and they do a great job of filling in for each other.  When dishes come to a table, there's a cloud of servers getting everything to the right spot at the right moment.  That cloud dissipates as soon as it's no longer needed, but it reforms when the time comes.

The wine person, Jen (or Jenn), was really very helpful.  Our group of 6 put down 3 bottles of wine.  We started with a North Fork Long Island chardonnay that she recommended and then moved to the Sean Thackrey Pleiades (bottled 2009) for what I expected would be the unique red wine that we'd consume.  (This was also a Jen recommendation.)  A problem arose when the Sean Thackery went dry: what to drink after that?  We went with a Languedoc wine that Jenn recommended, and it really worked well with what we were eating, even after the overpowering Sean Thackery wine.

And what were we eating?  I had two dishes: a farm fresh egg (which is kind of a classic here) and the happy contented pork.  Both dishes were excellent, but they came on beds of green and black that were a bit similar to each other.  It seems to me that somewhat might have nudged me away from the pork after I had settled on the egg.  But this is kind of a quibble.

The dinner was really an A+, and I'd have no compunctions about recommending this restaurant to anyone who expresses an interest in it.  But it just so happens that I came here one night after an excellent dinner at I Trulli (see my earlier review).  When push comes to shove, I trulli have to say that I liked my dinner the previous night a tad better than my dinner here at Blue Hill.  For what reason?  Maybe I've gotten maxed out; it might have been better not to experience these two fantastic restaurants back to back.

Good job, New York!  Now it's back to the other coast.

I'll have what Barack's having. Seriously, can a restaurant blow up any more once a popular sitting president has left DC to take his wife on a date there? Thankfully my girlfriend snagged a reservation for this past Saturday night a few days before our president's famous (or infamous) vist.

Despite all the attention, I can honestly say Blue Hill is every bit as deserving of the attention. For those who haven't been, think Chez Panisse (fresh, locally grown meats and produce with an understated vibe) meets Greenwhich Village minus the political statement. The tables are close together, yet unlike most restaurants where most couples try to ignore the conversation of their neighbors, diners here tend to be quite social with each other. It's with this feel, friendly service and weekly changes to the menu why I can understand why people come from all areas of the City to dine here weekly (though this is still an expensive proposition despite the fact that you can spend a LOT more on dinner in NYC). The room is small, so the noise level does pick up a bit as the night moves on as the restaurant fills and the crowd moves from old Manhattan restaurant to young (though this is not a restaurant that will threaten Sushi Samba's 20-something see-and-be-seen demographic). 

The meal started with fresh vegetables from the Stone Barns gardens, in our case sliced radishes and pea pods (which were unlike any pea pods I'd ever had). For our appetizers, I had ravioli with tomatoes and basil, while my girlfriend had a spring vegetable salad, which allowed both of us to sample a greater variety of the fresh vegetables grown at Stone Farms that are far superior than anything you can get even at your local Whole Foods. For mains, my girlfriend had the Wreckfish (a very dense whitefish), while I had the veal on account of the recommendation from fellow diners on our left and right. The fish was great, as was the veal, however the broccoli rabe my veal came with was incredibly oversalted. I was one "those people" who said something to the waiter, but they could not have reacted better. Within 5 minutes, they replated the meal with new sides and were incredibly apologetic, comping us each a glass of wine. I don't know if they actually did it, but they said they sampled my brocoli rabe, agreed it was oversalted and sent apologies from the kitchen (note to any in the restaurant business, even if you don't do this, this is the perfect thing to say to a customer when they send something back). Please do note, I'm not one of those people that sends things back. I only do under one of two conditions:
A. It can easily be seen, i.e. overcooked steak
B. Others taste and agree should be sent back
I really hated myself for doing this, but I just had to...

Aside from this one issue, the rest of the meal was great. The wine list is well selected at reasonable price points and the outstanding wait staff is tremendously helpful with it. As the appetizers feature Stone Barns' vegetables, the dessert menu showcases their fruits. We went with the Blueberries with yoguart, vanilla sable and honey and did not in any way regret the decision.

For those seeking to avoid the crush and/or frustration of trying to land a reservation, consider sitting at the bar you could probably snag a couple stools most anytime for a drop-in.

What can I say?  I had the birthday dinner of my dreams here (a week before the Obamas went, I swear!).  Doesn't really get any better.

- Amuse bouche w/ the freshest radish/cauliflower I've ever tasted.  Not sure if it was plain or soaked in the tiniest bit of vinaigrette, but either way...damn...so crunchy.  Like candy.  I wish there was more!
-Warm breadsticks were addicting...really hard to not keep eating
-Warm asparagus soup was absolutely addicting, delicious, creamy...ugh...the best comfort food
-Crab over pine nuts and mint...don't remember what else was in this dish but definitely my favorite of the night.  I'm a crab FREAK and loved all the textures and flavors.  This dish is a must get.
-BF got the lamb, which I'd never had before.  I liked it, but liked his veggies even more (asparagus were soo fresh)
-I got the wreckfish which was light and tasty, albeit a little undercooked to my liking
-Desserts blew my mind...chocolate bread pudding and this apple dish with honey ice cream.  Plus complimentary homemade truffles and coconut marshmallows.  LOVED.

Basically, believe the hype.  This place is worth it.  Great service and attention to detail.  Tyra Banks was there when I went and I freaked out.  Seriously, couldn't have hoped for a better birthday.

Ended a fine dining tour of NYC here, so I was fearing palate overload. No worries! I ordered two apps to make sure I had room for dessert... I got the slow-poached egg in hen's broth with fresh herbs --which was GENIUS.  Even my husband, who hates eggs, liked this. has something to do with the fact that the egg was laid that morning, probably by a happy chicken clucking around in the sunshine on Blue Hill's farm. Not too kosher to serve it in chicken broth, which was quite boldly flavored --almost like a sauce --and with the herbs it was simple, clean, and nourishing. 

I also got the octopus, which was prepared 2 ways --one, in thin, tender slices, almost like carpaccio, the other, the tentacles, grilled. both were NOT rubbery at all, and again, my husband who is not an octopus fan wanted to eat the whole plate. Even if you don't like octopus, it's totally worth a try. 

My husband got some crazy pork belly thing, which was tender and really tasty. The man next to us got it too and I heard him complain to his dinner companion that "some pieces are just pure lard." And he didn't eat them!! I wanted to tell him, dude, you are missing the entire point! If you go there and get the pork, expect much delicious fat. Don't be afraid, just don't make it a habit and work out regularly. It's worth it!  (did you see the Top Chef where Jeff got eliminated from the Stone Hill Farms competition because he trimmed off all the delicious fat? See, Tom Coliccio agrees with me). 

Our server was extremely knowledgeable and almost dying to tell us about the food --what wintered over parsnips means, for example (also very delicious!). 

We didn't get dessert cuz we were meeting a friend at Max Brenner's later on. boo!  but can't wait to go back for it!

From delicate chicken like I have never had before to moist and light mahi mahi, I loved every bite. I also loved the added "surprises" like farm fresh veggies skewered and displayed on a wood block to warm french bread with fresh churned butter and colorful seasoning salts. 

It was abundantly clear that peas are in season now because just about everything we ate had peas. From the mini pea "burger" to pea cannelloni, to the accompaniment to our main dishes, it was "peas galore." The cool thing about Blue hill is, throughout the year, you will get what's ripe, so if you come in winter you will get root vegetables, if you come in the fall, apples. I am not inclined to come in other seasons, because we went for my Wife's birthday and judging from the amount of candles in the place, a lot of people see this as a special occasion place. 

We were there for 3 hours, which is a little long of a time to sit for me. However, the time flew and we left full and content.

they started with veggies skewered and displayed in a very unique/cool way. delicious! (and this coming from a veggie hater!)

my salad was savory and yummy
had the pork - which was served soo many ways - sausage, pork chop, pork belly. a little too much pork for me.

yummy but petit dessert

child friendly - in that their tables are covered with white paper - great for drawing!! and they gave us a baby flashlight which my 2.5 y/o loved.

I read some of the reviews and wonder if the diners just didn't get it?!  

Service was impeccable. The wait staff was knowledgeable, attentive, engaging and quite frankly everything you hope for yet hardly expect & or receive when dining out.

Ambiance, intimate seating arrangement yet did not feel as if my party was involved in other patrons meals and conversations. (My one negative comment would be the floral arrangment was a bit obtrusive)

Food, was simply divine. Fresh, complimentary, flavorful and the presentation lovely.

Exquisite dining experience.

I would have given this place 5 stars, however the dessert was not good...thus I reduced rating.  Everything I ate was outstanding minus dessert...which was overpriced and not good.  The service was friendly and top notch.  I will definately return and just not order dessert!

This place tries to be the East Coast Chez Panisse but manages to fall short on many counts. 

First, the food is "fresh" (i.e. comes from the Blue Hills Farm upstate an hour or two), but it isn't tasty. And what's the use if it's not tasty? Especially at the prices Blue Hill seems to think they can command. For instance, I'd heard so many raves over "This Morning's Farm Egg," but it boiled down to paying $15 for a runny egg. Over some veggies. Sigh. 

Secondly, table service was aloof, and the hostess was downright rude. Two of us had walked by previously, inquiring about table availability, and received no more than a dismissive glare before the hostess simply walked off, leaving the coat check woman (who was the nicest person in the building!) to apologize. 

Finally, they totally jam people in here. Which can be fun if you enjoy listening to the couple next to you bicker or the old boys' club next to you get sloshed, but not for a restaurant that's supposed to be refined. 

Tip: You can apparently visit the farm upstate, where there's another restaurant and a more casual (but relatively expensive) cafe.

Not a huge fan.  Tiny space, mediocre food, very confused servers.  

I started with crab, had chicken as an entree, and some odd baked apple for dessert.  Chicken was undercooked, gummy, and was visually unpleasant. The crab appetizer is the recipient of one of my three stars; the other two, to the Warwick Valley Doc's Draft Hard Apple Cider.  Also loved the fresh carrots to start, and the bathroom decor.  Glad I've been, but will NOT be back.

Excellent execution with the freshest of ingredients which are aloud to shine on their own merits without any overpowering spices or sauces.  Best of class among the new american/season/local restaurants.  The space mirrors the food in its elegant simplicity.  Excellent service to boot.

Simply put, my favorite restaurant in the city.  The tasting menu with wine pairings is simply fantastic.  There's nothing better than the turning of the seasons in the city, and this place does a marvelous job of capturing the essence of the local seasonal movement that has become so popular.  The ivory salmon was amazing and the chocolate bread pudding is one of the best desserts I've ever had.

Dan Barber is the founder of this special restaurant. I came out here with my brother when I visited him in NYC. A friend had recommended this place to him. Notably, this restaurant gets all its meats and vegetables from their own blue hill farm, so the freshness and the quality of the ingredients is controlled and guaranteed.

There we had the tasting selection, which was essentially 5 dishes, including 2 small appetizers, 1 entree, and 2 desserts. There were also 3 amuse bouche, which are 3 very small dishes to open up the appetite -- "mouth amusers"

Out of the five dishes, my favorite dish had to be the "pig liver between two thin layers of crispy chocolate waffle" appetizer. Absolutely AMAZING, nothing like I've had before. Combination sounded weird, but the flavors went well together. For sure, the dish was the highlight of the night.

The main entree was a duck dish. Very tasty and tender, though a little small. The desserts were also very good and complemented one another well (warm and cold).

Overall, giving the restaurant a 4/5. Food was definitely good, but I believe the food was a little pricey for what we got. There are less expensive restaurants that have similar quality, IMHO. Definitely give this restaurant a shot, though! I enjoyed it.

I wanted to go to Blue Hill for quite some time so when my fiance made reservations for last Friday, I was very excited.  Unfortunately, I have to say, I walked away from the experience very disappointed.  While the restaurant ambiance was nice and the staff was primarily friendly, the food was where it fell short.  The dinner started with an amuse-bouche of fresh vegetables.  It was prepared and presented in a very unique way and was probably the highlight of the evening.  For appetizers we had the salad and the ravioli.  Both were good dishes although the portion on the ravioli was quite small.  For entrees, I had the chicken and he had the sea bass.  When my dinner came out, I actually wasn't sure it was what I ordered.  The white meat and dark meat were separated on the plate which was nice, except the white meat looked like and had a similar consistency to tofu.  I'm not sure how it was prepared but it had a very slimy texture and was not good.  The dark meat was raw in some places and practically inedible.  My fiance seemed happy with the sea bass although it was sitting in a very watery green sauce.  Perhaps it was just an off night because I've heard very good things about this restaurant but I probably won't be going back any time soon.

Blue Hill is magnificent. Period.

This place is the epitome of fine-dining, without the stuffiness that usually comes with the staff.  There was not an ounce of pretension from the hostess, server or sommelier.  

There was no pretension from the food either.   The presentations were simple and lovely, without sacrificing flavor.  From the fresh vegetable amuse bouche to the matzoh ball soup with fresh egg and fois gras to the dessert wine, it was all pristine and divine.

It is without a doubt one of the best restaurants in the city.  it is perfect for a romantic evening/special occasion.  I thought about the meal for the rest of the night AND the next day!

A truly elegant yet decadent dining experience!

Had a late reservation last night and at the end of our meal, who walks in but Dan Barber himself!  They don't have a service entry door, so all the fresh produce, meats and amazingness from Stone Barnes is paraded through the dining room.  
Ordered the chicken which was really good, but the lamb is to die for.  Braised octopus so good that we ordered two.  Service is impeccable.  One of my favorite meals in the city.

Went here with my wife for a nice date night.  It isn't the most romantic place (tables are kind of close together), but the food is top notch.  You have to go there with the right mindset...Blue Hill is all about fresh vegetables and meats.  The appetizer of raw vegetables needs to be appreciated for what it is, and for raw vegetables it is really delicious.  The portions aren't huge, but my wife and I came away saying this was the most flavorful food we have had in NY.  She had the sweet potato ravioli and I have the poached egg/lentil salad.  For an entree she got the lamb and I had the venison, both were great.  The food is almost like a flourless chocolate cake for dessert, it is so rich you can only eat so much.  The small appetizer portions were the perfect size.  The entree portions were quite large.  Overall, it was great!

Eating local, in-season food is a great reason to eat here. But even more of a reason is its flavor.  It's truly an experience of the earth. You can taste the richness of each bite, which hasn't been falsely created by drowning it in butter or cheese. It is simply an honest flavor...being celebrated on your palate. I have never moaned with as much pleasure through an entire meal as I did when eating here. The chocolate bread pudding, tilefish, lamb and lentils were each to die for. 

I asked the waitress why the parsnips tasted so damn good, and she said it was because they "remained unpicked underground through winter in order to absorb the nutrients of the earth". 

If only eating all food could be such a grounding experience.

One of the only restaurants in the city I feel meets the experience I have of culinary bliss in Stowe, VT. Everything was fresh, elegant and absolutely divine. Local and fresh seasonal ingredients, warm and attentive service, great wine selection. This is a place I go to as a lavish demonstration of my affections for someone I love and myself!

Blue Hill definitely knows how to pair ingredients with complementary flavors.  Starting from the amuse-bouche of mini beet-ricotta burger, which exploded with flavor and had a nice balance of sweet and tart, to the braised fennel, to the seared mackerel with refreshingly sweet apple-celery root broth and crunchy soy beans, every single element on the plate played a role in developing the rich layers of flavor.  The quinoa dish, for example, with crunchy grains laced with tiny chunks of pancetta, berkshire pork, and butternut squash was really good on its own, but eating it together with the boudin blanc on top added another level of complexity to the dish.  It was a very enjoyable meal, although probably not one that completely blew me away, but worth going to again.  Next time, I'll probably try the farmer's feast menu, which, on top of the dishes listed on the menu, also gets you some small treats in between courses.

Only went to Blue Hill once (not your cheap eat!) and ordered the tasting menu and it was simply amazing.  Each dish was surprising in its creativity and taste.  Not all the dishes were equal (the main dish, chicken, was actually disappointing) but some of the dishes were so extraordinary that it made me forget everything else.  I can't wait to go again!

This is definitely one classy restaurant.
It was a wonderful dinner in a beautiful setting but for some reason I was not as blown away as I should have been, given the reviews and hype.
Upon entering the restaurant, one finds themselves in a tiny alcove of red velvet curtains. Once you fight your way through the yards of fabric, you find yourself in a beautiful, elegant setting filled with Manhattan's upper east side-ish crowd.
We were given tiny samplings of vegetables served on posh silver sticks as starters. 
Artfully prepared and bringing new meaning to garden-fresh, I thought it was creative and memorable. 
Definitely brought a whole new level of interest when associating a cauliflower or two. Mothers, do try this at home when trying to get your kids to eat their greens.

We ordered "This Morning's Farm Egg"  to share and it was absolutely divine. The egg was very runny so if that grosses you out, stay away.
Otherwise it is liquid goodness when combined with the harsher texture of mushrooms and earthy broth. 
I had the Sea Bass for my entree. It came with soybeans and immersed in broth.  It was fresh but not terribly memorable. I think the key to this restaurant's success is definitely presenting their ingredients at its most natural state, which is a nice change from the usual sodium highs I walk out of restaurants with. 
My friend and I shared a wonderful bottle of wine from their impressive collection and ended the meal with a cheese sampler. 
It was a mixture of old and new world cheeses and I'm not gonna lie and say that that has any meaning to me, however the goat cheeses were delicious and provided a nice finish to the meal.
I probably wouldn't mind coming back but would hope to encounter something a bit more mind-blowing next time (and maybe a six-figure salary as well as this place was NOT cheap.)

The idea behind this place is great and I was really excited to go.
Before we even got the meal, i was pretty upset.
1. They stuck us in the back of the restaurant where there were on 4 couples sitting. It was extremely quiet there and we felt that we had to whisper the entire time. The ambiance totally sucked there.
2. I know it sounds little ridiculous, but for the amuse bouche,  the table next to us got these little beet burgers. My girlfriend and I who really love beets and were really excited to taste them. However, we didn't get any little beet burgers. I know it sounds ridiculous and a little petty, but if you are not going to give it to us and least tell us why. 
3. The food was pretty good, but very expensive and i don't think that it is worth the cost. I am still going to try the farm someday as I hope it will be a better experience.
Pricey but amazing local, seasonal food produced in an exciting and oft-times ingenious way.  Sit at the bar and let them take good care of you.

Simple. Waitress-poor. wine director-Excellent!. appetizers-sweet pot rav and the Maine crab meat Excellent!. entrees-Berkshire pig was a complete home run! emmer/quinoa at first was very good but after two bites we found it lacking in depth and didn't care to continue. palette cleanser tasted like poison so the job was a success there although I thought I was being murdered. dessert-the honey crisp apple was a farce, think I'd rather go to tast d lite. ambiance was questionable- the lighting was far too bright( we arrived at 10:45 and it was bright as daylight inside) we could hear the bartender across the room over my conversation at the table. regards to facilities I would like to say the bathrooms were spotless and very tasteful. might visit again hopefully to find better a server and pass on dessert.

We were both in the mood for something seasonal and sustainable. Don't ask me how you can crave sustainability but after two nights at Le Cirque, Blue Hill sounded devine. 

Below street level dining room with outdoor seating in a lush garden which is accessed through the kitchen. We ordered  a cocktail at the bar before they seated us. The host and bartender were very polite and professional. 

At the table the server greeted us and gave great explanations of the dishes.  This guy was peculiar but prompt and refreshingly verbose.

The food was immaculate. The ravioli weakened my knees and sent me into bliss convulsions. The pork was perfectly cooked as though held in the utmost respect.

The chicken...the chicken. The word doesn't seem fitting. I will use bird of succulence. Apparently utilizing a sous vide method the blue hill chefs prepared the most perfect piece of yard bird that I have ever tasted elevating this creature to heights of which it could not have achieved under power from its own wings. 

Wine list was well balanced. We enjoyed the deserts and coffee. 

I will be back several times.

Our dinner was very good; however, I was not as blown away as I had hoped to be.  We went here a few days before Christmas.  The fresh vegetable appetizer (which I guess is there amuse) and the cocktail we ordered was wonderful.  The appetizers were good, but not so good that I remember what they were. For our entrees we had a duckling dish with brussels sprouts and pig snout and ear that was served with farro and butternut squash.  The duckling dish was amazing.  The pork dish was just ok...the pork itself was great, but the farro with the squash did not work.  The side of marinated beets we also ordered was the best thing we had.

We were too full for dessert, and I saw that the tables around us were getting cookies/chocolates with their check anyway (even the ones that didn't get dessert); however, when we got our check, we did not get anything... perhaps they ran out.  Anyway I was disappointed after seeing them presented to everyone else.  I thought about asking, but how can you ask for a free desert?  3.5 *s  I don't know how this place got a Michelin star..
The menu always matches the vegetables in season at the restaurant's upstate farm. The bartenders are outstanding. You defnitely need a reservation since it's a small place and it's always full.

one of my favorite all around restaurants. A bit expensive, so it cant be a weekly treat, but this restaurant and dan barber re-define seasonality and freshness. Its comfortable without being to stuffy. The wine list is impressive and the attention to detail is great.

this is the greatest restaurant in the world! i've never tasted vegetables with so much flavor. i usually dont like brussel sprouts and cauliflower (my husband ordered), but these were outstanding. the warm baguettes reminded me of france. i had the sweet pea ravioli for an appetizer- sweet and delicious. i had the emmer & quinoa entree- good. my husband had the cauliflower steak- done up all fancy w/ a sauce and dried fruit and pine nuts. damn that was good! dessert was a chestnut crumble w/ the best chocolate mousse i've ever had. husband had apple crisp. everything was just awesome. i can't say enough good stuff about this place. service was also fantastic. i'll definitely be going back.

They have an impressive wine selection.  They have wine from vineyards that  either you've haven't heard of or very exclusive or very limited selection (distribution that's not available elsewhere).

The food there was exceptional.  They always use the freshes ingredients.

Food - Exceptional, fresh, American-style cuisine with a twist
Deor - Upscale but comfy, classic yet contemporary
Service - Very attentive staff
Atmosphere - quiet, calm and warm (kinda feels like a spa with the dim lighting)
Price - Expensive ($$$)

We did the tasting menu with wine pairing at the Manhattan location. One of the best dinners ever. Exceptional, attentive service. Beautiful space. Four of the five dishes were amazing (seriously, the best pork I've ever had...just edging out WD-50s pork belly) and the other was very good. I wish I could eat here every day. I definitely plan to go back...hopefully to the Stone Barns location next time.

I had extremely high expectations for this restaurant, especially with all the press and praise that Chef Dan Barber has been receiving of late. I was hoping for a Chez Panisse of the east. Well, not so much. My meal here would have been amateur night at C.P. 

Positives: I liked the feel of this place. We sat out on a heated back porch, some would grumble about having to go through the restaurant underbelly to get there, but I didn't mind. I thought it was cozy and intimate. The service was excellent. I admired the way the staff dealt with some of the high maintenance guests around us, particularly the gross mid-life crisis make-out session that was happening on the banquette beside me. My appetizer and dessert were very, very good - beautiful fresh flavors, especially the apple dessert, it truly celebrated the apple.

Negatives: The entrees. All four of us were unmoved and unimpressed by our main dishes. They were all lacking in balance and contrast. There was nothing that gave us pause, and it really put a damper on our impression of the place. Each of us had a different thing: pork, lamb and fishes ---- all were off the mark of excellence. 

Perhaps one has to get the tasting menu here to understand the Stone Barns reputation. But, I think that's a cop out. A great restaurant should never disappoint, from bread service to mignardises. Period.

Why would I give Blue Hill three stars?

Because I don't like making reservations a month in advance to feel like an asshole when I walk in the door. Somehow, despite being in communication three times with the restaurant, including a confirmation call on their end, we walked into the Manhattan location (post-my proposing and catherine's birthday dinner) to find ourselves being asked "if we were sure we had made reservations at this Blue Hill" by the hostess. I can not quite describe what I was feeling at that moment because you had to see that quasi-professional "I don't really give a fuck" smile the hostess had on her face.

After the manager was brought into the fore to sort out their obvious fuck-up we were given a great table, some free cocktails (which were made during this whole debacle), and comped an 80 dollar bottle. I'm not sure if we received extra courses but I believe so. They really did make every effort to make me forget that I was initially not welcome to be seated except at the bar that night.

The food was terrific. The fresh farm egg appetizer. The face bacon amouse bouche. The tasty home made butter. The lamb was perfectly cooked. Catherine ordered Venison for the first time ever and was a fan. I have only great things to say about our server and the food. It was truly one of the best (and biggest) meals I have ever had at a superstar chef restaurant but the occasion was marred from the very beginning because I had to fight for my right to be there after I made ridiculous preparations so that the night would be flawless.

I'd go back but maybe Stone Barns won't have the attitude next time.

Unquestionably one of the best restaurants in New York City 

Pros: Great, inventive menu with plenty of choices for all; organic and natural ingredients. Great for vegetarians

Cons: Hmmm...it's far from my apartment... 

Bottom line: Book a table for yourself! 

Review: I think this is one of the best restaurants in the city, that said, I'm a little biased. The food here is exceptional; the waitstaff are most accommodating and not in the least pretentious; and the wine list had something for every budget. Make no bones about it, it's expensive, but it's worth it. 

I went here for an anniversary a year or so ago and the food was amazing. Everyone who comes to New York on business that I know, I send here as it's just a fantastic restaurant. 

Usually a restaurant of this quality, prestige, and trendiness would have some pretension; but not here. It's just a down to earth restaurant with great atmosphere, food, and wine. 

The location is great too, it's tucked away in a small house in the village and it definitely adds to the experience. 

As an added plus, it's a great restaurant for vegetarians.  My girlfriend is a vegetarian and usually suffices on some side dish; but not here. She was offered a range of options and chose a Cauliflower steak, weird concept but it came out and was incredible.  It's her favorite non-vegetarian restaurant in the city!

Must try!

Any vegans out there: try Blue Hill.

No, I am not kidding.  

I took my girlfriend there for her birthday this week, and they just blew our minds.  For two vegans, that is no small feat.

We've eaten at the best veg places in the city - Candle 79, Pure Food & Wine, etc - and this place topped them all.  

Anyway, I had read very positive reviews and wanted to experience their local produce and high-quality ingredients. So, I stopped by and asked if they could handle us on the upcoming special occasion.  I was warmly greeted and told they could handle "any" special diets. 

They certainly delivered on that promise.  They told the chef we were coming ahead of time and he prepared an excellent 5 course vegan "Farmer's Feast." 

It included the following:

- a "roots and fruits" dish with amazing parsnips
- a silky smooth farro with basil oil, edamame and lots of greens
- a cauliflower "steak"
- a pre-dessert with 3 sorbets
- a *huge* apple dessert, with a sorbet, terrine and more

Everything was so fresh and each bite was incredible. 

And the service was perfect.  Best I have ever received.  They seemed very, very committed to making it an excellent vegan meal.

So, who knew.  I'm glad I looked into this and tried it.  I am now eager to experience the vegetarian tasting menus at the other 3 and 4 star restaurants. 

I can't recommend this place enough - whatever your dietary needs are. 

(However, if it's anything out of the ordinary, I would give them some warning ahead of time.)

The ultimate in seasonal freshness. I had never savored raw cauliflower in the way I did that night. Theirs happened to be a vibrant deep purple variety. The ingredients were the stars, including the kale and concord grapes. The cauliflower steak was so well done that I tried to reenact the recipe. Bravo to Chef Barber and staff! Looking forward to trying the one upstate.

I knew the food was going to be good the moment I stepped inside.  Was that a hint of pistachio over there?  Maybe some nutmeg in the corner?  It's winter, so that must be parsnip...    really, it looks inviting, and warm, not stuffy or cold, and no one is pushy or pretentious.

The waiter steered me in the direction of the brussel sprout appetizer, which, I believe, could turn even the biggest veggie-hater into a lover.  So simple, too, but isn't that what good food is all about anyway?

The bread pudding sang to me.  The wine pairings were spot on.  If I could afford it, I'd be here every day of the week.

My girlfriend and I had huge expectations going into this restaurant, but were left disappointed.  

First, the positive: The restaurant ambiance was nice, and the location (next to Washington Square Park) was perfect for a pre/post-dinner walk.  The service was excellent, the bread was good and the bottle of wine we ordered (a riesling) was tasty and relatively moderately priced.   

Negative: 

Food: The in-season vegetables featured in our 'seasonal' dishes, cauliflower and broccoli, weren't used in very inventive ways; a plain puree and citrus vinagrette, and in general, there just wasn't anything special about the food.  It was cooked well (good temperature on both the Cobia and Stripped Bass which we ordered as entrees), but on the Cobia there was a strange combination of mushrooms and dried fruits in a sauce which did not really compliment anything about the fish, and while the Stripped Bass itself was good, the puree it came with had a soup-like consistency, which hid the parts of the dish that didn't float to the surface, and just generally made it difficult to eat.       

For dessert we ordered the Chocolate Bread Pudding, which was lava cake.  Literally no different than lava cake, no other flavors hidden in there... just regular chocolate cake, with hot, melty, pudding inside.  A couple next to us was fawning over the same dessert for the entire second half of our meal, so maybe we missed something, but we just didn't find it special at all.

Atmosphere:  While the general ambiance of the restaurant is nice, the seating is very crowded, which is fine... space is limited, I get it.  But, the thing is this, at fancy restaurants there are often ridiculous people, and at fancy restaurants in the West Village there are almost exclusively ridiculous people; having two ridiculous couples carry on conversations 1 foot away from you on either side is a distracting at the least, and off-putting at worst.  Words and phrases from their conversations about god-knows-what tip toe into your range of hearing, and if you have a spastic attention span like me say goodbye to your dinner-time conversation.

Anyway, I guess we just expected more... the total bill for 1 whiskey, 2 appetizers, 2 entrees, 1 dessert and a bottle of wine was $237 including tip... not bad, but we could have gotten the same meal for $120 at any number of other places.

Simply said, Blue Hill is a place with excellent service that I can come back to time & again for a fresh & delicious dinner.

And it's true: fresh ingredients do make a difference in how the meal tastes.

The prices reasonable (in my opinion) but the entrees are between 24 and 38 dollars with the average being about $32.  The service is great - what you would expect, really.

The space is a little small and that can make your experience cozier than you might be comfortable with but its never bothered me.  I've been here three times, now, and I hope to be back soon.

Bottom line:

Good recipes made great by farm fresh ingredients make Blue Hill a must try.

LOVED IT HERE!

A lot of restaurants have some hit or miss plates but everything at Blue Hill was fantastic. They get their organic ingredients every day so the menu changes with whatever is fresh or in season. I ordered the "This Mornings Farm Egg" and the veal. Other people at my table ordered the tasting menu and a crab with citrus appetizer. The egg was perfectly poached and melted in your mouth. Perfection! One of the people in my party ordered the "Cauliflower steak" and although it sounds strange, it's actually very tasty. They take a huge head of cauliflower and cut a "steak" from it. I'd actually order that as my entree if I went again next time. 

Another plus is that they send out all these complimentary unique little dishes at the beginning of the meal. They must have sent out at least 5 or 6 for our party of 4. We were beginning to feel full before our appetizers arrived. They are presented in an abtract way which makes it very appealing to the eyes as well as the palate! The bread is also delicious.

You must give Blue Hill a try! It will change how you view fine dining. A very fun experience and I would definitely go again.

I ate here the other night for my birthday with my husband, as this place was on my list of must-do special occasion NYC dining experiences. It made a dreary, rainy day so much happier.

First off, we asked our server to describe the wines by the glass for us, and she did such an excellent job that I ended up going with something I'd never tried instead of a tried-and-true (but unadventurous) chardonnay. We shared the fresh farm egg for the appetizer, and it was very tasty, with the mushroom broth adding the perfect flavor. I had the seared cobia for my main course, and it was cooked just right, very rare and sushi-like, and went very well with the mushrooms and cauliflower. He had the cauliflower steak, which I thought was very inventive and just the right size. We also shared some brussels sprouts, and topped off our meal with some bite-sized pumpkin pie.

This place left us very happy, and perfectly satisfied. The only drawback is that the tables are very close together, and we couldn't help but overhear our neighbors' conversations. We sat in the back room, though, which I liked because it wasn't too noisy.

while visiting nyc we always do one nice dinner with friends....last year wd-50, this year we chose peter luegers. then a friend of ours who is the bartender at blue said come to my place. after checking the website and learning thats it is all food from a local farm all fresh and in season we said dear god yes! i was so excited for weeks to eat here.

the  4 of us sat at the bar, its very cozy, only seats about 9 people, and perfectly dark. 
our friend the bartender really worked his magic. he is very knowledgeable about the wines and has created some amazing drinks using alot of the ingredients that are in the food, his beet cocktail blew me away. 
we decided on the tasting menu and again were totally blown away. 
it was an amazing flow of flavors and fresh ingredients. from simple veggies to an amazing venison cooked perfectly no need for a knife it fell apart like butter. 
i was thrilled with every dish.
the staff is on top of everything, they are all very into the food and explaining what we are having. the space is small and cozy, not so loud that you cant hear yourself think. we were able to chat and enjoy the company and the food.

all in all i could go and do it again all over tonight.

One of the best meals i have ever had. And yes you can taste the difference. Fresh is best. I had the Morning Egg to start; my GF had butternut ravioli. For our entrees, I had the lamb and she had the Wreckfish; sides were brussel sprouts and potatoes. Fantastic--the brussels sprouts were actually broken apart so it was warm loose leaves. Awesome

My taste buds were in orgasm mode. I love it when you have a meal and everything has its own flavor. Even though I was just having wine by the glass--they made sure I had the perfect one for my meal. 

The chocolate bread pudding was the perfect close to a perfect dinner.

After reading the Serious Eats post on Blue Hill at Stone Barns, I decided that I making a resy at the New York outpost of the restaurant would be the next best thing (since getting to Stone Barns is kind of a hassle when you live in the city).  L and I had weeknight reservations and were promptly seated.  Although the average age inside the restaurant was maybe....40 yrs old (15 yrs our senior), that did not deter from my overall experience.  I had one of the most enjoyable dinners in the city!  We started off our meal by splitting the bean salad which was amazing.  It had several different types of string beans and a light green sauce that enhanced the flavors.  For an entree, I had the wlld striped bass.  It was a prety large portion of fish in a shallow soup of vegetables and beans.  The fish was perfectly cooked and delicious.  L had the pastured chicken, which she wasn't a big fan of, because it was a little too tender for her liking.  For dessert, we shared the peach crumble.  It wasn't amazing - perhaps their other desserts may be better.  I must add that the service was excellent. Though we were much younger than the rest of the crowd at the restaurant, we were treated with as much respect as every one else.  Our waiter even asked if my friend liked her entree, and when she said that it was too tender for her taste, he actually took the entire dish off our bill! Lastly, we were also given chocolate raspberry truffles as petite fours!  What a great way to end a great meal! I must say, this is one of the best restaurants I've dined at in the city and would recommend this for any foodie looking for an amazing meal, or any guy looking for a place to impress a date!

I had my birthday dinner at Blue Hill and the experience was quite extraordinary. Everything was so fresh because everything was delivered straight from their farm in Hudson Valley. I tried the Farmers Feast Tasting Menu ($72) pairing with Victory HopDevil beer, and I especially loved the starter (Halibut) and the main course (lamb). Fresh ingredients were the key for success and Blue Hill delivered. I also liked This "This Morning's Farm Egg"... I loved that title.

I agree with our previous Yelp reviewers about the noise level in the main dining room, but  we were in the back dining area so it was very quiet. The service was bar none.

If you're going there keep in mind that the portions are very small. Overall it was a great dining experience in Greenwich Village.

My Husband and I decided to go to New York for our 2 year wedding anniversary. After doing some research on the internet we decided to try out Blue Hill (due to the high reviews on Yelp and Zagat) Overall I have to say the food was pretty delicious!!! Very fresh. We both decided to go with the farmers feast tasting menu (at $72 a person) along with a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc (Menetou -Salon, Morogues, Loire France 2007) You definitely have to go on an empty stomach! (Although you are given small portions of food to try, it really adds up.) Our bill came out to a total of $240 (that's including tip.)
Was it worth $240 not really. But, it was our anniversary and we were on vacation.


Expensive: Yes

Romantic ambiance : No

Service: Our waitress was great

Pros:

-Fresh food, very tasty, great service!

Cons:

-Tables are way too close together (you can pretty much hear your neighbors conversation!) 

- Man in suit who are you? (I felt I was being watched while I ate) I think he was the manager? Owner?

Overall this place was good--- great fresh flavors, unique vibe and good wine. Service was hip and fun, not stuffy. The ambiance, however, was sub-par. The restaurant was cramped with tables closely lined next to eachother, which at times was a little transcendental for a romantic dinner given we were squashed between a lesbian couple on one side (the one woman was actually wearing the same shirt as my boyfriend) and a gay male pair sipping hot pink bubbly on the other.  Party on!

I can't say enough good things about our dinner at Blue Hill. We loved it!

I was looking for a small, intimate place with good wine & food to celebrate our anniversary. CH & Yelp gave me some good rec's but availability on opentable was the final deciding factor. 

We were lucky to be seated in the back dining area. I found the main dining room too noisy & a bit crowded for a Sunday evening. I would ask when you make or confirm your resy to be seated in the back. 

We had a bottle of Pinot Noir from Oregon that was delish. I love how they organize their wine list - by flavors such as light & fruity, earthy, etc - it really helped us make a decision. They have some a few economical choices (around $60) and plenty of more expensive ones too. 

I knew the food would be good given that they get a lot from the Stone Barn location but I really blown away. The farm fresh cauliflower, the veggies in our appetizers & sides, the perfectly proportions of meat in our main course ( I had the lamb, my husband had pork). These two things, the choice of fresh ingredients & the reasonable portions, make the meal enjoyable & worthwhile. You feel full after it all (don't skip dessert) but not stuffed. We enjoyed a nice walk afterwards which I don't think happens at many of the over the top places NYC has to offer. And yes the bread is awesome, tho it reminded me of pillsbury a bit. 

Blue Hill has a great staff. Everyone was polite but also busy - the place is jumping!

I wish we could go back more often but food like this does cost a pretty penny. Next celebration may have to be here!

Loved it!

Superb service, wine recommendations, atmosphere, and food.
If you don't freak out over farm fresh eggs like me, then you would have given this place a five.
However, this morning's farm egg left a lot to be desired. Didn't taste fresh and the prep served to cover the egg rather than highlight what should be its rich creamy yummy yolkness.

The crazy bread is warm and crusty and I think I ate about a week's worth of bread when I went to Blue Hill for dinner.  (It's not REALLY called crazy bread, but it looks similar to the breadsticks you get at Little Caesar's).  The food is simply prepared to showcase their ingredients; when I tried their salmon, I wasn't even sure what it was because I eat so much farmed salmon (terrible, I know).  

The egg I started with (this morning's egg) was creamier than anything you can buy at the supermarket and the vegetables just tasted....GREENER.  Everything was pretty delicious, but a tad on the salty side (especially the pork dish).  I actually ended up trading my pork dish with Chris because it was literally like eating a bucket of salt.

It's a surprisingly casual place and a good place for a Sunday night dinner.  I recommend having one person get the tasting menu and the other ordering a la carte, otherwise it's too much food!

I reviewed the Blue Hill at Stone Barns - hence the lower rating - it does not compare. 

Priced somewhat appropriately at $72 per person - the chef sent items were much appreciated. Out of everything we ate the bread was absolutely the best. 

Interesting parts were the wild bass entree and the strawberry desert - otherwise the dishes were very good, but we visited Blue Hill again to experience the new and innovative tastes we sampled at the one in Stone Barnes - as I said it just doesn't compare. This seemed like any other restaurant in its caliber - but just slightly above average - which is still good, just nothing special. 

Oh, as a side note, given the recent sighting of the most gigantic cockroach in the world (not here) it was a bit unsettling to see a visible roach trap in the back room. I understand these are old buildings but I would personally either paint it black or attempt to cover it from your more discerning (or roachphobic) customers eyes.

I went last night for a work dinner. Granted we were given the VIP treatment b/c of the person I was with, but the food was some of the best I've ever had. Really simple dishes executed perfectly. Everything tasted so fresh and flavorful, I can't wait to go back!

Of all my dining experiences in NY (including Daniel, Bar Boulud, Gramercy Tavern, Momofuku, Spotted Pig to name a few), Blue Hill was hands down the most memorable.  Excellently executed farm-to-table cuisine focusing on locally sustainable ingredients served in a friendly, well-informed, but non-pretentious manner.  Every dish had fresh, clean components not overly played with, with elements that complement each other beautifully.  The service staff, from the bartender to the management, are nothing less than warm, inviting, and passionate.  Blue Hill is the epitome of what every restaurant should aim to be.

Ambiance? Check.
Service?  Sure, altho the hostess was a little wobbly, but our waiter was a doll.
Food?  DING DING DING!

We had the Farmer's Feast w/ the wine pairing and OMG.  The heirloom tomato salad was first up, and we agreed we love burrata (sp?).  Next came the wild sea bass for me, and the sweet corn ravioli for my friend (who's allergic to fish) and wow - both dishes hit the spot.  His was sweet, mine salty and both done to perfection.  Next came the pork, for which I have no words... except maybe Delicious and Wow.  

We both didn't want the savory plates to end, but the desserts weren't super sweet and both were great!  My favorite was the first dessert: fresh strawberries w/ mint ice milk and a little bit of creme fraiche.  The second dessert was a cooked peach of some sort (4 glasses of wine in at this point!) with some more ice milk and shavings of... something.  

All in all, a delectable meal.  You can also order everything off the farmer's feast a la carte!!

This is what food is supposed to taste like. 

I've been sick of these supposed great restaurants that are more of the same and all about the crowd and decor and not the food. Blue Hill is about the food (and service) and I really appreciate that. 

Defintely take suggestions from the staff and be open to trying whatever they tell you. The Egg app was AMAZING. The pork was great and the desserts really impressed as well. 

Overall, Blue Hill was a breathe of fresh air for me!

My future roomie and I went here to celebrate our new place and we had a great time.

We shared the tomato salad to start. It had grilled tomatoes, cold tomatoes, some that I think were marinated and a yummy tomato sorbet. 

I had the wild striped sea bass for my entree. It was delish. It was served with fresh veggies from the farm. They were all cooked together to create a tasty broth for the fish. 

For dessert we ordered the chocolate bread pudding. The menu said it came with vanilla ice cream, but when our server found out we loved peanut butter, she went to check if there was any peanut butter ice cream left. There wasn't, but the chef offered to make some fresh for us. It was so amazing! Extremely decadent, but not too sweet. 

I cannot wait to go back as the seasons change to see what else is new.

Champignon in the / 
chilled corn soup marinated / 
in sweet blue heavens.

Wow!  Food here is awesome!  
As a birthday gift to me, we came and experienced the culinary greatness this place had to offer.  We had many "seasonal" & "fresh" dishes that created an orgasm of saliva in my mouth.  The food is picked daily from the cherry tomatoes to the freshly laid eggs from their farm upstate.  My wife opted for the Prix-fixe while I opted for my own couple dishes.  The portions are appropriate and pleasant to the eye.  The taste is delicious, clean and in some cases felt very refreshing.  Everything was carefully seasoned without being under or overwhelming as well as very creative with the ingredients used.  I'd recommend certain dishes, but it changes daily and seasonally.

Just go an check it out yourself and come back with a food coma.

I have heard about Blue Hill a few times, and have always wanted to try the place, but to tell you the truth; I'm never in the NYU area to make it to dinner.  What a huge mistake that I have been making these several months.  Had I known that this place is more than the organic-fresh from the farm-celebrity chef kinda place - I would have made reservations a long time ago.

Birthday celebration with S.O. at Blue Hill two weeks ago and I was totally blown away.  The ingredients are all from the restaurant's farm in upstate (is 30 miles north of NYC really upstate?!) Regardless, I was happy to see that the food preparation was not bastardized by all the typical frying, spices, sauces, and the latest ridiculous craze - "frothing".  

Beau had the crab meat and pork and I had ravioli and fish paired with a nice bottle of Italian sparkling wine then finished up with the blueberry dessert - totally delicious!!  I would definitely go back and recommend others to go.

I have to admit I didn't think Blue Hill lived up to my (extremely high) expectations, but it was a great meal, and one that convinced me to want to try out the restaurant at Stone Barns.

The tasting menu looked so-so to us, so we opted for ordering on our own.  We felt affirmed after spying on the couple next to us who ordered the tasting menu.  I started with the Farm Egg appetizer, which was quite nice, but nothing mind-blowing.  That could be my fault for ordering an EGG.  My dining partner had the tomato salad, which was disappointing when compared to the amazing heirloom tomato medley I had at Gramercy Tavern a couple weeks back.

The entrees were better: I had the chicken, which was extremely tender (as a result of poaching) and slathered with carrots, mushrooms, and a sauce that was a little too strong for my tastes.  I also sampled the creamy farro, which came with pork feet and belly.  It was fantastic, and the waiter said it was his favorite item on the menu.

Now, everything was fine at this point.  I was struggling between a three and a four.  It was the desserts that tipped the scale.  We had the blueberries and the peach cobbler.  Both were amazing.  The blueberries were encased in a creamy yogurt cake and topped with the most aromatic, fragrant honey in existence.  The peach cobbler was delicate and sumptuous: nothing at all like the hearty peach cobbler at Gramercy, but more delicious in my opinion.

Service was good, though our waiter seemed a little off.

Well first off it is a little hard to find as the signage is subtle and located in the lower level of a townhouse. But I think it's subtlety is part of its charm. I arrived slightly early and the bartender was extremely friendly. There was a couple of guys at the bar who eat there often, so it was generally a cozy vibe. The lighting is dim but not dark and they play subtle music in the main area while near the restrooms is more speakeasy jazz. They seated us earlier than our reservation and we ended being one of the last parties to leave. It was just very comfortable. We had the farmer's feast which was infused with fresh tastes. I miss getting really fresh food like I used to growing up in Michigan. We skipped the first wine pairing but continued with the rest. The waitstaff was great and knowledgeable.

Date Visited: July 15th
People: Megan
My tab: ~$140

Fabulous meal. Decided upon this place for Megan's birthday because Blue Hill at Stone Barn was a truly a life changing meal. This wasn't quite the same experience, but  have little bad to day. One of the few critisisms I had was that the pre-set menu honestly wasn't particularly exciting, especially compared to the Farmer's feast in Westchester. And the menu was a bit on the small side. Megan and I selected an interesting nebbiola and barbera blend (a super piedmonte?) from La Spinetta called "Pin" which was very drinkable yet not overly acidic, and pretty well opened after a few minutes in the decanter. I started with the grilled shrimp over gazpacho, which was excellent, while Megan had a poached fresh egg, supposedly "laid that morning at Stone Barn"  with mushrooms from the farm and a mix of greens and corn. I didn't get a chance to sample it but megan says "amazing." Following that I had the very tender pork, served over morels and a sauce consisting of whole peas intermixed with pistacios. A horribly ugly description of a wonderfully presented and tasting dish. Megan had the farro, which was new to me but is essentially lamb belly. Also amazing. We ended with 2 desserts, a bread pudding that was as good as stone barn, and a chese platter consisting of 4 tastes: 2 french and 2 american interpetations. Pretty interesting. I would go back in a heartbeat but more than anything, this place reminded me how badly I need to get back up to stone barn, where things are a little less cramped, a little sunnier, and a little more relaxing.

Blue Hill is close to my perfect restaurant.  A seasonal farm to table menu executed beautifully and in a crisp and elegant atmosphere that never feels too stuffy.

The wait staff is friendly, professional, and knowledgeable about the food and wine.  They have even gone the extra mile for me on several occasions from working around my boyfriend's food allergies to still prepare a fish he preferred to placing a candle on the edge of my mother's dessert because she had overheard me refer to the weekend as my mother's birthday weekend.

So many places are popping up with the localvore trend.  I enjoy going to places like marketable and cookshop, but this is the real deal and certainly a notch above.

My only complaint is that they don't have brunch.  I can only imagine how amazing it would be.

If you get the chance.  Visit Blue Hill at Stone Barns, their sister restaurant.  An experience.

Rating: 4.5 stars

Simply superb.  My fiance and I celebrated our anniversary here last night.  We had the tasting menu.  It was five courses.  Four of the five courses were absolutely heavenly.  Great selections of wine.

Ambiance: Very cozy, homey feel.  This place his pretty small, so all the tables are extremely close to each other.  Can be a little noisy, depending how crowded the restaurant is.  

Service:  Great, as expected, but not exceptional.

Food Recap:
Amuse: sugar snap peas, mini pea burgers, kale chips. all yummy!
First course: poached egg w/summer beans and pancetta.  not sure how they poached the egg, but it was amazing.  also, super fresh!
Second course: Wreck fish from south carolina.  I had never heard of this fish before but it was one of my fav dishes! this was accompanied by fennel, shellfish, and some other garnishings. Tasty!
Third course: young chicken over some sort of veggies.  the chicken was poached in buttermilk.  it was the breast of the chicken and part of the thigh with crispy skin. the chicken was tender and went well with the veggies beneath it. amazing how fresh it tasted.
Fourth course (my least favorite): cherries w/mint julip sorbet and sangria sauce.  this was ok.
Fifth course: warm blueberries with some sort of cracker topped with a souffle and accompanied by lemon froyo. loved it!!
Then they gave us a small dish of fresh blueberries. 

The menu changes almost on a daily basis.  Good and not good.  If you fall in love with a dish, chances of it being there when you dine again are slim. So that's not good, but the good is that you can always try something new there and count on it being good.  Many restaurants don't change their menu often b/c the constistency of good food is not there.

Last but not least, it's hard to tell at many places how fresh the food really is, but here, it was easy!

Wondeful place for foodies to try!

Can't wait to dine here again!

Last night my boyfriend surprised me by taking me to Blue Hill in Manhattan. We had gone to Blue Hill at Stone Barns a couple months back and loved it. BH Manhattan is just as special. We ordered the Farmer Feast, which was delicious. The service is helpful and relaxed. The decor is elegant and down to earth. The crowd is understated yet refined. If you want a guaranteed big smile from your significant other, this is the perfect surprise spot!

Hyped-up destination restaurants like this can be tricky.  Particularly with the local/organic foods craze currently whipping itself into a frenzy, I had all but prepared myself for an underwhelming experience of an overrated establishment.  But as has happened many times before, I stand corrected.  A combo of good timing, a little bit of charm, and outstanding food, made my visit to Blue Hill nothing short of wonderful.

Rolling with my favorite West Village foodie, we plied our usual trick of trying to snag a table post 9pm on a recent Wednesday.  The secret of getting in without a reservation is to try to sit at the bar - which fortunately for us, worked like a charm.  Making friends with our fabulous bartender, Rocky, also didn't hurt (and got us two free glasses of wine!)

For food we started with the asparagus (I love summer), and I had the ravioli.  Everything was light, fresh, and delicious.  The ravioli was bursting with flavor, the accompanying chicken, tender and succulent.  Pretty flawless overall.  Prices were what you'd expect at a fancy-ish West Village restaurant, but if you don't go crazy, you won't break the bank.  If it's on someone else's dime, though, I'd recommend the entire menu.  I'll definitely be back to try something else.

I'm really puzzled by the favorable reviews of this restaurant. Sure, the surroundings are pleasant enough, but nothing special. Though frankly, I could care less if the food had been amazing, but it's definitely not. Did we miss something?

I had been trying to get a reservation here since our last trip to New York but we couldn't get in last time around. We managed to get an early reservation this trip and we were really excited to have the chance to dine here with our two friends. I guess I was looking for something akin to the Bouley experience, but Blue Hill is far from that.
