What was good? The staff was friendly. The bread was warm and crusty. My Redbreast Irish whiskey was very nice and the Riesling recommended by the sommelier was fine, though not special. (A Spaetlase with their food would be a nice option.)

The amuse bouche was sugar snap peas with some strips of fresh basil. It was promising; very fresh tasting, thanks to the basil, and we were encouraged.

I passed on the prix fixe menu though it did sound good. Instead, I went with "This Morning's Farm Egg" (sounds nice) and a pork dish, both recommended by our waitress.

The egg dish was quite soupy which, I think is the idea (it does list broth, after all). But what makes it $14? Is it the foraged mushrooms? Foraged from where? Anyway, nothing special -- certainly not at this price.

OK, fair enough. Then the main course came. My companions all chose the lamb. The preparation of both the lamb and the pork seemed very similar. We all thought that the meats tasted steamed (perhaps they're braised, but why?), and they were all served on this plate of sort of vegetable gruel. I actually enjoyed my vegetable spread (OK, I'm being a little harsh here, calling it a spread), more so than the meat. It was all just a bunch of mush. My favorite part was undoubtedly the peas and nuts under the pork, but the pork was just nothing special.

We skipped dessert and went to Rocco's Bakery on Bleecker instead. Now that was good. Canoli and Italian ices.

All in all, for the price, this was really, really disappointing. I won't recommend it and I would not return.

Summary: Four stars overall.  Five stars for the food.  Three stars for the kitchen and service.  One of the best meals we've ever had, things are fresh, simple and creatively prepared.  Perfection was only marred by a kitchen that took an hour an half to produce the second course and a waiter that literally left in the middle of our meal and never said a word.

We came on a Sunday night at 8pm and people were still being seated at 9:30.  I had the three course tasting menu.  The first course, a single large scallop was probably the best I've ever had; tender, rich in flavor and perfectly cooked.  It was served on a bed of salad that tasted liked it was picked in the backyard.  The second course, the white salmon was as tender as sushi, and the third course the roast pork, was unbelievably succulent. My wife had the asparagus side dish and the lamb main course.  She said the asparagus was wonderful and the lamb was good but not great (a little tough.) On the whole this was an over the top meal.  If they hadn't taken 2  hours to produce it this would have been a five star dining experience.

Our first waiter seemed pretty inexperienced (no knowledge of the wine list, etc.) but he did his best.  He came back and after consulting with staff gave us a great wine recommendation (an excellent Spanish wine) and kept apologizing for the kitchen.  Then an hour and a half into dinner he disappeared without a word and our new waitress came by and said, "oh he only comes in to help out."

To this restaurants everlasting credit they kept bringing us free bottled water and extra desserts for whatever chaos was going on in the kitchen.

Definitely worth going out of your way for.  (Just have lots of patience.)

Went to Blue Hill recently for a "special occasion" dinner - and we loved it.  Here is the deal, if you want bells and whistles and clever presentation - this is not it.  This is simple, clean food that is locally sourced.  If that is something you think you'll like then this is the place for you.   I loved the service, the tasting menu was nicely presented and really delicious and I really liked the dining room.  The only reason I don't give it the last star is one of the wines we had paired with the tasting menu (actually with our dessert course) was really horrible and since it was at the end it kind of left a horrible taste in our mouths.  It was some Hungarian dessert wine but it tasted like cough syrup.  Otherwise an excellent meal.

Ah-Mazing! I took my boyfriend here for his birthday last year and it was the perfect place. It's low ceilings and dark brown walls with low banquets were very romantic. We had the tasting menu which was out of this world. Each course was a wonderful little culinary surprise. I don't even remember what most of it was, but it was all very nicely presented and so tasty. Service was excellent and very friendly. We really can't wait to go back!

I can see why Adam Gopnick hangs out with the chef at this establishment; Barber is a zealot when it comes to sourcing ingredients and preparation.  His vision blends the best of both coasts and his involvement with Outstanding in the Field suggests that the restaurant will continue this way for a very long time. Having said that, the only drawback of the establishment is the wine list. There are some fun wines, but the emphasis on ingredients just doesn't work with some of their choices. I thought the appetizers and soup courses were exceptional. By the time we hit dessert, we were committed Blue Hill aficionados.

My husband and I were lucky enough to experience Blue Hill on our last trip to New York.  It was the most delightful meal we've possibly ever had.  We both got the farmer's feast and loved each course, probably more so because they featured ingredients we might not have normally ordered.    The farm-to-table freshness was apparent in everything we were served.  Highlights included the amuse bouche featuring heirloom tomatoes with watermelon, delicious chicken with artichokes that made me realize how god-awful canned artichokes really are(and how frequently I eat them), homemade arugula salt and the continuously refilled crusty bread.  Wine recommendation was right on, and the service was also impeccable.  I can't wait to go back.

Some restaurants sit there on my list of "to do"s, never to be tasted until a proper occasion arises. These are the upscale restaurants of anniversaries and birthdays, of parent dinners and various special occasions. One such special occasion finally arrived when a fellow foodie, and best friend, arrived in NY and we went to Blue Hill.
Blue Hill is not the restaurant you want to take your football team or entire extended family to dinner, and not just because it is a pricey spot. It is a small and intimate space where we felt lucky to have a table (despite our reservations). For those unfamiliar with the restaurant, Blue Hill is one of those seasonal restaurants who gets their ingredients from their farm upstate. Their tasting menu (which we did not sample) changes daily and items are so specially prepared that they can run out of items on the menu. But onto the meal!
Our meal began with an amuse bouche.  Ours was a little selection of fresh broccoli and cauliflower. I found it a bit strange, but I suppose the purpose was to showcase fresh ingredients.  And there was bread.  The breadwas continuously refilled and was hot, crusty and delicious.
Melissa (my friend) and I both ordered the sweet potato tortellini to start ($14).  Served with swiss chard, pancetta, and mutsu apples, this dish was delicate and delicious. The sweetness of the sweet potato and apples was beautifully offset by the saltiness of the pancetta (I do love pork products). I also enjoyed the way the creaminess of the tortellini and sweet potato were balanced by the crisp apples.
Our companions ordered ordered the fennel soup ($10).  This dish was garnished with maine crab, tarragon, and candied lemon. I thought its flavors were not as interesting as the tortellini. It was good, but not necessarily something I'd order.
For the mains, Melissa ordered the veal ($34).  The veal was served over a stew of carrots and parsnips with toasted spices. It was a nice comfort food dish. Yet again, the flavors weren't very complex.
I ordered what I thought was the winning dish of the night - vension ($34).  It was served over braised red cabbage, beets, chestnuts and lardo (again with the pork product).  It was also pretty rare. And it was excellent! I had never tried venison before and was worried that it might be too gamey and chewy, but the flavor was excellent and it was perfectly cooked. Definitely a dish worth ordering again.
At this point, despite the small portion sizes, I was pretty full. But Melissa and I had to have dessert, so we shared the chocolate bread pudding ($10).  Served with a chocolate sauce and vanilla ice cream, this dessert tasted more like a brownie than a bread pudding. It was a delicious brownie - very classic, and almost like a molten lava cake when you reached the chocolate sauce inside. You can never go wrong with lots of chocolate and ice cream.
After our meal, we were taking our time chatting and catching up, but we could tell that the restaurant was in need of our table. So instead of ushering us out, they offered us a free round of drinks at the bar. Good service, beautifully prepared food, good customer relations, I would highly recommend Blue Hill.

First, let me start by saying that the food here is amazing.  It was not the best meal I have ever had but the two entrees we had were the best cooked/prepared entrees I've had in a long time.  I had the lamb and Rob had the pork.  The lamb was succulent.  It tasted like it had been brined before it was cooked as it was juicy despite being sauteed.  The pork reminded me of the berkshire pork in Momofuku's buns in that it was so buttery but without any of the fat.  The wine list is good and I had a glass of the rose malbec while Rob had a glass of the cabernet sauvignon.  We had started with the tortellini which was good but not amazing.  The lamb came with quineoa which was Al Dente and perfectly seasoned to match the lamb.  The pork came with a bed or risotto.  Portions are just right.  The rose malbec I had was very versatile and matched both the entrees very well.  Lastly, we had the chocolate bread pudding.  Now, I am a huge fan of bread pudding.  I used to make my own in the school cafeteria by tearing up pieces of choice bread, adding vanilla pudding and raisins, mixing the entire thing and leaving the concoction for a day or two in my college fridge.  And unfortunately, I was very disappointed with this one.  Maybe the dark chocolate is too strong of a flavor to be able to carry the sutbleness of bread pudding.  Maybe a bread pudding is too simple in its rustic nature to be appropriate for the menu but the chocolate bread pudding resembled a chocolate cake.  Sure you can use brioche to make bread pudding.  Sure you can use the best vanilla pods and whole cream and maybe even a couple teaspoons of Grand Marnier or brandy.  But despite how complicated you can make it, it is basically bread and pudding.   

On a last note, as soon as we were sat in the back, in between two tables of older people, I covered my somewhat revealing silk top with a full wrap.  The corner table on our right consisted of parents with their NYU daughter.  The dad was white-haired and scribbled notes all evening, in the manner of a wannabe food critic.  The table to the left of us was a couple of NYU administrators, who finished their conversation with "Thank you!  -   No, Thank NYU!!" followed by a laugh.  I've NEVER had this problem anywhere but, we had the extremely weird experience of having both of the tables on either side of us listen in on our conversations all night.  I don't know what's in the water but even after those tables left, the new couple that was seated next to us took over on the listening in.  Anyways, New Yorkers overall always have enough drama in their own lives that when you go to a place this crowded everyone is shouting on top of one another in order to be able to get heard.  Here, we dropped our inside voices to barely above a whisper and then stopped talking for a while b/c it was so awkward having those two tables of people just staring at us.  We weren't even talking about the most exciting stuff!!  

I occurred to me too late of course that we should have started talking about sex.  It would have been hilarious to have either the parents/child table storm off in outrage or have the school administrator table huff and puff in ackwardness.  That's what you get for listening in on others' conversations!!  Lesson to be learned here is try to get one of the booths/tables in the front half of the room.

Someone needs to regulate the haters....this place is fantastic!  I was 25 minutes late for the reservation (beyond my control) but they still allowed the girls to be seated at the table and order drinks while they waited for me. Our server was kind of clueless, but all was forgiven with EACH dish that was brought out. 

First Course:  farona beets - yes I do love beets and order them with nearly every given opportunity, and these have to be my favorite. I wish we also would have ordered the sweet potato tortellini but the group consensus was to limit our consumption for the evening...(please forgive me, I succumbed to peer pressure)...

Main Course: grilled hamachi (my pick); grass fed lamb and a duck special . Let me just say that I did not expect to love the duck as much as I did...I like duck, but i don't LOVE duck and normally wouldn't order it.  I am so thankful that my friend ordered this, I LOVED the duck here, it was excellent. So tender, so flavorful and it was so easy to continue eating this but it was time to switch plates.  Next up, the grilled hamachi...it was elegant and wonderful and everything I expected it to be and more, but I should have tasted this first because I kept salivating over the duck that was no longer in front of me.  After a few bites it was time for the grass-fed lamb which was also very good but alas, it was no duck! So how would I rate the dishes that evening? I think you know. Please do not interpret this to mean that the other dishes were average or sub-par in anyway, because that they weren't, it's just that I wanted to RAVE about the duck in particular because it was extraordinarily good! 

Dessert:  You can't even think about not ordering the chocolate bread pudding.  Please, please order the chocolate bread pudding. 

Oh and the table bread IS worth the calories...slap that butter on and enjoy!

Delightful. Blue hill is the complete package.  No one attacking you to get the check, lovely working staff, and above all the food is heavenly. I ordered the fennel soup ( simply describe as a nice chemistry of seafood with the lovely licorice taste of fennel ). The lovely bartender Rocky was warm and open to all the guests. No wonder this place won the James Beard Foundation Award.

Simply perfection.  Blue Hill has completely spoiled me to the point where I am now comparing all other restaurants against it, which is not really fair.  I go here twice a month and each time is absolutely wonderful in terms of atmosphere and food.  The ingredients are some of the freshest you will find anywhere and the quality really shines through in every dish, all the way down to the amuse.  I'm a pork addict and the pork I've had here has been amazing.  Someone else here described the pork belly as heaven and I absolutely agree.  I am not really one to eat fat, but after trying the pork belly at BH I am a changed woman.  It literally melts in your mouth.  The flavor is outstanding, especially combined with the crispy, slightly salty skin. Every dish I have had here has been phenomenal and trust me I don't say that often about many places.  I plan on taking a trip up to Tarrytown to visit the barn and I know I will not be disappointed.

PORK HEAVEN. No, let me rephrase that: PORK BELLY HEAVEN. I've had some good pork belly. Lots of good pork belly. But, this is the only place where the morsels of warm pork belly just MELTED in my mouth. Combined with the crispy pork skin, it's the best combination ever. Yes, organic Berkshire pork belly, you complete me. (Other than the pork, Stone Barns Sweet Potato Tortellini, This Morning's Farm Egg, Stone Barns Farona Beets were all excellent. Extra love for the tortellini, actually! The Grass Fed Lamb was the other entree and that was good, too. Yes, we got 2 desserts on top of that. We were rather glutonous but that's how we roll, I guess.)


I've heard Blue Hill is the Chez Panisse of the East and well, it could very well be true. The food here is very organic and down-home-farm-cooking but at the same time, very elegant and chic. Service is top knotch and attentive. I consider Blue Hill one of my favorite restaurants in New York City and exactly what I expect when I pay for this kind of price. I've now been here twice and again, extremely happy with the experience. The first time, we sat at the bar and last night, we got a table along the long wall. I have to say, I liked the bar experience better but then, I prefer the side by side seating... But wherever you sit, the food here is worth the time and money.

I don't really understand why everyone has such a hard-on for this place. Sure, I get it -- you have a farm, your food is made from fresh stuff. 

Big deal. I mean, when you combine the largest concentration of capital in the history of mankind with hyper-efficient logistics and transportation networks and it should be ASSUMED that every restaurant worth talking about, at least in this city, has farm fresh ingredients every single day.

The bigger problem is that this fetishizing of ingredients doesn't necessarily translate into the holistic experience of this dish, which, in Blue Hill's case, is boring, trite -- and in the case of the pork loin I had recently -- kind of overcooked.

I dunno. I guess I would go here again if I were married and had run out of options.

I ate here last night with my brother.   The food was amazing.   We had the Farmer's Feast.   One of the courses was a fresh poached egg.  Who knew such a simple dish could be so awesome.   The service was excellent.  I will definitely be back and will recommend to my friends.

The food here is made from the freshest ingredients which are grown on the restaurants own farm.  We had the Farmers feast which consisted of several courses (all fabulous) . The cocks comb salad was so memorable I'm sorry I don't have a picture of that dish!

Food and service was excellent. The only drawback was that it was very cold inside. It was 20 degrees outside and they had the air conditioner on. We asked the wait staff to turn it down and they tried but it never really warmed up. Otherwise, this place is great. The bread is warm and flaky, the wine list is more than sufficient, and I had the hamachi with brussel sprouts, which was excellent.

I was lucky enough to experience Blue Hill on my last trip to New York.  It was one of the best dinning events I have had so far.  And I don't want to sound like a whore...but I have been around in the restaurant world.  I usually feel that once you reach a certain price point that the establishment becomes nothing more than a scene and there is nothing better about the quality and flavor of the food.  Blue Hill does not apply to this formula.
The envrions are simple and elegant.  The server we had was funny, cute and personable.  He toed the line well of entertainment and not being in the way.  He was full of information about the menu and helped me make a solid decision that I enjoyed.  
I love the whole idea of farm to table.  Of course this will add to the cost.  But I feel that is a good reason for higher priced fare.  Most of the time you know the place got the lamb for the same price as everyone else and they just charge $40 for it...because they can.  With Blue Hills philosophy it gives them some good creditability.  
They offered nice pallet clensers between courses.  The wine list was fantastic.  Dessert was killer.  If you have the credit and love the art of food...this is the place.

We made reservations one month in advance for a special birthday dinner on a Wednesday night. My dining partner is in the service industry and was appalled by the nuanced way in which they ignored us.

We showed up for our 9 PM reservation and our coats were taken. We were seated at a good table....and then waited....without menus or water, sitting there, ignored by wait staff and hostesses who were cruising by our table. Finally, we flagged down a staff person and asked for menus. 

It was obvious that because we don't fit the typical demographic -- the two of us are young, queer, punky-looking Asians -- we were given sub-standard service. The manager never even looked at us and the rest of the wait staff effectively ignored us, while being attentive to other tables. We asked to order wine, and our server said that she had to go do something else and then would come back. When she returned, we asked for a wine suggestion with our entrees. She pointed at two wines and then described them by repeating the description on the menu -- it was obvious that she knew nothing about the wines. 

The food was excellent -- the best hamachi I've ever had, so fresh, and paired with a green mustard sauce. It's too bad that the service ruined it for me. 

I won't be returning  -- I will put my dollars elsewhere where we will feel more welcomed.

When my friend Nico suggested this place for dinner last Friday, I swear ---and he's going to hate me for this--- his eyes watered.

So, I knew we had to go.

He was right.

This meal haven is beyond any dining experience I've ever had.

We had a ten course meal (seven appetizers, entree, dessert and coffee) and each bite was magnifique.

We ordered the --fancy word-- for pork belly cooked in it's *good& fat and fish from their daily menu. The menu was beautiful, people. I take notice of menu and napkin quality. I'm not an expert, I mean, Nico had to translate the menu items as he's in the restaurant industry. 
The passion fruit souffle was devine!I felt like Cinderella.
A comfortable Cinderella.

Ingredients are completely organic, grown in their family ranch. 'This morning's eggs are literally from the morning. I could taste the difference! Really.
Fresh baked bread and homemade butter. Perfectly seasoned, crisp, fresh vegetables that teased and satisfied the pallete.  
I could taste the chef's love....
Fancy-word for mushroom soup was served in a beautiful, clear crystal coffee cup and topped with milk foam. ...mmmm......
I could get used to this...

Ambiance was perfect. Minimalist decor tucked in a gorgeous brownstone.

I'll get more info. on the actual names of appetizers and entrees.

Loved sitting next to Frances McDormond and Holly Hunter. But please.... we had a RESERVATION for 10PM and didn't get seated until 11PM!!! I don't care how posh a restaurant thinks they are (or how many drinks they comp)... by the time I was seated I was exhausted, tipsy, woozy, everything. SIgh. 

Had the tasting menu wight the wine pairings. Exceptional.... wish I hadn't been too exhausted to savor.

I have to give this place credit. There was 5 of us that ventured out and thought that we were eating at some place totally different than we had intended. They definitely pulled off what we out seeking though. 

The food was great. 2 friends tried a specialty they had never heard of and enjoyed it very much. We drank wine like water ate like kings and queens and didn't even realize we were in the wrong spot till our check came. : ).  It was a clean and quiet area that allowed the members of our party to chat freely without trying to talk over any surrounding sounds.  

The server was hilarious! He knew when to have fun with us and when to tone it down a bit.  He had my boyfriend going for awhile though. It was funny.

Awesome experience at Blue Hill! Took my friend for her birthday. We both love good food, and opted for the tasting menu. The bread arrives piping hot, with real butter. Then comes a series of amuse bouche (for those who order the tasting menu) - homemade potato chips, fried black kale, leek soup, chicken wing on a skewer., grilled country bread with 3 spreads - white bean puree, fresh ricotta, and (I think) honey butter. Fun little tastes of this and that, what a great way to start a meal! 

The tasting menu itself started with little scallops, cooked to perfection, sitting on a delicious creamy sweet potato puree with toasted pumpkin seeds around the plate. Lovely and delicious. Next came This Morning's Farm Egg, served over a bed of mushrooms and cheese, then they pour a rich mushroom broth over it all. This was fantastic! I wanted to lick the bowl.

Next came the main course - the Berkshire pork. Moist, tender shoulder and a piece of belly meat, super crispy and wonderfully fatty, served with autumn fruits (pear, apple) and a cippiolini onion and grilled fennel. Yummy!

Bring on dessert! We were getting kinda full at this point, but I can always make room for dessert! First one was mashed sweet potato with almond ice cream and pecans. Sweet and light. Then came the apple dessert - granny smith sorbet over cooked apples (so refreshing) and something like a little cake, with cooked apples over it, and a layer of custard, like creme brulee, with the top browned. This was great too. The meal was finished off with a tiny lady apple from the farm.

All in all, an amazing meal, the food tasted very fresh. Interior is cozy, dark, warm. This place would be good for a romantic meal, although tables are a little close to each other. Service was excellent all around. I'd definitely go back to try other things on the menu.

An amazing meal begins when the incredible mini loaves of bread arrive at your table. The Farm Fresh Egg in an earthy mushroom broth takes it to another level. The Hudson Valley Duck was gorgeous (I was practically eating it off the plate of the woman who had ordered it before me) and of course all of the vegetables are so earthy and real! My mates ordered the Cobia (very tasty - had never heard of this fish before) and the pork (I was getting stuffed tasting everyone else's dishes...).

Sadly the desserts just didn't match the savory dishes. All extremely well-prepared, but nothing popped in flavor like the savory items. So that's why only 4 stars this time. But there will be a next!

yeah yeah yeah, another fancy place. 
the food was absolutely great and the prices were as high as you would expect. 
i don't think i would go back here, it just wasn't that special. 
maybe i am jaundiced, but i just didn't feel that this place warrants itself.
just cause you have money to eat great food does NOT make you interesting or cool. these people are just boring jerks who have a lot of money.
wow, i do not usually go on a rant like that. 
it's just that i could live my  whole life without ever going to a place like blue hill again. 
I like to talk to people and enjoy my surroundings, not get treated fake nice cause it costs 35$ for a chicken breast.

This quiet nook of a restuarant can be easily missed on the street; it's within sight of Washington Square Park.  It's very upscale, and has its daily share of anniversary celebrators eating there.  We ate on a wednesday night, and found the service to be 5 star, ambiance to be 4 star, and food to be 3 star for the money.

The restaurant is rather pricey (main courses in the low 30's), and we went for the "Farmer's Feast" at $72pp, which gives you 6 "high cuisine" courses.  Turns out some of the courses were amazing and some were too "high end" for us - the lobster was chewey, the baby lamb chunks were too raw, and the hog's jowel tasted good but felt like a hunk of fat in your mouth.

The best part of the food was the suffle for desert - simply AMAZING and perhaps the best desert we've ever had!

The ambiance is low light, noise absorbing, candles, muted colors - perfect.  The service matches - friendly, helpful, going out of their way to make sure you have a great experience.

Yum!!!  It is fall and the living is easy.  Well at least in New York in the pre-apocolyptic summerlike weather happening in early October.  We can refrain from thinking about climate change while inside this beautiful modern/mid-century modern restaurant, where we secured seats at the bar, just dropping in around 6:30 or 7 on a Saturday night.  The bartender kept busy as she both filled all drink orders along with food orders from the bar.  My hubby later noticed that she personally tested all bottles that she opened - and swallowed!  I guess if you do that on a regular basis, you build up a capacity to drink and do your job at the same time.  She was great - professional yet able to keep up with some of the conversation happening around the bar, which included another couple from DC and a seasoned restaurateur about to open a place in DC near P Street.

The food was great - seasonal, fresh from their partner farm in upstate, nicely presented and flavorful, if you like to actually taste the meat and vegetables on your plate.  I had duck that was absolutely fabulous and the hub had wonderful Berkshire pork loin.  We had skipped on the tasting menu, but heard rave reviews from the couple who had ordered it.  The wine selection wasn't huge, but I wouldn't call it small either.  In addition to my Syrah, I had a raspberry margarita made fresh in front of me, which was awesome.  The meal and the whole experience (great location, interior, presentation, service) was definitely a highlight of our trip, but I will refrain from the five stars until after I've gone another time.

Blue Hill is somewhere between clean&modern and cozy&comforting.  You don't feel oppressed by the decor, but also won't feel intimidated.   The food is, as has been previously said, delicious, local and fresh.  

Regarding the service, I thought that their timing was a bit off.  Everything was moving at a normal, classy-restaurant pace (slow enough not to feel rushed, quick enough to not feel ignored)....  until we ordered.  Then without even 2 minutes passing, our appetizers arrived... voila!

Forty five or so minutes later our entrees arrived.  I could easily have waited longer for the appetizer so as to not feel abandoned during the intermission.  

But that's just quibbles.  The experience, overall, is excellent.

I was so excited to go to Blue Hill!  I had heard about the farm and sister restaurant in upstate and was really hopeful to find the fresh vegetation that I enjoy when I am in SF or Cali.....all grown on the farm, organically.  sounded right up my alley.

I walked into Blue Hill with extremely high expectations.  I was so excited for this dining experience but was a little let down.  

The service was great and they continued bringing hot delicious bread once your bread on the table becomes cold...all paired with delicious creamery butter.  The glass of rose champagne was amazing.  The dairy free chilled corn soup was excellent.  The chenin Blanc wine recommendation was perfect with the meal.  the desert....fresh peach cobbler with some type of mint or basil ice cream and chocolate bread pudding (both shared) were tasty and delicious.

The problem, I did not like my entree at all.  I had the cobia sans the pig fat....described to me like a type of swordfish fillet over fresh vegetables.  It arrived as toughish slices of seared rare fish that were fishy and our waitress specifically mentioned that it was not a fishy fish.

The beautiful, 6 ft tall, shaved head model like hostess was brilliant, and accommodated our request for a larger table than the party of 2 we were.....I am sure Blue Hill is her day job and she will be a famous model some day.

I would try BH again but might stick with the veggie entrees.

Wonderful! My wife and I waited until the last minute to make reservations so the only seating was at 10pm but it was worth the wait. 

The portions on the tasting menu were generous and the food delectable. The corn soup was heavenly and my wife's seasonal vegetables delicious. We've never tasted such delicious tomatoes and melon. The crab appetizer was the only disappointment of the night, but that was quickly forgotten when we tasted the Long Island Yellow fin Tuna (yes they catch Tuna off of Long Island...who'd have thunk it!)....any way, it was served rare and was delicious. Same for the Lamb and the duck we also tried. We finished with blueberries, corn ice cream (yes you read that right) and cheesecake. A seemingly bizarre combination that worked quite well. 

Friendly staff and warm atmosphere rounded out an excellent night.

As soon as you walk in to the restaurant, you'll be stepping into the dining area so expect to be a little bewildered just as I did.  I felt a little like I crashed a party (hypothetically speaking of course) and felt really rude, but the feeling wore off in 2 seconds as the hostesss welcomed us.  

I was super hungry so was ecstatically happy when the bread basket came out.  Not sure if it was because I was so hungry, but the bread tasted so good.  They were more like bread sticks that's crispy outside and warm inside and the butter was really good so it was the perfect combination.  (I have a big thing for butter & bread).  I had their crab appetizer which was flavorful and had a refreshing taste to it and the pork which was the most tender piece of meat I have ever tasted.  Everything tasted fresh and healthy.  I also loved the ambiance and the service was excellent.  It's a small restaurant, but it felt roomier than most since the tables were spread apart.  I'm a type of person that likes her personal space and really appreciate places that acknowledge that.  It was a treat dining here.  Don't you love it when places meet your expectations?

Blue Hill distinguishes itself from the other restaurants on so many levels.  So far, it has been one of my most satisfying dining experience in New York.  

Let us review the dining ladder:

1st rung: For the quality of the food, it offers a great selection of local seasonal ingredients, the prices are quite accommodating.  How many restaurants can even offer a "this morning's farm egg"?  (I was surprised how it was served more like an egg foam.)  I've been here twice and the soup has never failed me.  Especially with their warm bread and butter (even though it is not churned up at their farm).

2nd: It's an enchanting hideaway - almost difficult to find.  The lighting is perfect, floral arrangements are dear but not overbearing, and the dining space is perfectly arranged.

3rd: Their service is a perfect balance of professional and warming hospitality.  They are more than happy to share the photo album of their farm in Stone Barns and give you a tour of the restaurant's kitchen.  

And at the top: If you love Blue Hill in New York, you have an exciting destination that awaits you at Stone Barns.  I can't wait to visit!!

p.s. There was one disappointment in the meal.  The greens with pancetta was a bit lacking.  The pancetta were cut into too small of dices that provided minimal flavoring on the greens.

I love this place! its a really homey but sophisticated space with professional, warm and friendly waitstaff and the FOOD! oh the food is seasonal and fantabulous, and everything was perfectly seasoned. the ingriedients taste like they were just picked from the garden.  you dont go to get stuffed but to have a really healthy and wonderful meal.

Cute little place with a menu full of unique dishes and fresh ingredients. I found my meal to be tasty and filling but not to the point of making deliciousness noises. It was a kind of subdued satisfaction. I had the "farm egg" appetizer, which was a little foamy and strange for me, but I think they change it up daily, and I like the concept. However, there was not one vegetarian main dish on the menu, which I found ironic given all the cool combinations of vegetables they serve with the meat and fish - I'm sure they'd make a veggie plate if you were to ask, but I think it merits the little bit of extra thought it would take to add a meatless entree.  

Interestingly, I went here on mother's day on a date, and they were giving little gifts to all the mothers. I am a 26-year old non-mother, and I was interested to see how the waitress would handle this situation. She gave me the gift but said "I don't know whether you're a mother or not, so if not, in honor of being a woman!" Tastefully done.

i have been searching for this place since i went there on a date (her choice - god i love foodies) years ago.  We had the tasting menu and i must say that every morsel of food was thought out so meticulously 
I think the chef must be some rain-man of cooking; probably can't ties his shoes, but if you ask what to pair with a garlicky kalamata olive from the north of Greece...he does not hesitate "caramelized pears...definitely caramelized pears yeah definitely... " 

the cheese/olive course has left me dreaming.....

I was really excited to go to Blue Hill, maybe because of all the great YELP reviews. After wards I felt a little let down.  I liked how they use local foods and base their menu on the Hudson Valley. I had he beef and my wife had the lamb which while very good, I guess didn't reach my expectations. The service was exceptional, which if not would have lead to a three star review. To sum up we both thought we could have gone to a place like Union Square Cafe and gotten a larger serving and better food for the same price.
Great food and service.  Very cozy and romantic.  Recommend for a special date or a double date.

Well, I certainly admire the concept, and I like the name (seeing as I'm from Blue Hill myself), and the food was good, very Chez Panisse in concept and execution.  But there's a lot more spirit at Chez Panisse.  I think it's something about New York.  It gets all serious, even as far north as the Village.  (This is why I like Manhattan further downtown:  edgier, and more relaxed.)  What I like about Chez Panisse is that it still feels experimental.  Conceivably, a dish might not work.  But there's stretch in the concept.  This -- for what essentially is elegant but real food cuisine -- is too uptight.  It should be bit more fun.  You get the feeling from Alice Waters that she is slayed by the concept of local eating, not just because it's right, or because it's local, but because it's so darn good.  There's enthusiasm there that's missing here.  Being psyched is a good thing in life.

This is a darling restaurant!  I have been 3 times now, and if it weren't for my budget (not big enough!) I would go back again and again.  Try the dessert tasting menu! (Who would have thought you could do that to an avocado!) I have also had the full dinner tasting menu (we began at (9:30 and closed the place out after 3 rounds of dessert and petit fours at around midnight) My partner proposed to the dessert chef after tasting his pancakes (which I suppose are superior to mine ;)

The service is perfect, and the place is quiet, warm, cozy and perfectly romantic.   Make reservations - now!

Impeccable service. So friendly; so attentive! 

Having read all you can about the great organic foods here (that are harvested from within 250 mi only), I knew the meal would be really nice. I'd say I almost jinxed that, however, and expected the heavens in my mouth... but overall, very tasty and beautiful. Had the this morning's egg, venison with artichoke puree on some baby spinach and mushrooms, and the chocolate bread pudding. Each was simple with beautiful pure flavor. 

They also gave us a shot of warm squash soup and chocolate macaroons gratis. 

In drinks, the Long Island Rose we had was very nice (RE: service, the server let us taste both roses before going with the one we chose), and the espresso was so perfect, and not bitter whatsoever! 

Beautiful setting, very romantic. I did see people in casual attire, but definitely go and dress it up a little if you want. 

And to say once more - the best service I've had. It was not pretentious; it just felt like people were proud of their jobs there and were happy to make you happy.

Innovative Organic OASIS

So glad I grubbed here before Chef Dan Barber captured the 2006 James Beard award for BEST CHEF: NEW YORK CITY. Franco is the MOST charming GM from down under.  Rocky will keep you rolling with his adventures from behind the bar. The wine pairings are amazing --- ask Claire to surpise you since her palette is consistently being fine tuned by the Vino Vixens. Superb service: ask for Matthew, Andrew or Dave (in that order, of course).

The regular menu was inspired. The tasting menu (looked) somewhat less so.

All the food is local, organic, biodynamic, etc., which is good in itself, but the food was very very well put together.

One star off for:
-- somewhat uninspired wine list and a waitress that didn't really have much to say, so led us astray. "Drinking beautifully" does not describe a Syrah which falls off the cliff halfway through your mouth.
-- The back deck. Really, folks, this feels & looks like you just crammed it in. It's way too bright and sort of ugly-- especially after you've just walked through the warm, bubbly, conversational, well-lit front room. Make it a bit better. (Our waitress did, however, re-seat us without hesitation when we asked. It'd be nice to not have to, though).

I'd knock it down to 3 1/2 stars, but I'll kick it back up to 4 for the quality of the food alone.

Overall, quite good. This place knows how to braise a giant portion of lamb so that you've got a) way too much to eat and b) lamb that would fall apart under the gentle ministrations of a plastic fork.

Not that they'd give you a plastic fork, but boy was I the envy of the idiots who'd spent $8 on a "united snackbox" in the EWR-SFO flight the next day.

everythings comes from dan barber's restaurant/farm at the old rockefeller estate in pocantico hills. (blue hill stone barns is a great dining destination).  everything's grown on the premises, so expect things like your beets to be very beety, carrots to be pure with carrot flavors... and even their pork to be soft, toothsome, with a sticky fat.  This place reminds you how imoprtant ingredients are to food, and how far the ingredients can take the restaurants and speak for the restaurants purveyors. (in this case, the same people)

This place was impeccable, absolutely impeccable.  The first was exquisite and the service was remarkable.  I ordered the colbia, not knowing that it was fish, and when it arrived, I was crestfallen to realize that it wasn't a vegetarian dish.  My cousin explained the situation to the waitress and she immediately took it away and asked what I would like instead.  I got the cauliflower steak which sounded mediocre but was quite surprisingly delectable!  I was simply impressed with the great service, the ambiance, and the quality of the food.  I'll recommend this to everyone I know.

Honestly, I don't have a bad word about this place. I was just thinking: Can I give it five stars? Then I challenged myself to think of something about the meal that was not excellent, and I failed. 
  My momz and I got the "farmers feast" tasting menu, which I think is the way to go. It's 68 bucks and you get so so so much delicious food, I think it really is worth it. They started us off with like 10 amuse bouches, including beet chips, (yum), mini salted ricotta sandwiches (delicious), and an AMAZING applecider/celery juice concotion. The mushroom salad was great, as was the lamb (as exceptional as the lamb was the its accompanying side of roasted endive--hearty and satisfying). I loved the steamed cheesecake for dessert, it wasnt overwhelming like you might expect i would be. 
   We also had cocktails, and i had something called the orange glow: blood orange juice infused with tea, and vodka (some other tasty stuff was in there too)..great, although I like my drinks with more sauce, and this one was more juice-y than booze-y. However, what I was missing there in terms of alcohol I made up for with the wine pairings that went with the meal--perfection. 
 Service, also exceptional. My mom's allergic to shellfish, which we both forgot, and when they brought out a dish with crab in it, we felt horrible but said there was nothing to do, but we couldn't eat it. They promptly brought out another excellent fish dish within 5 minutes. They could have made us feel like jerks, since it was the fixed tasting menu after all and we should have said something, but they were nothing but accomodating.
  Yay Blue Hill, yay.

One of the best meals I've had in NYC.  I found no fault in anything from the wonderful service to the amazing food.  Everything was fresh and bursting with flavor.  A little pricey but worth it.  I would go back in a heartbeat.

In fairness, I can't lay all of the blame for our terrible evening at the kitchen's feet --- that honor goes to the pompous gentleman to our right who was enjoying dessert as we came in, and yet persisted in ordering glass after glass, extra course upon extra course, as he lectured at great volume the couple to his other side about French politics, the trouble with today's parents, the moral imperative of naming one's children with grace, and a dozen other topics he apparently held quite dear.

Dear lord, his braying was almost enough to distract us from the fact that every last thing we ate was criminally over-salted, from the emerald-green lettuce broth supporting a bevvy of Disney-adorable baby mushrooms beneath "this morning's farm egg", to the too-enthusiastically brined Berkshire pork loin (which was almost redeemed by angelic creme fraiche spaetzle).

We decided to pass on dessert, in favor of after-dinner drinks when I spied Chartreuse VEP on the menu --- I've always wanted to try it, but blanched at the $100+ price for a whole bottle. Was I crushed when they didn't have it? Not so much as I was unsurprised, as this was the third beverage we'd asked for during the course of the meal that they'd "just run out of". Uh-huh.

Oh, I'm really sad.  I fear that my expectations were too high because I was a little bit disappointed in my mouth at Blue Hill.   I think that people who love Blue Hill might also like an apartment full of white space and clean lines.  I like things a bit more dissheveled.  I thought the food was clean...to the point of being clear.  I like a chaos of flavors partying it up punk rock style in my mouth.  I want to be punched in the face by flavor.  Blue HIll is much more refined.  At least what I had was.  I had the Farmer's Egg (a great start), the cobia (which smelled to the point of stinking) and the bread pudding.  On the plus side, the service there was perfect.

There are not a ton of places that I will stop quoting Family Guy episodes and act like an adult for, but I made an exception for Blue Hill. Napkin on lap, I pretended to be some semblance of an adult, not quite befitting of the elegant, upscale, quiet interior. 

Blue Hill plays wonderful homage to lovely, seasonal fare, much of it raised upstate at Stone Barns, where they have a sister restaurant. The appetizers included a beautiful winter veggie salad with mushroom gelee (huh?), a crab salad, pancetta ravioli, all delicious. And unlike so many places where the appetizers far outpace the entrees, here the entrees were incredible too. They had plenty of fish dishes for my kosher friends, venison for my inner cave-girl, and veal for well... I guess people who like veal. (Yeah... I had nothing on that last one. Sorry.) The wine list was very well priced, with the majority of bottles being $60-130. 

The price tag of course was grown-up and adult too. So much so that in order to come here again, I may have to get a real job. But nah, that wouldn't be as fun.

FANTASTIC! One of the BEST tasting meals I have had. 

First, this place is beautiful, cozy, warm, romantic. The service is exceptional and very classy and professional. These people know how to run a restaurant. 

We had the tasting menu and each course was exquisite (and yummy!). The Maine lobster was to die for. The venison was cooked perfectly and the presentation of all the courses was perfectly done. The word I would use to describe the food is FRESH. 

The price for a 5 course tasting is $68. Not bad for such high quality food in a beautiful setting. 

I want to go back and try items off the menu. I also want to try Stone Barns and make a trip up there. 

Highly Recommended!

My two favorite dinners in New York last year were at Blue Hill; I went to both the West Village and the Stone Barns locations. The food here defines the term "haute barnyard" as it comes directly from the farm and onto your plate. Everything tastes sublime, is exquisitely presented and guaranteed to make the most of what the seasonal produce has to offer. Past standout dishes include warm mushroom salad, red snapper in a corn chowder broth and a pink peppercorn souffle for dessert. The wine list is fantastic, in fact we liked one of our wines so much that my sister (who is a wine buyer) ordered it for her store the next day.
 
The service at Blue Hill superior. It is attentive, well paced and never overbearing. When we dined at Stone Barns, we were having such a great time in the country that we decided to stay the night. Blue Hill called inns of various price ranges in the area and gave us a list of options at the end of our meal. When we decided where we wanted to stay, they called and made the reservation for us. The whole process was thoughtful, graceful and unobtrusive.
 
I would recommend either location equally, but if you go to Stone Barns do yourself a favor and go in the summer when it's pleasant to walk the grounds. In order to make the most of the experience, we arrived an hour or so before our reservation and strolled around, saw all the animals chilling throughout the property and had a drink in the lounge . It is such a treat to escape the city and dine in such a beautiful setting. It is well worth the extra time and money.
Fresh, seasonal, tasty, but not the flavor punch for which I hoped.  Loved the warm chocolate bread pudding, though.  If I went again I'd go for the tasting menu.

What a beautiful little restaurant ( I love the NYC style little discreet sign right on the street and down the stairs into the restaurant) and what stunning food! We enjoyed a 5 course tasting menu (with some additional amuses) brought to us with impeccable service, even as the restaurant got very very busy.  I loved the Nantucket  bay scallops dish, one of several to employ fresh juice (this one had a pear juice). I also loved the Greens Ravioli, and most of all we both almost DIED over the Milk Fed Capon.  Wow! So super tender and succulent....it must have been cooked sous vide.  We really appreciate the premise behind the menu as well ( local and sustainable) which was one of the reasons we chose to come here, and we both thought this concept was carried through exactly.  Thankfully, all the flavors and preparations were creative and exciting, and one could really tell there was much thought put into the dishes.  ( It does seem that often ingredient driven cuisine can seem uninspired) 
The wine director was extremely helpful and took care to choose our wines for us, which she did exceptionally well.  This was just an incredible dinner!

Probably my favorite restaurant in Manhattan - always reliable, after all these years.  The food is innovative, well thought out and tasty.  I suggest the tasting menu paired with some California wine.  If you sit at the tables in the courtyard, you will feel like you are in Napa, especially on a sunny day.

I have to preface my review by revealing that I'm a vegetarian. I'm never sure if my mediocore dining experiences happen because a restaurant is better at their meat dishes than their veggie ones.

I was excited to eat here, being a proponent of eating seasonal, fresh vegetables. Since I couldn't get a reservation, we made sure to get here soon after they opened at 5:30 p.m. to get seats at the bar. 

They served a chilled cucumber gazpacho as an amuse bouche. It was delightful: fresh, crisp, and bright. My green bean and fennel appetizer was just so-so. My companion's heirloom tomato salad was more interesting; I've never had fresh tomato and tarragon together before. Since there was no vegetarian main course listed on the menu, we asked what they had to offer and that night it was a celery gratin with a very soupy pistou. It lacked vibrance and freshness -- maybe it seemed more of an autumn dish? The desserts (peach cobbler with pistachio ice cream and an almond financier with sweet corn (!) ice cream) were both good...especially the cobbler.

Overall, it was a bit disappointing. Maybe we're just spoiled because we live in northern California where the food is mostly good and always fresh. For $30/entree I was expecting more flavor.

This was one of the best meals I have ever had.

It started with complimentary shooters of cucumber gazpacho.

We then tried the infamous "This Morning's Farm Egg" in a stew of mushrooms and lettuce broth, the heirloom tomato salad, the Maine crabmeat on fennel salad and green garden gazpacho, the Chatham Cod in dairyless corn and clam chowder, and special of the day sea bass in a vegetable puree.  All were prepared and presented to perfection.  Crisp, fresh -- dare I say nearly naked? -- flavors shone through in each dish.

Although quite full, we topped off this incredible meal with the summer berry coupe (which was good but did not reach the same heights as the appetizers and entrees).

The atmosphere is cozy and warm, with dark wood and leather furnishings.  Elegant and romantic.  [Note:  Although Open Table displays a casual dress code for this restaurant, we were embarrassed to find ourselves with no time to change out of our tourist outfits (T-shirt / tank top and shorts), and we stuck out like sore thumbs.  No one was dressed "casually" here!]

Small flashlights are provided for those who need an extra boost to read the menu.  There is a story behind the flashlights; see if your waiter knows it!

This place is amazing - wonderful, fresh, local food and great service. But be aware that it is expensive. If you have the cash, or a special event that you want to celebrate, then check this place out.

My fiance made a reservation at Blue Hill during a weekend in New York City (we are wannabe foodies from Chicago).  To reiterate some of the other comments: staff incredibly warm, but not obtrusive or annoying.  Perfect lighting, soft, but not dim.  No music - wonderful, as opposed to the next night at WD-50 where we could barely hear each other speak.  I had the hour-long poached egg appetizer, grilled Cobia for my entree and rhubarb cheesecake for dessert.  Fiance had the crab salad, duck entree and sour cherry cobbler.  

All in all a wonderful evening, would compare to North Pond in Chicago, with the organic, local and seasonal foods listed on the menu.  

I'm all for inventive menus, but Blue Hill uses simple classic flavors in a way where the flavor and food are what shine through - not necessarily the chef's new cool way to fry mayonnaise into little cubes.

Blue Hill was recommended to me by NYC ex-pats currently living in San Francisco. They billed it as the closest thing NYC has to a northern Californian restaurant.  Well, this can be interpreted as both a negative and positive comment. Ideally, "northern Californian" concentrates on fresh, local ingredients using cooking techniques that highlight the produce/meat/etc. without using loads of spices and sauces that masks its inherent flavor. Apparently with the rash of "northern Californian" restaurants I've tried in SF, it can also mean bland cooking without giving thought to anything beyond the transition of raw to cooked.

I'm happy to report Blue Hill definitely hits the positive mark! This restaurant is truly great. The interior is softly lit with a cozy, modern feel. The hostess was able to change my reservation for both the time and number of people on the spot. The server was friendly and I have to commend her for putting up with the inane, not-at-all funny, stupid-ass "jokes" one person in my party kept making (details are best kept as a faded memory).

I ordered This Morning's Farm Egg for the appetizer and Chatham Cod for the main.

Both dishes were absolutely wonderful. The mushrooms in the appetizer were cooked perfectly with the right amount of firmness and the broth served as a good compliment to the truly fresh egg.
The Chatham Cod had great flavor and was prepared to perfection.

The dessert was cheesecake and this was their only miss. The actual cheesecake was good but the accompanying flavors threw it off. It was way too froufrou-ed up. They overpowered the cheesecake and were too great of a contrast.

The dessert did not detract enough to take away a star from the rating. (Okay, maybe 4.9). 

So, NYC residents - try this place!! Great food that doesn't need an aura of pretension and showmanship.

San Francisco - pay attention. Fresh, seasonal cooking is not enough on its own. Blue Hill does it right.

On a side note, I found it interesting that this is the only NYC restaurant I tried that lists the origin of the ingredients. In SF, every farm, dairy, etc is named on the menu.

Unbelievable.  An absolutely terrific place.  Down to earth, you feel like you can ask a question about the food or wine without the staff turning up their noses...just a terrifically pleasant experience for foodies and wannabe foodies alike.

The tasting menu, if you're up for it, is excellent, but starve yourself before you arrive...it's way too much food.

Blue Hill is my new absolute favorite restaurant. I had the tasting menu on my most recent visit and everything was absolutely outstanding. The lightly smoked trout starter, followed by a translucent chunk of Chatham cod were unbelievable. Baby lamb with braised escarole was succulently tender and the little jar of steamed cheesecake was a lusciously sweet finish to the meal.

Fresh, clean flavors with "seasonal" and "local" being the key words here. A lot of the produce comes from the upstate farm as do the extraordinarily fresh eggs that are brought in each day for the famous appetizer "This Morning's Farm Egg", which features an uber-fresh egg perched atop greens and a turnip puree. A must-try.

Prices are very reasonable here considering this is extremely high-quality food. I would return in a second and I will!

Blue Hill is a delight! With fresh, flavorful food served in small portions that are just the right size, you always leave Blue Hill feeling satisfied and not too stuffed. Even the toasted bread they give you is good. When I last ate there, the crab salad was delicate and tasty. The duck was cooked just right and flavorful and the chicken was simple but brimming with flavor. The "strawberries and cream" dessert with lemon cake was light with the right balance of sweetness and tartness. Blue Hill's forte is its fancy flavors with simple dishes - delicious! Can't wait to try out Blue Hill at Stone Barns...

A restaurant that doesn't try to do anything except serve great food with great service in a pleasant atmosphere. No gimmicks here -- the food speaks for itself in its freshness and preparation. The dining room is quietly elegant with no music to shout over -- how refreshing! The service was impeccable and unobtrusive -- the staff knows what they are there to do -- to know their menu, present your meal, and attend to your needs. Looking around, I saw a room full of New Yorkers enjoying a real meal in a real restaurant, not a clubhouse of the fabulous trying to be seen. Beautiful experience.

One of New York's finest!  This gorgeous American restaurant offers a very grown up dining experience without being stuffy or uptight.  Slightly expensive, but it's absolutely, positively worth every penny for the fresh, seasonal food and impeccable wine list.

about: Blue Hill New York opened in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village neighborhood in April of 2000.The restaurant has evolved over the last two decades, sourcing ingredients from Blue Hill Farm, the Barber family’s dairy in Great Barrington, MA; from the Stone Barns Center for Agriculture in Pocantico Hills, NY; as well as from farms within 250 miles of New York City. Family Meal began in the summer of 2021 and welcomes guests to a menuless dinner experience of shared plates.

questions.question: Is this the restaurant the Obamas came for dinner?
